So, thus, Atra, this comes down to a discrepancy in belief, really. And that discrepancy lies in these thought processes:

1. 'Merry Christmas' operates as a predominantly Christian greeting.

2. 'Happy Holidays' operates as a universal greeting.

3. 'Merry Christmas' may offend people of the denominations involved in Judaism, Islam, Buddhism, Taoism, Atheism, Shintoism, Taoism, and other faiths not related to Christianity.

4. 'Happy Holidays' will not offend people of any denomination ("offend" being used in the purely literal sense, not in the sense that 'people will look at you funny.'), since it is a universal greeting, intended to include all people in a single phrase.

How is that an incorrect argument, in any way, shape, or form?

I'll grant you that very few will be offended enough by the phrase to make an impact upon someone outwardly. However, when the phrase "Happy Holidays" is strictly better in every feasible way, that means that there is no reason to not use it in those instances where offending someone is a possibility.

Quote: Teh Dude, 2005-12-19T22:17:50Z
Absolutely, "anyone" is an overgeneralisation.  The vast majority would not appreciate it and would prefer (or at least be less confused) to hear "Merry Christmas".

However, the argument still stands.  Please give me your thoughts on this with "anyone" replaced by "many people at all".

Right by majority is not a definitive answer as to why "Happy Holidays" is not a better greeting. The debate doesn't hinge so much on whom "Merry Christmas" would offend, per se, but rather who "Merry Christmas" would offend in comparison to who "Happy Holidays" would offend. And I don't think that you (Nor anyone) can claim with any reasonable evidence that less people would indeed be offended by "Happy Holidays" upon the same level as those who would be offended by "Merry Christmas."

Since "Happy Holidays" is a universal term (And why this is so, I'll explain below), it encompasses all ideologies into the greeting. If a person, therefore, has a problem with it, it isn't under the same justifications as a person who has a problem with "Merry Christmas."

The person who has a problem with "Happy Holidays" isn't having said problem because "Happy Holidays" is in any way offensive to them, beyond the thought that they dislike the greeting as the universal that it is.

Quote: Teh Dude, 2005-12-19T22:17:50Z
The interaction point is not entirely serious.  However, it is true that the only way to reduce offense to others to an absolute zero is by not interacting with anyone whatsoever.  In fact, you would probably have to go even further and eliminate all people.

It is true that someone, somewhere will be offended by it. I'm saying that being offended as such is under a different justification than a person being offended by "Merry Christmas." Under this definition, people being offended can be divided into at least two distinct categories: Those who are rightly offended, and those who are wrongly offended. My claim hinges upon this difference, in that getting offended over, say, a squirrel climbing a tree would fall under the "wrongly offended" category, whereas getting offended at the atrocities of Sadaam Hussein would fall under the "Rightly offended" category. This distinction is an important one to make and accept if one is to end up at the conclusion that "Happy Holidays" is strictly better as a greeting than "Merry Christmas."

Quote: Teh Dude, 2005-12-19T22:17:50Z
By way of example, there exist some people for whom any kind of season's greeting is abhorrent.  In this instance, saying either "Merry Christmas" or "Happy Holidays" will be offensive.  As such the best option is to say nothing at all to this type of people.  The only way to ensure that, when presented with a random individual, you do not offend them is to not greet them.

And while I do agree with this, this type of "being offended" falls under the "wrongly offended" category, that I outlined above. Why, you ask? Because, as you said, "Merry Christmas" and "Happy Holidays" will both have the same impact upon that person. But since we're on the subject, and looking at things from that person's perspective (Since this is about as neutral as I could hope to make people look at the situation), from his point of view, he can objectively determine which, of the two greetings, is indeed better. As I stated in my last post, "Merry Christmas" is a greeting that will offend anyone (And yes, that's an overgeneralization, but it works, in this sense, since the random sampling that I'm referring to is within the realm of reasonable functionality, compared to the opposite sampling) who doesn't celebrate Christmas, whereas "Happy Holidays" will only offend a single person from a single group at a time, not as a whole.

I don't think I explained that terribly well, so I'll elaborate:

Let's take, hypothetically, that we can amass a meeting of all people in the world, and judge the offensiveness of each statement, we do the following:

Ask the gathering how many would be inwardly or outwardly offended at a "Merry Christmas" greeting.

We then go on to ask the gathering how many would be inwardly or outwardly offended at a "Happy Holidays" greeting.

In this instance, the numbers of whom don't matter. What matters is the reasoning behind each justification for being offended. On the one hand, those who are offended at "Merry Christmas" may have a slew of reasons to be offended, and rightfully so. On the other hand, those who are offended at "Happy Holidays" may have an equal number and equally weighty reasons to be offended, but not rightfully so. This is the core of the argument that I'm trying to get at. To draw a comparison between the two is doing a disservice to the argument as a whole, because the justifications for the two are unequal in essence.

Quote: Kablizzy, 2005-12-19T22:17:50Z
Here you reduce my entire point that the statement "Happy Holidays" is meaningless in the UK to the phrase "not wanting to sound like an idiot".  "Happy Holidays" is meaningless and will make you look like an idiot (so not strictly meaningless as it displays idiocy).  People do not want to look like idiots.

Ah, but I'm not! This is the argument that has been provided thusfar, to justify why "Merry Christmas" is strictly better than "Happy Holidays." And such a justification is invalid to the argument at hand. Since you've clarified, I can go on to state the following: Regardless of "wanting" to look like an idiot or not, within a given region, it might be strictly better to say "Merry Christmas," since the population in that given area or region would be used to/desensitized to/oblivious to the phrase "Happy Holidays." However, this doesn't have any bearing upon whether a person will yet be offended in the same way by either phrase. Quote: Teh Dude, 2005-12-19T22:17:50Z
Finally, on what basis do you call this a "mismanagement of morals"?  Please tell me the set of ethics at work here?

It could be a number of things. When I stated that it was a mismanagement of morals, I should have more clearly alluded to the "correct" and "incorrect" justification of things. But the mismanagement of morals that I spoke of was as follows:

1. A person who is offended by "Merry Christmas" is offended because of religious and cultural implications and ramifications, hearkening back to oppressions and misdeeds done to certain groups of people in the past, and continuing on, in however small quantities, by those who refuse to change the phrase for this reason.

2. A person who is 'offended' (Offended in quotes, because the justification isn't on par with the justification of being offended by something genuinely offensive, but included for clarity) by "Happy Holidays is 'offended' because of global and regional traditions, leading to uncomfortable situations.

The mismanagement part comes when one tries to draw an equal comparison between the two. The reason why it can't be done is because the ramifications of both, and the justifications for both, are by no means equal in nature or practice. This is why the moralistic stances of both can't be equalized.

hey,

First of all, we're absolutely flattered by the idea behind N: Legacy. That you guys love something we made this much is inspiring. The name is cool too.

After _much_ deliberation, we're going to have to say that we can't
make a special custom version of N. here's our reasoning on the topic:

we learned when adding user levels to N1.4 that it's very difficult
to please most people and be as fair and unbiased as possible. By far
the biggest complaints referenced either our having not included
certain maps or authors, or our having included too many maps by
one author.

In light of that, we feel that by releasing a special edition of N
devoted to only a specific group's levels (regardless of the fact
that you guys are very talented level makers) we would be:

1. showing favouritism

2. opening the doors for tons of similar requests -- i.e everyone
will want us to make a special version of N with just their levels.

We think it's a _very_ good idea, and we hope you do decide to collect a
group of levels and release them together (for now, you could use the "type" field to get them in a particular order).

v1.5 will hopefully have a better userlevels system, which would allow
for multiple "userlevel.txt"-like files at once (we'll consider the possibility of using the user levels to replace the built-in levels), and/or episodes or
something similar.

I hope you guys understand the reasoning behind this decision -- we
want to support you, but we don't think we can do this specifically.
Please let us know if there's another way we can help though!

It makes us really excited and happy that people are getting so
creative and inspired, and doing such cool things -- which of course makes
having to say no so much harder.

Again, we're really sorry,
Mare and Raigan




Quote
Mare and Raigan,
  A few of us in the community are starting work on a large N project. Five of us - Maximo, Kablizzy, LittleViking001, Nevermore and tktktk - are each planning to contribute 100 levels to a huge levelpack. That's 100 episodes altogether, as many as you two put out with v1.4. If all goes well, we'll be ready to release them on New Year's.
  Now, there are some things we'd like to ask of you, if you can help us. We've been talking about the possibility of releasing all the levels in their own version of N. N: Legacy would have all of our levels put in the Play Game mode, as opposed to the regular metanet levels that exist currently. Our goal is to craft something from the heart, and something to tribute Metanet, and all the work that you guys have put into this game, and this community, for us. We have been discussing a plethora of options for Legacy, and the goal that we're shooting for is to create a sub-game to N. We would like to discuss the feasability of such a project, and will be more than happy to answer any questions about what exactly we're wanting to do with Legacy.
  But of course, what would Legacy be without you guys? Another point we wanted to talk to you about is whether you would want to contribute as well. Quote: Teh Dude, 2005-12-21T15:42:29Z
Is your argument basically along the lines: If we had no pre-existing seasonal greeting and we had to choose one, then HH is the best as it does not offend as many people as MC does?

Because if so, I agree.

Roughly, yes. Happy Holidays doesn't offend as many people in the same fashion (An important distinction in the argument) as Merry Christmas does. Relative offensiveness is the main criterion upon which we judge which greeting is the better of the two. In certain regions, Happy Holidays loses all meaning to those in that region. Therefore, Happy Holidays is the better of the two greetings, outside of those regions.

I think that's about as close as I care to get the argument this morning. Determining which regions those are, however, is the difficult part, and thus, a law or decree can't be enacted. It then becomes a personal judgment call for each person within and outside of those regions as to whether or not to use Happy Holidays as a greeting. In those areas where it's applicable, I can still definitively claim that Happy Holidays is strictly better. In those regions where Happy Holidays has no meaning, it still has some validity to those with whom it does hold meaning (As a Jewish person becoming offended at Merry Christmas in the UK is equalized to a Jewish person becoming offended at Merry Christmas in the US), however small that population may be. At that point, Happy Holidays wouldn't be a priori better, in that case (In the UK, Australia, etc.), but indeed worse.

As I said in my post to TDL, this isn't as universal as I had first claimed, due to the regional differences that you guys pointed out. Thus, my argument operates in places where this is an issue, instead of globally, since, as you guys have said, the greeting is meaningless in Australia and the UK. But my idea of right and wrong offensiveness plays fully into this notion, since people that would be offended by Happy Holidays would be offended in a very different fashion than those offended by Merry Christmas, as the justifications for both are dissimilar to each other. Stemming from that,

Exactly, which is why you can't decree it as a law. All it takes is some awareness and understanding for people to accept it as commonality, and, really, is the only way that such a thing could ever happen, with any success.

Quote: Teh Dude, 2005-12-21T15:42:29Z
So perhaps in an ideal world with a blank slate, we might come up with some universal greeting with no religious connotations at which others can take offense.  However, this is not an ideal world.

Very true, it isn't. One very important thing that backs all of my arguments (And too bad my old posts were wiped, or I'd search for this for you), is that solely because our world isn't - and can't be - perfect, doesn't stop us from striving for that perfection. Many of my ideals on morality, attitudes - pretty much everything applicable to Social Engineering and Social Sciences - Stems from the thought of what an ideal person, and an ideal society, should be. Whether that goal is attainable in full or not shouldn't stop us from trying the best we can to reach that goal.

For instance, I can tell you definitively that murder is wrong, from this standpoint. Not because God has decreed it to be wrong, and not because society has decreed it to be wrong, but because there are a number of emotional, social, physical, monetary, and many other factors upon which we can judge the correctness and incorrectness of... pretty much anything. I have a long way yet to go with the idealist theory that I'm operating on, but I'll eventually be writing a book on it.

Anyway, I will go out on a limb, right here and now, to state that eventually (No idea how long it will take), Happy Holidays will become the accepted greeting, globally. As Tolerance spreads, and cultural and regional differences thin between peoples (Heck, it's amazing that you and I are even discussing this, from different parts of the world, and all that), Happy Holidays will only become more applicable, as people become more aware of other cultures and regions around them, and less aware of the regional norms, as global norms begin to take over.

And, as horribly as I mangled that, yes, that's the bare bones of my argument.

#125680 2 2005-12-21T20:45:55Z Kablizzy
tktktk's analysis:

001: Rather unremarkable. Pretty enjoyable though actually, with the thwumps giving just a touch of puzzle.

002: A few interesting ideas used here. I liked how the gausses could shoot into the gold rooms.

003: Simple enough. I cant get all the bottom gold, and if its impossible to you might want to change that.

004: Nice tileset. I liked the way the rocket was lined up with the exit switch.

005: Reminds me a bit of Metanets value system. Some of those switches make this seem too much like a fetch quest, though.

006: Probably my favorite of these ten. The gold placement could be a little better, but the placement of the mines and bounce blocks is really nice.

007: Its a blast to play because it involves rockets and bounce blocks, but other than that its pretty generic. Also, on the left side of the two middle columns theres a curved tile on the lower and a 45-degree tile on the upper. That works much more smoothly than on the opposite side, where theyre switched.

008: If you start off going right, the switch laser will get you when you move at full speed. Move it one tile to the right to change that.

009: Very cool, the bottom section works really well with the laser/floorguard combo. Minor aesthetic point here, putting the floorguards on top of the gold will look better.

010: Very Metanetty. I found this surprisingly difficult for some reason, but not in a bad way.

011: Not that well done. Cant really think of anything to criticize, its just blah.

012: Very Metanet, I like how there are three distinct sections. This ones a definite keeper.

013: Funky. The lower section is fast-paced and fresh, and the angled tiles that make up the floor keep things very interesting.

014: Kinda reminds me of your map N Your Eyes, although not as good.

015: This is obviously a little repetitive, but it makes up for it with fast pacing and ease of play.

016: Completion is simple and fun, but the getting the gold just bugs the heck out of me.

017: The center, meaty section of the level was pretty fun to play. It might be nice to have some gold in those three down facing chambers.

018: Whoa, those drones are timed really weirdly. Im not sure whether I like this or not.

019: This is N in a nutshell right here. It may follow a tried-and-true formula, but it works especially well here.

020: The gausses give this a very different play style than it would have otherwise, as does getting the gold.

021: Simple, but I like it. The thwumps can be ignored, or serve as a shortcut.

022: Awexome tileset, nice use of minor puzzle elements. I think the mine side borders fit very well though.

023: Nice flow. The thing that stands out to me here is that if you try to get the gold by starting from the ceiling, youll die. I dont know whether that was intentional, but I think its cool.

024: Weaving through the bounce blocks to get the bottom gold is somewhat unique, the rest is same ol, same ol.

025: I like the multiple route thing, particularly the mine part for some reason.

026: Mmm. Symmetry again. Bottled drones make for some interesting situations. Side sections are so-so, running down the jagged gold area is kind of fun.

027: Even though they were all easy, I liked the way the gold caches obstacles were organized by difficulty.

028: Slightly above average chaingun map. Not a whole lot else to say.

029: Yay, originality! There were a lot of possible routes to this, and it was fun to experiment with them a little.

030: You really cant say much about maps of this type. Very easy, somewhat fun, and good for its size.

031: A bit sloppy, but average. The gauss turret section was a little different, but not much.

032: I liked this quite a lot. There were several options, and all of them were fun. I liked using the double bounce block jump to get the exit switch.

033: Very unique, there arent enough maps like this out there. The thwumps make this a nice action-oriented puzzle.

034: Not bad. I sort of felt that the map wasnt made to fit the tileset, but there were some elements that worked well together.

035: Urgh. The drone path was interesting, but there was a major problem with it. If you attract them at the very beginning theyll just keep moving around that floating block in a neat little circle. Plus, the map as a whole was very monotonous.

036: Easy, with many options, but also kind of bland and repetitive. The floorguards were rarely threatening, except if you want to get into the upper levels from the left.

037: Another one of those simple gold challenges that are neither great nor in any way bad.

038: Theres a Metanet level thats very similar to this. The platforms are well placed, and that essentially makes the map what it is.

039: I really liked this. It plays like a combination race and arena map, and the rockets give a mild resistance.

040: Very nice. The drone paths complemented each other perfectly, giving the map just enough of an element of strategy.

041: Cool. I feel like Im picking up on things that werent originally intended, but I liked how there were two ways to get the gold on the left. The right area plays pretty well too, with good bounce block placement.

042: Great concept, but it bugged me that much of the gold was impossible to get. The drone placement was a little frustrating too.

043: Impressive. Good tileset and use of symmetry to create an around the world style map.

044: The rocket/drone combo made this very intense. Gold was difficult to get, but I think thats a good thing.

045: I didnt like that the chaingun could shoot into the exit alcove. Interesting use of the double bounce block jump.

046: Astoundingly fantastic. There are at least three distinct ways to play the map. The tileset was both stylish and functional. The curves were used very effectively to escape from the drones. Probably my favorite level thus far.

047: Nice, but I dont know if the two halves of the map fit together very well. Also, theres no incentive whatsoever to use the bounce blocks.

048: The gold is the main part of this level, and the openness of the section made it ridiculously hard to get any substantial amount of it.

049: Obviously a very simple, complex, and well thought out drone puzzle. Reminds me of a few that Metanet did. Excellent use of trapdoors.

050: The semi-intricate drone system makes this a very exciting fast-paced claustrophobia style level. A definite keeper.

051: The switch get kept things interesting here, the bottom gold just seemed like filler. I liked both of the ways you could nab the switches.

052: The symmetry is a little off, in case you didnt realize it. Also, gold placement was a little sloppy. Other than that, nice work.

053: I liked this a lot. Everything was great except for the gold placement, I think it would be better to have it around the mines rather than making it so easy to get.

054: Interesting style. It was harder than I thought it would be to get the upper gold, that rocket is very persistent.

055: Hmm. Weird system of tubes, but it works reasonably well. The seeker drone allowed for some creative situations.

056: I like how this had you rushing straight at the rocket. The arena area was less original but still nice.

057: This looked very linear at first, but jumping through mines in some spots gives good opportunities for different routes and play styles.

058: Nice use of launchpads and lasers for a strategic combination.

059: Quite a difficult and unique puzzle. You dont see lasers used like this very often, and it was cool messing up their timing to actually help beat the map.

060: Simple fun. There was an easy boring way and a slightly less easy and more interesting way to complete it.

061: The drone timing is spot on here, I think. It doesnt do much, but what it does, it does well.

062: Enclosed map with drones. Cannot think of much to say.

063: Very easy, and great fun for such a small map. Its funny, I dont think Ive seen any like this before.

064: Its surprisingly intuitive to get around. Some of the gold looks kinda hard but really isnt. Sigh I feel like Im commenting on things that arent actually there.

065: My main qualm here is that the chainguns had a tendency to be really cheap. I think that hurt the map quite a bit.

066: Nice idea, but you mean to tell me that the lower bounce block gold is actually possible to get?!

067: I think the symmetry hurts this more than it helps. Doing the same thing twice isnt fun, at least in this case. Not terrible though.

068: Very nice, good sir. Getting the gold on the outskirts is good for a mild challenge. One of the gold pieces in the first room is off, by the way.

069: Getting up to the second half of the level, particularly with a rocket on your tail, is tougher than it looks. Only if youre trying for the gold, though.

070: Oooh. Brilliantly laid out minefield, especially the first section. Very difficult too. I could see some thought put into the mine placement.

071: The two mines at the beginning were interesting, because they took my natural tendency to hold right from the start and made it a reflex challenge. I dont like the drone timing of the upper rightmost drone, it interferes when you try to get the gold in that room.

072: Nice use of thwumps. Cant think of much else.

073: Nice take on the superliminal type map, getting the gold was fun. I dont get the purpose of the mines though.

074: I like the use of rotational symmetry. The number of drones made this very difficult, and that may or may not be a good thing. Im leaning toward good though.

075: I liked this because it was very neat, organized and contained. The drones gave it a bit of strategy, but it was a very nice easy map overall.

076: Simple, elegant, and gets the point across. Nice work.

077: The enemy combination made this intense, but it always felt like I was in control.

078: Uncomplicated, well-realized concept. The bottom four mines are pointless, but whatever.

079: Cool. Good use of mines and tiles to create precision jumps.

080: Interesting cant-quite-get-up-there pattern of gameplay. I liked the middle gold and how you cant get it all in one go unless you died in the exit.

081: Nice, a little asymmetry is good now and then. I liked the launchpad segment, but the lowermost gold felt awkward to get.

082: Youd think this concept wouldve been done before, but to my knowledge it hasnt. Im sure the upper center gold is possible, but its definitely tough to get.

083: Load times a little long here, but thankfully I beat it first time through. Pretty fun, good use of oneways.

084: Good strategic chaingun map. The launchpads made it easy to get around and worked well with the rest of the map.

085: I tend not to like this type of map, with the gold/mine pattern and all that. This one was better than most, however.

086: I thought I would like this, but it ended up that I didnt so much. You cant very easily get from the bottom to the top in the two center gold sections. Running under the homing launchers as they were firing was cool though.

087: Nice symmetry, I suppose. The launchpad/thwump thing doesnt have a lot of rhyme or reason to it, but it still works well.

088: I like the style, it reminds me of that one Metanet map. Yeah, you know. That one. A cakewalk of course, but oddly enjoyable.

089: Launchpad is fun to use. Exit gold is always nice. Other than that, fairly generic.

090: Plays better than I expected it too, since the rocket is conveniently simple to avoid except when getting the exit switch. Good one.

091: Pretty okay segmented map. The side gold is boe-ring, the slightly puzzly floorguards are considerably less so.

092: This was very well done, with a high level of polish. The bottom section reminded me of the bottom of maximos Float Temple.

093: Interesting race type map. Different routes for different styles of play is never a bad thing, either.

094: This looked like it should be in vein of maximos Lofty, but the thwumps hardly came into play at all. I found it much easier to simply ignore them completely.

095: Very good use of the concept. The laser drones work perfectly with this type of map. Well done.

096: Whoa, what quirkyness. Figuring out how to get the gold without the rockets following you in was a nice unconventional little puzzle. Much easier to go for the upper gold first, I think.

097: Quite a persistent little fellow, that rocket. One of the most fun maps of yours so far.

098: Interesting use of the thwump. Odd layout of the map as a whole, but it works reasonably well.

099: Good variety of enemies, me likey. It can be a little boring waiting for the laser to stop firing on the top part with the oneways. A very different sort of map.

100: I like the style. You probably already knew this, but its quite possible to get the exit switch without entering the level proper. Also, two of those pieces of gold on the left seem out of place.

101: Wow, the rockets have quite a remarkable tendency to go through tiles on this map. This is quite a frustrating level, mainly because getting to the exit is a little bit difficult. I still like it though; its unique, and thats a vital thing in this project.

102: Above average. For some reason I tried using the thwumps to get up before I realised how much easier it was to use the 45 degree tiles. Also, the left portion of the floorguard gold is quite a challenge to get.

103: I must say, Im disappointed in you for taking advantage of an idea thats been used so many times. Kidding, obviously. Weird, weird map, but hey. It works.

104: Is all that gold possible to get? Usually I dont have a problem with aesthetic gold, but when it looks like it should be gettable it frustrates me a little bit. But thats probably just me.

105: Just a quaint little rocket arena map. I like the floorguard, for some reason.

106: The use of floorguards as smart mines is sorta nice, aesthetically as well. Itd be better if you couldnt just run across the bottom of the map to the exit switch, methinks.

107: Nothing real special about this. The bounce block jumps were easy, but not quite as easy as they looked.

108: I dont like that chaingun. Chainguns and open spaces almost never work (see stepselfs Upper Bound for a rare exception). Other than that I enjoyed this quite a lot.

109: The center portion is really reminiscent of the Metanet map Avalon. Unfortunately, I like that map better. There was a little bit of awkwardness here.

110: Another nice style. Its a keeper. Nuff said.

111: Whew. Tough one. The break in the drones is really short, and you have to time it perfectly. Maybe theres some easier way that I missed, though, drone paths arent my strong point.

112: Very, very intense. Im not entirely sure what the locked doors are for, but theyre cool anyway.

Beltway: Nice tileset, nice use of optional switches. Thoroughly enjoyable.

Cat n Mouse: There definitely arent enough drones here. At least a half a dozen more should be sufficient. Seriously, though, this is nuts. Pure evil. But then, thats probably what you were going for.

Croc: Pretty decent hunted style map. See the circle closest to the exit? I think the one directly above it should be brought down a notch, maybe.

Desolation II: Meh. Its all right. As you might guess, Im inexplicably repulsed by that ungettable center gold piece.

Desolation III: I like the way the mines are set up here. Getting from the bottom third of the map back up to the middle section is difficult but rewarding.

Desolation: Brilliant use of angled tiles to get past the mines on the right side. Wish I had thought of it.

Downward Spiral Staircase: Very ingenious idea. Jumping on the sides of the steps is for losers; corner jumping is way cooler.

Downward Spiral: Not a good map at all, for several reasons. First, the trapdoor, which goes against the most basic of mapmaking principles. Second, the sheer boredom of all-golding. Third, the relative blandness of the rest of the map.

Gravity Complex: Now this is more like it. Very nice. You prolly already knew, but you can get up from the bottom. Also, Im not sure if the bottommost center gold is possible to get.

Grid 417: This looked low quality to me at first, but I actually think its pretty good. The many simple drone paths make the map as a whole complex.

Inside Joke: Nice picture of Cahleeforneeuh. Its hardly a jump puzzle, but the gold is kinda fun to get.

Ladder to Heaven: Rocket dodging at its finest. Thats all there is to it.

Lefty, Righty: Reminds me of one of maximos older maps. Definitely both easier and more fun to play at high speeds.

Sucker Punch: If I could pick one word to describe this, it would be functional. It does exactly what its supposed to do. Thats a very good thing.

Tower of Unobservance: Very appropriate name. Very appropriate ending. Well done.

#125892 4 2005-12-22T11:04:00Z Kablizzy
Overall Notes: Holy Christ, these are hard. LV and I chatted on these the other night, and we had 16 levels, mutually, that we couldn't beat whatsoever, and don't forsee being able to beat, without tweaking. Far be it from me to actually remeber what those were, but going through these, I'm sure I'll remember 'em. The design and flow of the maps are freakin' magnificent, it's just the difficulty that's getting me. And that's mainly the reason that I've taken so long with replying, I've tried to give myself ample time to try, try again. And each time finds me just as frustrated as the last.

The biggest problem, though, that I see, is that your maps are themed so well, and designed so intricately, that I can't very well critique the parts that I find difficult, since most of the maps can't be changed from their current form. So, keep that in mind, I'm not trying to be as much of an ass as it seems I am.

001: Vert Arena - Love it. Simple, great design. Keep it as-is.

002: What is Normal? - What is normal? Definitely not this map. I can't beat this. I've tried and tried, and can't do a thing... I've tried corner-jumping off the bottom, I've tried perpendicular jumping off the round slope, nothing. I say lower the difficulty here, so that folk like me can get back up from the bottom part.

003: El Hotel no es Moderno - Another one that I cannot beat. I suggest quarter-clicking the bounce block to the left a bit, to make it more accessible to the upslope. I've gotten up there once in 50-some tries, and I died to the gauss/drone combo shortly after.

004: Conspiracy - Another one that I cannot figure out. How do you get up top there? I've probably spent the most time on this one, and I just can't get it.

005: Launch Suspension - One that I've only beaten once, due to the inaccessibility of the exit switch. Perhaps adding a one-way or two up there to catch on the fly-by?

006: Pseudo-Survival - This thing is nuts with a capital OMFG. I don't know what kind of twisted mind made you come up with this one, but man, this'd better be, like, your last level. On a more serious note, the only time that I beat this map was on a fluke, and not due to any type of skill. The decorative gold kinda bugged me, since I thought that maybe there was a way to get it, but that's minor, compared to the difficulty. Since it's such a small map, I'm not sure what could be done to drop the difficulty, save for doors in front of the gauss or rockets, or perhaps having the thwump start one click lower. However, even during the times when I did get the thwump to return, I was so busy trying to avoid the rockets, that the thwump would either crush me at the switch, or shoot me off into a rocket or mine.

007: Unexpected Imbalance - Egads, this is beatable? Really? Another one that Blizzy can't figure out. I know how it's supposed to go, I just can't do it.

008 - Rawkstar Central - You guessed it! Another one Blizzy can't beat! Primarily, it's the descent from the trap-door hideout (Granted, getting up there is a bit of a chore), but I don't get what purpose they serve, as I can't actually stand on the platforms without a-sploding from the mines.

009: Zee Claw: Brilliant. The thwump near the exit is a bit odd-looking, but other than that, magnificent.

010: Enemy-Specific - I feel like I'm picking on you with all of this critiquing. But another map that I cannot beat. If it were one floorguard, I might be able to pull it off, but as it is, it's killing me.

011: Feeling the Heat - Yet another that I don't see myself beating. Perhaps if the Exit switch were one step closer to the left, but as it is now, the best I can do (In debug) is a few pixels away from the exit before getting shot.

012: You have Angered my People - Magnificent. No changes.

013: Brambles and Shambles - *Sob* ...No idea what to do here, at all. I've tried everything I can think of, and I haven't come up with a single thing.

014: Bunker Planet - *Thumbs Up* Fantastic. A tad bit difficult with some of the jumps, but beyond that, it's great.

015: The Shining Guns - /me shrugs, shakes his head. Couldn't beat it if I wanted to.

016: Overly Reliant - Can't do this one, either. I got up there once, but didn't have enough momentum to carry that top mine.

017: All's Fair in Hate and War - *Sets off Fireworks* A favorite of mine.

018: The Little Rocket that Could - Load time is a bit of a monkey, but the map is easy enough to get over it rather well.

019: Instability - There's one way that I've seen that you can beat this, and man, it's not easy. I love it, but it's freakin' hard. Not so hard that you'd have to change it, really, but hard enough to cause me a ton of grief.

020: The Forsaken - Jumping is really not my strong point, can ya tell? I can totally beat it, but it takes quite a while to catch the one-way, and stick a jump off of it. Magnificent Design.

021: Peekaboo - Classic. Love it. No complaints.

022: Stand Alone Complex - True Metanet. Fantastic.

023: Culture Shock - Great stuff. Love the placement, and the drone paths. Great Map.

024: Use the Thwump Luke - I can totally use the thwump... but not to actually beat the level. I usually use it to kill myself, mostly because I have no idea how to get anywhere in the map.

025: Funhouse - Sick, sick map. Once you figure out the jumppad you're shooting for, it's a snap, but bouncing around amongst those drones is so much freakin' FUN! Particularly watching N die, and bounce about. Awesome stuff.

026: Lost Ground - WHOAMG. Magnificent. You make great map, hundred percent!

027: Radioactive Spider - Another jumper. Hm. At least this one's doable. Difficulty on this one is just about perfect, and love the theme.

028: Ka - Oh, man, this was hard. Doable after a ton of trial-and-error, but totally hard.

029: Twisted Beacon - Metanet all the way. Kickass.

030: Levitator - Fan-freaking tastic. For some reason, this looks like it would be a FANTASTIC opening level for us at 00-0. Something we should consider.

031: Rush Hour - Freakin' great. Couldn't ask for a more flavorful map.

032: Hodgepodge for 400, Alex - Another unbeatable one. But I can totally pinpoint what bugs me about this level - It's the obstacles. I know that's the theme, but they seem so random, it gets to me. The jump-pads and one-ways could theoretically go, and be replaced with a pair of floorguards. The Drone puzzle was cute, but hard with the one-ways leading into it with a rocket tailing you. Without that, I feel there would be a better chance of beating the level. Didn't quite like the jumper bit at the bottom-left (Obviously, hehe), and not sure I like the thwumps, but the thwump thing is more of an aesthetic difference than a difficulty one.

033: Gaussian Eliminations - Love the map, but the terminal switch is a tad bit hard to maneuver in between those mines. I'd consider quarter-snapping everything out one from there, to lighten things up a bit.

034: Bounce Options - Very good level for diversity. If you choose to go a different path, you'll eventually find a good one. If you just go for the middle, it doesn't work as well. Either way, good, solid map.

035: Easier Done than Said - Classy stuff. Simple, easy, but not too easy. Great map.

036: Brave Olde World - Great map. Not much else to say.

037: Groundless - Another great one. Love it.

038: The Molasses Bandit - Very awesome. Not a whole lot of danger unless you try for the gold.

039: Laser Could - Man, you make hard maps. This one, not so much as the others, but these are all challenging in their own way. Love it.

040: Here's the Kicker - I can hit that first jump about 10% of the time, is there any way to shove that thwump back a quarter-snap?

041: Advanced Robotics - More jumping? My shift button's getting ground into the desk... If I wasn't so horrible at any type of precision jumping, I'd be doing a lot better at these. The maze part is good, but you sure made sure those mines were placed where they were gonna kill you, didn't ya? Great map, either way.

042: Freak Out - Great map, hard as hell. But I have a solution! Quarter-snap the blocks out in a few key areas (Like at the end), because this is yet another one that Blizz cannot do.

#137414 4 2006-01-30T10:17:32Z Kablizzy
Summary: I feel that, as a whole, your maps are great, but a bit on the too-hard side. I think that most of them need to come down a notch or two, because if I can't beat 3/4 of these, then a vast majority of the N playerbase can't beat most of these. The end ones were... too much for me after 4 or so hours of playtesting these and commenting on 'em. Perhaps I'll come back and start from the end, see if I can get a better bearing on the later maps.

00-0: Cracks me Up (----)- I loved the level, hated the tile squeeze. Then again, I dislike them on principle, but if the remainder likes it, I won't mind shuttin' up. In either case, great level, but I think it may benefit from a single gauss in the middle instead of the tile squeeze. Again, I'll appeal to the fellas on this.

00-1: Throb (----)- That's exactly what my head was doing after this level. I would say to snap the mines a tad bit lower, but that ruins the level. So, I like it, I think it should stay, but as a later level. Perhaps consider moving this episode later. I haven't played any other episodes yet, but I'll suggest something below.

00-2: Slaunt (----) - Magnificent. Loved it. Hard as hell, but loved it. I wonder if there's a way to put gold along the ceiling, hanging down like the mines are, probably in between the mines, so that you can kick-jump up to get the gold? Provide a bit more of a challenge, like Tim said.

00-3: Gangster (81.575) - Now this one, I found very easy. I ran across the bottom to the right, kick-jumped to the middle, bounce-blocked across the drones, and up to the exit without any danger whatsoever. Thus, it feels like it needs something along the bottom, and across the right side to provide a bit more of a challenge for going that way. I was thinking that perhaps bringing that middle block straight down, flush with the floor, that may help a bit. I'm not sure, I'll appeal to the others to see what they think.

00-4: Cacophony (72.575) - Great tileset, good play-style, although I was able to get straight to the door-switch and back with relatively little trouble. To combat this, I would consider moving the leftmost laser-drone up four or five tiles, and have the move algo facing down. This way,

01-1:Purport (87.975) - I didn't quite like the tileset, although I did like how it functions. The angled tiles seemed haphazardly strewn about, perhaps organizing them a bit more would help with the aesthethics? It plays well, but perhaps a bit more variety in the tiles (perhaps some facing up-down) would help?

01-2: Complimentary (----) - *Sob* You guys and your damn squeeze-y puzzle-y maps. I get to the bottom, and not back out. Not sure what I'm doing wrong.

01-3: Grandma's Monkey's On (74.350) - A lot like my 025, but tons better. Love it. Actually a good use of glitches, one that works. To me, I don't mind the glitch.

01-4: Babylonian (67.24...9? What the hell?) - Nice job. The switch in the cove is a bit oddly-placed, and there's no reason to head off to the thwumps at the right, perhaps consider switching?

02-0: Never Die Alone (84.025) - Fantastic level. The Tileset is a bit... bland, I'd ponder adding some pizazz with a short-angle tile, or something. Nothing functional, just something to tack onto the bottom of the existing platforms to make it look a bit more unique. Also, unless there's a reason for all that space on the left, I'd consider 5-tiling upward the whole way, or adding some other kind of flair over there.

02-1: Dia (77.975) - I agree with Tim, perhaps eliminating that mine would help, I'm not sure.

02-2: Synopsis (74.500) - How do you guys make such cool tilesets? I wanna be able to do that, too... Anyway, kickass level. No changes.

02-3: Remember Me? (74.250) - Not sure if the title is alluding to the use of the mine-switch placement thing, but if not, I'd take those mines out, provisionally, or put them in there in a different fashion. It's not a big deal, I just don't know how the same thing in two distinct maps will play out with players.

02-4: mum (----) - I'm wondering if that gauss is neccesary, it seems like the rockets do a fine job of keeping you on your toes. I know the gauss ties the room together, but it seems to ramp the difficulty up a bit much.

03-0: Rid (85.175) - Nice, simple, easy. Good stuff.

03-1: Palimpsest (----) - Very nice layout, although two things buggered me. First, the bounce-blocks in the corners felt a bit odd. Secondly, that floorguard is surprisingly annoying! Beyond that, love it.

03-2: Alumni Search (----) - Hate jumper puzzles, damnit! Hehe.

03-3: Yes Yes (----) - I shudder at the thought of teleporters on principle, and trap-doors that lock you out of places where you need to be. However, they're both decently executed here. I'm just not sure that they work well in the environment of such a lengthy map. I liked the flow, but if I had an opinion, I would cut this in favor of something a bit less intensive.

03-4: I Remember You! (----) - Again, the mine-clone issue, with this third map, it becomes an actual issue for me.

04-0: Seat Belts (83.100) - Nice small map. Those Chainguns, though... annoying little guys. I'm surprised I did this on my first try.

04-1: Which Old Witch (----) - Ye Gods. I can get one switch at a time, but no more than that. Hard stuff.

04-2: imbecile (82.850) - I'm not sure what to say about this one. At first, I thought it looked like my style of map, but playing through it, I found that it was much, much better. I just don't think there's a way to improve this one, even though it does look a bit plain.

04-3: Tantalize (----) - Fantastic Tileset, I'd put the exit terminal in the lower-left or upper-left, the actual exit in the upper-right, and the upper parts need to be more accessible. Like, the ability to kick-jump to the upper left, and perhaps be able to get up to where the Lasers are, somehow. Plus, gold and a sparse placement of strategic mines seems like it'd finish this map up.

04-4: Doublemint Slurpee (----) The gausses at the very bottom seem unneccesary. I think the map can do without them. The remainder seems great.

05-0: Sense (85.375) - Brilliant level. No changes.

05-1: Pair Down (----) - Fantastic. Great difficulty, great setup. Fantastic innovation.

05-2: Amazon's Indigenous Chickens (----) - Very nice design, great difficulty, but the jumppad trick seems a tiny bit on the counter-intuitive side.

05-3: Pisces Princess (----) - One of very very few instances of a multi-part map working so brilliantly. Love it.

05-4: Negotiate (----) - Great stuff. I love it, all-around. Having to use the thwumps and plan a route works especially well here.

06-0: Two-oo-ooh (----) - So, yeah, you got me here. I have no idea how it's possible to get up to the top-left switch. Even frame-by-frame in debug doesn't do it for me.

06-1: Feel Like the One (----) - I heartily dislike precision jumping, and this is probably the best example of it. However, I have no particular beef, other than it doesn't fit well with my playstyle.

06-2: Fallopian Gulp (----) - That, uh... sure is an interesting name. Nice drone-paths, but sitting and waiting doesn't sit (Get it? Hah!) well with me here. I guess I'm just as impatient as Tim.

06-3: Amiss (----) - Great tileset, Tight squeeze, man. Maybe it's the lack of sleep talking, but damn, your maps are hard. =p

06-4: Havisham (----) - Sorry, man. Didn't like this one much. Not the thwump-running, definitely not the bottom switch area. Even the times when I did make it down there, I got stuck in there like an ass. Perhaps if you keep those thwumps, except with a small part underneath those for the exit switch, that may work better. Like Tim said, the top part was great, the thwump-running was tolerable (Even though that gauss can't miss you most of the time), but that bottom just did it for me.

07-0: Bob (----) - Christ, and I thought I made hard maps. Again, magnificent tileset, great idea, difficulty is just a bit out of my range.

07-1: Rumble (89.600) - I won't even pretend like I had any damn clue how to get the exit switch, but Jesus, that's innovative. Love the map.

07-2: Versace Love (----) - You guys need to stop with the precision-jump and squeeze-tile fetish. It's unhealthy. Seriously. Hehe. Great concept, hellish difficulty. Not so much in any given part as it is just a long map with a lot of things that can go wrong. No changes, really, but just a damned hard map.

07-3: Phagocytosis (----) - No, I didn't beat this one, either. Yes, I suck. That bottom-left switch is hard to recover from and clear the floor-guard on the return trip, but very nice setup. Also, it seems as though your attention to detail is better than mine... I didn't even see where you used a one-way.

#137522 6 2006-01-30T20:17:32Z Kablizzy
Did I? How so?

Anyway, I couldn't beat 0-1, I still can't beat 0-1, I'm at 57 tries and counting now. I'm gonna give 'em another shot, just for the sake of being more fair than I may have been last night, but I don't forsee much progress being made. I found the vast majority of his maps ostensibly more difficult than all but the hardest Metanet maps in existence, and there are still a solid number of people who haven't beaten the regular game yet.

To take 3-2, or 0-1, for instance, precision jumping is boring, particularly when you can't do it with any regularity. I view you, Tim, as the best overall player in the N community, and I could say with confidence that there are a lot of things that you can do that more casual players, like myself, can't. For instance, your simple challenge series? I didn't finish a single one, and I know a couple of others who did likewise. I see myself as the low end of the bar when it comes to playing, but I feel that these levels need to cater, at least in some regard, to that type of player. I don't mind having hard levels amongst all of these, but my concern comes when the first episode and the 8th episode are of relatively equal difficulty. The ending maps of a column should be ridiculously hard, but I found the difficulties pretty much uniform throughout.

I guess, though, this all depends upon how hard we want the maps, really. If we want the difficulty of these maps ramped up from where the Metanet maps are, as a general rule, then I'd be more welcoming of the difficulty of these maps, as a whole. However, I am under the general feeling that maps should have a general difficulty throughout the map, and most of the maps here that I have a problem with seem to have a "sticking point" so to speak, where the map gets more difficult than the remainder. Hate to bring it up, but 0-0 is a great example of this. As a whole, the map has a flatline of difficulty, except for the squeeze-point, where the difficulty spikes for those unfamiliar with it. Particularly for newer players who don't have the same ability as others to make that kind of jump, I think that immediate spike in difficulty sets a tone for the maps. I know I'm not explaining this well, but I'll be glad to talk more about it so we can figure out exactly where we want things to be.

Mmkay, levels I still can't beat:

011: Feeling the Heat (I could've sworn I'd beaten it after you made the change), but I love the map. Don't think any more changes are needed here. Verdict: Love it.

013: Brambles and Shambles - Damnit, this is such a cool map, this had better be a lot later on in your episodes. If I see this at, like, 05-2, I'm coming to your house. Seriously, with all the squeezing and precision-jumping, the majority of my deaths are now to the timer. I would say add gold, but there's plenty to be had, it's just that the map takes a long time when you can't precision jump. Verdict: Love it.

015: Shining Guns - Holy crap, as soon as I posted on this, I beat it. Verdict: Love it.

016: Overly Reliant - Just not good enough to do this. Great map, as all of 'em are, I just can't. Verdict: Love it.

032: Crest Quest - I will beat you in your sleep. That is all.
Anyway, If any of your maps comes close to being a bad map, this is it. It's still above-par, but it feels as though the combination of precision-jumping and gausses makes for a decently tough map, overall. It seems as though, through two versions of the map, it just can't stick around with the rest of your maps. If nothing else, it still feels out of place amongst such great maps. In either case, I don't see it being salvaged much, unless you were to put a trapdoor switch in the upper-right, closing a door at the end of the level, for that last Gauss above the exit. You think you're home-free, and that thing snipes your head, it's disheartening. I hate having to take those measures in my maps, though, so I dunno. Verdict: Lump it.

051: The Last Safe Place - Can't do this yet, but I love it. Verdict: Love it.

053: Showoff - Now, I can't get to the exit terminal, how do you do so? Beyond that, I love the high-flying hijinks, even though those bounce-blocks kill me more often than they have any right to. Verdict: Love it.

062: Meteor Barrier - Now, I ended up beating this one, too, but is having the exit terminal switch that high up neccesary? There was only one way I saw to get at it, and that was launching yourself up the tunnel. While that's a neat trick, it took me a long time, and a lot of time-out deaths to get to it, I'd imagine moving it down a tile or two or three, or maybe even putting it elsewhere on the map, like on the left, in the niche in the second cluster, might help things out. Verdict: Love it.

064: Cash Eye - My only complaint here is the dumbtarded exit terminal placement - That thing needs to be accessible from another way than just the first jump-trick. Particularly since you only get one shot at it, there needs to be another way to get to it. Verdict: Love it, pending Exit-Switch accessibility.

065: Padded - Another one!? For the love of crap, you guys, ya'll need to get some counseling for these jumper puzzles. Verdict: Love it, but if I see another Jumper puzzle before I die, I'm throwing my keyboard at my dog.

066: Dead Air, um, Dear Air - *Keyboard goes flying across the room* Beat it, but there needs to be a lot more gold here - my highscore is 3 seconds, the rest have all hit 0.00. Verdict: Hate jumper puzzles, damnit!!! By which I mean, I love the map. Hehe.

072: Raining Nails - ... *Glare*

...

...

Run very, very fast.

Yes, I beat it. Yes, I love it. Verdict: Love it.

074 - Mineless, not Mindless - I will pay for your rehab from jumper puzzles. Get some help, man. As a friend, I want you to get better. *Grabs your shoulders* The first step is accepting that you have a problem! Verdict: Love it.

Now, just as an aside, 075 - 100 are perhaps the 25 best maps I have ever, ever seen in my entire time playing N. No offense to the others, but Goddamn, man, those are brilliant. So far as I'm concerned, you have like, two tweaks to do, put 'em into episodes, and you're done. Just as an aside, "This could get ugly," there is no way you can expect any sane person to get that terminal switch, right? o_O

#6745 1 2006-02-09T08:45:38Z Kablizzy
Today is a glorious day!

...For today, it is here. For months now, we have had a secret that we have been keeping from all of you. Around the forums, and around IRC, we have been dropping hints of "It's coming," and other assorted hints that most of you have probably missed. But now, it is here, and the veil shall be pulled back, to reveal what it is that has been coming, and why you absolutely need to be interested.

It all began as Maximo's brainchild. Back in early October, 2005, Maximo decided to comemmorate his official return to the forums with a bit of a treat. After a bit of work on the treat, he spoke to LittleViking001 about it, and LV quickly jumped onto the bandwagon. From there, nevermore, tktktk, sweep, and Kablizzy were asked to join the project, as well, to which we all graciously accepted. We all began working on this thing, and for the past five months, we have been collaborating with each other daily and nightly, working tirelessly to get this thing up and running. And now, it is finally here.

Now, some of you may have seen us planning for this. Mostly on IRC, during the early stages of planning, you may have noticed the "Legacy" channel that LV and Kablizzy and nevermore and Maximo tend to frequent. We masqueraded this as our staff channel, which, to an extent, was true, since all six of us are staff members. In reality, it was our planning channel for this project, and why we guarded it so fervently. So, back to the topic at hand. Over the past 5 months, we have worked every night on this project. We have slaved and tweaked, and we feel as though, after all this work, that we are finished, that the Legacy Project is finally ready for launch.

...So, what is the Legacy project, you ask? The Legacy Project consists of Six main members: Maximo, LittleViking001, tktktk, nevermore, Sweep, and Kablizzy. We six have - over the past five months - been working on a level-pack for N. Five of us have been working on the levels, while Sweep has been providing playtesting and website development. This level pack, which we have entitled "Legacy," consists of 400 unique maps, arranged in 8 columns of 10 episodes each. Each episode consists of five maps, arranged in the same way as the original Metanet levels. In addition, the play-style of each of the levels is reminiscent of the original Metanet levels, to which each of us have added our own particular flair and flavor to the project, and each level has our own unique touch to it. It has taken us almost half a year to complete this project, but it will all, in the end, be well worth it.

We hope you've enjoyed all of the preperation over the Legacy Project, but we hope you enjoy the project itself that much more. So, without further ado, visit the Legacy Website, and have fun!

#141622 15 2006-02-10T07:18:09Z Kablizzy
Kickass. I love 'em already.

Couple things:

Babylonian: I'd put some more gold on the right, above the homing launcher, and above the thwumps, probably just below the top-most platform, in that niche. That would provide more of a reason to go up there.

Dia: Perhaps adding another single drone at the top, as well? I think that'd be a great difficulty for the map.

mum: I like the thwumps, but I also liked the mine setup of your last map, I'd suggest replacing the mines.

placebo call: Still don't like the idea of teleporters, but I can live with it, I think.

Amazon's Indigenous Chickens: Minor aesthetic thing here: Replace the drone in the middle so that it's on top of the mine.

Negotiate: I think it's fine as-is, I thoroughly enjoyed playing through it. The others may disagree, though.

Feel Like the One: Still think the Exit needs to be lower in the middle, but it's still a fun map, overall.

Havisham: Still dislike those trapdoors, there's no way out once you're in, unless you somehow get both thwumps going at the same time.

Phagocytosis: OH. EM. EFF. GEE.

I would rather deal with the gausses, hehehe. Seriously, those mines are tough to navigate. I couldn't even get the first set.

Yes Yes: I kinda like the multiple-route thing, but intuitively, are the trapdoors neccesary? I think making this a shorter map, overall, would help a lot. I know you have a liking for more complex maps, but I think that shortening some, particularly this one (Where I, for one, didn't get to use either corner-switch area), by removing the trap-doors, and the middle way into the exit, and forcing players to go up top and deal with the drones, may help a lot.

Now, since we're getting into the last few weeks, I'm going to put a short list of maps that I don't think we should launch with in their current state:

Feel Like the One - The difficulty to navigate the map once you get to the bottom seems like too much of a factor in the map. Aesthetically, the only thing that I found displeasing were the doors at the bottom, they didn't seem to mesh well with the one-ways. Plus, the exit being up top bugs me, for some reason. Perhaps it's map-length, and I think that you should ponder shortening a few of them, this being one of 'em.

Havisham - Love the upper part of the map, but trap-doors shutting people in or out bug me. I would even go so far as to say that the gauss wasn't nearly as bad as the trap-doors, particularly with the current tileset, you could place the gauss so that it would only hit you at a certain angle and point while thwump-riding.

Phagocytosis - I'm not sure why, but this tileset just doesn't seem to yield itself well to anything that I like.

Yes Yes - I'd like to see the length on this one shortened, I think it'd do a lot better as a shorter map.

Polyphonic Spree - I just dislike this map. I don't even know what it is, it's just... It doesn't seem to fit with the rest of your maps. The rest of your maps seem to just be of a lot better quality than this one is. =/

Beyond that, I think you've done a superb job of doing all these up, despite problems in finding time and internet access to do so.

Edit: Oh, also, I'll be glad to format 'em, when I get a chance.

#142103 18 2006-02-11T06:45:26Z Kablizzy
Hm. I think I'll try to clarify a bit - Hope I can do a better job this time around, hehe. Also, I'd like for the others to chime in on these levels, in particular, so that we can get these finished, and we can finalize your maps.

I think that, with these maps in particular, my beef comes down to neccessity. It seems as though the base idea is fantastic, but that the execution took the idea a step or two too far. More clearly, in the instance of Havisham and Yes Yes, I think that both maps could do the same relative things that they do now, except a lot more simply, and a lot more cleanly.

Feel Like the One - The two main things that I dislike about it are these:

1. If you miss a jump up top (On the left switch or the right switch), there's no easy way to recover. The only way to do so is use the middle thwumps to jump back up, and I can't do that.

2. When finishing the level, it's required to thwump-jump up to the top, at least in some form or another.

I think that it's more of a problem with myself, on this level, than with the level. My play-skill just isn't something that allows me to do these tricks that you four can do. All-in-all, I love the level, it just gets frustrating when I miss a jump, and have to kill myself just to try the level again. So, while I would like to see a jump-pad in the middle, or the exit moved down, I leave this one in your hands.

Havisham- ...At the same time!? Here, lemme try it...

Okay, I see how it's supposed to work now. I think my problem with Havisham stems a bit from other sources. Let's see if I can clarify things. First off, I don't like the thwump-running here. Now, don't get me wrong, far be it from me to want you to change or delete a level because I don't like something, that's not what I want from all of this. However, in the runs that I did, only once did I actually have enough time to make it into the terminal cove, and beat the thwump on the return trip, and I screwed that up by jumping a bit too high, and getting caught in the head by that thwump on the return-trip.

So, with this level, I think that the problem isn't so much anything in particular, so much as it is the difficulty of the bottom part, as it relates to the remainder of the map. I guess, in short, I don't see the neccessity of the bottom part. I would even go so far as to say that having a straight alcove with the two thwumps, like so:

[image lost: post-16-1139642050.png]

...would serve much the same purpose. It wouldn't really lessen the difficulty so much, if the thwump paths were shortened (I toyed with some tiles in the drone path, with varying amounts of success), and I feel as though it would leave the map a lot more clean and straight-forward, and yes, shorter. Granted, there would be no need to get both thwumps going at the same time, but I think that's something I'm kinda shooting for.

Phagocytosis - Keep us informed on this one. I think it has a ton of potential, I just don't think we've found the right execution for it yet.

Yes Yes - After watching the demo for the new version, that's almost exactly how I did mine, but my beef here is that you didn't use either of the switches in the corners, either. They seem, as a whole, unneccesary, and to do the map, particularly to do the map quickly, they don't seem to be needed in the map. So, I fiddled a bit with the map, and took it down to a point where only the stuff neccesary to make the map work were included.

http://metanet.2.forumer.com/index.php?act...=post&id=138342

So, the main things that I changed were removing all of the trap-doors. I did this because I think that all of the things that needed the trap-doors to be there could have been done in another way. Namely, in the use of the one-way platform above the ninja at the beginning, in using the rocket-launcher chute as an in-and-out (Still keeping the part where you wanted to keep the rocket alive), and removing the neccessity for the middle exit chute by focusing more upon the outside door switches, and where they lead to. In essence, I like the idea of forcing players up into the top to deal with the drones, instead of it being an option, since it opens up a little bit of a challenge at the end, as well. Let me know what you think on this one.

And the rest, I'm enjoying quite a bit. I can't wait until we launch.

#6783 1 2006-02-11T07:25:34Z Kablizzy
First off, we need a name. Secondly, we need to figure out what we're doing with it.

Our choices? Well, they're limited, really.

1. We can simply run a contest for those who finish the levels first, supplying all of their replays for validation. In this, members would have to PM or E-mail us, and we would have to judge the entries as they come in, to validate completion of all maps.

2. We can have a contest, similar to the NTTS, where we judge performance. This would take an ungodly and enormous amount of work, and I don't quite like it.

3. I was pondering on this. And it may or may not work. Hearkening back to what Tim and Brad wanted, I think that it may be possible to code an "N Replay Interpreter," much in the same fashion as Nick has done for NUMA's N Level Interpreter. Ours would be quite a bit more primitive, but it could work.

What we would do... is we would have a place to submit the userlevel.txt replay data to a processor program that reads which level it is, and submits it to a database, which then compares the data, and ranks it amongst the other levels.

From there, we would have a highscore page, where it would list the top 20 highscores for each level, and it would have a text-box (Much like Arachnid's replay data thinger), except for the replay data that was submitted, so that people could copy said replay data from that textbox, and play it.

All in all, this seems relatively painless, if I can get a hold of Nick, I'll let you guys know how feasible this would be, and how much server space we could expect it to take up. Since Sweep's doing an awesome job for us hosting, I wouldn't want to put the burden upon him to have to deal with traffic the size of the entire N community through Madnesstemple.

And thirdly, we'll need rules (And in the case of #3, we'd need a security measure so that players couldn't submit someone else's run to the database).

So, did I explain that well enough?

I can see us putting our first news articles up in three distinct posts:

#1 (Now, March 1st, doesn't matter):

Quote
Today is a glorious day!

...For today, it is here. For months now, we have had a secret that we have been keeping from all of you. Around the forums, and around IRC, we have been dropping hints of "It's coming," and other assorted hints that most of you have probably missed. But now, it is here, and the veil shall be pulled back, to reveal what it is that has been coming, and why you absolutely need to be interested.

It all began as Maximo's brainchild. Back in early October, 2005, Maximo decided to comemmorate his official return to the forums with a bit of a treat. After a bit of work on the treat, he spoke to LittleViking001 about it, and LV quickly jumped onto the bandwagon. From there, nevermore, tktktk, and myself were asked to join the project, as well, to which we all graciously accepted. We all began working on this thing, and for the past five months, we have been collaborating with each other daily and nightly, working tirelessly to get this thing up and running. And now, it is finally here.

Now, some of you may have seen us planning for this. Mostly on IRC, during the early stages of planning, you may have noticed the "Legacy" channel that LV and I (And nevermore and Maximo) tended to frequent. We masqueraded this as our staff channel, which, to an extent, was true, since all five of us are staff members. In reality, it was our planning channel for this project, and why we guarded it so fervently. Secondly, particularly on IRC, I would change my username to Kablizzy with a number after it. In reality, I was keeping count. A very particular count. So, back to the topic at hand. Over the past 5 months, we have worked every night on this project. We have slaved and tweaked, and we feel as though, after all this work, that we are finished, that the Legacy Project is finally here.

...So, what is the Legacy project, you ask? The Legacy Project consists of Five main members: Maximo, LittleViking001, tktktk, nevermore, and Kablizzy. We five have - over the past five months - been working on a level-pack for N. This level pack, which we have entitled "Legacy," consists of 400 unique maps, arranged in 8 columns of 10 episodes each. The play-style of each of the levels is reminiscent of the original Metanet levels, to which each of us have added our own particular flair and flavor to the project, and each level has our own unique touch to it. It has taken us almost half a year to complete this project, but it will all, in the end, be well worth it.

We hope you've enjoyed all of the preperation over the Legacy Project, but we hope you enjoy the project itself that much more.

#145256 30 2006-02-18T10:50:34Z Kablizzy
Overall- Difficulty for the early maps needs to change, your easier maps should replace a lot of the 00-X maps, and a lot of your difficult maps early on should move down in the column in place for the easier levels you have later on. As a note, I fugging LOVE your 10-X levels, man. But anyway, the maps that I have had a problem with this past week is mostly due to the fact that I just don't think they're up to your standards. I would like to see if you could come up with even a handful more, because there are still quite a few maps here that I think are under your standards. Of those, I would be willing to roll with them, but I would like to see your maps at 110%, as opposed to just acceptable. I'd like to see more stuff along the lines of Rumble, Bob, Wild, Wok, Slaunt, Grandma's Monkey's On, and yes, even Havisham and ayer, and less maps like Versace Love, Wasting Away, Polyphonic Spree, and your longer, more complex ones. I know what kind of maps you're capable of putting out there, and I feel like your inability to be around as much has hindered the quality of the column, overall. When I see maps of yours like Bob, I think, Man, I wish he could do 50 maps like that, because I know that's the type of high-end stuff you're known for. So, I don't want to sound like I'm being an asshole and trying to make you feel bad over these levels, I just know that your usual stuff is far better than a couple of these.

I've been trying to do the same with my maps, see if I can come up with something revolutionary to replace some of my maps that would just be acceptable. Your mapmaking here is reminiscent a lot of my own during Legacy, I tried to make each level the perfect difficulty, and, in the end, they all ended up to be a rather flat difficulty. Some of these maps, I think, can have great places in your early-column, with just a simple tweak, and considering your need for easier maps early on, I think that lessening the difficulty on a couple of these (If even by just a tiny bit) would do wonders.

Throb - I love this map now, although the gold portion may make this a better candidate for a 00-4 level.

Slaunt - This one shouldn't be in the 00-X column, I suggest replacing this with a later level.

Cracks Me Up - I think I agree with Maximo, after playing this level as much as I have, half the number of switches here would put this right where it needs to be. Don't think this should be in 00-X in its current form.

Cacophony - Another one that shouldn't be in the 00-X, I don't think.

Dia: I think two drones at the top is too much. Zero was too few, and two seems too many. Perhaps try it with one? (Also, not sure about Sweep's comment, the same happens to me, but it doesn't affect me much, up to you) Particularly for an early level, I think one would do nicely at that point.

mum: Still liked the mine setup you had with the old one. I think that may work better here than just the plain tileset.

Alumni search: I would move the middle platform one tile left, and move this into your 0-column. You need easy levels at 00-2, 00-3, and 00-4 and to move those three elsewhere, and making Alumni Search your 0-02, and one of your new levels (Ebb Resistant jumps immediately to mind as a fantastic 0-00) would seem to be a fantastic 0-column difficulty. Perhaps even throwing a rocket launcher in there to keep it where it is, but that second jump is still a bit too much to do consistently.

Placebo Call- I agree with Brad - I would just cut this altogether. Your 10-X episode has far more promising levels than this.

Which old Witch - I agree with Maximo, for a map this early-on, taking the floor-guards out would work wonders, both for symmetry, and for difficulty-balancing. Even with just the thwumps, this is a hard map.

Tantalize - Another of those maps that should be a bit later. Not much, but a bit.

Doublemint Slurpee - The gold seems a bit concentrated at the top. Not sure if this was intentional or not, but I suggest putting some gold down at the bottom, to weigh things out.

Negotiate - Perhaps moving the Exit Switch to a more accessible spot? Perhaps even somewhere so close as the top-left? Either that, or move this to a (much) later spot in the column.

Two-oo-ooh - I know that a lot of the difficulty lies in the drones, but I would lengthen the entire level by one tile upward at the top, and one tile downward at the bottom. From there, lengthen the middle hallway, move the drones apart a tile, and it should be one of your best maps. This would also make a magnificent

Havisham - With this one, it wasn't so much a problem with the level as it is just a matter of simplifying the level to a point where it becomes inherently intuitive. I can't remember where I posted it, but there's a big difference between levels that appear in the Metanet version of the game, and the levels on Numa. Yes, there's a handful of standout maps on Numa, but those maps are the ones that most closely resemble Metanet levels, gameplay-wise. I wish I had my notes on Map Theory, but one of them has to do with why Metanet levels, as a whole, work so very well. One of the reasons is simplicity. There are certain maps of theirs that are complex, but they're complex in a very specific way. (Speaking of which after this release, and after Expanse, I'd like for us all to work on Map theory, and why maps work, and post that research on the Legacy site), but I digress. I guess it's more of an aesthetics thing, whereas it's just counter-intuitive enough to prove a problem. However, since you like it, I won't complain any further. I can now do the level consistently, but my main concern was having to be told how to do so before I cound finish it. So, if you feel that this won't be a problem for our playerbase, then I am fine with it, tentatively. But I do ask you to consider it from the player's perspective before including that in your final 50.

Bob - This should be a bit later, perhaps 8-4, even. It's hard, but it's great hard, suspenseful.

Polyphonic Spree - I don't see reconciling this one. I'd replace it with one of your five newer ones.

Swig of Stark - I'd remove that last mine, and consider adding a gauss in the middle, or off to the left side.

Yes Yes - Ohhhhh, oh. Oh. Oh, man. Okay, I see it now. In which case, I would just get rid of this one entirely. I see the map's theme now, and I now see why I dislike it. If it weren't so gimmicky, I would like it, but as it is now, I'd just pitch it. Granted, I'd rather not see such potential go to waste, but in this form, I'd just use one of your 10-X levels, they're so much better, quality-wise.

New Levels -

Love 'em. No complaints with any. MAKE MORE LIKE THIS, heheh. Ebb Resistant just screams 00-0.

10-4 makes me want to tear my hair out, I don't think those top two gausses are neccesary, nor the thwumps, and I think that one or the other should be removed or replaced (Gausses -> Homing Launchers may work well).

So, anyway, in conclusion, maps that I would consider cutting right now, in exchange for your newest 5:

Yes Yes
Polyphonic Spree
Placebo Call

And maps that I would consider cutting if something better comes along:

Cracks Me Up (Tentatively)
Remember Me?
Mum
I Remember You!
Which Old Witch (Tentatively)
Versace Love
Wasting Away
