News:

Quote
March 1, 2006-

Today is a glorious day!

...For today, it is here. For months now, we have had a secret that we have been keeping from all of you. Around the forums, and around IRC, we have been dropping hints of "It's coming," and other assorted hints that most of you have probably missed. But now, it is here, and the veil shall be pulled back, to reveal what it is that has been coming, and why you absolutely need to be interested.

It all began as Maximo's brainchild. Back in early October, 2005, Maximo decided to comemmorate his official return to the forums with a bit of a treat. After a bit of work on the treat, he spoke to LittleViking001 about it, and LV quickly jumped onto the bandwagon. From there, nevermore, tktktk, sweep, and Kablizzy were asked to join the project, as well, to which we all graciously accepted. We all began working on this thing, and for the past five months, we have been collaborating with each other daily and nightly, working tirelessly to get this thing up and running. And now, it is finally here.

Now, some of you may have seen us planning for this. Mostly on IRC, during the early stages of planning, you may have noticed the "Legacy" channel that LV and Kablizzy and nevermore and Maximo tend to frequent. We masqueraded this as our staff channel, which, to an extent, was true, since all six of us are staff members. In reality, it was our planning channel for this project, and why we guarded it so fervently. So, back to the topic at hand. Over the past 5 months, we have worked every night on this project. We have slaved and tweaked, and we feel as though, after all this work, that we are finished, that the Legacy Project is finally ready for launch.

...So, what is the Legacy project, you ask? The Legacy Project consists of Six main members: Maximo, LittleViking001, tktktk, nevermore, Sweep, and Kablizzy. We six have - over the past five months - been working on a level-pack for N. Five of us have been working on the levels, while Sweep has been providing playtesting and website development. This level pack, which we have entitled "Legacy," consists of 400 unique maps, arranged in 8 columns of 10 episodes each. Each episode consists of five maps, arranged in the same way as the original Metanet levels. In addition, the play-style of each of the levels is reminiscent of the original Metanet levels, to which each of us have added our own particular flair and flavor to the project, and each level has our own unique touch to it. It has taken us almost half a year to complete this project, but it will all, in the end, be well worth it.

We hope you've enjoyed all of the preperation over the Legacy Project, but we hope you enjoy the project itself that much more.

Daddaluma:

Okay. Here's a couple, all of which quoted from a 2002 NIDA study performed on the direct and casual effects of Marijuana (http://www.nida.nih.gov/Infofacts/marijuana.html)

Quote
One study has indicated  have indicated that a users risk of heart attack more than quadruples in the first hour after smoking marijuana(8). The researchers suggest that such an effect might occur from marijuanas effects on blood pressure and heart rate and reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of blood.

Quote
A study of 450 individuals found that people who smoke marijuana frequently but do not smoke tobacco have more health problems and miss more days of work than nonsmokers(9). Many of the extra sick days among the marijuana smokers in the study were for respiratory illnesses.

Even infrequent use can cause burning and stinging of the mouth and throat, often accompanied by a heavy cough. Someone who smokes marijuana regularly may have many of the same respiratory problems that tobacco smokers do, such as daily cough and phlegm production, more frequent acute chest illness, a heightened risk of lung infections, and a greater tendency to obstructed airways(10). Smoking marijuana increases the likelihood of developing cancer of the head or neck, and the more marijuana smoked the greater the increase(11). A study comparing 173 cancer patients and 176 healthy individuals produced strong evidence that marijuana smoking doubled or tripled the risk of these cancers.

Marijuana use also has the potential to promote cancer of the lungs and other parts of the respiratory tract because it contains irritants and carcinogens(12, 13). In fact, marijuana smoke contains 50 to 70 percent more carcinogenic hydrocarbons than does tobacco smoke(14). It also produces high levels of an enzyme that converts certain hydrocarbons into their carcinogenic formlevels that may accelerate the changes that ultimately produce malignant cells(15). Marijuana users usually inhale more deeply and hold their breath longer than tobacco smokers do, which increases the lungs exposure to carcinogenic smoke. These facts suggest that, puff for puff, smoking marijuana may increase the risk of cancer more than smoking tobacco.

Quote
Some of marijuanas adverse health effects may occur because THC impairs the immune systems ability to fight off infectious diseases and cancer. In laboratory experiments that exposed animal and human cells to THC or other marijuana ingredients, the normal disease-preventing reactions of many of the key types of immune cells were inhibited(16). In other studies, mice exposed to THC or related substances were more likely than unexposed mice to develop bacterial infections and tumors(17, 18).

And the following relates to Heavy Marijuana Use:

Quote
Depression(19), anxiety(20), and personality disturbances(21) have been associated with marijuana use. Research clearly demonstrates that marijuana has potential to cause problems in daily life or make a persons existing problems worse. Because marijuana compromises the ability to learn and remember information, the more a person uses marijuana the more he or she is likely to fall behind in accumulating intellectual, job, or social skills. Moreover, research has shown that marijuanas adverse impact on memory and learning can last for days or weeks after the acute effects of the drug wear off(22, 23).

Students who smoke marijuana get lower grades and are less likely to graduate from high school, compared with their non-smoking peers(24, 25, 26, 27). A study of 129 college students found that, for heavy users of marijuana (those who smoked the drug at least 27 of the preceding 30 days), critical skills related to attention, memory, and learning were significantly impaired even after they had not used the drug for at least 24 hours(28). The heavy marijuana users in the study had more trouble sustaining and shifting their attention and in registering, organizing, and using information than did the study participants who had used marijuana no more than 3 of the previous 30 days. As a result, someone who smokes marijuana every day may be functioning at a reduced intellectual level all of the time.

More recently, the same researchers showed that the ability of a group of long-term heavy marijuana users to recall words from a list remained impaired for a week after quitting, but returned to normal within 4 weeks(29). Thus, it is possible that some cognitive abilities may be restored in individuals who quit smoking marijuana, even after long-term heavy use.

Workers who smoke marijuana are more likely than their coworkers to have problems on the job. Several studies associate workers marijuana smoking with increased absences, tardiness, accidents, workers compensation claims, and job turnover. A study of municipal workers found that those who used marijuana on or off the job reported more withdrawal behaviorssuch as leaving work without permission, daydreaming, spending work time on personal matters, and shirking tasksthat adversely affect productivity and morale(30). In another study, marijuana users reported that use of the drug impaired several important measures of life achievement including cognitive abilities, career status, social life, and physical and mental health(31).

On Pregnancy:

Quote
Research has shown that babies born to women who used marijuana during their pregnancies display altered responses to visual stimuli, increased tremulousness, and a high-pitched cry, which may indicate neurological problems in development(32). During infancy and preschool years, marijuana-exposed children have been observed to have more behavioral problems than unexposed children and poorer performance on tasks of visual perception, language comprehension, sustained attention, and memory(33, 34). In school, these children are more likely to exhibit deficits in decision-making skills, memory, and the ability to remain attentive(35, 36, 37).

Let's begin there. Also, splitting this topic shortly.

Blizzy's chicken salad

1/4 head of lettuce.
1 - 2 Tomatoes.
3 cups chicken, cooked and cubed.
1 1/2 cup celery, sliced.
1/2 teaspoon salt.
1 cup mayonnaise.
2 Tablespoons lemon juice.
1/4 cup onion.
pepper to taste.

Serves 6.

1. Line a medium-sized baking pan with lettuce leaves, and line the edges with half-tomatoes.

2. Mix chicken, celery, salt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and onion in a medium-sized mixing bowl until well-mixed.

3. Pour into baking pan, cover in tin foil. Chill for 30-45 minutes, serve on buns as sandwiches, or as a side dish.

#7141 1 2006-02-28T23:52:24Z Kablizzy
Today is a glorious day!

...For today, it is here. For months now, we have had a secret that we have been keeping from all of you. Around the forums, and around IRC, we have been dropping hints of "It's coming," and other assorted hints that most of you have probably missed. But now, it is here, and the veil shall be pulled back, to reveal what it is that has been coming, and why you absolutely need to be interested.

It all began as Maximo's brainchild. Back in early October, 2005, Maximo decided to comemmorate his official return to the forums with a bit of a treat. After a bit of work on the treat, he spoke to LittleViking001 about it, and LV quickly jumped onto the bandwagon. From there, nevermore, tktktk, sweep, and Kablizzy were asked to join the project, as well, to which we all graciously accepted. We all began working on this thing, and for the past five months, we have been collaborating with each other daily and nightly, working tirelessly to get this thing up and running. And now, it is finally here.

Now, some of you may have seen us planning for this. Mostly on IRC, during the early stages of planning, you may have noticed the "Legacy" channel that LV and Kablizzy and nevermore and Maximo tend to frequent. We masqueraded this as our staff channel, which, to an extent, was true, since all six of us are staff members. In reality, it was our planning channel for this project, and why we guarded it so fervently. So, back to the topic at hand. Over the past 5 months, we have worked every night on this project. We have slaved and tweaked, and we feel as though, after all this work, that we are finished, that the Legacy Project is finally ready for launch.

...So, what is the Legacy project, you ask? The Legacy Project consists of Six main members: Maximo, LittleViking001, tktktk, nevermore, Sweep, and Kablizzy. We six have - over the past five months - been working on a level-pack for N. Five of us have been working on the levels, while Sweep has been providing playtesting and website development. This level pack, which we have entitled "Legacy," consists of 400 unique maps, arranged in 8 columns of 10 episodes each. Each episode consists of five maps, arranged in the same way as the original Metanet levels. In addition, the play-style of each of the levels is reminiscent of the original Metanet levels, to which each of us have added our own particular flair and flavor to the project, and each level has our own unique touch to it. It has taken us almost half a year to complete this project, but it will all, in the end, be well worth it.

In addition, we have renamed the Dronies forum subsection to The Legacy forum subsection here on the forums, found in N -> General Community -> The Legacy. Within, you'll find discussion threads for the Dronies, Bitesize Numa, and a Discussion thread for the Legacy Project.

We hope you've enjoyed all of the preperation over the Legacy Project, but we hope you enjoy the project itself that much more. So, without further ado, visit the Legacy Website, and have fun!

Most of the time, it's pretty clear at who should be a mod and who shouldn't. Oftentimes, there are certain members who just stand out so much that they almost force you to pick them as a mod. Okay, we've all had a small break, and I think that Legacy was one hell of a success; despite the handful of naysayers, everyone seems to absolutely love it, and I'm proud that we got the massive response that we did (1000 page views in a single day? Ye gods!).

I had hoped that it would've been bigger, but with the petition for Legacy to join the ranks of v1.5, we may be able to re-submit the request to Mare and Raigan, in the form of inclusion with v1.5; see what they think on it now that it's been released, and people love it. Even if we get the levels included in the v1.5 bundle, I would be more than happy, and it seems as though the players would, too (I'm still interested in what Raigan was going to post in the "It's Here" thread the other night. ). Of course, we'd have to fix a couple things (Like that mine out of place in that one map), but overall, I feel as though Legacy went over incredibly well.

But, I do have a reason for posting; What do we do next? I think the NTTS should be our main priority, since Spect is wanting to work on it, followed very closely by NC7.

In that vein, should we nominate maps, and let the public vote on them, have the public nominate maps, or just pick maps ourselves for them to play through for NTTS highscores?

Also, we need to get a bit more creative with the NTTS prizes this time around; It seems as though The same old Sig-and-custom-title with a T-shirt grand prize is gonna get old after a while. However, the NTTS has always been known for the prize (Well, ever since I came up with it, anyway), and I'd like to have *something* for the winner.

Also, I should've mentioned this before, but I didn't get 'round to it: Should we put a Paypal donate banner on the site? Perhaps grabbing some revenue would help counter-act the cost of prizes?

Anyway, that's all from me tonight, I think we all did one hell of a job on Legacy.

#153216 26 2006-03-09T21:36:03Z Kablizzy
Being a zombie is hard, in general. Survivors almost never end their turn in what we call "Zombie Range," which, in essence, means that Survivors will stay hidden out, as opposed to roaming the streets. In doing this, it becomes extremely hard for lone zombies to gain levels early-on.

With Kerrick, I wanted him to be a zombie, but I made him a Survivor to start, just to stockpile experience before I went off to die. Leveling went much faster with hit-and-run tactics, hiding out in overly-barricaded buildings, and free-running in and out to catch stray zombies for quick exp.

So, in short, it's no surprise that you haven't seen anyone - I guarantee the suburb(s) that you're in just have survivors hiding out in the buildings that you're passing.

That's probably your best bet.

What I did when I began was I loaded an empty map, and practiced types of jumps off of the bare walls. When you walljump in a corner like that, hit jump twice rapidly, as opposed to jumping and then jumping again later. Try some techniques with that, and then add in a slanted tile in one corner, and practice jumps on that. Then try it with a rounded tile, and so on.

#155553 24 2006-03-18T07:47:56Z Kablizzy
See, I'm not really with Suki on this one. I appreciate the effort, but I don't enjoy the zealotry with which the effort is moving forth. There's a guy, who sits out front of my school's library, with a 'Jesus Saves' sign. Every person that walks by, he says "God bless you," and this is, like, all he does. I've engaged in a very productive discussion with the guy, and he recognizes me now. We have ourselves a bit of a routine - every time I walk by him, he asks me if I've found Jesus yet, to which respond "Jesus' footprints are still elusive." He laughs, we move along.

Now, my point is that this guy is trying to save me. And I know he is, and he's fuggin' awesome for it. But that's because when we had our discussion (And it was a lengthy one, at that; One that I wasted four hours and missing a class for), it was productive because he gave me ground with which to work.

I asked him, "How do you know that there is a God? Or, moreover, if said God is the one to whom you pray?" He answered, "I don't, and I can't. It's not a matter of knowledge, it's a matter of faith."

This surprised me. Up until that point, every theologian or religious uh... what's the word... religiously inclined person to whom I had spoken had told me, without question, that they know, factually, that there is a God, and that said God is the one to whom they pray. When I confronted him with the evidence on Evolution, he agreed that what we have on Evolution is our best bet as to how species came to be. He also said that it could very well be that Evolution was a pile, to which I agreed.

But the reason that our discussion (Read: not debate) was so fruitful... was mainly because he was willing to admit things to me that no one else has been willing to admit. Just doing the debates that I've done over at relig, I've never met a person with a theological background to agree with me, and with whom I agree.

This man was freaking brilliant, not because he has something that other believers don't, but in that he admits that other believers don't. When I debate with people online, I ask them hypothetical questions to which there is one and only one answer... to which I get an aswer that fits their own view of reality, and only that.

Also, this hearkens back to the whole thing where people just throw fallacies at the problem, and then ignore it when they're proven wrong. To which I've conclusively proven many times, in an attempt to get people to the very point where this man is. And yet, the attempts have been unsuccessful. If only there were more people with a more objective view upon the situation, akin to this man (I hate referring to him like that, I wish I knew his name), Religion would become all the more appealing.

Anyway, back to my original point. This all ties into the thought that there can be, roughly, two distinct factions of believer; Casual Believer, and Zealous Believer. The former is the type who truly believes that there is something out there, but not in the way that claims the impossible to justify it. The latter, of course, is the type who jams their fingers into their ears, and speaks from tradition, rather than from the soul. Those in the former situation, of course, are the type who are most likely to save people. They are truthful, and willing. The latter would, by all logic, be less inclined to save someone, since they are... "Bushy" (Har har, I reference myself).

So, my point isn't akin to Suki's much at all, rather than it mimics his own beliefs with logic.

Welcome to the NTTS 3!

The NTTS - NUMA Time Trial Season - is a highscoring/demo-contest and the ultimative challange for everyone who likes playing N!

- me (spect)
-
-

- No cheating. We actually can't prove you fbf'ed or whatever, but cheating is baaad.

- If you post a demo you're not allowed to edit the post or the demo won't count.
- You don't have to participiate every week. I recommend it though Also, there is no real list of competitors. Everyone can join

There are two categories in which your demos can get Points:
- Time
- Style

Time will be the Time which is displayed in Userlevels. The one who has the best time wins^^
Best Time:  5P

2nd: 6P

4th: 2P
5th: 1P
[/veryunclear]
[/unclear]

The Week starts with [insert map here]. Good luck and have fun!

Dronn: JUST WATCH THE DEMO. JUST WATCH IT! DO IT! OMFG FIRST TRYZ!

Continent: I... Hm. Less gausses on the left, maybe? Perhaps one gauss and a laser drone over there? Those gausses are odd to get by.

Delegation Comes to Mind: You know how I feel about jumper puzzles. You know how the community feels about jumper puzzles. Why even subject yourself to this punishment? =p

Anyway, seriously, I don't know, I just don't like this one much. The rest look good.

Quote
Adverse Judgements: Gah! I made a map for Expanse just like this! Yours allows for a little more control with the launchpads, though.

Alaska's Got Nothing On Me: The idea is really cool, but I never have any idea which way the drones are going to go, which results in semi-cheap deaths.

Angsty: I didn't feel this met the high standards I generally have for your maps.

Arbitrary: Hooray for hallway maps!

Arkitekt: I like the drone timing here, it gives a nice strategic feel to it.

Big Monster Thing: Intense and stylish. Rock on.

Closet Monster: Unique. I have a feeling your decision to have only one vertically aiming gauss was a good one.

Common Denominator: The oneway set up was spot on here. Nice.

Daedric Temple: Interesting. I quite enjoy getting to the exit without triggering the trapdoors.

Enigmatic: We think a little too much alike, I guess. My last map submitted to Numa was named Enigmatic. Very cool map though, I like the tileset.

Grenades: A little simplistic, but it might be good as an early level.

I Quit My Day Job: A thing of beauty. Fantastic.

I'll Take My Bass Deafening: That's a very cool effect with the seeker drones. I like it.

Meely: Reminds me vaguely of your maps Plue and Spalding. Excellent flow.

Misplaced Some Files: Metanetty. The first part really reminds me of 18-2 of the main game levels.

My Mobile Army: Genuinely fun. I really like the role the laser drone played in this level.

Newsbreaks for the Poor: Style here is great. The drones are a challenge without being too overwhelming.

One Upping: A very unique map indeed. The switches that opened up the gold caches, in particular.

Partial Credit: I love the use of "5" tiles in this one. Great as far as open chaingun maps go.

Save a Lot: Wow, the enemies in this map have a real tendency to gang up on you. I still thoroughly enjoyed it, though.

Shoplifting: Brilliant. The gausses consistently kept me on my toes.

Square Holed: Quite a bit of strategy involved here. Very nice.

Strafe: As you might have guessed, I really dislike this. There's almost always going to be some luck involved if you try for the gold.

The Dividing Line: The primary motion here is creative but highly repetitive. Can't say I enjoy this too much.

The Growth Seems Exponential: Another nice one. Minor aesthetic suggestion, it might look better to change the "E" tile just to the right of the exit switch to an "8" "Q" tile to match the rest of the tileset.

Transparency: Not your best. A little bland, in my opinion.

Weak Minded: LV-esque and fantastic.

#158436 40 2006-03-27T08:13:19Z Kablizzy
I don't think that the argument lies in that the deity knowing which path leads to where. The idea of Omniscience lies in knowing what the person will choose. Not may choose, but will choose. In other words, it's not the knowledge of A, nor the knowledge of B, it's the knowledge of which path the user will go down, upon which the argument hinges.

How could a deity know this?

Well, because he would know everything. Akin to what I was saying a page back, according to someone's past history, and all the combined experiences of that person, I can tell you, within a medical setting, what a person will choose. Not because I'm omniscient, but because, based upon the events of a person's past, it affects their choices. So, this doesn't always work. Sometimes I take a shot in the dark, and totally miss. Why is this? Because there is, obviously, stuff in that person's past that I can't see, nor take into account, that made them choose the way they did. Thus, were I Omniscient, and able to know those things that I can't know as a Human, I would be able to correctly predict that person's choice.

Now, this all hinges upon whether there is indeed Free Will or not, obviously. Because, in order to predict something, it would have to be false that we have Free Will. Which, in turn, bases itself upon whether said Deity would or would not be Omniscient, and whether said Omniscience would indeed be able to predict someone's actions. Which, given the human mind, and its operations, I fully believe it could.

#159215 13 2006-03-29T04:52:07Z Kablizzy
As it is now, these rules are OBSOLETE. The new rules for season 2 will be up shortly, as well as the new judges, as well!

Here are the comprehensive rules for our Numa Time Trial Society. The Numa Time Trial Society (NTTS) is designed to get more N players to play user-made maps through Numa.

Here is the NTTS Team of judges:

Rahl,
Maniac,
Maximo,
Daddaluma,
LittleViking001, and
Kablizzy

Here are the judges and players who are currently on my watch list:
There are currently no judges or players on my Watch List.

For those of you unfamiliar with the watch list, if a judge does not perform his/her duties during a given week, I put judges on the watch list to see if they continue judging and/or contact me during the week. If they do not for two consecutive weeks, I will relieve them from their duties as judges. The NTTS judges need to be reliable, as the contest can not succeed without a sturdy judging team.

As far as players, any players on my watch list are deemed unable to play in NTTS tournaments. If a player is caught cheating, spamming, or doing other unsavory things that I - or any other judge - thinks unworthy, I will declare that any and all submissions from that player are null and void, and will not be judged.

The Time Trials are separated into two parts. The first part consists of the above judges nominating maps from the Numa archives. All maps selected must be found on Numa, and Each Judge can nominate up to two maps per week. Once each Judge nominates their maps, the judges and/or contestants vote on which map the contestants play in the corresponding poll. The map that gets the majority of the votes becomes the map that contestants play through. If there is no clear winner in the poll, or if the judges cannot decide on a map for the week, and a map needs to be posted for the contest to begin, I will choose a map to post as that week's map.

The second part consists of the judging. Contestants must be registered forum members (This makes our job a whole lot easier, trust me). Forum members can play through the selected map and post their demo data in the NTTS contest thread. Judging will be explained later in the rules.

As far as Demo Submissions go, each member is allowed No more than Two demo submissions per week. This allows contestants to watch other demos, and discover routes that they wouldn't have thought otherwise possible, or otherwise try to improve their time.

Once all submissions are recieved, the judges will begin scrutinizing the demos recieved. The judging will begin on Thursday mornings of the second week of submissions, and will end on Sunday Evenings that week. The judges will then vote for a winner, a runner-up, and a second runner-up in each of the four following categories:

- Time: Time is an important factor. The speedier you finish a map, the better off you'll be in this category. A competitor's Time score will be measured by the number of frames it took to complete the map. Players who complete maps will be given priority over those who do not complete maps, regardless of their Time score. As in the actual game, we will also take into account the amount of gold retrieved during a particular run. Each Gold piece will subtract 80 frames from your overall Time score. With the implement of N v1.4, the scoring system for Time may change, depending upon the implement of the ability to play Custom Maps in the actual game itself. If so, then the Time category will be discussed between the judges, and we will decide upon a new scoring system.

- Style + Entertainment: Style is also an important factor in how we will judge. If you complete a map with more fluid motions than other contestants, you'll have a better chance at winning this category. If you backtrack or make a mistake, that will count in this area as well. We will also judge on how entertaining each contestant's data is. If a contestant bores the judges, he/she will get a considerably less score than a contestant whose moves wow and amaze. This category is primarily the judges' discretion, and there is no set scale for judging how "stylish" or "entertaining" a given demo is.

- Creativity: Being creative is what this contest is all about. If you can do something that no one else can, like, say, jump in between two mines that no one else can get through, that will give you some brownie points in the Creativity area. Also, if you can use the map and the surroundings to your advantage better than the other contestants, you'll get a good score here. Also, how well you execute said creative moves will be taken into account for your Creativity ranking. Creativity isn't simply limited to the path you choose for a certain map, or how well you performed within the map, it also takes into account things that no other competitor thought of, yet could easily do.

- Completion: We will also be determining scores by checking to see how completely you finished the map. For instance, some maps can be completed without opening all doors and without getting all gold. We will judge this category based upon how complete a user's demo is (All Gold, all triggers, etc.). Depending upon the goals of the given map, There may also be map-specific goals, such as survival time in survival maps. These map-specific criteria will be included in our judging of the above categories. For instance, Least Shot At is now a map-specific goal, as opposed to a full-on category, and would be taken into account under Style, or Creativity. Survival time will be taken into consideration under Time, and so on.

Now, as far as scoring goes, Each judge will vote for a winner, a runner-up, and a 2nd runner-up for each category. First place in a category gets 5 points, second place gets 3 points, and third place gets 1 point. Fourth place and beyond earn no points. In the event of a tie, points will be awarded for each contestant to tie. We will declare 4 weekly winners each week, and each week's points will also carry over to the competitor's seasonal total. At the end of the Season, which we will determine the length of later, we will declare 4 Seasonal Champions, one in each category, based upon the number of points they recieved throughout the season. We will also be declaring an NTTS Season 1 champion at the end of the season. this means:

First Place in a category:......5 Points
Second Place in a category: 3 Points
Third Place in a category:.... 1 Point

And assuming that there is a tie in votes, each player recieves the number of points for the place in which they tie.

Submissions and judging will be done on a two-week basis. From the time of the Thread going up (Which is usually Sunday Nights), Contestants will have 10 days to submit their map demos, which is usually going to be the following Wednesday at 23:59 PM PST (GMT - 8). After which, the above judges will scrutinize each contestant's demo data. Once the Submission time has passed for the week, NO further demos will be considered. Official judging begins on the second week of submissions, on Thursday mornings, and continues through Sunday night that week. Point totals, both weekly and cumulative, will be posted on Sunday nights, just before the next week's contest.

The seasonal point totals in each category, as well as the overall point totals will determine which player is our categorical champion, as well as determining our seasonal champion!
That's it for now, if I come up with anything else, I'll be glad to post it right here.
#159216 14 2006-03-29T04:52:12Z Kablizzy
Welcome to the NTTS Season 3!

The NTTS - The N Time Trial Society - is a highscoring/demo-contest and the ultimate challange for everyone who likes playing N!

Judges:
- Spect
- Kablizzy
-

The rules should be quite obvious:
- All demos will be made in Userlevels, using the map for that week.
- No cheating will be allowed. Any cheating from any player will automatically disqualify that participant from the remainder of the contest.
- Once you post a demo, you are not allowed to edit that post for any reason. Thus, make sure the demo that you post is the one you want to submit.
- Only one demo per week will be allowed. Any demos beyond the first will be disqualified from that week's contest.
- Anyone can join, and participation every week is entirely voluntary (Although, participating every week gives you a far better chance of winning).
- In your post, please include the time that you finished the level with, for ease of reference.
- It is in your best interest to post your demo late in the week.

The contest is quite simple. The NTTS lasts for ten weeks. For this season, during each of these ten weeks, there will be chosen a pool of ten maps from Legacy, one map for each of the contest weeks. Each participant plays through the map for that week, and submits a completed demo to the contest. Everyone is allowed to submit One demo for the week, and each demo will be judged in both categories.

Demo submissions last for seven days from the start of the week, after which, the week is over and no more demos are allowed. At that moment, the judges begin deliberation, and rate the demos (see below for more infos about rating).


There are two categories in which your demos can be rated:
- Time
- Style


Time will be the Time which is displayed in Userlevels. The top five fastest demos will take the following points for the week.

Best Time: 5P
1st Runner-up: 4P
2nd Runner-up: 3P
3rd Runner-up: 2P
4th Runner-up: 1P

The judges will then rank the demos by Style. This is entirely judges' discretion, but this includes such things as tricks, route-finding, execution, close calls, and so on.

Most Stylish: 5P
1st Runner-up: 4P
2nd Runner-up: 3P
3rd Runner-up: 2P
4th Runner-up: 1P

At the end of the ten-week period, the person who has the most points will be named the winner of the contest.

This Week begins with this post, and starts with 5-4: Rawkstar Central. All demos must be in within one week from this post. Good luck and have fun!

#159558 68 2006-03-30T00:48:14Z Kablizzy
Quote: Daddaluma, 2006-03-30T00:24:50Z
You make the choices. You are the one determining your future. God only knows what you will do tomorrow because its what you will do. Its sounds stupid and tautological, but really its that simple. You would have done the same thing had there not been any God in the first place.

That's entirely the argument for predetermination. Which is exactly why I think that everything is indeed predetermined, because, simply, you will do what you will do. You're going to choose what you're going to choose, and that's that. It's not a matter so much of having the choice, but being as it is when you're presented with the choice, you can't choose both, because your mind is made up well before you even know what the choice is what you're going to do.

So, in that vein, it can easily be said that, taking desires into account, that Free Will is an illusion. When you choose what you choose, you choose that option for a reason beyond your own understanding, and that option which you choose couldn't have been chosen any differently.

It's not as though you're really, actually *choosing* anything, right? I mean, you know, on a level that you can't consciously understand, whether you'll drink coffee or orange juice tomorrow morning. Why? Because the events during the night will determine the type of rest you will get. Conditions around you will lead you to either getting a good night's sleep, or a bad night's sleep. Taking this simple hypothetical a step farther, let's say, arbitrarily that, if you get a bad night's sleep, that you'll drink coffee, since it will be harder for you to awaken tomorrow morning, and you'll feel as though you need the boost for the day. If you get a good night's sleep, you'll drink orange juice.

So, now, let's take it one step farther, to where you are. Let's say you get a horrible night's sleep, but decide to drink orange juice anyway, because you're choosing, for whatever reason, to ignore how tired you are, and drink orange juice. It's that very reason that you decide whether to ignore events or not which is in contention. But I'm putting forth that the reason that you either decide to go with the status quo or not go with the status quo is solely and entirely dependant upon predetermined factors that we, as humans, can neither comprehend, nor see.

Following from that, each and every one of those factors, no matter how large, small, or insignificant, influences each of our decisions to the point where we feel as though the insignificant ones *are* indeed insignificant. But they aren't. And here's why;

We tend to ignore the things upon which we deem insignificant. But if we were to take every last deciding factor into account for any given decision, and if we were able to analyze, and say, assign a point value, positive or negative, to every event or thought or reaction, or conditional in your life, as it pertains to any given event, choice, or decision, we could easily track what a person's given decision would be, based upon said numbers, positive being one choice, and negative being another. The fact that we can't, and probably never will, be able to track or determine a good majority of those factors, or assign any type of numerical significance values to it, doesn't lend anything to the credibility or discredit of the thought.

Am I making sense on that?

I could give five examples, right here, right now, of non-liberal media, and those examples just happen to be where 99% of the WORLD get their news from.

The main thing that I can't stand about the current administration is the blind support. It doesn't matter what us liberals say, because we're filthy liberals, and we're trying to corrupt America's youth, or whatever their reason is. It doesn't matter, at that point, what we say, because they've gotten everyone convinced that we're all just out to get them. So, you claim that you haven't found that Republicans say "Democrats won't do any better!" And then you go and say it yourself. Do you see the hypocricy there? It was a "We're doing everything right, and they wouldn't do anything right at all!" talking point, and it did have an impact, and, from the looks of the current debate at hand, still does.

In the same vein, no one cares if a Liberal does something wrong, because they're not running the country. Who cares if Jackass Q. Liberalface does something wrong in Bumfuck, Montana? Not everyone gets their news from biased news sources. Anyway, on a more serious note, Fox News (Yes, I watch Fox News a lot) ran a poll, asking people to call in with reasons why the President should or should not be censured. They gave a reason for why they thought that way. The calls that came in saying that "no," he should not be censured, were things like "Where has your respect for our President gone? Mostly because I can't fathom what this man has done to *warrant* said support; Thus, this thread. Anyway, the callers that didn't think the President should be censured didn't provide a reason, they didn't state why he shouldn't be censured, it was just a "We should follow our president, where has the respect for our President gone!?" There are few things that anger me more than arrogance. There are few things that anger me more than ignorance. ...

#164498 2 2006-04-13T22:47:17Z Kablizzy
Linus: These are exactly why you are a part of this team, man. I'm speechless, these are great.

Nowhere is now: Brilliant. That jump on the left is a bit more tricksy than I'd like to see, but that's no big deal, really.

Usurp: Those chaingun drones are relentless. I can't get the switch half of the time, but I love the map. It may need a tone-down in difficulty somehow, but great idea.

Timesplitters: Goddamn loved this thing.

Digital Entrapment: Killer map. Love it.

Scarlet Rain: I rather enjoyed this. You're right, it does feel kind of incomplete, particularly in the upper middle-right, and lower middle-left. Not sure if a bit of extra gold in there would help, perhaps jagged wisps from the floor and ceiling?

Dupe the Egocentric: This one's growing on me, really. The Drone paths are really odd and hard-to-predict, even when you know where they go.

Genocidal Virus Massacre: Oh, you *have* to do the whole thing? Bleh. I was thinking you could get back up to the exit after hitting the exit terminal without having to go the whole thing. I kinda fiddled around with it, and came up with a couple ideas, just to give people a choice of whether to go for all-gold or just finish.

Oreoplane: Two things that I can readily see: Mines and Gold. Perhaps some more tiles, perhaps an open bounce-block field on either side, perhaps a bounce-block design or gold/mine/bounceblock design on the outside, but as it is, I think the difficulty is fantastic. Perhaps thwumps coming from the ceiling, or from a modified ceiling would also help.

Gizmotech: I'd say yes, definitely, but I have no idea how to not trigger the floorguard on the return trip.

Sag: I love this tileset, I just don't like the squeezes at all. I've included a couple modifications to the level that I thought would help. The left part or the right part need to be more accessible.

Lava Drama: I really love the concept, but I wouldn't go for the gold, I don't think. Not sure if the gold placement is good, but the level is good.

Legoland: For some reason, I find this hard. I can't get enough lift to carry a jump to on top of the thwumps. Great concept, though.

Noir: Love it, although perhaps some decorative mines would help?

Remorse: The one time I got this was on a fluke. So, not sure what to think. The level kinda operates on that concept of not

Poor Orphans: Interesting. I love the tileset here. Not sure what else to do beyond gold, really.

Simple Switch of Syringe: It's good as-is. We have a whole lot of "If the drone sees you, you lose" maps already. I like it in this form a lot.

Lotus: I like this one as-is. I'll appeal to the others on difficulty.

White Widow: The only one of your maps this time around that I absolutely can't stand. I hate race maps in this setting, especially ones of this caliber. I'd port this one off to Numa.

Foyer: Love it. Great map.

Aluminum Sun Overcast: The one drone on the right has a faulty algorithm (And don't you tell me he's supposed to be like that, either... *Glare*), but beyond that, magnificent level.

Chalet/Despot Chalet - I like the concept between the two, but I think one will suffice. Perhaps you could combine the two as a two-tier level?

Wartorn: I like this. Awesome stuff.

#180556 20 2006-05-26T07:29:29Z Kablizzy
Quote: The Daily Llama, May 26, 2006 04:02 am
That's... hugely eletist, but one of the few things I can actually see working.

And, you know, (maybe just because I'm feeling extremely disenchanted with the general populace of the human race at the moment), I think that I'm rather in favour with the concept of a NUMA with voting rights.
Ah, I take it you haven't seen my little friend...

...Ahem. All kidding aside, it is indeed terribly elitist, but it would serve many purposes:

First, we would need a set criterion for current voters. I'm thinking (And this is completely arbitrary, mind) that users with above 500 votes on other maps would be a good start. If we wanted to get technical, of those 500 votes, I'm certain that Arachnid could implement a system where that given user's average rating given will have to be more than a 2.5, or something along those lines.

A second criterion (If that didn't work), would be number of rated maps (Say, 25 or 50, perhaps). In this form, we could set a limit for those people who have had their maps rated, and stuck around Numa. This would display not ignorance or apathy for the ratings system, but a knowledge of the ratings system on a level that they don't so much care about the rating a map receives so much as simply making the map. In the same vein, we could grade, in addition, by that user's average map rating. In doing so, a user who has a higher rating would likely be less inclined to rate others' maps down.

If that doesn't seem good enough, we could even collect data and judge by number of maps submitted (Say, 50 or so), and even by time on Numa (Anywhere up to a year would seem like a good criterion to judge upon).

An ever more drastic step would end up simply hand-choosing members who have given out higher average ratings, I'm certain that Arachnid logs that type of thing (And no, I would definitely not make the cut for most of these, I'm a harsh judge on maps, particularly these days, and I barely have peaked some of these criterion).

So, on top of this, we could even go one further step, and implement the above (Tweaked of course) criterion for voters, and *then* look at their average rating, on top of all that. Or, alternately, we could even just take a look at everyone's number of 0 ratings, and oust someone with a percentage of 0 ratings amongst ratings given (Hidden, of course).

From there, each new member that signs up would have to prove their ability to rate maps fairly, and leave good, constructive comments. We can put a limit on their time in the community, on their number of comments left on other maps (And yes, what about bad comments left? But if someone is detrimental enough through 250 comments left that they wouldn't warrant the ability to vote, then they would easily be removed prior to the time when they would join the community.

This is a really easy, simple solution to the problem that is Numa. No, it's not a cure-all, but it is far better than anything that we can do short of abolishing it altogether.

(Whoops, just saw MCP's post, yeah, exactly like that. You have to actually prove that you're able to be a respected member around here, and able to judge other people's work with a level head.)

It'd be "Here's some reasons, this is a plague, no Gay Marriage, no gay partnerships..." So on and so forth. The arguments that I've heard thusfar are absed in religious doctrine, not on any of the following points. So, what, is the Liberal Media pulling the wool over our eyes?

Trying to trick us into legalizing gay marriage... for... what? What would be the gain in trying to get Gay Unions legalized if all of this is correct and true? Is it some evil conspiracy to pass around STDs amongst the homosexual circles, or something?

Quote
* One study reports 70% of homosexuals admitting to having sex only one time with over 50% of their partners (3).

* One study reports that the average homosexual has between 20 and 106 partners per year (6). The average heterosexual has 8 partners in a lifetime.

* Many homosexual sexual encounters occur while drunk, high on drugs, or in an orgy setting (7).

How is sexual promiscuity detrimental to our society as a whole, though? Not only could I say similar things for heterosexual encounters, but I could even take this in the fashion that these behaviours have manifested solely because Gay Marraiges and unions are illegal. The propensity for not committing to a single partner could just as easily be attributed to their lack of ability to wed, not to mention the argument that the percentage of sexual encounters in heterosexual circles while intoxicated or high is in the same percentile. 'Many' is not a quantifiable, researchable number. Had that been a percentage vs. percantages of heterosexual couples, I may think differently, but even this early on in my evaluation of the list, this thing is looking less like a list of reasons, and more like a list of propaganda. Remember, all this is from another message board, and to be honest, I really can't trust this mystery person's agenda behind it.

Quote
* Many homosexuals don't pay heed to warnings of their lifestyles: "Knowledge of health guidelines was quite high, but this knowledge had no relation to sexual behavior" (16).

Pre-fuggin'-posterous. Not the quote or the information, but the underlying point. The underlying point doesn't seem to address the fact that many heterosexuals don't pay heed to warnings of their lifestyles, and yes, it's in a different fashion (General health vs. Sexual health), I think the point still stands to be made that the above is just a bit more than biased. Granted, I don't have a study of this, but, speaking in horrendously general terms, I've never seen a gay man die of high cholesterol. I've never seen nor heard of an overweight gay man. Of course they exist, and of course that's hearsay, but I think that, as a whole, homosexual men (In particular) are on a level of health that *outdoes* the level of heterosexual health. This is something I'll address further below.

Quote
* Homosexuals got homosexuality removed from the list of mental illnesses in the early 70s by storming the annual American Psychiatric Association (APA) conference on successive years. "Guerrilla theater tactics and more straight-forward shouting matches characterized their presence" (2). Since homosexuality has been removed from the APA list of mental illnesses, so has pedophilia (except when the adult feels "subjective distress") (27).

I can't argue against this, beyond the 'storming' part being irrelevant to the main point of the bullet, which is the relation of homosexuality to pedophilia (And other like 'disorders').

Quote
* Homosexuals account for 3-4% of all gonorrhea cases, 60% of all syphilis cases, and 17% of all hospital admissions (other than for STDs) in the United States (5). They make up only 1-2% of the population.

* Homosexuals live unhealthy lifestyles, and have historically accounted for the bulk of syphilis, gonorrhea, Hepatitis B, the "gay bowel syndrome" (which attacks the intestinal tract), tuberculosis and cytomegalovirus (27).

Unhealthy lifestyles? That's ridiculous, and we all know it. That same sentence could have been far better worded as 'Homosexuals have historically accounted..." and left it at that. Unhealthy lifestyles is an entirely different matter than unhealthy sexual lifestyles, and the farther I continue down this list, the more biased these things seem. Granted, I haven't read any of these reports in their entirity, but whomever compiled this list was horribly unprofessional about the language that they used. Had they really expected to make a valid point, their points would be far more consice and clear-cut.

Quote
* 73% of psychiatrists say homosexuals are less happy than the average person, and of those psychiatrists, 70% say that the unhappiness is NOT due to social stigmatization (13).

* 25-33% of homosexuals and lesbians are alcoholics (11).

* Of homosexuals questioned in one study reports that 43% admit to 500 or more partners in a lifetime, 28% admit to 1000 or more in a lifetime, and of these people, 79% say that half of those partners are total strangers, and 70% of those sexual contacts are one night stands (or, as one homosexual admits in the film "The Castro", one minute stands) (3). Also, it is a favorite past-time of many homosexuals to go to "cruisy areas" and have anonymous sex.

And? What does any of this have to do with Gay marriage? The first bullet, in particular, means absolutely nothing to the argument at hand. Plus which, social stigmatization and inability to lead a given life are two entirely seperate things. Thus, the argument can again be made that by outlawing gay marriage (Not in the overtly legal sense, but in the sense that it's not allowed in any form right now), it is detrimental to the gay community as a whole.

On the second bullet point, the study seems to conveniently fail to mention that the alcoholism rate for all americans, (according to the NIAA in 2004) hovers around 31%.

As to the third bullet point, again, the argument could be made that is a direct result of their inability to marry legally.

Quote
* 78% of homosexuals are affected by STDs (20).

Yeah, that's a shitload, can't argue with it, beyond sticking to the point that Gay promiscuity could be attributed to the entire problem at hand.

Quote
* Judge John Martaugh, chief magistrate of the New York City Criminal Court has said, "Homosexuals account for half the murders in large cities" (10).

Good for him. I would like to see that one backed up, a lot. 'Cause really? Half? Seriously. Half? Think about that number for a moment, and then look at the statement again. Doesn't that seem a *bit* preposterous to you?

Quote
* Captain William Riddle of the Los Angeles Police says, "30,000 sexually abused children in Los Angeles were victims of homosexuals" (10).

Over what time period? Is that 30,000 in a year, or over a span of 20 years? Is this compared to anything, or is it a standalone statement?

So, y'know, I'm done debating this. I was gonna respond to more of these, but eh. If these folk've got something valid to bring across, then by all means, but all I see in the lower half of that list is the same propaganda bullcrap, and my friendship with you is too important to continue getting riled over this. You know as well as I do that a number of those are silly, and I understand the point that you were getting across. Still, though, I haven't seen any of these arguments used in any valid way, and I now know why.

#191900 15 2006-06-20T10:07:53Z Kablizzy
Upon playing through these a second time, I found a couple things that I wanted to get down on the forums.

Edit: Jeez, I was freakin' harsh. Sorry, man.

Acoustic - Ehhh. This seems like another maximo map, to me. Nothing quite special about it.

Ask Ze French - Excellent map.

Broken Escalators of Meyhem - The more I play this, the more I look at those thwumps, and think, "Noob map."

Continent - Could've sworn I've commented on these before.

Delegation Comes to Mind - Graaaah! Blizzy Smash!!

Disruptmentalism - I wish I knew what to do about the difficulty here. Perhaps even knocking the left and right-room floorguards altogether? They're just doubling as thwumps, really.

Dronn - Amazing map.

I never did trust bubbles - Like the tileset, perhaps add some mines?

I think I bit my Lip - I still like this, dunno what the others think.

If Gauss Could Kill - Wooo!

Marginally Irrational - Still a great map.

Sober or Justice - Love it.

Some Kinda Monolith - Still awesome.

Something to do with the Weight of the World - Very nice.

The I in Team is Lonely - So hard to get 'round those drones.

Akatosh - Nice stuff.

Alaska's Got Nothing on Me - Really hard to find a route, but once you do, great map.

Arbitrary - Magnificent.

Arkitekt - Really needs a difficulty check.

Big Monster Thing - Maximo, at your best.

Blackout - At first, I thought the left jump-pad would take you all the way to the top, and the right was simply an alternate gold-route, but now that I'm mistaken, hm. I don't know what I was gonna say.

Choices to Make - Love it, but it's probably too difficult for the average player.

Closet Monster - Love it.

Common Denominator - Ehhh, don't like this thing. You may even want to just do away with the bottom, and run with the top, difficulty-tweaked. That seems like that'd make a good level.

Controversy - Very odd and funky, but I love it.

Crey - Brilliant level.

Daedric Temple - Nice, although we discussed a bit about some problems last night.

De-Dance - Fuggin' beat this beast tonight, it's all about the run, and if you don't have it, it's freakin' hard.

Enigmatic - This is the Anthem, but your damn hands up.

Explosion of Light and Sound - The only problem here is that you want to go too fast with the map, and you can't. Not so much a problem with the map, though.

Full Bloom - We both know this one's a bit awkward. Great concept, maybe replace the gauss up top with another set of drones?

Grenades - Good stuff.

I don't know - You know I wanted this back in there. =D

I Quit My Day Job - Whoamazing. One of the best maps I've ever seen.

I'll Take My Bass Deafening - Woot! Nice level.

Lag - Ehhh, need that many mines? Kind of a weird level, you're really stepping outside of yourself for this pack.

Make a Wish - Funky stuff, love it.

Meely - Seems unfinished, as I said over IRC, not sure if it needs mines, or what, but it seems like a cheap version of Plue, somehow (And, just for the record, yes, I expect all of the maps this time around to be Plue-material).

Menorah Wars - Amazing.

Misplaced Some Files - Still hate that first jump up the shaft, and I still think that first part has no place in a map-pack. If there's one thing we've learned, it's that kind of stuff just doesn't make it when we're being scrutinized like this.

Mucky Muck - Great map.

My Bag of Tricks Runs Deep - Gah, that inner jump is WAY annoying. Even the alternate route doesn't lessen the blow all that much.

My Mobile Army - OMFLVMAPS!!!!1ONEONE.

Newsbreaks for the Poor - Unbelievably cool.

Partial Credit - Gah, you and your open-space Chainguns. At least give us somewhere to dodge 'em... Heheh.

Passion - Geez, you're making some funky maps this time around. I dunno, this seems really, really odd, with the half-gold and the tight drone-spaces. Not sure what to do about this one, though.

Quasa - Amazing map. Love it.

Quizzical - Sweet stuff. I seem to hate Trap Doors, though, 'cause I don't really like that function, but I'm sure I'm overreacting.

Remake? I'll Pass - Not really an Expanse map. Great for Numa, though.

Reverberate - Amazing, amazing map. Difficult, though, I can't get past the first four or five pillars with any regularity.

Sam Fischer is not a Ninja - Feels way too like Lucidium's old Meteor Shower, except not as refined.

Save a Lot - Magnificent stuff.

Shoplifting - Great concept, but I feel a bit bored with it, upon playing through it again.

Shuri Shuri Kin - I want to like this map, I love the tileset, but there's really only one way to do the map, the 12 gold that's in there just isn't worth sticking around to get, even for a highscore. I'm not even sure if more gold would fix it, either.

Silent Observers - Neat. Feels really awkward, but really fun, really unique.

Skyline - Ah, I remember this thing. I still can't do it, in any form. Perhaps removing a drone or two would work?

Smallest Monument the The Smallest Man - Beyond the typo in the name, I love this, although it seems like shaping the outer-box in the same "n" shape would be freakin' deep.

Some Abstract is going on - Seems unpolished, but still alright, I suppose.

Some City Line - A bit sub-par, otherwise decent.

Square Holed - Don't especially like this one. I almost, almost do, it's a great concept, but it's not fun to play through.

Steppy - Sorry, hate this thing. It feels unfinished, and The jumps are too hard to pull off through the gausses, I just don't like this at all - Especially when you have so many better maps.

Stitch and Patch - Amazing, amazing stuff.

Strafe - I really, really almost like this. It's just the whole "Chainguns killing me every time I do something" thing that gets me. I have yet to find a solid and consistent way of getting to the top. Also, the bounce-blocks seem a bit too clich, I'd reccommend doing some tiles instead. I attached a type of tile I was using tonight, I think it'd fit pretty well in a couple spots, instead of a coupld of those bounce-blocks. Here y'go:

[image lost: post-41-1150798073.png]

Sundrop - I love everything about this map except for the bottom mines: The middle ones

Sure Did Grow Quickly - I hate those doors. That looks terrible. The remainder of the map is good, unless you go left, when you have to sit at the upper-left and wait for the drones to get to a point where you can jump past 'em.

Technis - Dark and funky, but very odd. I'm not sure what to think about this'n.

Tendrills: Amazing stuff, love this thing.

The Dividing Line - Fun as hell, looks awful. Also looks very similar to one of my rejected levels. I'd count this a bit lower on your list.

The Growth Seems Exponential - Very nice, very challenging.

The Thing is Dead, Jim - Neat idea, but a bit tedious with the back and forth. Let's see what the others say.

Upsidaysie - Ehhh, I like the idea, but it's just not as fun as your better maps.

Vento - Killer, man, but a bit awkward.

Weak Minded -OMFGLVMAP!!11ONEON

WolfBane - Amazing design, but hard as hell to get the gold without gettin' shot in the face.

#192372 4 2006-06-21T04:34:00Z Kablizzy
I still make horrible maps. Every single day, I pump out twice as many piles of crap as I do good maps. Your best bet is to go into Ned with a blank screen, like, right now, and just put a handful of E tiles somewhere. Do a cluster here and a cluster there, maybe connect them together. Perhaps you want the map to look symmetrical, perhaps you don't. Then, imagine what kind of enemies might go in there. Try some drones, maybe a rocket launcher. Then look to see if there would be a good place for an exit, and the exit switch, and if not, make a place for it. From there, give it a quick run-through to see how the ninja interacts with the environment that you just created. If something seems to flow well, leave it. If not, then knock out a part of a tile.

From there, add some innate objects. Put in a couple bounceblocks, add a mine or two or three. Put in some gold. Now test it again, see how it works. If you think it works well, then go with it. If not, look at it, and ask yourself, what is wrong with this map?

Through this, I've been making this map that I've described. I'll attach it here for ya.

What I did, is I created the center islands first. I then smoothed them out a bit, and added drones. I didn't have a goal for the map, so I created the outer islands, and ran through. The islands themselves didn't seem to be too playable, so I threw in three bounce blocks. I then added the gold, and the rocket launcher, and added mines to garnish. Put the ninja on the right, exit switch on the left, doors underneath. In fact, I think I'ma submit this badboy to Numa.

And, don't worry, we're working on something that should be done soon, it'll definitely help with things like this.

Anyway, from there you can start fiddling with designs and messing with different clusters and areas to work with. Look at metanet maps and maps from the top authors, and see what kinds of maps they do, don't try to mimic them, but take a part, and make it yourself, in Ned, and then mess with it. mangle it up, and see how you can affect it. Keep doing this until you have something entirely unique and your own.

#192802 21 2006-06-22T03:17:13Z Kablizzy
That's a pretty awesome map for a first try, TK. Just a couple notes:

* I think the map could have been done better in a smaller space.

* It seemed as though you had too many pent-up ideas working at once.

* The aesthethics were a bit off.

But all of those are normal for mapmakers in your position, so don't sweat it.

However, a couple things to keep in mind. First of all is the idea of standardization. When you have a plethora of objects (In this case, I think you used one of every object), it's harder to grab the player's attention.

The second idea that you may want to look into is minimalization. When you include less objects, and less object types, and try to accomplish similar things with less objects (For instance, if you have fifteen one-way platforms, and you realize that the player can bypass four of them entirely, then you should remove those four), your player can identify more easily with the map.

The third thing that you may want to focus on is theme. Try themes. Try making maps with just laser drones and mines, or just thwumps and floor guards. This helps the player better understand that you were trying to grab their attention with something fresh, and unique, and planned.

So, I took the liberty to edit your map a bit, and add and subtract some things. I'm not sure how it turned out, but it touches on a couple of things.

First, theme. I standardized the layout of the mines and the gold. This provides a consistent theme throughout the map. I also lessened the space that the map took up, and moved a couple of the enemies around.

Finally, I rounded out some of the corners with 1-tiles, just for aesthetics.

So, anyway, not to say that this is better, per se, but it addresses a couple of the most-commonly overlooked things in maps.

Edit: And yes, I do realize that the level is unbeatable now. I was simply illustrating a point.

Quote: Beo, June 25, 2006 02:44 am
I was having an argument with someone over this:

You know that old saying about how if there were a roomful of monkeys on typewriters, they would eventually type one of Shakespeare's sonnets purely by accident? It's quite obvious to make the step and say that if there were an infinite amount of monkeys, or they typed for infinity, then every possible combination/arrangement of letters would eventually be typed.

From there it's obvious to conclude that if the universe is infinite, then every physical possibility must exist somewhere in the universe, as every possible arrangement of the particles that make up matter exists as there is an infinite space for them to occur in. The person I was arguing with didn't understand this, and neither did my parents. Please prove to me why I am wrong.

You're wrong because there's a fault in logic at work here. For instance, let's say that, in terms of atmospheres, there are (Hypothetically, of course), three types; Hydrogen-based, Oxygen-based, and Nitrogen-based.

Now, even if the universe were indeed infinite (Which it logically cannot be, unless it somehow steps outside the rules of coherent thought, which is also entirely possible, but we're only human, so for the sake of argument, here we are), then one out of every three planets would be either Hydrogen-based, Oxygen-based, or Nitrogen-based. Now, let's say that, when a planet forms, the Hydrogen-based planets form farther out, while Oxygen- and Nitrogen-based planets form closer to a given star.

Now, from there, we don't have enough evidence to postulate that exactly 33.33% of the time, a planet will be a Nitrogen-, Hydrogen-, or Oxygen-based planet. Why? It has to be one of the three, so it would have to average to 33.33%, right? Even if there were infinite space, the physical possibility of a condition forming does not follow into that physical possibility actually doing so.

Now, arguing that there is infinite space out there is rather shaky ground to begin on, as when the space approaches infinity, it becomes more and more exponentially possible that said Nitrogen-based planet will be out there somewhere, but it doesn't dictate that it *has* to. Even with the smallest, most miniscule impobability, it is still within the realm of reason that a given instance could or could not exist. With an unlimited, and unfathomable amount of space, though, it is almost certain that said condition will be met (Nearing 100%, as closely as it possibly can get), but it isn't a given.

Although, I'm not big on Infinitum Theory, so my dribble is merely speculation. S'how I see it, anyway.

Because scientists have already prooved that the universe didn't always exist.

Ok, here is what I am trying to say...

The universe has not always existed. That has been proved by scientists. Before the universe existed, which was everything, there was nothing. Imagine something like this.

There is a computer that just got turned on. At the point it was turned on, there was absolutely no information on it. This computer is the universe. To turn it on would be to start it. Lets say the person turning it on is God. Lets also say that God built, or put together this computer. So at the point God turned it on, he was, lets say, creating the universe. So what do we have right now? A computer that is on, but is empty. So, you could say it is a space with nothing in it. This could be the "vacuum".

Ok, lets stop this story for a second. What do we have?

1. God built the computer.
2. God turned the computer on.
3. The computer is empty, so it is like a vacuum.

This is where I think people are getting mixed up. When I was saying "before the universe", I was talking about before the "computer" was built. I think people were mistaking "before the universe" for when there was nothing on the computer, but the computer existed. A vacuum takes up space, right? It has got to be somewhere. Well, what I am talking about is before there was a place for that vacuum to be. Or, you could say before the computer was built. I know its hard to understand, but stick with me.

Okay. Very well thought-out. Let's get into it.

First, scientists haven't proven that the universe has not always existed. Existence theory is still a very valid theory, but because of the Big Bang Theory, Existence theory has gotten far less attention. The concept of infinity in an ever-changing universe may still be correct (Think akin to early Europeans thinking that the world was flat vs. finding out otherwise - The Big Bang Theory could be entirely wrong, as could existence theory - There could be theories out there that we are as yet completely unaware of).

So, let's take your argument in kind. I'll (thankfully enough) only need to refute one point of yours. So, let's take your analogy in kind. Let's assume that this computer got turned on, and turning it on is starting it, like you said. The point of contention comes when we ask "Who or what started the computer?"

You say that God started the computer. Big Bang Theorists say that the Big Bang did so. You have no information nor evidence pointing to the thought that God started the computer. Your argument that he started the computer is, and I quote, "Let's say the person turning it on is God." I could make a similar argument, stating, "Let's say the thing turning it on is the Big Bang," and it would hold the very same validity to your argument as a whole - Which is none.

So, your computer analogy isn't quite valid, in that it isn't the only way for things to be. With an open mind, you can understand rather easily that there may be any number of ways that the universe started, none of which are definitively God. You can hold your belief in it, but your belief runs on pure assumption, and nothing else. The only thing that scientists have behind their Big Bang Theory is what we have been able to observe - And that which seems to be causing the red-shift in other galaxies may have been caused by something akin to the Big Bang. Thus, you can't say with any certainty that God was the one that began the process. It may very well be that he did, but there is an equally great chance that it was not, and in either case, you couldn't claim that it was to begin with. Since we are assuming that God was the one that turned on this computer, the remainder of your argument that was based upon it fails, due to ill-gotten premeses.
