1. My argument about you not being at the Big Bang is entirely valid, within the context that I put it. Taking out of context, and making it seem as though it were a main premise in my argument, when it was nothing but a simple refutation of a sub-argument of yours skews my entire position. You claim that the Big Bang has proven that the Universe hasn't always existed. This is a priori false. Why? Because of Existence Theory. Why is that relevant? Because Existence Theory is one that contradicts the Big Bang theory. Thus, neither have been proven yet. And, in doing so, you can't make the claim that the Universe hasn't existed as proof, because we honestly don't know. Does that make sense?

2. There are indeed things that are beyond human comprehension. Can you comprehend the notion of Infinity? No, humans don't have the mental capacity to fully understand what Infinity means. We have the comprehension to ponder it, and we can define the notion of it, but this is why we can't think of something that goes on forever. Can we comprehend something smaller than a quark? No, we can't, because our mental capacity doesn't allow us to do so. So, in the same vein, we can't comprehend anything that may or may not have existed prior to the Big bang. You claim that since this is so, it must have been God that built our computer. This is obviously flawed. Why? Well, when we ponder the Big Bang, we think of it as the beginning of our Universe. This may not be the case. The Big Bang coule be something entirely different than what we think it is. Our Universe could be a product of something entirely beyond anything that we can even ponder, so if we take into account t he idea of a Big Bang, we also have to take into account the possibility of the Big Bang being something far beyond the realm of just simple creation - Because it could be. If we are to think the Big Bang is definitively creation of our Universe Happening, we may as well liken it to thinking that the world is flat, because this is all based upon our perception of the world around us, and our Universe. So, to be intelligent creatures, we must be able to learn from our past mistakes, and tread carefully through future theories and beliefs, as we can see from our history what we've done wrong.

3. You can't say that there needed to be a cause for the Universe existing. Why? Well, two reasons. First of all, because of Existence Theory being valid. Solely because the Big Bang theory contradicts the theory that the Universe was always here doesn't mean that the Big Bang theory is the correct one to follow. Secondly, because of the inability of humans to comprehend certain things in our universe. You claim that there needed to be a cause for the Universe Existing. Why? Why is it entirely impossible that the Universe just is? Why does there need to be a cause for Existence at all? This was the point I was trying to make with our inability to comprehend certain things in our Universe. We, as humans, can't comprehend such things as what may have occured before or during the Big Bang, just as we can't comprehend the Infinity of the Universe having always existed. We can't comprehend something that doesn't have a causal relationship with something else, but that doesn't have any bearing upon whether those things are true, relevant, or if they exist.

4. See my point number 4 below.

5. Eh? Did I misconceive or misrepresent something that you put forth? If so, then by all means, bring it up.

6. That was not in any way, shape, or form my argument, or even a part of my argument, so I'll thank you not to misrepresent it in that fashion. The comprehension premise is a part of a higher understanding clause which, in turn, acts as a refutation of a single form of your arguments, which, amongst other premeses, leads to your argument being false, as you've presented it.

So, to continue:

1. That's entirely my point. We theorize about it. We don't know that the Big Bang happened, and that's entirely the point that I'm trying to get across. I could theorize that the Flying Spaghetti Monster was the cause of the Universe, but that doesn't make it so. That seems to be the core of your argument, wherein you just assume that God made our computer, and leave it at that, discounting other theories based upon nothing at all, or even faulty premeses which adhere to a non-proven theory.

2. You're putting words into my mouth. We can't comprehend certain things, and this topic is here so that we can all glean a better understanding of each other. You didn't address the comprehension point at all with this, this is simply a fallacious tactic called a 'straw man' fallacy, where you claim that I'm saying "We can't comprehend things," to which you respond, "why is this topic even here?" Which isn't a valid rebuttal. When I talk about comprehension, I speak almost strictly of the idea that since there are certain things that we can't understand, we can't use Universals as proof.

3. Ah, but you can't. Just because the sky is blue here doesn't mean that the sky is blue on another world. Just because the quark is the smallest thing *that we know of* doesn't mean that it isn't the smallest thing in existence. Just because the Big Bang theory is the predominant theory doesn't mean that it is the correct theory. Just because everything that we observe here has a cause/effect situation does not mean that everything always will have a cause/effect situation. This is why the idea of comprehension is important. You are assuming that because there is a cause for things here means that everything, forever and ever, in all instances, without deviation, must have a cause. By this logic, you have to be so careful when using Universals, because so rarely are they true. I could say that all cats are orange tabbies, but simply claiming things based upon what I observe is incorrect. This includes, in no uncertain terms, causality, as causality is a universal.

4. God must be a part of the Universe, as 'Universe' is derived from a Greek word for 'Everything.' Other definitions for Universe include "Everything that exists everywhere." Thus, you must claim that God is a part of the Universe, or God is not a part of anything, and therefore, is nothing. Thus, prior to the Big Bang, God must have existed. Since the Universe is everything that exists, then God was the only thing that existed, and thus, God would be the Universe. So, unless you can define Universe differently, or unless you can prove definitively that Everything that exists doesn't include Heaven, God, Hell, and/or other planes of Existence - In which instance, you must also claim that the term 'Universe' is defined incorrectly - Then I'm not sure what else you would be able to to claim beyond that God is a part of the Universe, and beyond defining your own unique belief system, which we can get into later.

5. It's extremely helpful, if you'd bother to actually address my points. I asked you a number of questions, which you promptly ignored. Did you think I would simply forget that I had asked you the questions? Did you think that by posting something emotionally charged rather than something logically relevant to the discussion at hand, that somehow my points would magically become invalid?

6. I'm glad you asked, and if you would like for me to take a side, I will do so. My position is rather simple. I posit that you cannot claim that God created the Universe, nor can you claim that he turned the computer on, and I have represented why. In taking a side, I further posit that the only true understanding of the situation is a logical and rational analysis of every thought process, and a rational account of each, in turn passing judgment upon that which is the most logical, rational, and well thought-out. Of course, we can't make that jump yet, because we really don't have enough information to make a decision for proving where we came from.

1. There are a multitude of theories, doctrines, and beliefs that attempt to explain the creation of our universe.
2. None of these theories have proven true.
Thus,
3. Claiming that any given theory is true is inherently flawed.
Therefore,
4. Only a rational acceptance of all current theories, doctrines, and beliefs as equal weight is the correct position to take, until further information enters.

Of course, this leads to an entirely different argument, but I will leave my argument at that. I'm confident that I'm supporting my side fully and very well, because my position is a direct antithesis to every other position out there, since every other position is, at their core, "We can prove our point better than you can prove yours," all of which being false positions. My position stems from years of debate against those like you who claim that your position is the only right one because you have some magical evidence that has never been valid nor relevant. My debates are all point-counterpoint, and you're the one positing your argument with your 'evidence' and 'good points,' and I am refuting it. If you'd like to refute my own position, then by all means, do so. I have yet to have a single soul fully refute a point of mine (Yes, Daddaluma, I know, that was a political debate).

00-0: Late Bloomers - I really loved this, it's a really neat conceptual map, and it plays pretty well. I didn't quite notice anything vital that they should have added/subtracted from this.

00-1: Rise and Shrine - Another simple, fun map. The only real problem I saw with it was the gold placement. It could have been done far better, along the sides of the pillar, and along the sides of the outer walls of each pit.

00-2: Central Star - I really enjoyed this map, and I loved the tileset structure on the outside, I rather thought the concept was neat, as well. I also loved the star structure, but I thought the bounce blocks could have been better placed along the outside so that maneuverability could be a bit better.

00-3: Sneech - I thought this, as well, was amazingly done. It has a great balance of enemies and gold placement, jumping, and tileset. I loved the design, and the additional tileset work on the right.

00-4: De Toren - I hated this one. The one-way platforms seemed randomly placed, and the entire map lends itself to two ways of making it up the tower - First, you can simply walljump the left side, and jump over, taking an unbelievably easy way back to the exit. The second way is to cheat the one-ways, or just button-mash randomly, which isn't terribly fun. I'd say this map is good on paper, but shouldn't have made it in.

#197131 10 2006-06-30T21:20:29Z Kablizzy
Checkered Past by stepself
A unique blend of mine jumper, action map, puzzle map, and aesthetic masterpiece, Checkered Past by Stepself was, and still is, one of the most inspiring maps in recent history.
"Quite possibly one of the greatest action maps ever made. No joke, this is absolutely incredible." (Jiggerjaw12358)

Aspire by tktktk
Combining some of the most unique gameplay, and stylish level-design ever, Aspire by tktktk has all the elements that a good map should have. Combine riveting close-calls with a fun, quirky environment, and you have the recipe for one of the greatest maps to ever grace Numa.
"Totally the best thing ever. And I didn't just make this quote up, like, right now." (Kablizzy)

*Blink* ...Ahem. Yeah, it didn't have any good quotes, so feel free to quote me as saying anything, and I'll post it in the thread. Heh.

Hedge by Zorn
Not many maps these days can be classified as 'groundbreaking.' But that is exactly what Hedge by Zorn accomplishes. With a unique tileset, and shockingly difficult play, Hedge defined the modern maze map in a way that none other could so much as dream.
"This... is... just... plain... wicked. 5/5" (OvrIndnsea)

Acrophilia by stepself
Not many minefield maps can so succinctly explode onto the scene like stepself's Acrophilia. A brilliant test of speed and control, Acrophilia masterfully blends all of the elements of a classic N map.
"You are a genius. I haven't seen a map like this before and the object placement is like, perfect... 5/5" (krusch)

OR

"5/5 and favourited. This is fantastic... absolutely brilliant... a truly magnificant map in absolutely every way imaginable. Thank you so much for this... I mean, well... well done. This is fantastic. Truly deserving of number 1." (formica)

I know that both would need to be cut down, but the grunt-work is done there.

Artificial Intelligence by littleviking001
When you think of great maps, one can hardly even begin without thinking immediately about littleviking001's Artificial Intelligence. Easily one of the first truly legendary maps, Artificial Intelligence is heralded to this day for its in-your-face brilliance.
"Simply amazing, amazing level. This is why you're one of the best! 5/5!" (Kablizzy)

As for this one, I posted my own comment today, since there weren't any others. Dunno if the contradiction with my earlier comment will matter here or not.

Framework by tktktk
If one map were to define fun, it would be Framework by tktktk. With a fun theme, fantastic design, and unfathomable gameplay, Framework is undeniably one of the greatest N accomplishments ever.
(Don't have a quote for this one either)

And that's all I've got time for today. See ya's!

#199020 10 2006-07-05T02:07:51Z Kablizzy
I'm in full belief these days that this is Hell. And of course, not the stereotypical Hell of pitchforks and demons and fiery pits, but a psychological, philosophical, emotional Hell. Because, really, when you ponder it at length, you begin to ask yourself, "What is the worst thing that could happen?"

And, of course, you think Eternal Damnation. But if you narrow that down a bit, you think Eternal Pain. But if you ponder further, you come to realize that the worst thing imaginable isn't pain, really. Not in the way that we think of Eternal Damnation. This is rather awkward to explain, but the greatest punishment wouldn't be pain, because there would be another level, a deeper level to the pain. Thus, if you think of pain as a punishment, and in terms of punishment, you think that human nature would dictate that one would learn a lesson from such pain. But the point of the Eternal State of Damnation wouldn't be learning a lesson, really, it would be the unending, everlasting pain.

Thus, the deeper level of pain would be lack of knowledge of said pain - ignorance. So, really, the worst pain imaginable wouldn't be the pain itself, nor the concept of pain, nor of damnation, but ignorance to the fact that said pain exists; under our bed, just at our doorstep, and around every corner.

Yet, we cry, "Why? Why?" when this pain manifests, not even coming close to understanding that the pain was there all along, simply looming as a shadow, always there, in light or dark. In darkness, even though one cannot perceive said shadow, it still exists. It simply requires the light with which to see and project it.

So, in my own mind, this is my personal Hell. For what? Why, I don't know, for I have no life lesson to learn. This is my punishment, this is my damnation.

#200263 240 2006-07-08T10:47:03Z Kablizzy
Ohhhh. Hm. That's awesome. I'm stoked for the changes, as well, and I'm excited that an entirely new dynamic will be created. Plus, with new drone paths, wall and ceiling guards, and so on, this opens the door to further packs for us to release. (Yes, I know, 1000 maps is quite enough, but hey, a man can dream, hm?)

Also, hey, to accompany my post in Shaun's Map thread, I just wanted to say a couple things. LV, maximo, sorry, but I'm leaving you two out for this one. We all know what you guys are capable of.

Tim - I always thought of you as a highscorer, you were always king of the hill, the original giant of the scoreboard, but I never really pegged you as one of the great mapmakers of our time. Sure, names like LV and maximo are must-haves on said list, but if I remember right, your first map on Numa was Poetry in Motion, and afterwards, you went right into the Simple Challenge Series, which I hated (Due to my inability to so much as finish even one). So, when maximo brought you onto the team, I was excited to see what you could do in this type of atmosphere, and for Legacy, I liked your stuff quite a bit. But this time around, your maps have been so high-quality, that I can't fathom how your name doesn't appear on everyone's top 10 list from here on out.

Linus - I first saw your Numa maps, way, way back when, when you were putting out your DDAs. Then, after making a handful of maps, you went back to your DDA roots, throwing Ring of Fire and Tattletale in everyone's collective faces. I remember when Tattletale ousted Kablizzy's Cavern Three from the top-rated map spot on Numa - It was a sad day for me, and I remember thinking how awesome Tattletale really was to obtain such a following. But I never really thought of your levels as the best around. Generally, I thought that they were a bit long, and drawn-out, and I never thought twice about too many of them. But when I saw the type of mapping that you brought to the table for Legacy, I was pleasantly surprised. Your Legacy maps went over great, but what really blew me away was your Expanse pack. I was shocked that some of the stuff you were able to do with those maps was even possible, and I am just floored by the unbelievable quality of your maps this time around.

Lucidium: Ah, I can't leave you out. Your mapping reminds me a lot of my own mapmaking. When I look back at your Numa maps, I can see you progressing as a mapmaker, right before my eyes. Being the man who voted on 50% of the Numa maps, way back when, I held so much respect for you outside of your mapping. I never saw much from you, because you never really mapped a whole lot. You were more of an entity that simply commanded respect. So, for the longest time, I really didn't even know what kind of maps you made. And then, Pressed for Time hit. And then Meteor Shower, and then Precarious, and then Jacks, Tenacious, Carbon Chains, Valves, Compartment, and they blew the community wide open. I still remember when Meteor Shower kicked Kablizzy's Cavern Three out of the Top spot on Numa. But I loved the map. You can't match a map the caliber of Meteor Shower. So, when you agreed to be a part of the team, I was ecstatic. I'm expecting great, great things from you, because you're a Legend in your own right.

So, with that said, I want us to start ramping Expanse up, which Sweep and Tim are spearheading with the organizing of our Userlevel threads; I'll be getting to maps ASAP, just keep bugging me to play and rate.

I also want to get some more opinions, and some more activity in general. If we're going to finish these projects in good time, we've gotta start some planning on them, and we've gotta begin getting our Expanse maps ready to roll, I'm looking towards September 1st as a decent date. We won't announce that, of course, but that seems like a good time for us to be wrapping this thing up.

So, P42 launched today, and I thought they did a great job on it. I think they could have used a bit more leadership and organization within the team, but I am happy nonetheless to see that they pulled it off, and that people are liking it. With that said, I think our next project is a bit of a site redesign and update. I would like for our frontpage to have more than just text, as I said a while ago, perhaps we can get some ideas flowing for that? I think my portal idea went a bit awry, as that image is far too big to expect people to load on a regular basis. I think that something small and something similar to what the Dronies site has (Just a shadowed image of an N map, with parts of the map labeled as links to our various projects / sites, and so on). What do we think?

#200852 11 2006-07-10T07:07:59Z Kablizzy
Alrighty, I'm back onto this. Sorry this took me, like, 4 months.

I'ma go through and rate them all systematically. If there are similar levels, we'll make a judgment call on it whenever we get 'round to it.

Erm... I haven't done any reviews yet? Well, let's get our hands dirty. Also, trying a new format.

13.6 MK - Beautiful tileset, absolutely love this thing, although I think this would be better cased as a Numa map, or perhaps for our {4}th map-pack.

3753 Cruithne - This thing made me single-handedly hate rocket launchers again. With that in mind, this is oodles of fun, is there any trick to the top-right section? There's usually more than one rocket that follows me up there, just curious. Keeper

A little TOO simple - Hm. Strangely enough, this was indeed a little too simple. It felt like a Blizzy map, and chainguns in the open just isn't fun on my end. Don't quite like the hidden door/switch, but eh, I'd Numa-tize this one.

A Mean Spirited or Spiteful Remark - First of all, I <3 the name, and the significance to the map. Secondly, amazing map. Not keen on the half-hidden exit and switch, but other than that, Keeper

Angel Island - Absolutely amazing little minimalistic map here. I would go and put this one on Numa, or save this for {4}. I'd rather see this in {4}, actually.

Barbed Wire - Decent. Nothing too flashy.

Beware of the Puppies - Neat concept, didn't quite like the close calls that many times in a row.

Bridge of Sighs - A-mazing. Simply amazing. Again, the aesthetics of the exit being half hidden are kinda iffy, but this is just too good. Keeper

Broken Bridge - Another great concept, I like this one a lot. Keeper

Cathedral - Blew me away. Freakin' amazing. Keeper

Confinement - Definitely a {4} map, in my eyes. One of your better maps, for sure.

Cutting it Fine - Simply brilliant, as a later level. Keeper

Equidistant - Another fine map. Love it. Keeper

Fillin' in Time - Again, pet peeve of the exit door being untraditional, and I'm not sure if the floorguard is neccesary, but I could definitely see this as a later map. Borderline keeper.

Finglonger - One of the few maps that I can say wouldn't benefit from anything else. Great map. Keeper

Good Things Come in Pairs - Um... okay, yeah, you've got me on this one. It'd be fun if it weren't counter-intuitive.

Gourd - Decent, probably a Numa map. I've had bad luck with these types of tilesets before (I had two or three in Legacy that everyone just hated).

Held up by Magic - Genius, I love this thing. Keeper

Hurdles -Ahhhh, this thing. I'd put this into {4}, this is exactly that type of map. Although, it would make for some neat variety in the pack. Borderline keeper.

My Pillow is all Spiky - I'd Numa-tize this one. Too drawn-out, quite a bit too complex.

Oops upside your head - Not sure on this one. It made me vomit up an Al Sharpton-shaped ball of clay, but I still had some fun. When in doubt, I say Numa it.

Peekaboo - I love this for {4}, which is looking to be an amazing set, if we go by some of this.

Piston - Christ, you're an innovator, man. Never seen anything like this. I'm not even sure what to think of it, it's so new.

Polarisation Mechanism - Beautiful. I <3 this thing. Keeper

AHA! That made me realize that I gave you my review over IRC for most (If not all) of these.

Anyway...

Rush - THIS is a {4} map, to the extreme. This would be the epitome of what the reject pack would be.

Seen it Before - Neat little map. Not sure if it's up to quality, but yeah, good stuff. I'll appeal to the others on this.

She Fell Over - Remove that locked door, and this is unbelievable. That free-standing door just doesn't fit at all. I'd also put gold in the spot where the switch goes - also, you missed a mine, in the bottom-right.

Shimmering Well - Nice, not much to say here. Keeper

Shomb Belter - My eyes literally widened when I saw this thing. Fantastic. Keeper

Sidle - Argh, this thing. I don't like this one at all.

Sunbrick - What an amazing, little, innovative map. Keeper

Surface Tension - Oh, damn, I just had an idea like this tonight. Great map. Keeper

That was a stupid Place to put them - {4} material, not too keen on the mechanic at the end, but yeah. I love the map, but I dunno about the ending.

In fact, you may just wanna start a reserve pack, or portion of your maps, for {3} and/or {4} and/or Numa. I've resigned myself to having to do so.

The Beast Within - Nice little jumper. Very simplistic. Keeper

The Big Jump - I'd take this one to Numa, or the reject pack.

These Bubbles Don't Look Right - I like the level a lot, but it feels a tad bit off. Not sure what it is. Keeper

Transverse Wave - I'm so close to loving this, the play is just a tad bit clunky. Not sure what you could do to fix that.

Vulnerable - Magnificent, man. I love it when the Drones all get going on you one after another.

Okay, I think that's all of 'em! Hope this helps!

#201209 12 2006-07-11T06:52:15Z Kablizzy
Okay, man, time to give a proper critique -

Blame the Foo - Love it, although the exit tiles look a bit odd. Perhaps you should experiment with curved tiles over there, as well, in the same shape as the upper tile structure? Keeper

Edit: I worked with this, and it didn't look good, I included my suggestion anyway, even though the map really is fine as-is.

Come Swat Flies with me - Fun map, ugly tileset. Not sure if this is good enough to make it in.

Do not Annotate - Amazing concept, incredibly fun. Didn't quite like the cheatability, but I think it's good as-is in either case. Keeper

Drain - A bit odd-looking, but definitely fun. The whole chainguns in the open concept still bugs me, but this is decent.

Gladly put up with you - Loved the bottom, loved it, loved it. I hated the trap doors, and the bars coming from the walls, but I loved the bounceblock-mine-gold combo at the top. Upon looking at the map, I think it may benefit from just putting the pair of exit switches in the bottom-right tunnel, removing the jutting portions of the walls, and bringing those bounce-blocks down a bit more. Or maybe keep the jutting portions, and just not making it required to get up there, not sure. I just thought the upper part kinda ruined the map.

Edit: Toyed with this a bit, I think the functionality here is relatively the same. I thew in a jump pad, but that looks horrible. Doesn't play too bad, though. Included in the attached suggestions.

Guilty - Fantastic. Keeper

On a Roll (This Time) - Again, love the map, but I didn't love the bottom part at all, I felt that kind of detracted from the map, as a whole. I think your style is better complimented with simpler concepts, and I think the bottom part pushes this one into "too much." Perhaps putting gold where those switches are, and putting the exit switch at the top-middle? I don't think closing the bottom off is the answer, because, aesthetically, it looks great, but I think the added requirement of being down there is a bit much.

Edit: Included in my suggestions attached.

Ich bin ein Berliner - Strange little map, but fun nonetheless. Keeper

Impediatry - I love this level, but it seems like it's a bit on the cramped side. I think there may be too many enemies here, you might want to try to combine those three gausses and rocket launcher into a single gauss, or a single rocket launcher, in the middle-top, that has the line of sight that the other four have. Not sure if I explained that well, but I think a single gauss would work tonnes better. Perhaps lowering the jagged column that the rocket launcher is nestled beside... Egh. I'll just edit the map to show you what I'm thinking. It'll be attached below.

Edit: Included in my suggestons attachment.

Jazz - Best map in the pack. Keeper

Jeff is a man of many layers - Eh, decent. Nothing too special about it, but not bad.

Landscape - Nice, although the ability to cheat the floorguards is a bit odd. Keeper

Nerve - Funky-Fresh. That upper-left switch is freakin' hard to get. Keeper

Postman Shaun - I'm not sure why I don't like the name, but fantastic map. One thing, though - You need to widen the landing spot in the upper left by half a tile. I find myself having a hard time hitting that spot. Keeper

Edit: I remember why I didn't like the name. I had a fantastic name for this, and it's slipped my mind, since.

Slightly Tangy Symphony - Bleh, I didn't like this one at all.

The Eraser - Amazing. The middle gameplay is a tad clunky, but nonetheles... Keeper

The Trickster - That Chaingun really bugs me. I'd like to see it have a wallfollow algo, and go from the middle/top-right, and follow the ceiling, or something. It's annoying as hell where it is now, and I'd like to stay away from bugs like that. Keeper

Too many Rockets - Hah, beautiful map. Keeper

Your Mother Told you Never to Play with Thwumps - Name needs to be shortened, but beyond that, this is good. It's fun to thwump-launch yourself across the level. Keeper

Edit: Adding the suggestions.

About your suggestions...
Gladly Put Up With You - I have to say, I really, really dislike this edit. I don't know what to say, I'm not sure why you dislike the trapdoors, they're soooo fun to climb, that was always the best part of the map for me.
Impediatry - I agree. It is too cramped. The edit you've done, is, for me, hit and miss. I don't understand the tileset change (it's removed a really good bit of flow) and the movement of that gauss is harder than the one before (that's sorta inter-related with the flow, they go hand-in-hand). The removal of the rocket makes perfect sense, as does the removal of the gauss inside the mine section.
I'm On A Roll (This Time) - You're spot on with this edit, with exception of the exit placement. The switch placement is fine, but as soon as you put the gold in that bottom section you're making it so the exit is in the way, and you have to fetch the switch later instead. I've fixed this, you'll see it in the next upload, but, anyway, you're completely correct about this level.
Blame the Foo - I agree that the tiles around the exit are awkward but I like the style, so I've swapped them round so it's easier to jump onto and off from. However, the tilechange you made in the drone section totally takes out the fun part of the map for me; walljumping off the far wall onto the convex curve and sorta swinging back out before the drones arrive... if you do it right it's just awesome.
Postman Shaun - I'll shorten this to Postman. And I'll widen the landing area. You're right on both.
Your Mother Told you Never to Play with Thwumps - shortened to Never Play With Thwumps.
The Trickster - you're right, removal of bug-use is preferable, and here it is very possible, I just need to time it right. Good suggestion. Also, I'm moving the exit switch to somewhere nicer, you'll see that in my next update.

And also...
Jazz - I'm actually kinda dissapointed this is your favourite one. I don't really like it. Well, I do, but for me it feels like a copycat map. It's nice, polished and fun, but for me it's been one that I don't like on a personal level. This sounds really stupid, I know, but yeah, there you go.

Gladly put up with you - I'm not sure what it is, it may be the length of the map that's bugging me, I'm not sure. I think I might have a thing with optional-type maps, where you can spend more time going for some gold, or finishing the level. I suppose I think that it caters to a wider playerbase that way, or something. No big deal on this one, just something that kinda bugged me. I still love the bottom part, I'd rather see the focus on that, perhaps as its own level? I dunno, the top just feels... mmm... tacked on? If that makes sense? Eh, I dunno.

Imediatry - Just toying around with placements to get the main idea across, really. The tileset change was so that the gauss could see more of the map, but that wasn't imperative at all. The gauss is indeed harder in that spot, but again, it was more of a conceptual move, as are all of my suggestions - just to get the idea out there for you to make changes.

I'm on a Roll (This Time) - Glad you liked the idea, I think I can even see the edit that you put in. I'll be looking forward to it.

Blame the foo - Aye, I just did that for aesthetics, really. I had the exit sitting on a flat, and the switch in the curvey-part, and the exit just looked horrible in a curve itself. I do enjoy the tiles in the drone section. Looking forward to this one, too. Great map.

Postman Shaun - Hehe, I wish I could remember that dang name, that's the only reason I would have brought it up.

Jazz - It's a unique level, a great concept, I've never seen anything like it, the tileset is great, the floorguard-mine-bounceblock combo is brilliant, the gold is placed magnificently... it's just all around a great map for me.

I'll be using Tim's scale of Poor, Okay, Good, Great, Excellent. I think that's a good standard for us all to start using, with okay maps and poor maps being under the limit. Ones in bold are ones that I think you should cut, due to a number of factors, which I'll include in each one.

Akatosh is okay, that gauss at the end is just dumb
Alaska's Got Nothing on Me is Excellent
Arkitekt is Great
Choices to Make is Great
Controversy is Great
Enigmatic is OPMGFMOPQT3OMEOTM3Q
Explosion of Light and Sound is okay
Full Bloom is Great
If Gauss could kill is good
I'll take my bass deafening is great
Join the Party is okay - Plays clunky, linear routes on these type of maps isn't all that fun. Like Tim said, you're afraid to move, really, I sit on that middle block almost the entire time, and then dive face-first into a drone.
Menorah Wars is Great
My Mobile Army is Great
Nothing like tetris is good
Processed to Perfection is great
Reverberate is okay/good
Sleepless in St. Louis is Great
Stitch and Patch is great
Sundrop is great
Think Tank is excellent
Weak Minded is great
Arbitrary is great
Ask Ze French is excellent
Big monster thing is okay/good
Closet monster is excellent
Continent is okay - Feels unrefined, definitely what I'd call below the standard.
De dance is poor/excellent
Disruptmentalism is excellent
I never did trust bubbles is great
I quit my day job is excellent+
In case of nuclear winter is excellent
Meely is good/great
misplaced some files is okay, you know I hate that beginning. Like I said over IRC, we already know that "In order to do X, you must do Y" is a bad form for a map when the Y factor is as technical as something like this. Plus, you have far better maps.
Newsbreaks for the poor is excellent
Passion is poor - Again, you have far, far better maps than this. I don't like the tight spaces at all, and I think that this could easily be bettered with one of your other maps.
Shuri Shuri Ken is good
Silent Observers is great
skyline is excellent
Some kind of monolith is good
Steppy is okay - I think we've established that jumper maps that are this frustrating are bad form. Like I said a couple months ago, just because you and Tim can do it doesn't mean it's a good idea to roll with.
The Dividing Line is okay
Upsidaysie is good

One of the main reasons why I think that those above should be replaced is because you're overlooking some fantastic maps in your 'sideboard,' so to speak. And there were even some (Dronn jumps immediately to mind) that weren't even considered, that I think would far, far outweigh some of the less savoury maps here. Now, I'll admit, on misplaced some files, that it's a fun level, overall. It's just that when there's a part of the map that is even potentially that frustrating, it detracts from the map, as a whole. So, with that said, some of your sideboard stuff should most certainly be in your main levels.

Edit: I mean, what happend to Mistakes Happen? I don't know? Mixed Emotions? Prevailing Wind? Tendrils? TENDRILS, MAN!? Okay, I admit, these aren't great maps, in any sense, but I think they should've at least been in the running, especially when you still have maps that would make good or great status in your et cetera pile. I mean, I'm remembering the days of Up-Down, and stuff like Upsidaysie can be so replaced with better stuff, man. Especially seeing your stuff for [3], going back, I feel that a few of these could just be better.

Also, I'd like to see what everyone else has to say on these. Ahem.

Blackout is excellent
Crey is excellent
Downscale is okay
Grenades is great
Mucky Muck is excellent
Save A lot is excellent
Some abstract is going on is okay
Technis is okay
The growth seems exponential is good
wolfbane is good

I mean, it's not a big deal to log in and see a banner with pink ponies... is it? I mean, seriously. It's not porn, it's not violent, it's the cutest fucking thing imaginable, and people are... bitching about it? Trying to say that it'll drive new members away, or something?

I mean, if I got you a birthday cake that said, "Happy Birthday Kerron," would you enjoy the cake, or would you throw it at the wall, complaining about the spelling of your name?

I think I may want to repeat that last line for the rest of these fine folk: I mean, if I got you a birthday cake that said, "Happy Birthday Kerron," would you enjoy the cake, or would you throw it at the wall, complaining about the spelling of your name?

From my vantage, that's what this is all about. I mean, you can't tell me that there's any real harm in there being ponies in the banner for a few days. So, what would the big deal be over everything? If they were indeed designed just for us, we could go create our very own Metanet board, and put ponies in the banner for our own snobbish entertainment, but we don't. Why? Because it's fun to do it here! It should be fun for everyone! No one should be in the least bit incensed over this, at least, not seriously. I love the pony resistance, I think it's hilarious to no end. Why? Because it's all in good fun. But those who are seriously calling this thing "teh gheyz" aren't really having fun, obviously... but why? Why wouldn't they log in and chuckle at the banner? How detached from the lighthearted part of reality does one have to be to see that banner, and rather than think, "Hahahahahah. What the Hell is going on now?" instead think, "OMFG I HATE YU AWL1!!!"

Am I making sense with all that? I mean, why would it even be a big deal? What is it hurting? Same thing with the Y&BB, I still remember that we had serious complaints that we were "out to get" the little guy, or something. I mean, do we not all see how ridiculous that is, in hindsight? I mean, my main question here is "how hard is it to have a laugh or two?" Is it really neccesary to cry out every time something abnormal happens? Is it really that big of a thorn in everyone's side that something fun and irreverent goes down every now and again?

So, finally, I wasn't even a part of this until about 20 minutes before it happened. But I'm the most outspoken about it. Why? Because it's a waste of everyone's time and energy to make a big deal out of something so entirely trivial to everyone's life. Not only is it a waste of your time to actually, seriously fret and worry about something, but it's a waste of my own time when I have to post things like this to make everyone understand why something like this is silly. Like I said, if we can't have fun with life, what the Hell is the point?

It is definitely a virus, most notably, a worm that has named itself svchost.exe. It is highly dangerous. Also, you can go to http://www.geeksquad.com for a free virus scan, you can also do a google search on AVG Antivirus, that should pick it up. You can also download Ewido anti-spyware, that sometimes picks things up that others wouldn't.

I'd call Geek Squad, or someone similar immediately. It costs money, but at this point, you have little choice. Also, if you have something like Spyware Quake on your box, you should definitely get a professional.

Edit: If you search google for 'svchost.exe', you'll get a few results telling you how to search for the svchost.exe process, and where it should be located if it isn't a virus.

All Aboard the Underground - Great.

Antitetris - Great.

Blind Spot - Good/Great. Personal dislikes aside, this is Great.

Bloomberg - Great.

Catacombs - Good.

Cavern District - Excellent.

Cottage Factory - Odd, but Good.

Crashing the Life of the Party - Great.

Diamond Studded Pretzel - Okay. Just didn't really feel this one as much.

Earl of Tastyburger - Great.

Edgeraid - Good.

Elbow Room - Good.

Electric Rollerskates - Good, I keep trying to find a flow to this map, and it just isn't coming to me.

Everest on Steroids - I dunno, this one seemed to... anti-grow on me. Okay/Good.

Flagship Dynasty - Good/Great. I'm indecisive tonight.

Garden Heart - Poor. Too long, drawn out, and cluttered. Don't really like this one at all.

Hanging Garden - Okay. A bit better than Garden Heart, but it seems as though one of the trapdoors is missing entirely, And even the addition of that, the map plays to be too long and weird.

Live Through - Great. Much better version of my map, "The Burrows," although I am terrified of how the Chaingun changes will affect maps like this.

Mainframe Deathtrain - Great.

Ode to Puppy - Excellent.

Onboard the Mothership - Great.

One Step Down, Two steps up - Good.

Reversible Cannon - Okay.

Scramble - Great.

Set Phasers Phor Phun - Excellent. Very Metanetty.

Shocking First Bullet - Good.

Sidequestium: Excellent.

Spherical Playground - Good.

Spindrift - Okay.

Sterrance - Poor. I actually got around to playing this bad boy seriously today, and I finally got to the exit switch, where the gauss can't help but get you every time. If there was a map I'd not want in, this would unfortunately be it.

Stratevasion - Good.

The Clouds Forbid It - Great.

The Guardians - Okay. I'm not a Jumper-type guy.

The Vancrags - Excellent.

Theatrical - Excellent.

Tic Tac - Great.

Tile-High Club - Excellent.

Twisted Cities - I was so about to rate this one badly, but then I found a way to do it without resorting to some insane trick. This'n is good.

Ultracramp - Yeah, I get the name, but I don't even have time to land most of the time 'fore I can get the jump off. Beyond that, excellent. Not that I want you to do anything 'bout it, but it's something to note.

Urban Freeflow - Great.

Walkin' On Air - Excellent, despite my utter dislike for trapdoors.

This gave me an idea. An idea so great that my head would explode if I even began to know what I was talking about.

Anyway, the concept is simple. For future versions (N2 and beyond), a piece of 'gold' (Red gold, blue gold, whatever) that grants temporary invincibility. I think that this would function on a number of levels, but most particularly, it would open new *types* of levels to consideration. For instance:

[image lost: post-16-1154372392.png]

In otherwise impossible circumstances, the Ninja could do things that he couldn't do. Of course, making it a power-up would likely open the door for other types of powerups, as well, but in this instance, I believe, it would open the door to more mapmaking ideas and more complex types of levels. Getting a switch can only be implemented in so many ways. =D

Of course, Invincibility powerups have been suggested before, but the idea stemmed from the image above. The invincibility image would be that of a 'force field,' of sorts. Thus the merit of the re-dredging.

#209980 2 2006-08-01T18:47:05Z Kablizzy
I agree wholeheartedly. Their 0 and 10, 1 and 11 columns were blow-me-away, but as I went on, it seemed that they got too intricate for their own good. One thing that I was shocked about was how much I disliked Baraba's maps - I usually love his stuff, but this time around, he had nothing that wowed me. Take 06-0, for instance. It's a puzzle jumper, it took me 20 minutes just to figure out how to get into the middle area (Which is entirely my fault, but I digress).

All in all, they did a killer job, but a number of the levels, primarily Baraba's and Pariah's, aren't my style at all. Which is rather just a personal dislike of mine than anything that was wrong with the maps. Just didn't quite fit my tastes.

Mostly, the things that bugged me were aesthethic quirks - For instance, KA's maps were great fun, but aesthethic messes; Doors in half-positions (Not covering full areas) always bugged me, but beyond that pet peeve (As I know most people don't care), these were great.

krusch did a killer job on his maps, his 05 was a bit lacking for me, but I rather chalk that up to my playing those maps before, when they were in earlier, less-refined stages.

I noticed that they seemed to have a difficult time ramping up difficulty, and pulling all of the episodes into a line that would integrate them smoothly. Things like 04-0, I noted, should have been earlier, while things like 04-1 should have been later. I attribute this almost entirely to their rigid structure with which they assigned episodes. As individual levels, these were amazing, save for a map or two that would rather belong to NUMA; so, beyond a couple personal dislikes, this thing blew me away.

All in all, this is the best levelpack we've seen to date. So, publically, I'm going to rave over the pack, so as to generate further interest (And, as my little experiment yesterday showed, if I like something, the community likes something), and to get more people into playing the maps.

Quote: Atilla, August 21, 2006 08:04 am
The comparison to the word "retarted" "stupid" "crazy" and "queer" are not valid. All of them have an intrisic negative meaning. The word "gay" does not; indeed, it used to be very positive until it became associated with a group which is widely disliked and discriminated against. Using it as a derogatory term implies that to be gay is a bad thing. This also applies to the other terms, of course, but they are not discriminatory (well, except possibly for "retarded") because by their very definition, they are bad. Of course context matters. If two of your drunken friends (of the same sex, of course) are hugging each other, and you jokingly say you didn't realise they were gay, that's fine. However, using the word with intent to insult and deride is not.

Personally, I also find being referred to as "white" rather offensive. Why should I be lumped into a group based on the colour of my skin? It doesn't tell you anything about me, except that I'm vulnerable to sunburn. It is merely a form of prejudice based on an obvious physical attribute, even worse than the usual run of superficial judgments because it's also racist, not to mention often innacurate - many who identify as indigenous Australians (who are regarded as "black" by people who care about such things) are of caucasian appearance.

However, the comparison to the word 'dumb' has full validity.

This has nothing to do with this thread, but would you just listen to me for a little bit? See, I went to the local Yoshinoya today. Right. Yoshinoya. And the damn place was packed so full of people, I couldn't even find a seat. So I looked around a bit, and I found a sign that said "150 yen off". What the hell is wrong with you people? Are you idiots or something? Any other day you wouldn't even think of going to Yoshinoya, but if it's 150 yen off, you all flock in here? It's just 150 fucking yen! 150 yen! And you're bringing the kids too. Look at that, a family of four going to Yoshinoya. Con-fucking-gratulations. And now the guy's going, "All right! Daddy's going to order the extra-large!" Shit, I can't watch any more of this.

Yoshinoya should be fucking brutal. Two guys sit facing each other across a U-shaped table, and you never quite know if they'll suddenly just start a fight right there. It's stab-or-be-stabbed, and that's what so damn great about the place. Women and kids should stay the fuck away.

Well, I finally found a seat, but then the guy next to me goes, "I'll have a large bowl with extra gravy!". So now I'm pissed off again. Who the fuck orders extra gravy these days? Why are you looking so goddamn proud when you say that? I was gonna ask you, are you really going to fucking eat all that gravy? I wanted to fucking interrogate you. For about a fucking hour. You know what? I think you just wanted to say "extra gravy".

Now, take it from the Yoshinoya veteran. The latest thing among the Yoshinoya pros is this: Extra green onions. That's the ticket. A large bowl with extra onions, and egg. This is what someone who knows his shit orders. They put in more onions, and less meat. A large bowl with the raw egg, that's really fucking awesome. Now, you should know, if you keep ordering this, there's a risk employees might write you up. This really is a double-edged sword. I really can't recommend this for amateurs.

Hey, listen to me for a moment, a'ight? I don't care if it's not related to this thread. Just listen!

Yesterday, I went over to the Ristorante di Milano for a simple meal. Yes, THAT Italian restaurant, Ristorante di Milano.
But the whole restaurant was so crowded, I couldn't even find a seat for hours!
Then I saw a poster that said "Special offer! 12 discount".
I thought to myself... geez, that's so fucking amazing. You guys don't even normally visit Ristorante di Milano.
All you bastards came here just for that stupid-assed 12 discount.
Just for those 12 Euros. TWELVE FREAKIN' EUROS!!

Then I saw some parents & children. A family of four eating out at the Ristorante di Milano. Damn, so much for that bitch's home-cooked family feast.
Then one of the little brats said "Daddy's gonna order a large Bruschetta Fegatini".
I couldn't believe it! Uuuuuggh, are you out of your fucking mind!?
Shiiit, i'll pay you 12 just to move your stanky fat-ass out of a seat.
Dude, you just don't go to the Ristorante di Milano for that lala-oh-i'm-so-happy dinner bullshit.
It's where you pick a fist-fight with the fucking guy sitting across 'yah in that U-shaped table.
Kill or be killed. Heh... now that's the kinda shit I like.
Ladies, kids, stand back... 'cuz everything's gonna get FUCKED UP NOW.

After waiting for ages, I finally found an empty seat. But then, the guy next to me ordered by saying "A large Neopolitan pizza with a LOTTA' pepperoni".
Dude, that just pissed me off even more. Shit, you just don't say "lotta' pepperoni" nowadays, ya' freaking bastard.
How the fuck can you say "lotta' pepperoni" with that "oh, i'm so fucking cool, hur-hur-hur..." look!?!?
Damn, I was THIS CLOSE to standing in front of his face and yelling "DO YOU EVEN LIKE EATING THAT MUCH FUCKIN' PEPPERONI!?"
For a freaking hour, I was THIS CLOSE to doing that.
Shit, I bet you just wanted to use the words "lotta' pepperoni" out loud. Wow, you're so clever.

Dude, you gotta be like ME. See, now I know what's "all that" in the Ristorante di Milano.
What's cool right now to say is "Pennette con Ricotta & Melanzane". That's it!
You see now, a large pasta serving with aubergines & ricotta is what the hardcore Ristorante di Milano freaks eat. Like ME.
Saying "Pennette con Ricotta & Melanzane" means that won't get a pizza, but they put a WHOLE MESS of pasta.
Mmmmm... a lotta pasta, now THAT'S what I call a meal.
But anywhoo... ordering that is kinda' like a double-edged sword. Cuz' then the waiters might notice you the next time you come by.
So yeah, I can't reccomend this to noobs.
For you, just go order a Prosciutto e Melone al Ventaglo. That's as far as you can go, you know what i'm sayin'?

I began this project last night, and we'll see how well it holds up. I'm looking to do twenty-five levels a night, for four nights. All of these maps were done within the past 24 hours, and I'm hoping I can do this three more times before I burn out; We'll see how this holds up.

I'd also like for nine other people to participate, doing twenty-five levels a night, for four nights, after I am done with my four nights. When forty nights have passed, we should have, between us all, 1000 levels, in a gigantic, non-episodic levelpack. With that said, here are my first twenty-five; I'll be taking the first nine people to post in this thread as additional participants, and further participants will be standby participants, in the instance that a person doesn't finish their levels on time. In the instance that someone doesn't fill their requirement, the maps that they have submitted will stay in, but further submissions will not be accepted. I'm not even sure if I will meet the requirement of twenty-five maps per night, but if we can do this, it will be a huge addition to the community.

If anyone is unable to commit the time and finish the twenty-five maps per 24-hour period, that person will be ejected from the project, and the next person in line will be taken. The order of mapmaking will follow the order which you sign up, and will be added to the list as I can. Please keep in mind that twenty-five maps per night for four nights is huge, and please consider it carefully before participating.

I mean, for instance, I eat at the same place almost every day I work. Good food, cheap enough, fattens me up nice. So, the other day, I come back into the store with one of the cups, and he notices it. He says to me, "God damn, is that all you fucking eat?" in one of the most insulting tones I've heard.

Do you see that? Can you guys grasp what goes on there? So, on the same tangent, I tell you guys that I'm pretty middle-of-the-road, and then you come along and tell me I'm not? Upon the basis of the thought that you haven't personally analysed the data yourself? It's hard to grasp, man, I just can't get my head around stuff like that. That's why I go off like that, it happens all the time - I present people with evidence, I ask people questions to answer, and it all goes completely ignored, it's infuriating. Time after time, the most pertinent thing I have to say on a topic is the first thing to be "conveniently overlooked," and it gets to me.

And sure, we'll go down this road (Notice how I actually take up challenges people offer, everyone?).

First, I view some facets of Protectionist doctrine to be good - Mostly because it can prevent further outsourcing in exchange for those workers here in dire need of jobs, particularly at a time when the economy isn't exactly booming. Not a terribly big fan of the WTO, but hey, it does its job, I suppose.

Second, I enjoy the idea of Small-Government conservatism, and I think the Federal Government should loosen its grip a bit on the country, and leave in more room for local- and state- governments to fight in.

Third, I am very much into an assertive role with foreign countries, and I think that certain types of assertiveness with other world leaders can far easier breed a global community (Paired with the correct answers) than the isolationist viewpoint.

Fourth, I'm more of an Institutional Conservative. I rather like the idea of slow-change and turning things over at a ready pace, instead of barreling through things as a maniac. In doing so, whether the government ends up being more right- or left-leaning? I could care less. Mostly because of my adherence to objective thought.

Fifth, I am a man of traditional American values. I fully believe that a moralistic way of living is *the* way of living, and the Liberal antithesis to this (One of greater freedoms for citizens) is more or less balderdash. I think that the dominant forces in Western Society today are trying to unmake what our country was founded upon, and the traditions and institutions herein are rather sacred.

Sixth, I am fervently opposed to drug legalization, and I think that things such as alcohol should fall back into Prohibition.

Seventh, I am considered a Fiscal Conservative, as I dislike excessive government debt, and see a large National Debt as what will be our ultimate downfall.

And finally for tonight, I'm a big fan of compassionate conservatism, at its core. I think that it's noble to help countries in need, and I fully support the idea of Workfare, despite my own critical analysis of it. Mostly because welfare does indeed breed a poor work-ethic, and it does perpetuate a culture of poverty, which I'm opposed to.

And really, I think that the country's societal aspect is indeed becoming too Liberal. But at the same time, I think that the Republican party is way, way too conservative. There's more intricate stuff, and my position on things like Gay Marriage and abortion stays at a middle-ground, even though I refuse to take the conservative stand on them, because it is so militant. With that said, while there are a number of conservative ideals that I adhere to, there are at least an equal number that I don't. And those that I don't, I fight just as I fight those liberal ideals that I disagree with (See my debate with Foxhunter, October '04, I believe).

Quote: Black Sheep Boy, October 02, 2006 01:41 pm
My story starts, like so many others, with a girl.

An actress, actually. And an extremely good one, who's starred in quite a few Australian films, had many guest roles in well- known Australian television series, and is currently filming for one of the main roles of an arthouse short film which will be shown in a lot of festivals.

I'll make this brief and to the point- I have never met a girl like this. She is extraodinary in every way... I cannot describe how many cliche's she fills my heart with. I want to say "I love her", but this is... too large a comment for a 17 year old to make. And yet I constantly find myself thinking that I might, or that I do.

And this girl, in the last two films she's been in- and in the one she's filming at the moment- is making out with a large variety of guys. 1 in the last film, as well as a sex scene (which didn't actually involve much physical closeness- very artsy stuff) and 2 in this one. One of which unzips her jacket and engages in some on- screen fondling of... well. You can figure out the specifics for yourself.

And I understand the distinction between acting and, in real life, 'feeling'. The difference between experiancing emotions in the context of the stage (think of Stavislavski here) and in real life. And I understand that acting is a large part of her life, and I truly don't want to make it awkward or unpleasent for her- or to make her feel guilty for doing something that's such a large part of her life. And I've talked about this with her, too- for hours, just tonight. We got rather deep and philosophical about the whole issue, and I realised again how great it is I can connect with this person in such a way, and on such a level, in which I have never connected with any other person.

But here's my problem.

We've discussed it. A lot. And... it shouldn't cheapen kissing. It's not the action which carries the romantic connotations, it's the intent behind it. It means nothing on the screen, when it's directed and you have to rotate slightly to stay in the light- I understand this. Intellectually. And yet I find myself not wanting to kiss her in the same way as I did before. It's the same act, but the act is meaningless. Only the intent and the feeling behind it counts for anything.

And I don't want to think and feel in this way. That nothing is real, nothing is meaningful, and- professionaly- a person can make out with another and it means nothing. I don't WANT lips, tounges, and saliva to mean nothing. I don't want holding her and kissing her and holding hands to mean- on a physical level- nothing. I don't want everything in my life to be reduced to the more abstract concepts of intent and motivation and feelings. And yet this is the mindframe in which I find I have to think. One which I hate.

I hate being stood up whenever her agent calls- turning up to the location of our planned dates only to recieve a delayed text message saying she can't make it. (Which, thankfully, has only happened once.) I hate planning to meet her and see her and then her being prevented from seeing me, after I've turned down invitations with friends and caused them to grudge my devotion to the few times in which I can see this certain girl. I hate barely seeing her- sometimes once a week, sometimes twice, sometimes going for longer when she's needed a lot for filming. I hate not being around her, and I hate being prevented from seeing her, and I hate that she's so busy and we can't just be normal dating adolescents, lost in eachother and the rush of hormones.

I hate the constant looming threat that she'll get a really great role that'll mean she'll have to move overseas or interstate. She came relatively close to one, and we decided that if she were to get it she would go, I would support her, and we would keep a long distance relationship for the 9 months she would be away. And, whenever I considered the possibility of her leaving (which is more or less a constant, low level threat,) I felt like death.

And I hate myself for hating all of this. I wish I were fine with it, and I wish I were more supportive and able to just continue on, fine and happy. It's not that I'm not jealous of the other guys, and I certainly don't feel threatened. And the girl in question has told me, several times, that she'd hate it if our roles were reversed and I were the guy forced to make out with a multitude of girls for my work.

It's not an issue which is festering inside me. We're open. We've talked about it, a lot, in discussions which keep on veering towards the deeply philosophical. We understand eachother- which really is amazing, considering the depths of the issue we've explored.

And yet.

As much as I... think I might love her, I do hate all of this. I'd think that she's not the right sort of person for me, but she's insert pseudonym here! And if you knew her, you would understand that there truly is no other person anything like her. She's so different from anybody else I've ever met- funny, deep, beautiful, and it sounds like I'm reeling off a list of major selling points. But it's not that she's great with the selling points and 'top of the range'. She's insert pseudonym here, which manages to make her the most important thing in my life in a way nobody else could ever be.

She's the most important thing in my life. And also the most painful.

I suppose I know better than anyone what you're going through. I couldn't imagine the little lady kissing someone else, it tore me up just knowing that she had to hug another guy (She's taking acting classes as we speak, and had some scenes like this). She even refused to kiss a guy in a scene she was doing, and I admire her for that.

I... eh, that's not what this is about. Anyway, long-distance relationships are hard. Right now, I'm in almost the same situation as you are - I get to see the little lady once a week, once a month, sometimes more often, sometimes less. And it kills me. It kills me that we can't have our life, it kills me that we can't be ourselves, and whenever we want to meet, and can't, it just destroys me.

And now, the little lady is going overseas, and it's going to be hard. It's going to be a Hell of a hard time, and I wonder if she will find someone else. And she wonders the same. Absence makes the heart grow fonder, though, and we have promised our lives to each other. And that is the key. I know that I want to spend the rest of my life with her, and she knows that she wants to spend the rest of her life with me, and the only thing that is really standing in our way is her trust issues. She doesn't believe that I am faithful, and that makes things hard.

Anyway, enough of me. The important part is to keep in whatever touch you can, and be sure that feelings haven't changed since last you talked. Be sure to set aside time to actually talk about these things, ask her, "How are you feeling about this," ask her how she feels about you, about the relationship, and so on. Maybe that's bad advise, I don't know. Just speaking from my own perspective.

As much as you love her, you seem like you're unsure of where you're going. Are you planning on something more serious? Are you afraid of losing her?

#237052 12 2006-10-04T03:42:30Z Kablizzy
What I did with Vehemence (Plug) is while I was creating the levels, I would watch TV, and I would pick out a word or two from whatever program I was watching.

For instance, the Colbert Report's "The Word" just had "Stephen Thinks it's a documentary" on the screen.

He just said "Science and Faith," "In Theory," "Separating Fact From Policy," and "11-Dimensional Multiverse."

All of which are decent names. Beyond that, think indie. Vehemence stuff like "Versa" (Named after Vice Versa, without the first part) makes for a good name. Also, a play on words such as "Logical Phallus-y." has always done well for me in the past.

Another good way to take a name is to pick out map features, and name it like that. Another of my Vehemence maps is called "Double Scepter" because it looks like a scepter, with two heads.

Finally, things that make fun of map names, such as "This is not a map name." make for fantastic names.

Hope that helps.

Quote: iangb, October 09, 2006 02:16 pm
Anyway... on-topic. I don't think that making an initial assumption based on past experience is an act of faith.
For example, I assume that Dave's fridge contains food. What faith is used then other than that my past experiences with fridges are an accurate guide to my future experiences with fridges? I could be wrong in my assumption - it is impossible to tell the contents of Dave's fridge. But my assumption is not based on faith.
But would you be willing to say you're certain that my fridge contains food. If you're not willing to say you're certain and would claim "Dave's fridge probably contains food", I can see how you reached that assumption through reason rather than faith. If you claim that you are certain that my fridge contains food, I'd assume you're reaching that conculsion with some degree of faith.

The truth is, I refuse to examine the inside of my fridge, fearing that when I do the fridge will not contain any food. For the time being, I'll just forgo examining the fridge and assume that the fridge both contains and does not contain food. Which means I should both go grocery shopping and forget about shopping and instead go to the bar. No one examine me for the next few hours.

Just as a bit of an aside with the "Dave's Fridge" analogy, there is yet another way of looking at it. There could be *items* in Dave's fridge, but those items may not be edible (read: baking soda, a stop sign, fruit cake, and so on. And no, fruit cake is not edible). Draw what comparisons you will.

#239982 27 2006-10-12T10:06:39Z Kablizzy
Not if it begins to impose upon another person's right to not choke. Particularly when it's a hygenic choice on the part of the non-bather. If it were something where, say, they couldn't under any circumstances bathe... well...

Anyway, things that are 'rights' must also be isolated as 'personal rights,' lest we fall into murder being a 'life choice,' or something, y'know?

Edit: And particularly when, as Suki said, it is something that is easily fixed, and due entirely to his own 'negligence.' Were it a medical condition, it would be entirely different, but in this case, I side with the law protecting the "TAKE A BATH" portion.

Edit: Also, such things as being black, being homosexual, or practicing atheism aren't things that occur in the same vein as a foul odor. See, being black isn't something that *can* be attributed as offensive. It doesn't do anything to anyone else. But when something (Such as a smell) is forced upon you, then it steps over that narrow line. Same thing with Atheism. Unless the guy starts screaming out, "There is no God!!!" over and over again in the restaurant, it's not actually infringing upon anyone's... well, anyone's anything. And even then, it falls more under the 'disturbance' category than one of idealogical difference.

In addition, being black, homosexual, or Atheist aren't things that can be *fixed*. They are things that are inherent to a given person. You can't simply tell someone to stop being an Atheist, or to stop being gay, or to stop being black. You can, however, tell someone to take a bath. It is hardly an infringement or inconvenience upon that person, whereas asking someone to change their entire belief structure or color of their skin would be.
#240124 42 2006-10-12T19:52:13Z Kablizzy
Quote: Dave, October 12, 2006 12:06 pm
I never threw black into the mix. However, you can tell someone to stop being atheist or gay. It was done all the time, way back when. Until the 1970's, homosexuality was even classified as a mental illness. In fact, there was a time when a person could ask someone to leave their place of business if they thought the person was gay. An entire town could be sexists against this person until he changed his behavior. After all, behavior--regardless of what you think--is changable. Any type of behavior can be assumed to be offensive to some. At what point does behavior which can be deemed "offensive to some" warrant legislation?

I agree that it's a fine line. I just think that legislation on anti-smoking laws opens the proverbial door for people to pick which types of behaviors are deemed offensive and decide which among those they should outlaw. I'd hate to see the day where two lesbians aren't legally allowed to make out in front of me on the flight to Topeka last week after they figured everyone was asleep but I was totally awake and watching them and surreptitiously trying to maneuver my hand into my jeans while the dude next to me reclined with his headphones on blaring John Cougar Mellencamp's "Wild Nights" loud enough that I could faintly hear it over the roar of the left engine which I was unfortunately seated beside. Also, I don't think second-hand smoke is as dangerous as it is made out to be. Agencies spend a lot of money trying to alter statistics in such a way that it benefits their cause. "Jackie died of lung cancer. Her husband smoked. Therefore, Jackie died of secondhand smoke." Ignore all the other factors in the generation of this data and you have another statistic to add to your collections.

Anti-smoking legislation is just a way for chewing gum companies to shore up profits. Yeah. You heard me. Is it just coincidence that Wrigley's is the highest contributer to the passive smoking administration within the EPA? I think not. Consider these figures next time you see someone chewing some delicious Wrigley's Spearmint gum, instead of smoking a cigarette.

Very true, but is Atheism simply and solely classified as a behaviour? Is homosexuality defined solely by the act of boning another guy? See, with such things as Atheism, particularly in this instance, can't be classified solely as the behaviours that you practice. Frankly, you can never throw a person out of a restaurant for their lack of faith because first, I would have a difficult time finding an example of a setting where an Atheist's behaviour was sufficient to get them thown out. And secondly, Throwing that person out for disorderly conduct would more likely be the reason for removing them than for 'practicing Atheism.'

Same thing with Homosexuality. Viewing two men kissing does no harm to anyone, physically or mentally. By those standards, lawmakers would be quite foolish to pursue legislation to prevent gay couples from kissing in public. So, yes, while homosexuality was considered a mental illness, that seems to point more strongly towards the human tendency to make horrible, misinformed decisions rather than towards the idea that anyone can ban anyone for anything. So long as such legislation was defined correctly, I fail to see a problem. For instance, the only reason that smoking legislation opens the door to other types of legislation along the same lines is because we, as humans, tend to be illogical about... well, just about everything. It's hard to find a person who is completely objective; one would have to be born into the Amazon jungles to even near societal objectivity in their decisions, and even then, there would come a time when that person's viewpoint were skewed in some way.

So, it's not so much an arbitrary definition of which behaviours are deemed offensive as it would be an actual, rigid definition of which behaviours are actually imposing upon others, and which of those behaviours stem from a deeper feeling, belief, or set of moral codes. Certainly, homosexuality stems from a deeper feeling of attraction for one of the same gender. Atheism stems from a personal religious belief. And I have a hard time finding a similar comparison with not bathing. Now, of course, cultural factors could indeed come into play there, as I know that there are some cultures that don't bathe, or at least, not terribly often. Thus, that would have to be a factor in any legislation that would go down. But so long as it would become a legal requirement to maintain a certain level of hygiene in X, Y, or Z settings, then I don't much see a problem.

The only problem that I do see here is an unwillingness from all parties to actually sit down and rationally think about things, and base legislation upon what is right and wrong. If folk on Capitol Hill and in Big Business would stop having hidden agendas and start trying to better our country for the sake of bettering our country, I think this wouldn't be much of a problem.

McP: The problem with being nude in public is that we, as a country, have established laws against it, because we, as a country, believe that it is infringing upon others. Not sure where I'm going with that.

#242773 15 2006-10-18T05:00:13Z Kablizzy
Quote: mc_george, October 18, 2006 04:08 am
Quote: Kablizzy, October 18, 2006 01:14 pm
I don't know enough of your maps to make a decision. But the real question here is, "Who cares what we think?" Make your maps for you, not for us.
I think it might just be me, but don't we make maps for people to enjoy? And not solely for ourselves. I know that I thoroughly enjoy playing my own maps, and am happy when others find them fun.
But what happens when others don't find them fun? Threads like these go up, and people quit. In my time here, I've probably seen two hundred of these threads, and it's only led me to believe that the correct reason to map is not for other people, but rather to map for the sake of mapping. In doing so, you eliminate the possibility of being disappointed. If you make maps for yourself, and for the sake of mapping, then people will enjoy them that much more, because of your love for making the map. That's how I became a good mapmaker. I began to make maps for myself, instead of for pride, and people, all of a sudden, began to like my maps. So, if I'm happy with my maps, I have no reason to leave when other people don't, but if other people like my maps, then it's just an added bonus.

This map is the perfect example of something I like to call "Liberal Art". This is that blank canvass. This is a failure. Some people may say that the simplicity is astonishing, and that it speaks to them on a primal level. Quote: "Kablizzy's Manifesto"
[C]onsider the following; I read an article not too long ago in the newspaper that said something along the lines of this; If you have money in your pocket, and money in a bank account somewhere, you are among the top 2% of the worlds wealthy. Of course, my response to this was simple disbelief. Honestly, I cant fathom that half of America would be so poor as to not have money in their pocket, and money put away somewhere. But it happens. This means, that of the 6 billion people in the world, I am technically richer than all but 5.9 Billion. So, the point of the article was that I should be happy that I am in the top 2% of the worlds rich, right? My answer to that, of course, is a resounding, Hell no! There is no joy in knowing that I, being as poor as I am, am somehow better off than almost the entire population of the entire planet upon which we live? Sit and ponder that for a moment. You, who are reading this now, are probably in the same position as I am, or better, and according to the article, which was entitled Count Your Blessings, would have you believe that you should be thankful every day for what you have. Which, of course, we all should, to an extent. However, knowing how hard that I have had it in life, just to think that 98% of the worlds population is worse off than I am indeed is a miserable outlook. There are Chief Executive Officers of companies here in the U.S. whose severance packages are worth more than what entire countries earn in a year. There is something terribly wrong in that. So, no, I am not happy that my meager little life is better than everyone elses. I am distressed that everyone elses life is worse - actually worse - than my own.

So, this year, instead of simply being thankful, let's do something. Make a donation, whether it be to the salvation army, or to another charity, or, Hell, directly to a poor Pakistani family, let's do something this year.

I'll only post one thing, since I'm on a short time limit here, but as to that link;

Read the title for me. Okay, lemme stop you there. What's the agenda of that article? To prove that God exists. What's the means to do so? Causality and Entropy. Now, which of the two notions in the article was presented first (As the basis), and which is presented as the means? If you can answer those for me, I think that you'll come to a very simple and clear answer.

But in order to prove that there is a higher power, one must assume that said higher power exists to begin with, because we have zero (Lemme repeat that a couple times, for emphasis) - None, nada, nothing, zilch - in this universe that points to anything except what is in the Universe. By that same logic, I can say that Causality and Entropy prove that there is an alternate dimension, or that this "Deity" is a plate of linguine. The problem with attempting to prove that there is a God is the same thing with proving that unicorns exist - Because there is nothing in the Universe to point whatsoever in any way to this thing that we call "God."

So, posting that is no better than posting "Evolution proves that there is no God!" Because that's just as false. You cannot, under any circumstances that I've been shown, in all the years that I've debated, prove that there is a God without first the notion of God. Thus, if I go on, oh, I don't know, let's say... A crusade to prove that there is a Flying Spaghetti Monster that rules our universe, by the logic of Entropy and Causality, the thought has exactly as much validity as the notion of a God ruling the universe.
