Quote: macaddict_17, 2006-11-29T01:58:24Z
Obviously, the theory of evolution tries to explain the world's existence based on the premise that there is no God.

Actually, evolution does no such thing. Evolution is localized to metamorphosis of species, and has very little to do with the world's existence. Not only that, but there is no premise that "there is no God," in the theory of evolution. It is based upon what we can observe, and solely based upon what we can observe. By that logic, the theory of evolution must also be based upon the premise that unicorns do not exist. It must also then contain the premise that there is no such thing as an alternate dimension. It must also state that Heaven does not exist. It then must also state that there are no ghosts, and go further to state that the paranormal doesn't exist. Does Evolution do any of that? No, not at all. It isn't concerned with the idea of a God, it's only concerned with what we do know. It doesn't matter what we don't know, what we *do* know is this, this, and this, and from that evidence and nothing else, we have drawn this conclusion.

See, here's my problem, though. It's not evidence for a higher power or intelligent design. Why? Well, because it's the same exact proof for *Looks up at scythe's signature* Well, for Calvin and/or Hobbes being supreme commanders of our universe. The remainder of the argument is sound, but in order to do this:

Therefore,
C. There is a God

You MUST have a premise assuming that there is a God. Otherwise, there is a logical disconnect, because the conclusion fails when done again with, as I said, a plate of Linguine. It has exactly the same foundation for saying, "Therefore, squids that exist outside of the universe are purple and no other color, ever!"

So, even if it were evidence, it requires something else to link the "evidence" to God and only God. Which is why it needs to be a part of the argument, and thus, has to assume that there is a God to begin with. Even if you go through the logical process, and provide sufficient evidence, it still has to be shown that there is a God, and that said God is a cause. Because, otherwise, as I said, the plate of linguine is suddenly in the running for creator of the Universe.

On Science: Would you then also criticize Yahtzee for not taking into account Monopoly's rules? Of course not.

Science deals with what we can observe.
We can't observe God.
Phase 3. Profit.

Have you seen scientists that believe in God? Absolutely. Because Science doesn't care if there's a God or not. Evolution states what we think happened. Period. As I said, there's no premise that says, "There is no God, therefore..." Ever, anywhere ever, ever, ever in Science, ever. The theories are numbers and ideas, and I will resign my position as Admin here at Metanet if you can find those five words in any Scientific Theory that has been but forth in a premise. Not just in things that Scientists say, but in the theories themselves.

Quote: blue_tetris, November 29, 2006 10:48 am
Make a webcomic.  Join the IRC.  C'mon, man, the forums are an end unto themselves.  They don't demand that you serve a purpose.

Exactly. Egg-freakin'-zactly.

See, that's the thing, guys. Everyone is wanting to be "a part" of something that already exists, but if you look at the folk who are in those positions, we are the ones who have pioneered things around the forum. And, of course, all of the mods here are kind of "big" personalities, and we all have our claims to fame, but if you think about it, this... cabal, of sorts, that we've put together... we've formed for the sole purpose of bettering the community. The Legacy Team began as just a map-pack group, and look at the impacts it's had on the community.

But my point is that you don't have to be a maximo or a Dave or an Arachnid with some huge ballzerko idea to blow everyone from their seats. Any contribution helps. I respect anyone who has put on and finished a contest here, all of the RPGs that have gone down, the projects and ideas, we're all a part of the same community, and no one gets left behind.

But something that bugs me a bit; Dave and LV and KA put on InsomNicon last week. And 10 people showed up to do it. Out of, what, 5000 members? Granted, most are inactive, but where were you guys then? The IRC is free, and we always love to have more people there on a regular basis. I mean, Hell, I didn't even plan on participating because of my schedule, but I jumped on IRC, and I saw what fun everyone was having - The atmosphere, the camaraderie, and I said, "Hell, why not?"

I mean, InsomNicon, as tiny as it was, had a monstrous impact upon me - Personally, I can't wait for the next one to come about, because, while I was sitting in the IRC channel, and sitting on Vent, every time Dave and LV and KA would go into the private channel to grade, or to discuss the next round, or every time a spectator would come into #InsomNicon, it was just a party atmosphere. When that clock hit on the hour, everyone frenzied. We all laughed, we all groaned, some dropped out, some rejoiced. But that's what it's all about.

I mean, even when we did the Hall of Fame last year - About half way in, we had 4 votes in. Four!! No one took any initiative to vote or participate, so what'd we do? We started a carpet-bombing campaign. We hit up the IRC topic, and we started PMing people to get their votes in. And y'know? 92% of our total votes came *from* that campaign.

And not to advocate bugging the Hell out of people, because if a Noob came in here, and started PMing people to "checx out mi map pacck!" ... Well, another story for another day.

But hey, Webhosting comes cheaply. The N wiki needs a Hell of a lot of work. We need collaborators for upcoming Legacy projects. We need some of these subforums to get more active. The TMMLT was a fantastic idea, and I'd like to see that go again once this one is through with stricter guidelines, and I'm sure that sketch is gonna need help with that. What ever happened to the NEHS? Do we have any artists in the community that feel unrecognized? Did everyone notice how that Squid guy came into the community and wowed everyone with his 3d animation? I'm about to piss myself right now, just thinking about how cool that's gonna be.

Maybe someone should take up Ninja Skyboat Racing Xtreme. What a freakin' cool concept that was. Maybe someone should collab a gigantic webcomic to rival The Real N. mascote went and compiled an entire program so that people could enjoy The Real N offline, and conveniently.

Beyond that, Web Riddler is almost dead. So are Suki's religious Debate forums. Taking up the reigns at either of those places would be a big step to helping the sites that we're connected to.

There hasn't been a good highscoring contest in a while. It doesn't have to have the NTTS logo to be successful. Perhaps something that returns to the roots of the NTTS would be groovy. Same with Nedcon. The best seasons of that are long past, but that doesn't mean that something old can't resurface from the ashes, y'know?

I was telling KA and LV this evening, that I see a new Golden Age of Metanet coming, and soon. We have a stronger community now than we've ever had; Numa leadership may be changing; The Real N is flourishing, every day, people like LimiterRelease and that squid-dude are exploding onto the scene with a vengeance, and old-timers like TDL and Suki have returned.

I can feel the air when I come to the forum, it's very reminiscent of the early days, what you guys all call "The Golden Age" of Metanet. This is precisely the time where leaders come out - This is where old fogies like me kinda fade into the background, and where the newer guys take the spotlight. This is your community, fellas, and it's precisely what you make of it. BWD's mp3 station was a brainstorm and a half, and I know the rest of you can either come up with something, or revive something that has since been forgotten.

Hell, get together with the 8 biggest people on the forum, and do something up huge. Split the cost of a website, and... I dunno, do what you can do with it. Talk to one of us, we're more than happy to help (And, of late, we've been getting bombarded with requests for X, Y, and Z). Get together with 8 *random* people on the forum, and do something. Start a fansite for N. Host N art somewhere. Go take a ceramics class, and sculpt a little, Grey-clay Ninja. Heck, make a whole collage. Make the collage out of Legos. If I hadn't given mine away, I'd totally do that shit. That'd rock some faces in. Plan something for Robotology; Legacy already has three or four things planned for when it hits. Hell, even something so small as logging into Questionswap, and asking "Have you heard about Metanet, or their Popular freeware game, N?" does the trick.

What I'm getting at, is when you feel lost, and feel like you don't have a place, that's precisely the time to *carve* yourself a place. Twist: I can see you running a contest, you have an assload of posts, you're recognized by everyone, and if you wouldn't doubt yourself through these topics, you'd have a boatload of influence. That's one thing I learned about myself, just before I joined the forums, and that was this notion of confidence. Why am I where I am? Why am I one of the most influential people on the Internet? Because I know that I can be. I've had random visions lately about being President of the United States, and as much as it frightened me, I got this funky enlightened transcendent thing where, in my mind, that shit was *possible*, man. How crazy does that seem now? Fuggin' insane. But at the time, it was just a hand's width away. And a lot of you are a lot younger than I am, and you've got nothing but time to make a name for yourselves. Hell, if I'd have had access to the Internet 13 years ago, I'd own everything by now. I'd be buying and selling chunks of the Internets for 100% profit, and Ted Turner would be my personal chamber-maid. So now is your time, man. And the same goes for every last one of you. In fact, I'ma give you guys the password to the Unfathomable Secret:

Vestige559

Keep all that in mind, read the topic, and do what suits you best.

***Marked***

I think this, right here, is most people's problem with theists. It's not really the Bible, or the idea of a God, because if we could all just co-exist, I don't believe, Obby believes, whatev. We still can chill on Vent and shoot the shit with each other.

But when you cross that boundary, and say, "My reality is the only reality," that turns people off. And I think that's what most non-believers are really crusading against. Science doesn't say, "My reality is the only reality," but rather, it says, "This is what we, as Homo Sapiens, are able to observe, and these are the processes we use to go about validating these obervations." It doesn't pretend to have the answers, it just says, "Well, this is what we've got at the moment." And, since it doesn't pretend to have one formulaic solution to the Universe, then I don't see how you can begin to argue against something that shapes our world. Particularly not something so massive as Science. Shit, the reason that you can even be here, sitting at a computer, typing, is entirely because of Science. Not because there's a piece of God in the computer screen, but because electricity works. 100% true, it works. You can't disprove that. But the problem comes when you say, "My way is the only way, and if you don't see it my way, you'll burn!" No one's going to respect you in the least for that. And I really, truly think that most of us who are fed up with religion are fed up with it for this very reason.

And beyond that, if you're the only one that understands the truth, exuberance, how come your last post is 100% false? Christianity began around 70 A.D. Period. It has existed now for 1936 years or so. Period. What's that? Truth? Understanding? It seems as though you have neither. How can you feel so infallible, anyway? How can your faith be 100% true to everyone, the world over, with no exceptions? Christianity has to be false, at least in some part, if not solely for the existence of other religions, but for the inherent idea that the religion was not only preceded by others, but preceded by others who claimed their own ideas to be just as infallible. Were the pagan Gods of early Babylon as "true" as your religion? When you get to Heaven, if Marduk were sitting there to judge you, where would your truth be? Why are you so sure that Marduk and Ishtar aren't waiting to judge your folly? Based upon human reality? The reason that you are wrong isn't because you're Christian, the reason you're wrong is because you claim immortality. You claim to be infallible. And no human can ever be infallible. That is a fundamental, universal truth. And considering your age, I would imagine that you've made many mistakes in your life, and you've committed many sins already, and that you will do so many more times before your death. So tell me, how can you be infallible?

Y'know, maximo is probably the most religious person I know. And he's a brother to me. I would die for that man, because despite his belief, he doesn't point at me and call me a heathen, he points at me and calls me a brother in return. Because he and I share something that transcends God vs. Big Bang - We are both humans, and that's all we can know. He believes in God because it works for him, and he knows that. But, more importantly, he knows not to put forth something like, "God is teh troof! Science is teh falsss!" because he holds a fundamental understanding that the two aren't at odds. To him, God is tangible, because of the things that have occurred in his life. And he knows that, to me, God has been this intangible, distant figurehead. And that's fine with both of us. But he knows that God can't be proven, just as I know that God can't be disproven. And he knows just the same that the Big Bang may very well have happened, but he also knows that just because the Big Bang may have occurred doesn't mean that there is no God; the two ideas can co-exist nicely. He knows that evolution could be entirely true, and that if there is indeed a God, that anything is possible. And I know these things, too. And not because of where he or I come from, but because there is a certain, basic truth; We don't know, we can't know, and the only true position is one where we do what's right for us, at that moment, and what will help us help others. So, claiming that you're the only one that knows the truth is no way to debate, but beyond that, it's no way to be a human being. We both share the common knowledge that, as humans, who think and breathe, and who exist in this place where we both are, whoever we are, and whatever caused us, that we share more commonality than difference. And *that* is the only "Truth," exuberance. "I'm right, you're wrong" is something that a 16-year old would say. It's something that someone who hasn't even yet experienced a small sliver of what life has to offer would say.

And that's why Obby can now debate well. Because he too understands these things. He believes in God; I do not. So, to me, by stating that you're entirely right, and that I'm entirely wrong, just immediately invalidates anything productive that you may have to say.

It's funny, if I put up a thread right now, asking, "What does Kablizzy believe?" I bet that not a single one of you would get it anywhere nearly right. Because my belief system is built from the ground-up. And I don't think in all of these debates, that I've ever divulged more than a small portion of what I personally believe.

So, no, you're not wrong because Christianity is false, you're wrong because you claim to know that you're right. The most powerful knowledge is the knowledge that "The only thing I truly know is that I don't know."

I then went on to ask him if he thought that band was the greatest band ever. His answer was 'yes.' I then asked him to do the same with me. He asked me what my favourite band was, and I replied in kind. He then asked me if I thought that band was the greatest band ever. My answer? 'No.' My friend was baffled by this. He asked me, "Why wouldn't you believe that your favourite band is the greatest in the world?"

And the reason is this: Solely because it is in my tastes to like a given band or a style of music has no bearing upon whether or not my favourite band is the greatest band ever. I did a little experiment recently, and I want to share it with everyone. I asked a friend of mine what his favourite band was. He replied. I then went on to ask him if he thought that band was the greatest band ever. His answer was 'yes.' I then asked him to do the same with me. He asked me what my favourite band was, and I replied in kind. He then asked me if I thought that band was the greatest band ever. My answer? 'No.' My friend was baffled by this. He asked me, "Why wouldn't you believe that your favourite band is the greatest in the world?"

#265479 12 2006-12-06T10:47:37Z Kablizzy
My worldview? It's pretty complex.

Worldview Name: Empirical Agnostic Theist, Objective Observationalist, Secular Pantheist/Nontheist (Self-term: Universalist)

Foreword: First off, I most readily classify myself as a Non-Theist (Formerly Anti-Theist, prior to that, strict Atheist), due simply to the depth of each term not fully classifying who I am or what I believe. Although, it isn't quite as simple as that, I do believe in something, although I'm not sure what that something is, and that's where the Pantheist/Theist ideals come from. Tonight, I think I've done a halfway fair job of classifying a part of what I believe in the above, but calling myself a strict Universalist seems to encompass enough of the smattering of my ideals so as to provide it with credence as a simple tag. Good freakin' lord. As extensive as this is, it's only scratching the surface. With that said, enjoy, and if you have any questions, feel free to ask.

Nature of God: The nature of a deity cannot currently be known. Separation of belief and observation should be key in how we live. What we can observe isn't any more truth than what we believe, but what we believe involves faith, and should be separated from what we can observe, as what we can observe is tangible to us in the moment, and the six senses that we can use (I consider thought a sense) are the only ways that we can perceive the world around us, and thus, are the best tools that we, as humans, can use to do so.

I consider myself marginally more enlightened than the average human, by my nature, although I have no explanation or train of thought as to why. But things that everyday people cannot wrap their heads around, I can do easily. On occasion, I get flashes of insight, I suppose you would call them, into what I can only refer to (For lack of an actual phrase to call it) as the very nature of the universe. It is not anything rational, logical, or contiguous, but rather, a visceral response to thought processes that occur in my mind. The processes don't so much provide me with words, ideals, phrases, or images, it feels as though they are more closely related to an inexplicable connection to the Universe itself. It's as though I am constantly connected to an otherworldly entity whose energy I can sense, or feel, sort of in the way a dog can hear things outside of the perceptible range of humans, and how certain telescopes can measure the UV spectrum, I feel as though I have an otherworldly sensory connection to something on a slightly different plane than others do. Most often, I refer to this entity simply as "Universe," as I believe that the Universe is, in some ways, self-sustaining, and it would not shock me if there were some "intelligence" to it (Whether said intelligence is one of rational thought, or simply a naturalistic, reactionary force). Amongst the processes that I can explain are a time sense and what I feel is a universal directional compass. I know what direction I am facing at all times, but not just in relation to North, South, East, or West, but in relation to the world as a whole, to the sun, the other planets, and so on. I seem to be able to mentally step outside of myself for brief periods in order to envision myself in a more universally spatial manner. In this form, I borrow from tenets of Naturalistic Pantheism, in that I see the Universe as something other than the purely physical, but not necessarily as something divine or intelligent. If you're not confused by now, kudos, because I think I just confused myself.

Akin to Atilla, I have no idea how the Universe began. I feel that there is something outside of the Universe, but as to what, I am not sure. I can envision what feels to be something larger than our Universe, and I think it an interesting concept that the Universe continues larger and larger, into infinity, the universe that we are in comprising but a single atom inside a single molecule in a living or inanimate object far larger, which in turn is encased in a similar universe, and so on. I enjoy the phrase, "A Universe within us all," to illustrate this, but again, it is not so much a theory as it is simply a feeling. There are certain doctrines, usually called "Multiverse" doctrines, that explain this more in-depth, but I don't really adhere to one or another in particular. I also feel that once the Universe came into its current form, that the observable physical laws that we have tested to be true are, at least in some form, correct. As I said elsewhere, mathematics works because it is provable. Physics works because it is provable. But the reason that the two Sciences are provable is because the methods we use to go about proving them are relative. The Arabic numeral 2 is a completely arbitrary term, and thus 2 + 2 = 4 means literally nothing without the language and the connotation behind it, but when looking at the idea from a higher thought standpoint, one can see that two apples and two more apples makes the number of apples that is represented by four. Whether the characters used to depict that are Arabic or Roman, the philosophical backing is there.

I am not so sure that the Universe is expanding, I feel that Existence theory is a very valid theory to explain the Universe, and not to ignore the ideals that are presented to call it into question, but for the idea that there may be causes beyond that infinity that could be the missing link to our equation. but I also feel that we, as Humans, may not ever have the answers to the origins of our existence, and thus, may be forced to settle for what we currently have at the time of our demise. The human ideal is one of pure wisdom and understanding, but even beyond that, to a transcendent thought where proofs and observation are no longer required. I feel very strongly that we, as humans, cannot claim anything to be entirely true beyond any reasonable doubt, because what we know is relative to our experiences here on this small, insignificant speck of the Universe. What we can know is what may work for us while we are here, and while our situation is such that we cannot know anything about the remainder of the Universe through observation, those things that are true for us now must always be under scrutiny, and must always be willing to be malleable and willing to change and update.

Thus, I also consider the most rational stance in the area of observation is to withhold judgment. In the area of belief, I choose to believe in some sort of higher power, although I am not certain what, who, why, where, or how the being came into existence, what it wants, if it has goals or thoughts or incentive. It is no more absurd to believe that we came about randomly than it is to believe that we came about through intelligent design, but of the two choices, my preference would rather stray towards belief in something larger than myself. Not for fear of divine punishment or retribution, but for the sense that there is something more intelligent than I; More wise than I; And who does have all of the answers.

I also fully believe that if there is a God, it is not a figurehead of miracles and human intervention or creation - it is rather something incomprehensible by the human mind, without form or thought, motivated purely by something completely intangible by you or I, that I can best refer to as its 'nature.' It did not send Jesus or Allah or aliens or Buddha, and no Religion's interpretation (Or any denomination thereof) of what God is can ever be the correct stance. In thinking this, I also borrow from certain tenets of Hindu Universalism, int he thought that all religions and belief structures are on neutral ground, but Hindu Universalism states that all Religions should be given the same credence, while I make the distinction that credence should only be given in a strict setting, but if it is given, that it should apply to all religions. While they may all strive to explain the same entity, the idea of salvation at the hands of a merciful or benevolent God is very likely not to ever occur. Which segues nicely into Death.

Nature of Death: The nature of life and death for humans is the same as any other living or cyclical organism or function that exists in the universe. Stars are born and die, planets are born and die, humans are born and die, and the nature of everything is quite cyclical. In this thinking, one's death isn't a death, per-se, as the energies that are within us to keep us sustained and alive don't necessarily die along with us; Where they go, of if they go anywhere, I have no idea. I am still unsure as to the idea of a soul, but I have begun to classify and structure the ideas and tenets of thought, which I compare most closely to the hierarchy of matter that we currently look at in our studies of the physical. I have termed this idea to be called "Ellisance," and to explain it would require an explanation of the Universe itself, but here are the basics:

The world can be divided quite easily into two areas: Physical and tangible things, and things that are not so easily classified. The former carries such things as matter; Solids, Liquids, Gases, Plasma, rocks, planets, stars, organisms, anything that we would call real and observable. Ellisance, on the other hand, is more abstract - It would deal with such things as thought; Ideals, notions, souls, such things as the paranormal (The existence of which lends a bit of thought that all we observe is not as much of reality as we may believe), things like Gravity, energy, movement, time, and so on, would all fall under the category of Ellisance. Emotions, intents, thoughts, chaos, entropy, willpower, even the unspoken laws that govern the universe would be categorized under the notion of Ellisance. Ellisance is the law, the fabric - it is why gravity exists to make things fall, it is why time flows forwards, it is the shape of fate. Ellisance is a stuff, as well as a law - your body is made of matter, but your soul is made of Ellisance, as are your thoughts. How the hierarchy therein works? Hell if I know. But this is one of the notions that I alluded to above that people seem to glance sidelong at me, thinking that I am wholly insane. A classification system for a soul or for thought seems absurd, but it is something that I can fathom, and grasp, and even begin poking at and analyzing, in an abstract sense.

And a rather abstract quote that I grabbed tonight:

Quote: "Incubus @ New Skin"
Until the 20th century, reality was everything humans could touch, smell, see,and hear. Since the inital publication of the charged electromagnetic spectrum, humans learned that what they can touch, smell, see, and hear...is less than one millionth of reality.

I do not believe in a physical, tangible, or otherwise fathomable afterlife; I believe that once we die, our energies may transform in a way such that we experience a certain emotion or thought or experience, but such an experience would be so unlike anything that we know or are used to here, that we cannot for certain say what it is. I don't believe Universe has anything direct to do with this, but I believe that we all become or take from a part of Universe in some way when we die. Where our energies go from there may or may not be a tangible place, but I believe that such energies are re-integrated into the energy of the universe, and in some way are used to power the occurrences of the Universe.

Nature of Right and Wrong: Right and wrong are completely relative terms that only come into play when we speak of will and intent; In doing so, and in characterizing God, we can attribute right and wrong to God itself. Thus, I believe that making the concepts of Good and Evil relative to things that have willpower or intent or motives is a necessity. For instance, is it wrong for an asteroid to impact a planet and destroy the life there? Absolutely not - It would be chance. The asteroid had no motivations to kill, or to destroy, something was simply in its path. Is it wrong that a star supernovas, regresses, and forms a black hole? Not at all. It is a function of what the star is, and one would assume that it is a necessary function of what the universe is, since it seems to be naturally occurring in the cyclical productions of what the star is.

Thus, right and wrong are closely tied to will and intent, and will and intent are, as far as we know, organic and relative. But right and wrong seem to contrast with instinct and nature, for an animal who kills for food is only doing what comes naturally to it, and is not necessarily committing a "wrong" act, despite robbing its prey its right to live. It's particularly important to make the distinction between right and wrong in the area of what is natural, and it doesn't seem as though human law and human thought can correctly achieve that balance. As is illustrated in the sacred texts we have around the world, there are certain ideals of social right and wrong, but I am not sure if those social norms and expectations can be attributed to natural things, either.

For instance, cruelty to an animal can be portrayed quite differently than cruelty to a human, and we tend to give ourselves preferential status over other organisms on the planet due to our ingenuity, and the notions of right and wrong can be quite heavily debated as to their origins, purposes, and execution, and as to whether such laws can be universal, or whether they can only apply to humans, or whether they should be wholly flexible, and interpreted on a case-by-case basis. Of course, human err plays largely into this as well, and could never succeed with perfection. Thus, as a student of law and logic, but also as a free-thinker and a theologian, I tend to become torn between what is logical and what is inherently apparent.

Nature of Origins: Where we came from? Honestly, I have no clue. I don't pretend to know. I do know that we can't know, and the best shot that we have at explaining where we came from is to understand and analyze what we can observe, and classify the things that we can while we have the capacity and the ability, but at the same time, to not rule out faith as an answer for why we *can* observe. I tend to look at the notion of Universe as all-encompassing, with observational sciences falling underneath, as though the Big Bang is a valid cause for *our* immediate existence, Evolution is a valid cause for our even *more* immediate existence, but the possibility of an intelligent power setting those things into motion being fully within the realm of reason. Thus, I don't ever feel as though science and religion or science and belief systems have to be at odds, because the explanations that we come up with, scientifically, may be entirely correct, but also, those explanations could have unseen causes *themselves*. Thus, for us, science cannot be wrong so long as it is provable and have functional applications (For instance, mathematics and influences of electricity, computing, and so on), but insofar as Science being used to prove or disprove a given cause, or to further a given motive, it can't much be used as such.

I could go on and on and on, but I think I'll stop there. I keep going back and adding things to this long-assed post.

Quote: lord_day, December 13, 2006 04:06 pm
Quote: Kablizzy, December 13, 2006 08:09 am
100% predictable, given enough information.
It's impossible to get enough information, even with the most advanced technology. When we measure things, we affect them, and (on an atomic level) possibly changing their paths. #269962 42 2006-12-14T08:55:28Z Kablizzy
Quote: Clovic, December 14, 2006 08:39 am
I believe with both Lord Day and Blizzy on this one. I think it /is/ possible to predict everything given the information, but the chances of obtaining the necessary tools to predict everything involved in a single, minute, action is unimagineable. You'd have to discover and solve an almost limitless amount of data for a single action. It's not only impractical, but likely will never be able to be done.

That said, in a metaphorical world where we have said tools, I think it would be possible to predict what someone will do to a certain point.

Though, that certain point is extremely accurate here's where I disagree with fate, predestination, and whatever else you want to call it. I believe it is in our capacity to defy the events and causes leading to an action. Our actions are influenced by an innumerable amount of things including, our own thoughts, our experiences, our observations, and so much more, but I think it is possible for our own thoughts to over-ride everything else in certain instances.

Though, I'm a romantic in just about every aspect of life and this idea is how I hold onto the idea of heroes and "magical" things happening and such things that you only dream about. I must say though, my romanticism doesn't stem from being naive, simply wanting to believe something unusual, or anything irrational. I believe in balance and for balance to be maintained, such things must happen. They happen rarely, very rarely, but they must happen in my opinion.

...On second though, maybe you don't want insight into my thoughts.

While I certainly agree with the first part, it's not necessarily fate or predestination so much as it is following a logical chain of events. The point that I'm trying to make is that defying the events and causes leading to an action is, by definition, supporting the idea that those actions can be predicted. Let me give an example:

1. You are in a completely white room. You have no memory of how you got there. There is a white table, a white plate, and a chocolate chip cookie on the table. The only sense you have is that you are not hungry. Do you take the cookie?

2. You are in a completely white room. You have no memory of how you got there. There is a white table, a white plate, and a chocolate chip cookie on the table. The only sense you have is that you are hungry. Do you take the cookie?

While a simple analogy, it holds all of the information that you need. Given the situation of a clean state, and a human operating entirely upon instinct of hunger, that person will act 100% of the time in a predictable fashion in each instance. More clearly, your choice isn't a defiance of a pre-set outcome; your choice *is* the pre-set outcome, based upon the previous things that have occurred. All of those influences that have an affect upon our actions and choices are the reason we make those choices. The reason we stop to give a certain homeless person change is based upon all of our past experiences, judgments, successes, and failings. If you stopped to give change to a homeless person in 1997, and was raped by that homeless person, given your past, you may or may not be inclined to stay away from homeless people in the future. But, given that scenario, I would put my money on the predictable outcome being that any person with a relatively normal upbringing will stay away from homeless people from that point forward. Given counseling, and a positive and optimistic outlook on life, that person may get over the inherent fear, and still give change to homeless people.

But go back and read that. That's exactly what I'm talking about. Those variables in our lives, no matter how small and seemingly insignificant, are precisely the things that we base our decisions upon. So, it's not so much a matter of fate, it's a matter of whatever happens in your life is a result of what happened in your past. Broken bones are a result of falling off four-story buildings, domestic abuse breeds long-term psychological problems. But on a deeper level that we can't understand, there are smaller factors that may tip the scales in a given direction. Say you're walking down a lonely street; on the boulevard of broken dreams. Every day, you walk the same route, until one day, a Tuesday, you wake up early, and decide to take the scenic route. You take an entirely new way to work, and your whole day shapes from there.

But what caused you to do so? Upon analyzing, you could say that the sun was shining that day. You could say that stubbing your toe in the shower had an impact. You could say that waking up early had something to do with your new route to work. You could say that it is the knowledge of the day being a Tuesday. But what caused you to wake up early on that Tuesday morning? You could have had a restful sleep the night before. The neighbor's dog, for once, was quiet and unassuming. The night before, you could have gone to bed early. Why? The previous day could have been tiring. You could have had too much to do at work on that Monday. Why? Perhaps it was the vacation you took last week.

See where I'm going with that? When you wake up in a bad mood, and you don't know why, I bet there's a reason. That reason may not be apparent or tangible, but it's there, I'm certain of it.

Worldview Name: Atheistic Anarcho-Capitalist

Nature of God:  Does not exist, and those who believe he exists are mentally deficient.  Well, I wouldnt go that far actually.  I dont think that the people who feel there is some spiritual element to the world are idiots.  But the people who lump a whole lot of hooey on top of that (cough cough Christians, Jews, Muslims, Hindus, etc), are delusional to an incredible degree.

Nature of Death:  The brain stops functioning and what we think of as I ceases to exist.

Nature of Right and Wrong:  Right and wrong can be boiled down to property rights.  Every person has the right to not have their personal property aggressed against by anyone else.  Your body is, obviously, included in the term personal property.  Rights can only be negative, not positive.  That is to say, rather than saying, I have a right to life, you have to say, I have a right not to be deprived of life by another person.  Rights are universal, and apply to everyone at all times.

Governments, by nature, violate these rights, and as such, should be eliminated entirely.

Nature of Origins:  I subscribe to whatever the scientists think is the best/most rational explanation of the times.  It may not be correct, but its the best theory weve got that doesnt involve magic.

Quote
Right and wrong are completely relative terms that only come into play when we speak of will and intent; In doing so, and in characterizing God, we can attribute right and wrong to God itself. Thus, I believe that making the concepts of Good and Evil relative to things that have willpower or intent or motives is a necessity. For instance, is it wrong for an asteroid to impact a planet and destroy the life there? Absolutely not - It would be chance. The asteroid had no motivations to kill, or to destroy, something was simply in its path. Is it wrong that a star supernovas, regresses, and forms a black hole? Not at all. It is a function of what the star is, and one would assume that it is a necessary function of what the universe is, since it seems to be naturally occurring in the cyclical productions of what the star is.

Thus, right and wrong are closely tied to will and intent, and will and intent are, as far as we know, organic and relative. But right and wrong seem to contrast with instinct and nature, for an animal who kills for food is only doing what comes naturally to it, and is not necessarily committing a "wrong" act, despite robbing its prey its right to live. It's particularly important to make the distinction between right and wrong in the area of what is natural, and it doesn't seem as though human law and human thought can correctly achieve that balance. As is illustrated in the sacred texts we have around the world, there are certain ideals of social right and wrong, but I am not sure if those social norms and expectations can be attributed to natural things, either.

For instance, cruelty to an animal can be portrayed quite differently than cruelty to a human, and we tend to give ourselves preferential status over other organisms on the planet due to our ingenuity, and the notions of right and wrong can be quite heavily debated as to their origins, purposes, and execution, and as to whether such laws can be universal, or whether they can only apply to humans, or whether they should be wholly flexible, and interpreted on a case-by-case basis. Of course, human err plays largely into this as well, and could never succeed with perfection. Thus, as a student of law and logic, but also as a free-thinker and a theologian, I tend to become torn between what is logical and what is inherently apparent.

#272735 91 2006-12-18T03:22:29Z Kablizzy
Quote: sweep, December 17, 2006 09:28 pm
Quote: blue_tetris, December 17, 2006 10:25 pm
I wouldn't go so far as to say we have "two years of corrupted votes".  Most of the votes on NUMA were made in earnest.  The screw-ups are an exceptional few.
Name a map that has been on the top rated page for longer than an hour. Then consider the likelihood that this map never received a sniper vote.

Pretty unlikely, right? I'd say that's pretty corrupted. Yes, the vast amount of votes are perfectly fine, but the extent of vote fraud could well be even worse than we might think.

Kablizzy's Cavern III... Tattletale... Meteor Shower... Mount Doom... I could go on!

Anyway, kidding aside, we *need* to hold off until we know what we are doing with the future of NUMA. We should not go forward with a reset, or an update until we have a solution to the problems that currently plague NUMA.

With the recent developments around NUMA, it is obvious to me that we need a change. But in order to suggest a change, we need to identify the problems. The problems, as I see it, are most commonly associated with ratings; sniping, and multi-accounting. both of these things circulate around the central issue of ratings, and I don't see any other problem with the NUMA system.

So, identifying the problem of ratings, what can we do to prevent abuse? Well, new leadership was a great start, and I want to give a big thanks to Nick and Pembie, and Sweep and maestro, for the parts that they are playing.

However, how are people able to make sniping and multi-accounting a problem? Because they are able to abuse those systems. Rating a map down will always exist so long as we have a ratings system, there is no doubt in my mind about that.

But multi-accounting? We can eliminate that quickly and successfully by only allowing certain accounts that meet a set criteria to rate.

I will once more provide a link to my earliest idea; located here

I also want to call attention to Jakel's suggestion in this same forum.

Now, beyond this, the voting system could be abolished altogether, and/or replaced with the favourites. Beyond this, even something entirely new could be done. This is a time for brainstorming and new ideas.

But three things are clear:

1. Multi-accounters must be eliminated in every form. Snipers are not *as* much of a big deal, and even though it would be ideal to abolish sniping as well, there is no way to eliminate sniping without changing the ratings system in an irrevocable manner.

2. Ratings are not the reason NUMA exists.

3. We *do* need changes and updates.

So, through all of this, we need to reach a consensus on which action to take before taking any action. Whether this takes days, weeks, months, we need to take due process with this. We cannot rush into this.

#272796 97 2006-12-18T08:07:27Z Kablizzy
Quote: Arachnid, December 18, 2006 07:51 am
Quote: Kablizzy, December 18, 2006 03:22 am
However, how are people able to make sniping and multi-accounting a problem? Because they are able to abuse those systems. Rating a map down will always exist so long as we have a ratings system, there is no doubt in my mind about that.

But multi-accounting? We can eliminate that quickly and successfully by only allowing certain accounts that meet a set criteria to rate.

I will once more provide a link to my earliest idea; located here
Addressing your linked suggestion:
- Basing who can vote on an average rating of 2.5 or above, or in any way preferring people who vote high, is a bad idea. 2.5 _should_ be the average vote - half the votes should be above this, and half below (the actual average on NUMA is almost exactly 3.5). A low rating is not automatically a bad one, and setting a threshold of 2.5 would simply raise the '0 level' - the level at which a rating or vote is essentially 0.
- I don't generally agree with the idea of having criteria to be met before someone can vote, besides registering. Whatever criteria you set, you're going to exclude people that have legitimate contributions to make and include those who are just out to abuse the system.

One half-baked idea that's occurred to me is a friends-based rating system. You indicate who your 'friends' are on NUMA - those you trust - and ratings are calculated individually for you, weighting votes by your friends most highly, followed by votes by their friends, and so on. This has several issues, though, mostly technical:
- Requires implementation of a social networking style 'friends' system.
- There's no single 'leaderboard' people can refer to. You can no longer say you're "in the top 10".
- There'd need to be some default for when you're not logged in, which may just become the current system all over again.
- Since ratings have to be calculated in a fairly involved manner, and will vary for every person that's viewing them, there are potential implications for system load. Calculating a top-rated list would be even worse.

Oh, of course, I didn't mean for the numbers to be anything concrete, and you're right, it would be a very elitist and very... what's the word... segregated? way of dealing with things, but I really think the idea of a friends system should be looked into. Also, you're right, that portion of my suggestion dealing with average ratings was kind of dumb, because people who vote highly aren't necessarily better members of the community than those of us who tend to be more critical with votes.

The problem with my system, as I see it, is just that - Some people would undoubtedly be left out in the cold, regardless of how much tweaking was done. But perhaps certain tenets of my system, and from other systems being proposed, could come together to fix these seeming problems that our users are having. The multi-account problem can be dealt with in other ways, too.

For instance, perhaps, upon registration, there could be an IP-check coded, or something. But of course, why stop at limited ideas? The sky is the limit, so long as we're committed to making NUMA a good place again, and really, there's no better place to start than on the user-side, and the confessions recently are a step in the right direction.

#13197 1 2006-12-29T04:09:38Z Kablizzy
Welcome to NedCon8!

Happy New Year!! This year, The Legacy Team is starting things off right with the eighth season of the Neditor Contest! This season, we have a brand-new theme for participants to work on; ReMixes!

For those of you unfamiliar with the idea of ReMix maps, a ReMix map is, in essence, an interpretation of another person's map. There are two types of ReMix maps; Conceptual and Literal.

A Conceptual ReMix map is where you keep the essence and the idea of the original, but change the tileset or playstyle of the map, with the same general idea and feel. For instance, if one were to ReMix Mount Doom, one could keep the tileset, and ReMix the map's context, as seen in this map, where the map's tileset was changed, but Mount Doom's concept stayed intact.

A Literal ReMix map is where you keep the structure and form of the map, but change the theme or essence of play. A good example of a Literal ReMix would be this map, where Mount Doom was turned into a DDA, using the same tileset.

This season's theme being ReMixes, participants can ReMix any map that has been posted to NUMA as of prior to this post. Any NUMA maps that were posted after this post may not be used.

Each contestant is allowed 2 submissions TOTAL for the contest. You may ReMix the same map twice. If the total number of submissions received reaches 25, each contestant may submit an additional map, for a total of 3 maps each.

All entries must be submitted to NUMA under the same name as you use here on the forums. If your NUMA account name and Forum account name are different you must send me a Personal Message so we can verify your identity. Each submission must be your own unique work, any map plagiarized from another member, or any map submitted from a non-member will be thrown out accordingly.

Each submission must be posted in this thread, along with a clearly-labeled link to your ReMix map, as well as a clearly-labeled link to the original map. The link to the map that you are ReMixing must be in your post, and it would be preferable if the link to the original map were listed in your NUMA submission, as well.

Here are the stipulations for this season;
  • All maps must be submitted to NUMA. (With the exception of those who don't have access to NUMA)
  • A link to all submissions must be provided in this thread. Along with that, a link to the original map must be provided in this thread.
  • Manual code editing of any kind may not be used.
    If the map you are choosing to ReMix has manual code editing in it, it is a good idea to choose another map.
  • All objects must be completely or partially visible. Completely hidden objects may not be used.
    If the map you are choosing to ReMix has hidden objects in it, it is a good idea to choose another map.
  • There may not be any purposeful use of bugs, glitches, or other unsavory map making tricks. If there is any Grey area, send a personal message to one of the judges, and we will pass down a decision on whether the trick is allowed.
    If the map you are choosing to ReMix uses bugs and/or glitches in it, it is a good idea to choose another map.
  • Any map violating any of these requirements will be disqualified from the contest, with no exceptions.
  • If you wish to protest a score, send a personal message to one of the judges, and we will pass down a decision on whether the score is acceptable.
    Posting in this thread to contest a score will result in immediate disqualification from the contest.
  • It is your responsibility to double-check scores on your maps, not ours.
  • There will be no editing of maps once they are submitted to this thread. We use an honour system for this, so if you are caught editing your maps after they are submitted here, you will be immediately disqualified from the contest.
  • You may not use pre-existing maps for your submissions.
There will be three judges (Myself, LittleViking001, and KinGAleX). The cumulative total of the three judges' scores will be the participant's Total Score.

Each submission will be scored out of 50 points based on these catagories:

Fun, Difficulty, Creativity, Execution, Other.
  • (0-10) Fun: How fun is the map to play? Would a person who plays through the map do so again and again? Is the map enjoyable and exciting?
  • (0-10) Difficulty: Is the map too difficult, or too easy? Is the map a bowl of porridge? Are there any points in the map where the difficulty is too much for the idea of the map?
  • (0-10) Creativity: What sets your map apart from the others, and from the original? Why is this a memorable map? Did you do anything new here that people haven't seen before? What changes did you make to the original map that made the map unique?
  • (0-10) Execution: How well did you ReMix the map? Were the base elements of the original map still contained within?
  • (0-10) Other: This category is used for criterion that don't fit into any other category, but the judge feels needs to be mentioned.
Our Submission Deadline is going to be February 14th, 2007 - Valentine's Day. at 12:01 AM.

With all that said, good luck to all of our Neditors, and you may begin!

#13212 1 2006-12-29T23:39:08Z Kablizzy
First of all, Happy New Year!

Today, it has come. Ten months ago, we began on a journey, entitled "The Legacy Project." It began as a simple map-pack, but grew into something that none of us had anticipated. Who could have predicted that maximo's "Return Pack" would sprout its own legs, and flower into something so massive as the Legacy Project? Surely, not I. In ten months, The Legacy Team has brought the community many things, but more importantly than that, many others have followed in The Legacy's footsteps to create their own map packs and their own projects, to amazing fanfare. The reason that we began Legacy was first, to contribute something large to the community, and second, and more importantly, to inspire others to do the same. And I, for one, am ecstatic to say that the contributions that you all have given the community have far surpassed my expectations. I know that we are looking forward to more things from all of you in the future.

And now, we are entering a new Golden Age of Metanet. 2007 will be the year that Metanet breaks out of its mold, sheds its cult status, and becomes a heavy hitter in the gaming world. And we are proud to say that this year will be a large year for The Legacy Team, as well. And to start 2007 off, we have a number of treats for you all.

First and foremost, we would like to announce three new additions to the Legacy Team; KinGAleX, blue_tetris, and krusch! As busy as our schedules are, as a team, we decided that we need some new faces in Legacy. As of today, KinGAleX, blue_tetris, and krusch will all be helping work on projects for the team on a permanent basis. I fully believe that there are few men in the community who have done the kinds of things that these three have been capable of - The P42 pack, the Pony Parade, the Camisade Collective, The Sunday N, the Real N, The Map Manifestos, The Super Hard Column, the Super Fluffy Map Packs... I could go on for days. Now, as much as LittleViking and I have been working with KinGAleX and Dave at The Real N, this is more of a formality, and we fully feel that krusch has the talent and the prowess to inject some new ideas into future projects of ours.

Secondly, starting today, we are announcing the beginning of NedCon Eight. The NedCon contest series, started by Maximo, has been a great inspiration to mapmakers and fans of N alike. NedCon has been around as long as the forums, and has gone through many different forms, and this season, we continue the tradition set by LLCoolDave and maximo with a new theme: ReMix maps! All of the information needed to begin participating is included within the thread, and all questions should be directed there. Once you're done here, head on over to the Neditor Contest Eight thread and check it out!

Thirdly, today marks the start of a new tradition here at Metanet. What initially began as a casual activity amongst those of us who frequent the IRC and the Ventrilo server, the concept of Monday Night Numa Maps is one that died out rather quickly after its inception. It was popular enough, but the idea simply faded from existence. However, just recently, Clovic brought the idea to me that we should make the Monday Night Numa Maps a tradition, and the MNNM League was born. For more information on the MNNM League, and how to join, visit this thread.

Fourthly, today marks the end of the Dronies 2006! Voting has ended, and we will be tallying the votes as soon as is possible, and we will be posting results as soon as they are counted. Good luck to all participants, and thanks for all of the enthusiasm!

Fifthly, the Legacy Team website is getting a makeover! Before now, the site has been rather simple, as Sweep is the only one who can update it. But within the coming weeks, we will be updating the site, both aesthetically, and functionally, so that updates will occur much more frequently there, to let you all know about upcoming Legacy projects, current endeavors, and perhaps even some Metanet News.

Sixthly, I know that I have yet to hand out prizes for past seasons of our contests, so if you are missing a prize, please me and let me know what I have yet to do for you. I have a bit of a surplus of money, so I can do the T-shirts now and get them shipped out within the week, provided our post-blizzard conditions don't stymie my progress further.

Next, I am proud to announce the long-awaited dedication maps for iangb, Lucidium, and spect! We have been saving all of our big guns for today, and we felt that hanging on to the dedication maps until today would likely be the best move for publicity purposes. We thought that these three should get as much exposure as possible, as they were the best of the best during Legacy's Origins contest. So, without further ado, you can find the dedication maps here;

iangb
Lucidium
spect

And finally, the coup de grace. The moment that many of you have been waiting almost a year for. Today, we are launching Expanse, our second of three map-packs in the Legacy Trinity, our map trio. Expanse adds 300 levels, all made by The Legacy Team's seven members - maximo, nevermore, LittleViking001, Sweep, tktktk, Lucidium, and myself - As well as the maps made by Pariah, iangb, Echarin, and Barabajagal for their magnificent showing during the Legacy: Origins contest and during NedCon 7. Expanse is meant as an expansion-pack, of sorts, to Legacy, continuing in the same vein as the original pack, with new ideas, new map styles, and hopefully, some brand-new perspectives upon the game. Over the past ten months, we seven have tirelessly played and re-played through the pack, tweaking and balancing, and arranging the pack to be in tip-top shape for you all to enjoy.

Download Expanse

List of who made which levels

Alongside Expanse, we are proud to present the Legacy: Expanse Contest! Like the Legacy: Origins Contest, the Legacy: Expanse Contest is designed to provide incentive for you all to further enjoy the levels that we provide. The contest is a race, and a challenge, to find the fastest, most skilled and most dedicated players here. The first 20 people to complete Legacy will be awarded and recognized for their accomplishment. Please, please, please read all of the rules before entering, and follow the submission rules included here;

Contest Rules

Contest Sumbission: TheLegacyProject@gmail.com

Contest Deadline: March 1, 2007

Contest Rules:

- Once you complete the Legacy: Expanse pack in its entirety, you will submit your N userdata.sol file by e-mail to The Legacy Team for review. For help finding your .sol file, please consult the first post of this thread.

- E-mails must be marked "Legacy: Expanse Submission" in the subject line, along with your N username. (Ex. Legacy: Expanse Submission - Kablizzy)

- All Submissions Must include completed Demo data from each of the 300 Expanse levels. MAKE SURE YOUR DEMO DATA IS COMPLETE. Incomplete submissions may result in disqualification.

- Please be aware that your .sol file contains your username and password. The Legacy Team will not use, store, or even look at this information. If you are still not comfortable submitting a file with your password in it, you can change your info before submitting. Inside the Configure menu, set your username as LegacySubmission and your password as dummy (with the e-mail address left blank) and press "change user." You can then submit without any private information being sent.

- In the case that your .sol file is very large, you can upload your file to iHud.com and e-mail the link given to you to The Legacy Team. iHud is a free file-hosting service that allows for files up to 50 MB in size without requiring users to register.

Prizes

- A chance to contribute to The Legacy Team's third map-pack, due out during late 2007!

- A Custom Signature, for use on the forums!

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- Access to the Custom Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A place in the N Hall of Fame, alongside the greatest N players!


For the Second Runner-Up:

- A Legacy T-shirt, custom-made by the Legacy Team!

- A Dedication map on Numa - the N User Map Archive!

- A Custom Signature, for use on the forums!

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- Access to the Custom Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A place in the N Hall of Fame, alongside the greatest N players!


For the remainder of the top 20:

- Access to the Custom Forum Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- An "Expanse Finalist" sig tag, for use on the forums!

For those who finished Legacy: Origins

- A Custom Signature signifying your placement amongst the top 20 in both contests!

Welcome to The Monday Night Numa Map League!

Beginning today, January 1st, 2007, The Legacy Team presents a weekly activity for mapmakers of all kinds. the MNNM league is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, the thread will become locked, and all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined timeframe.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted in this thread, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member will post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in this first post for everyone's enjoyment!

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

At some point, you'll figure out its pattern, and how the gauss fires, and the timing. Do the same with rockets, drones, and so on, and then try it with certain tiles that you're having a problem with.

Just open up a map, put in a smattering of tiles that you're having problems with, and try all sorts of jumps and button combinations, and such.

#13396 1 2007-01-08T03:45:19Z Kablizzy


Good morning! Welcome to week two.

This week, we will be focusing upon symmetry. Symmetrical maps can be manifest in a number of ways, but the most pertinent way is shown in the tileset. Of course, your tileset doesn't need to be symmetrical to qualify this week, but some large part of the map must be. Rotational symmetry and other types of symmetry are fine, so long as it is a significant and consistent theme to the map.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted in this thread, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member will post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in this first post for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks maps are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Homing Launchers

Administrators:
  • Kablizzy
  • Clovic
  • KinGAleX
Rules:
  • All submissions must be entered into NUMA.
  • Each submission must have a link to the map placed here.
  • Your map must be made and posted on Monday. If it is Monday where you are, consider the map as valid.

#285142 6 2007-01-13T09:32:06Z Kablizzy
I thought Expanse was a Hell of a step up. I now know what the niche is for the trio, and I think that our first one lacked a focus that we had for Expanse. I chalk it up to experience and just being able to reflect on what had already gone on seemed to help immensely. Plus, just on a personal note, my mapmaking has grown exponentially just between Origins and Expanse.

In fact, I just went back through my Legacy stuff, and I realized that the maps that we made for Expanse were so much more refined than those for Legacy, mostly because of the experience of us knowing, "Well, this didn't go over well, let's try this and this," and I think the map quality is better overall for it.

Beyond that, I counted up how many of my Legacy maps would have definitively made it into Expanse (I didn't count maps that I was iffy about), and I came up with around 25, one quarter of the maps I did for Legacy. Not that they were bad, but the level that we expected Expanse to be seemed to jump a few notches.

Just to look at things like Mother Must I? and Constellation versus Arrant and TMZ... I think I, for one, have bettered my mapmaking by a lot just taking part in this project. And, some of the maps that the fellas put out on the table were just mindblowing the first time I saw them. A lot of this stuff had so much more oomph to it, and thusfar, Zenith is shaping up to be much the same.

Good morning! Welcome to week three.

This week, we will be focusing upon multiples of seven. Objects, tiles, anything that can be found in multiples of seven can be valid here. Objects, enemies, anything that you can put in the map that is in multiples of seven qualifies as a valid entry.

Announcement: I don't have the full pack up yet from last week's posts. If someone could compile it and post it here, I'll update it as soon as I get home from work.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted in this thread, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member will post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in this first post for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks maps are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Good morning! Welcome to week five.

This week, we will be focusing upon Alternate Routes (Thanks exuberance). Alternate Route Maps, for those of you unfamiliar with the idea of Alternate Route Maps, they can include many different themes and ideas. Alternate Route Maps can be maps where finishing the level is very easy, or very apparent at the start, but contain gold as a second option, or other exits. Alternate Route Maps can also be two or more distinct ways to finish a map, or maps that even combine all of these elements! If you come up with other ways for Alternate Route maps to manifest, please post them here, as I'm sure I didn't cover all of the possibilities.

Announcements:
- Okay, we're up on time this week!
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, January 30th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Homing Launchers
