At first, it was an empty threat, just to get people to, y'know, reflect and think about what they're doing and what they're saying, but when no one does that, then I need to make an example of someone. I don't like doing it, I don't want to do it, but my duty here is to the betterment of the forum, and if it isn't apparent that the staff isn't happy with the way things are run, and if our idle requests are being outright ignored, then something with more emphasis and impact needs to be put into place. I don't think that it's difficult, by any stretch of the imagination, to sit back for a second and think, "Okay, I'm about to post this, this, and this... Should I post this? Maybe this was a bit harsh. Is this part against the rules?" and so on.

Quote: scythe33, 2007-01-29T03:52:06Z
Good. I'm-a nitpick like crazy. First, one man's "horrendous insult" is another's "silly joke" and yet another's "friendly gesture". For example, if I called you "f*cking nuts", you'd probably take that as an insult, yet in my school, as well as most schools in the district, "f*cking nuts" is somewhat of a complement. You might think that it's obvious I could see "f*cking nuts" being taken the wrong way, which is exactly why I used it as an example. There are other sayings like that that are far more ambiguous to me, and I've used a few of them here; if I've offended anyone, i'd like to take this opportunity to apologize. (On second thought, a better example might be "Kablizzy is the sh*t").

Yeah, I probably would take offense to it. And you'd probably wonder why. But that's the point. It'd be entirely your fault, and it's 100% not your place to decide. For instance, the reason that calling something "gay" is enforced as a rule is because people do take offense to it. I don't care what you and your friends do, I don't care what inside jokes you guys share, I don't care if "f*cking nuts" is acceptable to you, because to others, it wouldn't be acceptable, and it is solely your own responsibility to take things like that into account. If you went up to a large, intimidating man and called him f*cking nuts while poking him in the the chest, you'd better believe that he's gonna take offense to it. If he kicks the shit out of you, is it his fault? No, in no way. It is 100% your fault for not taking his thoughts, feelings, and actions into account. Sure, he shouldn't ever take things to that extreme, but you should've known not to act like that. Don't stick your finger in the horse's ass, you won't get your teeth kicked in. Don't put yourself in that situation, and bad stuff won't happen to you. In the instance of "Kablizzy is the sh*t," if someone took that out of its context, then it's their own fault for taking things out of context, simple as that. If someone doesn't know that would be a compliment, then that's no fault of any rule, that's the fault of the person interpreting the phrase, yes? Yes. So, if I tell you to go wipe your Chick'n Bits on the next Trolley to Abbotville, and you ban me for it, would that be a valid reason? Hell if I know, but it's not the rule's fault that there are going to be Grey areas. And if you stay on the safe side, and don't tempt technicalities, you'll be fine. I mean, you actively have to *try* to get banned over crap like this, you really, really do. And everyone that's played ignorance to it, I've called bullshit on, and y'know what? I've been right every single time. Everyone knows exactly what they did, exactly why it was against the rules, and most have still acted indignant to me over it. I've even had someone say to me, "Well, yeah, of course I want him dead, but is it really that big of a deal?" One of the main reasons that I take such action against the people that I do is because of my idea that good people are good, and bad people are bad. If you're bad, get out. If you're good, keep on keepin' on. Again, anyone who can breathe and think can know and understand what "right" and "wrong" are. Unless you're literally dumb like a sack of potatoes, you know what being upstanding is, and sure, there are technicalities and misunderstandings and what-have-you, but seriously. Don't act like a jackass, and you won't be treated like a jackass. Doesn't that seem terribly intuitive?

I attribute flaming and trolling to vandalism and petty theft. There are laws against both for a reason. Law enforcement can ask nicely only so long before something more serious needs to be done. If we could simply ask people not to vandalize or steal, that'd be great, but it's when someone - or a group of people - end up not only ignoring the requests outright, but doing so as blatantly as they possibly can, that something needs to be done, yes? Remember that UCLA kid that got tazed, like, six times? The police can only ask so many times before having to do something. And yes, the force they used was excessive, as is this rule. I'll admit that this rule is over-the-top, in fact, I'll be the first one to admit that, but all of that could have been averted if the kid had just shut up, got up, and walked away, like he was supposed to. Had the kid not instigated the situation, nothing would have come of it. Take, for example, a guy who breaks into your house, slips on marbles, and stabs himself on his own knife. He then sues you for the marbles being in the entry way, and wins (Yes, something like this actually happened). Whose fault is it? Definitely not yours. You're just trying to keep the peace, and that's where I'm coming from here. If you run a stop sign, and blindside someone, and they get out and beat your ass, yes, they have some fault, in that they shouldn't have acted the way they acted, but don't run stop signs and that stuff won't happen. Don't point the gun at your face and you won't get shot. Don't be a doucheoff, and you won't get treated like a doucheoff. Have a vendetta against the cops? The Fuzz tryin' to harsh on your mellow? I'd bet ten bucks to a doughnut it's your own Goddamn fault. How EVER could I know something like that? Common Goddamn sense. And that's something that no one has anymore. I mean, people wonder why they're on their fourth marriage? Stop dicking up random chicks and rushing into marriage. Get in trouble with the law much? Stop visiting bars and getting in bar fights. Stop hanging around with the wrong crowd. Complaining that you have to be on crutches because your legs no longer work? Well, you should have stopped skydiving after the first seven broken legs, shouldn't you? Don't like being poor? Should've payed more attention in school, Paco. Always in trouble with the law? No, it's not always racist cops - Stop hanging out with criminals and I guarantee that you'll get in less trouble. Guaranteed. I could care less how much you enjoy playing dice, illegal dice games are illegal. Pot is illegal. I don't care how much you want it not to be - Shut up and deal. And, by the same token, don't want to be banned? Simple, don't flame or troll, and don't be an insubordinate prick. WOW! ISN'T THAT AMAZINGLY PROPHETIC!??! What compels these assholes to be this overly-offensive pile of dick to absolutely everyone at all times? Like I said, I don't care what you want or what you think, rules are rules, the staff's decision is final, shut up and take your medicine. Me? I know everything that happens to me is in some way my own doing. That's common Goddamn sense. I bring a lot on myself, and I take full responsibility for it. Others should do the same. I don't care if you're angry, I don't care if you're disgruntled, take it elsewhere if you need to get some aggression out, just don't bring it here. Just don't be a jackass to people, and this rule won't affect you. Be upstanding, and the rule flies far over your head. Be civil and cool to people you meet, and they will be civil and cool to you, and more importantly, nothing will come of this rule. Anyone ever heard of "Do unto others?" Why don't we do that all the time?

So, I will, without fail, from here on out, automatically and permanently ban anyone whom *I* judge to be trolling or flaming until it stops. I use my own objective judgment, and I'm in this position for the sole reason that I *can* use my objective judgment, and if anyone doubts the job that I do, and the job that I *can* do, then I can only point to my record staffing forums and websites in the past. And of course, I will say that yes, I do make mistakes, and yes, I do make some controversial decisions sometimes, but you have to understand my position here. I do my best in making these decisions, and the reason that I'm an Admin here is to make the controversial decisions. It's what I do. I'm a community leader because I have the capacity to do so, and I know that I can't please everyone all the time, and I've accepted that. But if any of you can't trust that I'll honestly do my best in this position, then we have a serious problem with where we are in general. And, again, that's why this thread is here. To let everyone be heard.

If people can't get it through their heads that I'm serious about this, then it will only get worse, and that's not something that I do to further any motives of my own, but to further the motives of Metanet. It's not something that I do because it feels good, because it doesn't. Do you know how hard it is for me to even kick someone from the IRC, let alone ban them from it? I'm a pushover, man, I'm the type to say, "Stop, or I'll kick you," and everyone just laughs it off. It's SO not easy to be laughing with a guy on IRC one moment, and kickbanning them the next. And people take stuff like that personally, but no matter my responsibility to the forums and to the IRC, I'm still friends with you. But if you break a rule, I have to step in, for the good of the forum, for the good of the community, and do something about it. And that's really my point. If I have to ban Suki, I'll ban Suki. I love the man to death, but as a friend. As an Administrator, if a rule is broken, then as an Administrator, I'll have to do something about it. People who are at the receiving end of a kick or a ban might not understand that, but if I kick you from the channel, I'll still be more than glad to chat it up with you via query, because my friendship with that person hasn't been affected. Like, if I banned KA from the IRC staff channel for some reason, I still love him, I still have all of my respect for him, but in that instance, my duty would be fulfilled, and we can continue on as we were. I'm friends with literally everyone here, I don't have a single enemy or person that I dislike, and to actually bring myself to black hole someone from the community entirely would kill me, especially someone who I'm close friends with, y'know? But that wouldn't in any way affect my friendship with them, from my perspective. So, when I look at this rule that I've 'concocted,' I see it as a "Hey, guys, shape up," rather than an insult or my being a Netiquette Nazi, it's a flare to attract everyone's attention that things are getting out of control, and to reel in the behaviour a bit. If, after a few weeks, everything's been going smoothly, then I won't care about the rule, and I'll retract it. I'm not a hardass, you guys know that. I won't use this rule to go nuts and ban everyone, the rule has only come into effect once since I put it into effect, and I think it's doing its job very nicely, because I've seen a definite decline in the flaming and trolling lately.

All the rule is there to accomplish is to make people stop and think, which they weren't doing before, so there has to be something there to back it up. If someone won't stop and think, "Hm. I wonder if this would be insulting, because someone's feelings might get hurt..." on their own, perhaps the threat of losing their access to the community entirely will inject a *bit* of sense into them before they post.

It is my place to make and enforce these rules for the good of the community, and in my own judgment, the flaming and trolling needs to stop, from all parties. I don't own this place, Keron doesn't own this place, and none of the mods own this place. This is Mare and Raigan's to do with what they see fit. However, our job, as mods, is to promote Metanet and make sure it flourishes, and each of us represents Metanet with the things that we do. And every one of you represents the community with the things that you guys do, and through the things you say. But above all, it's our place to make sure that the community runs smoothly, and if that isn't happening, then we have the power to change that, because we have been *entrusted* with that power. It's our responsibility to see to it that this place doesn't descend into brainless anarchy, and it's our duty to make sure that Metanet does well. I sincerely want to see Raigan and Mare prosper in ways that no other game designers have prospered, and that's perhaps the most powerful motive for why I do this. I feel as though Mare and Raigan deserve it, and they have given something so powerful to me in N, that I want to give back to them in the best way that I know how. I've got no real talents except my penchant for writing and logic. That's all I've ever had going for me, is my mind, and this is how I use it, helping Mare and Raigan. Because I believe that Mare and Raigan deserve to make it big in gaming, and the same goes with the other places that I staff. And, while I'm still young, and while I still have my mind, I want to do what I can for the causes that I believe in. If I could apply my experience here to something that much more important to the world, I would, but I see these places as stepping stones to bigger and better things. And, all of this, I feel, is just an opportunity for me to refine my way of thinking and my administration skills for when they may need to count. If I ever become a high-ranking official anywhere, I have to be able to make decisions just like this, and those decisions will likely have exponentially larger impacts than the impacts that my decisions here have. And I won't get the chance to write my thoughts out from the comfort of my home, and I won't get the chance to justify my decisions like this, but in order for me to understand myself well enough, I have to be sure that my decisions are the most ideal for whatever situation I'm in.

If you went to another forum from here, telling everyone about Metanet, and were acting like an idiot, I would go there and personally request for them to ban you, because you represent us through the things you do. By the same token, people that come here looking for help don't deserve an "RTFM NUB," and while yeah, they should indeed read the manual, or open the readme, or whatever, it's not your place to inflict upon them the four hundred people who have come to the forums prior to them asking the same question. I do not want our community to be that of common internet slugs, because that's what the rest of the internet has become, and I take a Hell of a lot of pride in being able to say that I'm associated with one of the greatest communities in existence. And up until this point, the forums have run in an absolutely magnificent fashion due in part to the way we run things. We have been far too lax on these things, and it has pushed us in the opposite direction from where we want to go, but more importantly, it has pushed us in the opposite direction from where Metanet needs to go. This forum will be enjoyable when all of the ill-behaviour returns to acceptable levels, and we can all chill and be cool with each other. When I look at a suggestion thread, and see three replies, all of which alluding to "GTFO U NUB," I will not accept that in any form. Is it really that difficult to understand that there are certain things that you really shouldn't do?

So, yes, I am a bit zealous in my practice and a bit stringent in my standards, but has it not payed off? Do my forums and sites not run well? I've really heard little except praise for how I run my forums, and while yes, from a user's perspective, the rule might be a bit harsh, take this into consideration;

If you were training for the boxing match of your life, would you rather have your coach be as lax as possible or as stringent as possible? If you were the President of a company, and your workers were slapping each other and throwing pieces of paper and acting raucous, wouldn't you ask them to stop? Of course, because what they are doing is detrimental to something that is not only important to you, but important to the company, as well. My point being, the rules are being enforced strictly because how this community runs is everything to me. It is my livelihood, it is what I spend my time on. Anyone who knows me well knows that Administrating and Moderating is my life, it is the one thing that I have found in my life that I am truly good at. Everything else, I'm just some mediocre jackass, but doing this? I can call myself one of the best. And not for my own benefit, but because what I do makes an impact. I've made an impact upon you all in my time here, and whether that impact is good or bad, I hope that I have at least taught everyone a lesson in what morality is, or how to be logical, or how best to love. I hope I've taught people the virtues that I live by, and why they work for me. I hope that I've taught people why Monogamy is awesome, and why chivalry isn't dead. I hope that I've taught people that it *is* possible to make an impact just by being yourself. I hope I've taught people the virtues of good grammar and why hacking is wrong. I hope that I've taught people a little bit about humour, and about seriousness. I hope that I've taught people a little something about love and hatred. I hope that I've taught people something about what it means to be an upstanding person, but more than anything, I hope that I've taught people about life. Whether you like me or whether you hate me, you have to admit that I make an impact. And as hard as I try, I can only hope that the impact that I make is positive, and that it is positive enough so that people remember who I am and what I do. The only thing that is important to me is that I make an impact in the world, and for the better. And that is what I do here. It's what I was put on this Earth to accomplish. And that's all I can do is try my best to make the world better.

***Marked***

Oh, and Atilla: I've been to plenty of forums more lax than this one, and I've been to plenty harsher. It generally depends on the userbase and size. This is a pretty small community with an average age that seems to be about 16, and who says we should be like the rest of the Internet, or the world for that matter? Kablizzy was arguing specifically against that, and just because NUMA these days is littered with n00b maps does not make a n00b map good. We're not trying to emulate the way other people do things, we're trying to improve on it, right? I defy you to present a single time a member has been seriously emotionally damaged by anything said on the forums.
/note: i'm perfectly happy with the way that things have been running here. i'm also fine with kablizzy's new rule on flaming. but i'm arguing against the position that this place is too lax.
It helps because we can get sued and lose the community, that's how. The Child Protection Act is in place so children under 13 years of age aren't exposed to adult materials, and offensive language is classified in there. That's why every single forum you will ever go to with any inkling of professionalism will have a clause for these things. But beyond that, even though that particular law expires at age 13, it's the responsibility of people like myself to keep stuff like that out of a child's hands. If someone were to post links here to an adult website, and Forumer found it out? That's it, end of community. And that's not something that I'm willing to jeopardize for something that is so, so unbelievably silly. Beyond, that, it's in the Forumer terms of service, and we could lose all of this permanently over something unbelievably trivial. That's why I have to be strict on this stuff, and why I say that we're too lax, simply because we have no choice in the matter.

The point I made about B&T is that we should not have users under 13 here at all. For that alone, we can lose the forums. Right now, we can lose the forums, just for the B&T. Right now, if a guy from Forumer started browsing the forums, and saw B&T, we'd likely no longer have the forum. I can't stress that enough. Thus, there is no reason for B&T to exist. Why shield children? Because it's what we have to do. I personally don't agree to it, but I have a duty to enforce it. It is my responsibility to do so because of the people and the ideals that have come before me, but more importantly to what I have to do immediately, because Forumer tells me I have to. And every host that we go with will have the same or similar rules. Some may be a bit more lax than others, but until and unless we get our own place to run without an overlord like Forumer, we have no say in it. And even if or when we did get our own server, free of Forumer's rules, we would still probably have a clause like that anyway. It's not my place to change it, because it is the way of the world. You guys know that I don't much have a problem with cussing, but it really does no good to raise kids with it. I can't see a single thing wrong *with* shielding them from offensive language, really, and I can't imagine someone with an overbearing *need* to cuss, beyond simply raging against the machine. I mean, I don't have an answer as to why profanity and obscenity are considered taboo and vulgar, but they are. There are some people who don't like it, and a good majority of places have rules against it. Do I cuss? Shit yes I do. Do I cuss outside of B&T? Shit yes I do. But I do so because I can use my common sense and determine where it might be kinda appropriate. Is it ever neccesary? Nope, but it can be used to emphasize some points, and I use it as such. See a couple sentences back. Can others do the same? Not usually, so they get warned for it. But it's usually not because they cussed, it's because they cussed *and* they're doing a ton of other stuff *and* they don't seem to be reforming *and* on and on and on. So whether you believe that their reasons for having those rules are valid or not is irrelevant. We have these rules, and we need to follow them to the best of our ability.

And onto being too lax. This is why I say we're too lax; We're supposed to punish things that are against the rules, like vulgarity outside of BnT. We're supposed to ban users under 13. But we don't. We let things slide. We let you guys troll pretty much as you wish, we let you guys drive folk out of the community, we let you guys flame and spam and do all manner of other things without a whole lot of consequence. Despite the disclaimer, the BnT is against Forumer's ToS. If they were ever to look at some of the stuff in BnT? We'd probably lose the forum, regardless of disclaimer. Why? Hell if I know. Why is vulgarity offensive? No idea. It's certainly not immoral, but it offends people. Is it my place to tell them that they're wrong? Certainly not. Thus, the rules. The rules elsewhere cover these things, and ours don't. So it's not so much a magical, "Why don't we do this? These guys are doing this," but rather the fact that their comprehensive rules cover their asses, legally and otherwise. What legal issues could possibly come of this? I have no idea, but that's the reason a lot of these rules come into being. I mean, SomethingAwful has more stringent rules than we do. Something Freakin' Awful. If that doesn't speak volumes, I don't know what does.

#13880 1 2007-02-05T09:46:29Z Kablizzy


Good morning! Welcome to week six.

This week, the theme will be No Active Enemies. Maps with no active enemies are mostly maps with mines, or jumper puzzles. But this can also extend to race maps, and maps intended to convey a specific purpose (For instance, N-Art). I would like for these to be playable, since N-Art that can be done in less than 24 hours is probably gonna be pretty terrible anyway, but the gist is that there should not be any enemies that seek you out. No Gausses, no rocket launchers, no drones, no floor guards, and most certainly no thwumps.

Announcements:
- Okay, we're up on time this week!
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, February 6th.
- I will have last week's .txt file up shortly.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote

#298473 18 2007-02-18T03:13:59Z Kablizzy
Quote: Tsukatu, February 17, 2007 09:29 pm
The first type of fake person - what if that is how you really are? What if you don't have a core personality, and only have one that's subjective based on who you're talking to?

I've been known to be of the second variety, but only when something serious catches me off-guard. This is almost always when I ask someone something just to make conversation and they start rambling about something serious, and I'm left nodding politely and thinking, "I couldn't care less about all of this; I was just making conversation. I wonder when he's going to shut the hell up."
For example, I was at work about to leave for the day when one of my coworkers at the customer service desk pointed to a lady and asked if I could help her out before I leave because she had been waiting there for a while. So I go around the desk and ask if I could help her. The first thing she says is that I'm very nice but that my coworker working behind the service desk made her want to cry when she said "can you help that lady." She talked about being mistreated and what she would do were she the manager for about ten minutes as I nodded politely and feigned interest in her monologue. When I finally found a spot to tactfully ask why she came to the store, she presented a fax machine that had a missing cartridge. Then she went on to talk about this car accident she was in, her resulting coma, the doctors' attitudes, the deaths of every member of her family, her trouble in buying the car in which she had the accident, the attitudes in general of people driving winnebagos, spiritual "energy balance crap," her time in medical school, her time spent with patients as a psychiatrist... the lady would not stop talking for another 45 minutes. She was just monologuing. She was sensitive enough a person that I needed a particularly appropriate spot to bring up the reason she was there, so I spent the whole time with a plastic smile, feigned interest, and feigned sympathy. I probably could've convinced her that I was actually an angel come down from on high by the time she left. You can bet that the next thing I did was talk behind her back to my coworkers and my family.

So if it was a fake sympathy kind of thing... maybe she didn't care, got sucked in, and remained polite so she wouldn't hurt your feelings.
I'm very, very like this. I can relate to absolutely anyone, at any time, because I change modes depending upon who I talk to. I've learned to adapt in that way because of my customer-base; It's so diverse, that I need to shift and improvise with each person to maximize sales. Everyone loves me, and why? Not because I'm generally likable, because, really, I'm rather lackluster and unimpressive, but because who I am when I'm around you is palatable, and even likable. In fact, I hate blunt people much in the same way - I find them rather tactless and boorish most of the time. A lot of people who come into my store thing I'm the second coming, because I'll do shit just like Suki here does - It doesn't mean that I'm necessarily backstabbing you or whispering behind your back, but if one of my customers pulls one of those 45-minute monologues (And oh, yes, they are oh-so-frequent), you can bet the second you hit the door, I'ma slump over, call you a whore, and repeat the phrase "for FORTY-FIVE MINUTES, man" a few times too many. It's another person's nature, and it's an entirely valid one, I think.

Beyond that, very much like what Suki said, I don't really have a core personality. If you put me in a completely white room, alone, with only one way out, I would likely never, ever find that way out, because I'm a social creature by nature, and without another person in that room with me, I would probably just sit there until I starved. I take on the personalities of people that I'm around. If you talk with a southern drawl, and hang around me for an hour or two, I'll take on a southern drawl, as well. If you're all bubbly and happy, I'll be the same. It's something that makes me far more adaptable and far more likable than the average person - People are almost forced to like me. People like me are fantastic at damage control, and feed off of others. If I don't have someone else around to do stuff for, I don't do it. If no one calls me, I don't call anyone. The only real initiative that I've ever taken is for the sake of others; For instance, it took a bet with Clovic to get me to stop eating at Chipotle - I'd made numerous promises to myself to stop, but why should I? Not for me. When I have a day off, it's spent sitting around. Why? Because no one else has anything for me to do. I'm reliant on other people to tell me who I am. It's what makes me the people's champion, everyone loves me because everyone can relate to me in a significant way.

#14132 1 2007-02-19T08:57:15Z Kablizzy


Good morning! Welcome to week seven.

This week, the theme will be Chaingun Drones. Chaingun Drones are perhaps the least-respected of the drones, and they are perhaps the most versatile. Their random nature tends to put people off, and they are often used incorrectly, but with care and careful planning, Chaingun Drones can be the most useful enemies in the game.

Announcements:
- After a one-week hiatus, we are back online!
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, February 27th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Homing Launchers

Administrators:
  • Kablizzy
  • Clovic
  • KinGAleX
Rules:
  • All submissions must be entered into NUMA.
  • Each submission must have a link to the map placed here.

  • Week 7: Chaingun Drones

  • Week 6: No Active Enemies
  • Week 5: Alternate Routes
  • Week 4: Drone Paths

Map: Expanse 16-4 Totally Repwnd
Author: AMomentLikeThis
Original Map: Expanse 16-4: Fritz
  • (0-10) Fun: 4/10 - I'm not sure, I didn't really have a good time playing through this. It has all of the elements of a good mine jumper, but the thwumps just spoiled the fun for me entirely. It would've been fine without the flying boxes of doom, but as it was, it just didn't strike me as something I would want to enjoy playing through more than a few times.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 6/10 - The map fell on the high side of difficult for me. As I said above, it has all the elements of a good mine jumper, but those thwumps just skewed the map in a direction that it didn't want to go.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 5/10 - The map really didn't wow me any. It was a pretty straight-forward idea, and nothing revolutionary was done with it. The mine-jumper was accentuated by the thwumps, but I think it could have been quite a bit better. Coupled with the Ninja and the Exit/Terminal being in the same spot as the original map, I think this could've been done quite a bit better.
  • (0-10) Execution: 7/10 - I really enjoyed how you remixed the map. One of the main issues with the original map was the ease with which you could beat it, and how the right side defeated the purpose of the map. While I disagreed with that, I think that you made a good attempt at bringing the nature of the map to where you felt it belonged, and for that, I think the ReMix was pretty well thought-out.
  • (0-10) Other: 6/10 - I really liked the mine placement, and I thought that you should be commended on spending enough time to know how and where to get it right.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 28/50

Map: Happy glass lever dog
Author: bhauth
Original Map: Shy glass lever dog
  • (0-10) Fun: 4/10 - The map was decently fun, but the only real part of the map that was overwhelmingly so was the existing part, at the bottom. The one-way thwump combination was interesting, but something with it felt lacking, in a sense, especially with that homing launcher getting at you on the bottom. The last bounceblock area was more a pain than anything, and overall, I just didn't quite think that it did anything for the original, and were it a lone map, I don't think it would be able to hold its own.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 5/10 - Upping the difficulty of the map seemed to be a mistake here, and while I think the mistake was rather with remixing one of the greatest maps in existence from one of the greatest mapmakers ever, making the map more difficult didn't seem to make the map any more enjoyable at all. I think a big drawback of the maps thusfar in the contest is the map choice. We seem to have chosen the greatest maps, which, in a contest like this, would be akin to ReMixing the Mona Lisa. When you shoot for a map that can't really get much better, any changes that you make to it will almost undoubtedly make the map worse.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 4/10 - Nothing really happened to the map, except added and unneccesary difficulty. The remainder of the map stayed the same, but nothing was added to the map that didn't seemingly detract from it. I think a better way to go with the map would've been a conceptual ReMix, since a literal ReMix really can't do anything that the original did any better.
  • (0-10) Execution: 2/10 - As I said above, I think a different map choice would have been far more ideal for this type of map. It really didn't seem like anything fit very well at all. Sorry, man.
  • (0-10) Other: 4/10 - I liked the effort you put into playtesting the level.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 19/50

#14240 1 2007-02-26T20:20:44Z Kablizzy


Good morning! Welcome to week eight.

This week, we'll be focusing upon E-tiles. Insofar as tilesets go, you may not use any tiles except E-tiles and open space. Any amount and type of objects are viable, but the tilesets must be blocked. You may not use any 5-tiles, only blocks and spaces. Deadline extended by 24 hours this week, due to the thread going up a tad late. With that said, go, go, go!

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Wednesday, February 27th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Homing Launchers

Administrators:

  • Clovic

Rules:

#301383 91 2007-02-26T20:47:09Z Kablizzy
Map: Guess Who
Author: max_ride
Original Map: The Underworld part XVIII: Cave of Spirits
  • (0-10) Fun: 5/10 - It was decently fun, but some of the portions felt really, really forced. It didn't feel like they were calculated, and in a lot of places where a single rocket would do, there were two. Where a single mine would have done, there were three. Better placement would have helped this map out immensely, as there were a lot of places where you could have done things in a much more aesthetically-pleasing manner, as well as a manner where they would be far more fun. There were a couple places in the map where I wondered where the Hell to go, and the only way I could find out what was going on was getting blindsided by a thwump that I had no idea was going to come at me. Again, it seemed like you guys took the best maps you could, and ReMixing the best maps you can find is only going to hurt your chances to be able to better that map. Now, that's not to say that you should have gone and picked a noob map, but it would have worked a lot better if the map choices were better.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 6/10 - On the high side of mediocre, it was pretty good, but the difficulty problem really comes when comparison with the original map comes into play. Contextually, you made the map a lot more difficult than it needed to be. The original map was rather minimalistic in nature, and the addition of all of these errant elements really seemed to hurt the map, both difficulty and fun-wise.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 7/10 - It was definitely creative, though. You turned the map into... almost a race map, and with not too much effort, and that was a pretty refreshing jump in innovation for me.
  • (0-10) Execution: 3/10 - I think the map could have gone in fourteen different directions, and it just seemed like the way you picked to ReMix it was not the most flattering.
  • (0-10) Other: 5/10 - Nothing extra to say, really, except that I think that the map was pretty middle-of-the-road.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 26/50
#301387 92 2007-02-26T21:04:47Z Kablizzy
Map: Tribal Men Say
Author: frogs
Original Map: Pillar
  • (0-10) Fun: 9/10 - I was shocked by how much fun I had with this map. The aesthetics looked good at first, but the double-rocket launchers in an enclosed space rather turned me off. But after playing through the map even a handful of times, I really got into the groove and started liking the map more and more. I really didn't notice any of your maps before this, but I really, thoroughly enjoyed this.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 7/10 - It was a tad on the hard side for my tastes, though. I think that a single rocket on the right, with a bit better placement, and a bit more of an open shot and room for tracing would have worked incredibly well here. Another problem I had was the spike in difficulty on the right, as opposed to the drop in difficulty on the left, but overall, it stayed pretty good throughout.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 8/10 - I thought this was pretty brilliant. I'm a big fan of aesthetics, as people know, and this was very, very pleasing to me. I never liked the design of the original, but LV is one of those mappers who can break all the rules, and still come out with a fun map. But with this, you seemed to take the map, turn it into something unique and original, and you kept the aesthetics at a pleasing level. Good job.
  • (0-10) Execution: 9/10 - It was surprising to see such an off-take of such a good original map. The way LV does things would probably throw most people off as to how to ReMix a map of his, but I think you nailed it just as well as anyone could've nailed it. It seemed to keep the spirit of the original, while incorporating a whole, entirely new level of play to it, and I think that your version topped out on the original pretty famously.
  • (0-10) Other: 8/10 - I thought the gold placement was superb, and the update to the tileset was done really well. I thought the squeeze was a bit uncharacteristic, but it wasn't something that so much detracted from the map as it just distracted a bit. Good, solid entry.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 41/50

Author: apg
Original Map: Amorphous
  • (0-10) Fun: 6/10 - I wasn't all that thrilled with what came of this, and here's why; It was innovative, it was quirky, it had flair, it had aesthetic design, it just didn't have that replay value. With that said, the minimalism and the simplicity really seemed to work pretty well here.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 7/10 - Gotta admit, this was too easy. As I said above, some errant drones may have spiced it up a bit. However, the difficulty (Or apparent lack thereof) didn't really detract from the overall fun and theme of the level. I really liked that about the map. The original was pretty difficult, and the downshift in difficulty seemed to be a good direction to go. Beyond that, with the unorthodox nature of the map, I think it could have done well to not necessarily be more difficult, per se, but a bit more creative with the challenges. Again, the minimalism plays very well into this area, and it was definitely good as it is, but the prime version of the map that I'm envisioning in my mind could have still been very minimalistic whilst still containing some additional ideas and challenges, perhaps a multiple route or two, an Easter Egg route, and so on.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 10/10 - This was absolutely brilliant. I think that you did a fantastic job of separating the elements from the original, making this version your own, and giving the genius and unique twist that I'm sure that no one else could have done with their other entries. This, even this early, gets my pick for Best Creative Map, just because the idea came into your head to ReMix it in such a way as this, and to pull it off as well as you did was just amazing.
  • (0-10) Execution: 7/10 - I thought there were a couple different ways you could have taken the map, neither of which would have been as creative, but both of which would probably have had more of a replay factor, and it probably would have been a bit more multi-dimensional, even though it would have lost some of the creativity that makes it unique.
  • (0-10) Other: 7/10 - I really liked the aesthetic appeal of the gold, and how you took the objectset and made it your own. Good job overall.

#14295 1 2007-03-05T06:04:15Z Kablizzy


Good morning! Welcome to week nine.

This week, we'll be focusing upon Survival Maps. Survival maps are the types of maps where there is either no exit, or some function where the player must survive a certain period of time before continuing to the exit. Survival Maps have suffered a bit of a downfall as of late, and I'd like to bring them back with the furiousness.

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, March 6th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote

  • (0-10) Other: 6/10 - I really liked how the platforms became more precarious, but disliked the idea at the same time.   • (0-10) Fun: 6/10 - The fun factor here seemed a bit lacking, and I think I know why. The bottom part was great, but upon reaching the outer portion of the map, the rockets up top did their jobs a bit too well. The empty space looks too cluttered, but beyond that, it plays cluttered. In a game based upon flow and upon movement, restrictions of movement like this tend to detract from the experience as a whole. The center area with the gauss and gold was nice, but again, the restricted movements were especially prominent here. Now, with all that said, the map was still really fun, and even dying to the rockets was a treat sometimes. I think placement was great, although it could've been a bit more sparse, but overall decent job.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 6/10 - The map wasn't so much difficult as it was difficult in spikes. The difficulty was pretty steady throughout the first portion of the map, but as I said above, upon getting out to the edges, the rockets would hunt you down. And, this would be a big deal if the flow of movement were open, as in the original. In atob's version, the launch pads provided an easy escape from said rockets, and the high-flying antics of the original were especially missed in this version. So, on top of that, once you get the rocket patterns down, the map is a breeze, and that kind of affects the fun factor in a negative way.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 6/10 - There wasn't really anything wowing about the map mix, it was rather standard, and, while this map was a difficult one to mix well, I think that there were at least a couple different ways it could've gone to give it more flavour and zest.
  • (0-10) Execution: 5/10 - I really expected better from a mapper of your caliber. I think map choice played into this a bit, but the above factors just threw the map off, it seemed to want to go in a different direction than you took it.
  • (0-10) Other: 5/10 - Nothing much to add here.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 28/50

#303444 100 2007-03-08T10:29:39Z Kablizzy
Map: Rants St.
Author: bufar
Original Map: Mixed Drinks
  • (0-10) Fun: 4/10 - Hoo boy, what to say about this. I really didn't like it at all. I'm not generally a fan of these type of maps, but even so, I made every attempt to be as objective as I can with this. I can see where the fun is supposed to be, but this just isn't the type of map that I can do. When I play N, I look for a map that will give me the best time, and special map types have really never done that for me. You all know my reputation for hating jumper puzzles, puzzles in general, survival maps, Boss maps (Way back when), and all other kinds of odd maps (Hell, I've even come to hate my own WraNgler series), but even so, it was enjoyable seeing how my demos would turn out. But personal biases aside, while playing through the map, the instructions for the map took far more of the center stage than the actual map and gameplay did. The editing steps for the ninja and the time spent trying to figure out what the map was intended to do was a bit of a pain.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 5/10 - Again, this was just not my type of thing, but all that aside, I think this was a bit on the hard side. And, I do understand that the point is more or less about the difficulty of making the demo, and the ensuing reward. However, with this type of map, it is so difficult to balance exactly how hard a given task is going to end up being.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 9/10 - I thought you did a fantastic job turning the map on its head and bringing a new flavour to it, while still staying true to the element of the original. The alternating doors seemed to work great, the mine placement was superb, and I just thought it was a brainstorm overall.
  • (0-10) Execution: 8/10 - You seemed to do a great job of keeping everything in order, keeping it simple, yet challenging, complex and minimalistic all in the same map. Absolutely superb way of taking the map to the next level.
  • (0-10) Other: 8/10 - I freakin' loved the design, the tileset was innovative and stylish, and the fact that you took this map, conceptualized it, remade it in your own way, and brought it out flavourfully and the fact that you had this in the MNNM for fuggin' symmetry, of all things, is just a mindblower.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 34/50
#303446 101 2007-03-08T10:50:06Z Kablizzy
Map: Bravery
Author: McP3000
Original Map: Burn Bolt
  • (0-10) Fun: 8/10 - Loved it, I really did. I thought the flow was great, and while there were a couple places where a couple pixels made the difference between a ledge and a mine, I had a blast playing through it. It was a great play-through, and I could definitely see something like this making it into the main game, as perhaps a column-ender.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 7/10 - Difficulty spikes kinda hurt the map, and the length really got it in the difficulty area. The difficulty was relatively flat, overall, but sometimes, you can maximize too much space in order to make the map that much longer, and then putting a spike at the end makes for some frustrating times. I think a shorter map would have suffered a lot less from difficulty problems. With that said, I think the rocket and gausses could have been placed a bit better, but overall, a decent job of keeping the difficulty where it should've been.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 7/10 - Wasn't really the most innovative of things, but in ReMixing the map, the entire flavour of the map switched up, and it seemed like a good way to take things. I think you could have gone a bit easier on the mines, especially the ones that wouldn't have come into play as much, but overall, really good stuff. Even though you didn't change the tileset much, with a couple tweaks to the objects, you were able to pull off an entirely new and unique map that was able to take on its own aura on.
  • (0-10) Execution: 8/10 - Everything seemed to come together well, but one thing really stood out to me. Splitting the final room into two sections really, really felt like a good move. It seemed like the map just wanted to do that, and when I finally got there, I just nodded in approval, like, "Yeah, this fits." Other than that, good stuff.
  • (0-10) Other: 7/10 - The original had a lot more going for it, aesthetically. I'm a big subscriber to minimalist theory, and the whole "less is more" camp, and I don't think the ideas have failed me yet - In either case, I think you could've done more with less on the map. You did some really cool effects with the tileset, but I think you could've shortened the length up a bit, and it would've flown (Flowed?) quite a bit better.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 37/50

#14413 1 2007-03-12T08:36:34Z Kablizzy


Good morning! Welcome to week ten.

The theme this week will be Unfinished Tilesets. I always adored NedCon #3's theme of manipulating existing tilesets, and I wanted to bring that to life here in the season's last installment. Each tileset was purposefully constructed to be unfinished, and there are a couple of rules for the maps, listed below. We will be taking a two-week break after this week, to discuss the second season and to compile all of the current week's maps in a single format.

http://numa.notdot.net/map/82187
http://numa.notdot.net/map/82188
http://numa.notdot.net/map/82189

- You may move the ninja.
- You may not subtract from the tileset.
- You may, however, add to the tileset.

Now, since this is the last week of the season, there is a special stipulation: Each participant may submit up to two maps this week. In fact, I would like to see people do more than one map, because I purposefully made the tilesets so that they were rather open-ended, but at the same time, themed.

Announcements:
- This week will mark the end of Season one.
- Each participant may submit two maps this week.
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, March 13th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote

#305016 104 2007-03-13T21:34:32Z Kablizzy
Map: Rue the Remixed Whirl
Author: AMomentLikeThis
Original Map: Rue the Whirl
  • (0-10) Fun: 6/10 - It was pretty dang fun. I loved the implementation of the mines and floorguards over the original to give it a more linear feel, but this map suffers the same fate as the original does, which is once you get it, and once you beat it, there's really nothing more to the map. And given that there is only one distinct route (Yes, the right side is possible, but not within 90 seconds, and not for lil' ol' me.), it limits the map horribly, especially when that route is a precision jump. So, decent, but I think map-choice could've been better.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 3/10 - This is an example of difficulty gone wrong. Even with the initial map, the difficulty of the map stays constant, spikes ferociously, and then drops off again. It really should just be that one jump, the switch, and the exit, that's all the map would need, difficulty-wise. Even in the original, this was a problem, and while the map was pretty fun-filled and creamy, it's one of those maps that just doesn't fulfill the difficulty slot well.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 7/10 - You did a decent job, I absolutely loved what you did with the tileset, and again, the floorguards and addition of mines was great. Didn't like the trap-door drone thing at the top, but that's a small part of the map. Overall pretty decent stuff.
  • (0-10) Execution: 6/10 - I really thought you could've gone a number of different ways with the map that just didn't seem to pan out. You did pretty well, just nothing new and overly exciting, it was just the same map.
  • (0-10) Other: 6/10 - The tileset looked really really good, but partly due to the fact that the original was such an innovative tileset. Points anyway.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 28/50

Original Map: Fluid Dynamics

  • (0-10) Other: 5/10 - Nothing much more to say here. Edit: That's not true. I freaking loved the map name. Absolutely magnificent.

#305086 107 2007-03-14T02:52:12Z Kablizzy
Map: Dictator School
Author: MaximumRide
Original Map: Bubblegum
  • (0-10) Fun: 5/10 - Quite a bit of fun, and under normal circumstances, I would've loved this thing, but there were a few parts that just didn't do it for me. Rockets and tunnels just isn't where it's at, and gausses and tunnels either. The map felt very cramped, and very limitating. In a map like this, it likely would have benefited from minimalism and the whole "less-is-more" doctrine. By the same token, there could have been less action up at the top, as the whole map felt imbalanced by the open bottom and the enclosed top. By the same token, having to loop around three-quarters of the map just to reset a floorguard got a bit tedious, the bottom and top-side switches really weren't placed all that well, the exit switches were atrocious to get to, that along with the rockets really just ruins the ending.... It just got hung up in a lot of places. With that said, and with all the rules that it broke, it had a very MTI-ish quality to it, in that, even though it broke these rules, it did well in what it was supposed to do.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 6/10 - I found this rather too hard. The rockets on the sides would just lock on, and wouldn't let go, and the four tunnels that they followed you into would just get you every time. The thwump/angles were a nice addition, but provided for unneeded deaths, and the floor guards at the bottom may have been better served being consolidated into a single guard, in the middle, with the launchpads raised on the 5-tiles. A couple extra design issues could have been solved by lowering the middle set a tile or two down, making the tunnel easier, and I think that making it possible to obtain the exit switches, and plow through into the middle, and use that jumppad to get to the exit would've been fantastic. A lot of times, in a competition like this, our verdict on difficulty will almost always be "too hard" rather than "too easy."
  • (0-10) Creativity: 8/10 - I thought you brought it to the table here. You mixed things very well, and had a good head to turn this map on its head. Good concept.
  • (0-10) Execution: 7/10 - With that said, as I said under "fun," I think a lot of things could have gone a handful of different directions and been far more effective. With that said, it was very stylistic and the design was great, but it definitely could have been much, much better.
  • (0-10) Other: 5/10 - Pretty average map, due to the drawbacks, could've been better.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 31/50

HERE COME THE PRIZES!

As with the Legacy: Origins contest, we mentioned some Mystery Prizes at the start of this contest, which were revealed then, since you all already knew what they were going to be. The first of which, of course, is that our top three participants will be immortalized in the N Hall of Fame, alongside all of the other greats that have been, and will be, inducted into the N Hall of Fame.

The second mystery prize, which was earned by Caero alone, is the chance to participate in the Legacy Team's Next big thing - The Zenith Levelpack! Alongside the Expanse release, we foretold of a third pack that is already in the works - Which will carry the final 300 maps to complete the triumvirate at 1000 total maps.

And finally, here are the prizes (Please host these on your own, and save them to your computers, they may disappear otherwise)! Those who placed in both Legacy: Origins and Legacy: Expanse receive their very-own signature tag as well! There is something else in the works for those who finished both Legacy: Origins and Legacy: Expanse, and word on the street is that it ties in to the Zenith contest! With that said, enjoy!

For all of the Top 20:



For Dual-Finalists:



For Caero:



For lord_day:



For Cerberus:



Custom Title Requests are due to myself or Littleviking001 via PM, and Dedication maps for Caero, lord_day, and Cerberus are forthcoming, both on NUMA, and in the Zenith pack.

For the three of you who won Shirts, PM me, and we'll get that taken care of.

Now, on to Future News! Currently, we are working on Zenith, of course, and working on finishing up on NedCon 8, which will be our last NedCon. Sweep and I are also working rigorously on getting me everything I need for this year's Dronies (Nominations always being accepted!), I'm redesigning the Legacy Site as much as I can muster with each day, and we are in the works with a new contest that will pit teams against each other for the grand prize - A map in the Zenith map-pack!

But the real news is the other top-secret projects that we've begun on. They're so far removed from everything else we've done, it's pretty amazing. Those of you who read The Real N on a regular basis at the new site already know what this stuff is, in some form, and those of you who don't read on a regular basis should head on over to The Site and check things out!

Map: Electrolysis
Author: Pheidippides
Original Map: Lysis
  • (0-10) Fun: 4/10 - You made a beautiful, flowy map all about precision jumping and drone-dodging. Also, map choice was awful, like I said earlier on in the competition, some of you guys just picked the absolute best maps you could find, because they were your favourite maps.   • (0-10) Difficulty: 5/10 - Not so much difficult as it was rife with difficulty spikes, and that's a large minus.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 7/10 - Drone paths was a creative way to go here, I liked the concept. Everything else was rather generic.
  • (0-10) Execution: 4/10 - I thought this could have been done a lot a lot better. Also, again, map choice seemed to hinder where you wanted to go for the competition, and, on a pretty literal level, nothing happened to the tileset, and especially so in that nothing positive seemed to go into the tileset.
  • (0-10) Other: 5/10 - And everything else was rather average.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 25/50

#307938 112 2007-03-26T21:19:30Z Kablizzy
Map: you SO Are
Author: Aju
Original Map: You Are
  • (0-10) Fun: 7/10 - I really had a blast playing through this, but one drawback that I noted was that I didn't have as much fun as I did with the original. Beyond that, the map seemed empty, and the fun factor kinda suffered because it didn't feel like it was inspired. I mean, the map came out great anyway, but this is one of those instances where minimalist theory kinda falls apart - Just a single laser drone? I mean, I don't know what else you could have done to it, I just know that this one probably wasn't the best of it.
  • (0-10) Difficulty: 9/10 - This is perfect, insofar as difficulty goes. The fact that the laser drone can hit you at every step of the way is big, although you likely could have positioned it a tile or two more conservatively and had a bit better results.
  • (0-10) Creativity: 4/10 - I really can't say that this was very creative, though. It seems like something that I would do while remixing - starting off by deleting the mines, and with a lone laser drone in there, but it also seems to want to go other places beyond that. It seems like the map wants more than just the single drone in there, y'know?
  • (0-10) Execution: 7/10 - And again, despite these problems, the map turned out pretty great, in either way. It was fun, it was still quirky, solid entry.
  • (0-10) Other: 5/10 - No extra comments here.
COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 32/50

Map: The long road to success
Author: Collin_Janzen
Original Map: The Blue Danube
  • (0-10) Fun: 2/10 - Hoo boy, where to begin. First off, you NAN'd a mine while making the level, so the level couldn't have been presented in a way that is positive. COMPREHENSIVE SCORE: 10/50

#308333 44 2007-03-28T17:07:35Z Kablizzy
The only problem that I see with society defining a word is that it falls into the trap of things like "gay" and "1337" being *actual* words. Things like "yiff" would soon appear in dictionaries, and "niggerwagon" would make an appearance, given enough societal popularity. If the popular definition of "black" became "white," given societal views, and "stabbing" came to mean "innocent of murder," then how can language *ever* work? For instance, if the popular definition of "gay" becomes "bad," then gay would both mean "happy and high-spirited" and "homosexual of the male persuasion," and "bad." If, given enough time and usage, the term "gay niggerwagon yiffbucket" would appear in daytime sitcoms and in college-level theology texts.

Granted, this is an extreme example, but there should be some level of objective definitionalism in what a word means. Simply relying on society's definition of a given word destroys everything that language has to offer.

For instance, I love wordplay. I love coining phrases, and I do it quite often. I've coined the phrase, "nutfuck," meaning 'an orange thief, or a buffoon', and I've also coined "crooked straight," meaning "amazing beyond belief; orgasmic."

Of course, neither of those words *actually* mean anything, but in context with those who have heard me say either of them, those people know what they mean. However, even if everyone in the world began saying either or both, the meaning would be simply what everyone wants it to be. Which, okay, granted. That would be the societal beginnings of those two phrases. However, the terms "nut," "fuck," "crooked," and "straight" would all retain their original etymology and their original meaning. So, while Atheism might *societally* mean active denial of God, it will always hold the definitional meaning of "not theism."

So, yes, scholars do set the definitions, and atheism *should* mean, strictly, "not theism." The societal implications of it are irrelevant in high-level debate, mostly because the definition of things should be the only one that can be historically and etymologically agreed upon, since societal definitions are rarely, if ever agreed upon. Atheism could mean seven different things given a person's location, from New York to London to Tehran, and the only benchmark that *can* be used for debate is the scholarly definition.

Edit: A better example. The term "fudgepacker" means, societally, "one who gives anal sex." While, societally, this is fine, definitionally, the term "fudgepacker" means "One who packs fudge," without innuendo.

Quote: Ethrel, March 29, 2007 02:39 am
Kablizzy:
The general public does define language, however. If the definition of stabbing became 'innocent of murder', then the court of law would then find people stabbing rather than innocent. While in it's transistory stages, people would have other words to use, avoiding the conflict. That is the beauty of the english language, or any language really. Over the past 200 years, it has changed a lot, and it will continue to change and adapt over time. It will remain suited to our needs (the general public's needs). Sim ply because you want to believe that it is not happening, does not mean they are not. Look at your examples. Things like Yiff would become part of our dictionaries. Yes, exactly. If you say yiff, and everyone knows what it means, how is that different from having it actually published in some book? You need it published in order for it to exist? Simply not the case in reality. Yiff is a word, because society uses it, and it's definition is derived from society's mind (when I say society's mind, understand that I mean that the individuals in society agree, thus forming a certain mindset for the general public, A.K.A. society). such is the case here with atheist. If society believes it means something, then that is what it means simply because that is what everybody understands it to mean. The fact that it should not mean what society thinks is simply irrelevant.

Oh asnd simply because you believe that society should not define words and that it should mean whatever it is that it should when looking at the roots is also irrelevant. By using that as an argument, you are ignoring the reality of the world. The human mind controls the language, not the geneology of the word itself. Because of this fact, I also believe leet-speak and chat-speak will both become (either separately or combined) a language of it's own, recognized as such worldwide. I agree that it will be a sad day, however that is the truth of reality, which is hardly ever idealistic.

While good points, you overlook the fact that there can't be a completely variable definition. Again, regional differences come in nicely here. While "lift" means "to raise up" here in the states, it refers to an elevator in the UK. Without a scholarly, dictionary definition of the term, both and all interpretations of the word become entirely meaningless, because every word goes on to mean everything.

Your example on yiff fails in a vital way - Even if "everyone" agrees upon a definition, there will always be variance. That is why we have scholarly and idealistic definitions - To eliminate the confusion. That's why we have dictionaries - To tell us what these things are, definitionally. That's why societal views don't currently and can't ever define what a word is, was, and will be - It's the scholarly and analytical definition of said word that oversees what it is. When the scholarly view of these words adapts to what a word means, then it does indeed become that word. Take gay for instance, again. To be gay, 100 years ago, meant happy. Now it means homosexual, and it will soon become to mean "bad" as well. Why? Yes, because of the societal implications. But does gay mean "bad" now? No, under no circumstances. Why? It lacks the definition as such. Gay is not defined as "bad." When it is, then it will be accepted enough to mean, definitionally bad. But until then, it cannot.

In that same vein, yiff is not a word. Yiff will not be a word until it is accepted in the scholarly circle. Yiff is a colloquialism, and regarded as substandard. Thus, until it has the scholarly definition, it will stay a colloquialism, and will not be regarded, definitionally, as a word.

So, there can't ever be 100% societal truth to what a word means. It's not my personal belief that society shouldn't define what a word is, it just doesn't. There's always that threshold between societal acceptance and strict language. Idealistic as it may come across, there is a large distinction between what is, what should be, and what can be. This is a case of what is, rather than what should be. There's no ignorance to what the world throws at me, it's simply a case of "Bling" not being a word. And it won't be, regardless of societal acceptance. That threshold must be crossed first.

#314164 12 2007-04-19T03:45:07Z Kablizzy
Quote: DemonzLunchBreak, April 18, 2007 07:21 pm
The reason that I ask this is because omnipotence seems impossible on many levels when criticized logically. God is described in the Bible as omniscient and omnipotent. Well, for starters, this statement is redundant. To know something is a type of power, and a god with all powers would be able to have such a power. Obviously. But wait! It gets wackier!

If god is omniscient, then he obviously knows what he will do next. He is therefore unable to do anything else. There is something that he is then unable to do, and he is therefore not omniscient or not omnipotent. That would work, except that omnipotence implies omniscience. Omnipotence therefore does not exist.

Another side paradox:

Could god make an object that he can't move?
Could god make a taco so spicy that he can't eat it?
Could god overpower himself at his most powerful?

If god can make the object, then he can't move it, therefore he is not omnipotent. If god can't make the object, then there is something that he cannot do, and he is therefore not omnipotent. The same logic applies to the taco, or the overpowering.

What do you think? Does this logic imply that omnipotence is impossible?
First and foremost, human understanding of something infinite automatically kills your argument. Not you nor I nor anyone can understand the concept and execution behind omniscience or omnipotence, which, at the basest level, makes any anthropocentric analysis of the concept of a deity's "range" fail.

So, if God knows what he'll do next, that doesn't mean he can't do anything else. I don't get where that comes from. Knowledge of a universal dimension doesn't predispose that entity to not being able to interact with that dimension.

Your "Could God..." questions don't work either, unfortunately. Mostly for this reason; Can God exist and not exist at the same time? Can god exist outside of a paradox? What is the relation between omnipotence and paradoxes? Would God ever need to create a hypothetical situation where a paradox would be his own downfall? Can there exist two deities at the same time? Does God have strength? Does God taste? See? Hear? Take this into account; Is Omnipotence infinite? In the literal sense. Is Omnipotence literally an infinite gesture?

In either case, the logic fails on a couple of levels, and solely due to a lack in our own understanding of what a truly pure form of Omnipotence *might* be doesn't predispose any given answer.

Edit: Demonz, logically define God for me, if you will.

#314216 3 2007-04-19T09:08:09Z Kablizzy
The film portrays the persians *in the film* as transsexual cannibal monsters, and the greeks *in the film* as heroic and kickin'. That's protagonist/antagonist plot, and nothing more. Anyone who takes something else away from the film than what it is (Unless, of course, Leonidas turned to the camera, and said, "Filthy persians. Let's nuke 'em! *Ker-Wink*") is simply looking for trouble in places where trouble isn't there. As Dave so satirically put it, this has occurred many times in the past, most notably (And I suppose most recently) the portrayal of Jews in Mel Gibson's Passion of the Christ, but really? Was there really, seriously any portrayal there? Or was it just some dudes out in left field stretching to justify what they already think? People will go well out of their way to find causes and answers, effects and volleys for anything - This is no different. If there were a country today called "Persia," and a number of valid comparisons could be drawn directly between the movie and real-life folk, then an issue of slander or defamation may be quite relevant. But as it is? It's a sub-medieval portrayal of what seems to be an entirely fictitious story (I haven't seen it marketed as anything but loosely based upon historical events), and its avant-garde presentation seems to absolutely scream artistic endeavor. Those who read more than that into it are doing just that - Reading more into it.
