#17335 1 2007-09-27T03:23:38Z Kablizzy
This thread is for our composers. If you can compose music, both for yourself, and (More importantly) for others, sign in here. If you do more than one (Compose and Edit, for instance), please sign in to both threads.

Please, in this thread, only post once. If you have questions, pose them in general discussion.

Now, for you guys, what you'll be doing for the project is directing. We'll have a head producer that's going to oversee the project, and then we're going to have the rest of you guys work with individual musicians in order to produce differing levels of composition for the project.

You guys will be the visionaries, you guys will be dictating where the project goes, and beyond the individual projects that we'll do, you guys will be overseeing each individual piece. Now, depending upon how many of you will be composing, each of you will be responsible for a number of songs.

The first thing you should do, as a composer, is sign in here! Once we know how many composers, musicians, and editors we have, we'll divide you guys into groups of at least one composer, one musician, and one editor each.

The second thing you'll want to do is put up a thread for your group's project. This is where the individual compositions will be happening. Within the thread, we'll be getting together teams of musicians to create the pieces that you'll be composing for. This will be in addition to the individual projects that we'll be working on. I'm thinking that each team will only have to do a single composition, since it's such a big task, and since we'll likely be doing one or two individual compositions each.

Thirdly, you guys will need to keep in touch with me to be sure your group projects are flowing along nicely. I'll be trying to give you guys themes to follow for the pieces, but it's up to you guys (The composers) to be sure everything is on-beat and it's up to the editors to make sure it all sounds good. I'll allow for a lot of creative freedoms for these things, but I don't want the songs to be dance mixes, or anything like that. This stuff needs to be very up-to-par with my expectations, and if it isn't I'll let you guys know what's going on in my head so that we can get together and fix things.

And finally, it's your job to keep in touch with the other members of the group, and to make sure things are moving along nicely.

Beyond that, keep active, keep in touch with me, and welcome!
#17336 1 2007-09-27T03:23:43Z Kablizzy
Hey all, and welcome to the Metanet Orchestra. Use this thread to discuss any errant concerns, pose questions, and so on.

Objectives -

First and foremost - We'll be doing music for a number of different projects, the first of which being for the Legacy-produced Knytt Stories level. As such, the vast majority of what we're going to be doing for this is going to be strictly instrumental. Almost all of the music will be ambient in nature, and it should mostly fill the role of background music - With the exception of intro/cutscene/ending credits, most of the music will be filling the role of classical pieces, but we'll also be doing a lot of jazz, some electronica, a few rock pieces, and we're going to try and make each of the pieces unique and innovative - That's what we're looking for here. Innovation.

Secondly, we'll be doing some individual pieces so you all can get a good idea of where we want the project to go. I would like for you all (Those of you who can, that is) to download Knytt Stories, if for no other reason than to hear the music and understand where we want things to go. For thsoe of you who can't download Knytt Stories, I can put all of the music and ambience together (They're .ogg files, so they may need conversion) in a .zip file and host it for you guys to hear.

Anyway, for this stage, each of you will be doing at least one individual song to specification. Classical Musicians might be seeing a lot more action during this stage, since the individual pieces will likely be piano- or classical types, and most will be pretty easy to pull off.

Next, we're going to be dividing ourselves into three groups - Composers, Musicians, and Editors. The composers will be overseeing the individual projects, directing what direction each song takes. The Musicians will be working closely with the Composers to create these pieces, and once each part is finished, the editors will piece everything together, add theme and ambience, and make everything a finished product. These tracks will likely be more complex, but will still focus upon background music, but these can be a lot more abstract and will probably end up being our theme music for the level.

So, third, we'll probably be putting all of these songs into a compilation Metanet album, so these songs that we're going to create will not only have to work for Knytt stories, but they've got to be relatively standalone. For those of you who were around for "It's Dave!", this will be pretty similar in form.


Tools -

Knytt Stories - Knytt Stories is perhaps the main thing you want to be familar with, at least in some form. If you have the ability to play .ogg files, then simply go into the Knytt Stories download directory (If you put it where I put mine, it'll just be C:\Program Files\Knytt Stories), and search through the data files, under "Ambiance" and "Music". The easier wa to go about this is to open up the level editor, and cycle through the music (To do this, when you open the level editor, you can either load an existing level, or create a new one. On the left, you should see "Music," "Atmos A," and "Atmos B." Left-clicking on the numbers beside these cycles through the music and ambience tracks. Holding down the music/ambience buttons will play the track, or setting the number of music/ambience that you want to play and holding down the "play all" button will play the selected music track and selected ambience all at once - To let you hear how things mesh together.

Now, if you have a Mac, sorry - Knytt Stories is PC-only. But as I said above, I can compile the .ogg files from Knytt Stories, .zip 'em up, and host them somewhere.

OverClocked ReMix - Fantastic place to find inspiration, and to get a feel for what I want out of video game music. Are there any games from your youth whose songs you can recall, even now? That's the type of stuff I want. I can still remember almost the entire Chrono Trigger Soundtrack, and Final Fantasy 6 sticks with me to this day. This has happened with a lot of games over the years, and I want to create a similar theme. The tracks on OCR are available in a number of ways - You can get them through the site individually, you can download the torrents (Which are HUUUUUUUUUGE, but well well worth it), or you can head over to Last FM and download the songs individually from there. You can also browse their site for a specific game's music, and see what the artists have done there.

SoundSnap - SoundSnap is one of those places where people congregate and upload a bunch of different sounds for musical purposes. Now, you may be asking, "Why don't you just use some of the 30,000+ files there?" Well, I want original stuff from you guys, and I want it to be a lot more unique than the common stuff that SoundSnap has. So, I warn you in advance - use this sparingly, and only if you absolutely have to.

FindSounds - FindSounds is an internet search engine specifically tuned to finding sound clips on the Internet. It's very useful for the types of things that we'll be doing. Beyond that, FindSound Palettes does the same thing, except it allows you to edit music and categorize it - But I believe that Palettes costs cash, so use this at your own risk. Again, I'd like for us to come up with our own unique stuff instead, but we can always augment it with stuff from here.

Of course, there are other sites, like the Freesound Project, and ccMixter, and there are some great audio editing programs out there (Of which I only really know of Garageband and Audacity, I'll let you guys post the ones you use), although I've heard that some of these programs deal in copyrighted material (Namely, Garageband - If this is false, quell my fears), so let's be careful with what we use, alrighty?

Now, let's have a bitchload of fun, and welcome!

Please, in this thread, only post once. If you have questions, pose them in general discussion.

Now, for you guys, what you'll be doing for the project is playing the music. You guys will each be doing an individual piece as well as a group piece, and if you have time and motivation to do more, then we'll do more. The key to this whole project is contact. Keep in close contact with me, whether via PM, E-mail, IM, or through the subforum here - We need to be able to stay on-track, and we all need to be able to set aside the time to get this project completed.

The first thing you should do, as a musician, is sign in here! Once we know how many composers, musicians, and editors we have, we'll divide you guys into groups of at least one composer, one musician, and one editor each.

The second thing you'll want to do, once we get groups assigned, is get in touch with your composer in their composer thread, and start thinking about what kinds of tunes we're going to be composing in the groups, and then once that gets done, we'll start recording individual parts, and the editors will mesh them together.

Thirdly, you guys will need to keep in touch with me to be sure your individual projects are flowing along nicely. I'll be trying to give you guys themes to follow for the pieces, but it's up to you guys to be sure everything is on-beat and it's going to be up to the editors to make sure it all sounds good. I'll allow for a lot of creative freedoms for these things, but I don't want the songs to be dance mixes, or anything like that. This stuff needs to be very up-to-par with my expectations, and if it isn't I'll let you guys know what's going on in my head so that we can get together and fix things.

Fourthly, for your individual projects, ask me as many questions as you need to, and then just play. I know that we have a harp player, and really, a piece with just the harp would be freakin' amazing to me. Same with just a piano. Also, if you think your instrument might be lacking, lemme know. I'll hook you up with one of the editors to give you a drumbeat to work with, or hook you up with one of the composers to give you a part to play - Anything that I can do to make this easier on you, I'll do.

#17340 1 2007-09-27T05:01:53Z Kablizzy
This thread is for our editors. If you can edit music (Which means being able to use music-editing programs, combine tracks, add drumbeats, and so on), then sign in here. If you do more than one (Edit and Compose, for instance), please sign in to both threads. In this thread, make sure you list what programs you can use, and a short sampling of what you can do (For instance, being able to mesh tracks together would be foremost, having the ability to convert sound files would be another) with the editing programs.

Please, in this thread, only post once. If you have questions, pose them in general discussion.

Now, for you guys, what you'll be doing for the project is finalizing everything. For all of the individual projects, and for all of the group projects, you guys will need to be able to make everything sound professional. If volumes are too high on a track, or if a drumbeat is too prominent, you guys will need to be able to equalize things, and make the tracks sound great. From my experience with editors and editing software, if you're good at it, you can make anything sound good.

The first thing you should do, as an editor, is sign in here! Once we know how many composers, musicians, and editors we have, we'll divide you guys into groups of at least one composer, one musician, and one editor each.

The second thing you'll want to do, once we get groups assigned, is get in touch with your composer in their composer thread, and start thinking about what kinds of tunes we're going to be composing in the groups, and then once that gets done, we'll start recording individual parts, and you guys will mesh them together.

Thirdly, you guys will need to dictate to your groups and to the individual projectiers whether or not they're on-track. If something sounds horrible (If the track has too much static), let them know that you'll have to edit the track to minimize that.

Fourthly, you guys will need to be able to make the tracks sound good. For instance, if we have a jazz piece with a Trumpet, a Guitar, and a Trombone, you'll have to overlay the tracks in a way that makes them sound fantastic and finished.

And finally, it's your job to keep in touch with the other members of the group, and to make sure things are moving along nicely.

Beyond that, keep active, keep in touch with me, and welcome!

#369035 19 2007-10-02T09:56:05Z Kablizzy
Okay, let's get started!

I think we've got everyone in that's going to be in - For those of you just getting in, play a bit of catch-up, and spend some time going through the pinned threads. Make sure you hit up the sign-in threads so I know where to put you guys in the groups.

For those of you already here, likewise - sign in to your appropriate threads. If you guys don't know where to sign in, just ask.

Also, everyone be sure to hit up the roster thread, make sure you're there - I'm going to be using that list a lot, so if something is missing or wrong, let me know ASAP.

First off, I'd like to introduce you to the project manager, Borealis! He, along with myself, LV, and Sendy will be overseeing this project. If you need anything, just ask here or hit one of us up via PM or IRC, and we'll get things going through those means.

Now, let's start with individual projects - You guys will each be responsible for at least one individual piece with your best instrument. For instance, weisslenny is a harpist, so the main thing I'll want from him is a harp piece. Those of you who create synthetic and digital music, feel free to follow in Brttrx's footsteps and drop a handful of songs.

An important thing to note here, and someone clarify this for me before we move forward: If you're using copyrighted loops to create your music, please don't. I believe that programs like GarageBand come with loops for music creation - Drum Loops, Synth Loops, Froot Loops... Well, I've heard a couple rumours that programs like that may copyright their material. So, if we can confirm whether they do or not, that would be great.

Now, you guys will have a good deal of creative liberty with this stuff, but if something doesn't sound good to me, I might ask you to revise a piece. Now, the first thing you guys are going to record is a rough draft. It doesn't have to be perfect form or pitch, it just needs to be something that gives me an idea of what you want to do for your individual piece. I realize that not every instrument can stand alone as well, so don't freak out if you're playing a tripod, and are worried about getting a piece together from that. Also, for those of you who can't really compose your own music for individual pieces, let me know, and I'll see if we can hook you up with a composer to compose something for you.

Everyone's individual rough draft pieces will have an initial deadline of October 15th - This gives you guys two weeks to get an idea, play/record/upload it, and post a thread for it here. If you're doing more than one individual piece, use a single thread, please. It'll keep the project nice and shiny.

Now, if you want more info on what I want for your particular instrument, post here or shoot me a PM. As a general rule, though, my response will be "Something unique, and unobtrusive," but I can go into further detail. You can also consult with Borealis, because he knows the score.

Once individual pieces rough drafts are up, I'll give some critique, and you guys will have another two weeks to polish the piece and get it more structured. If you need more time than that, let me know, and we'll extend the date. From there, we'll give two more weeks, and then two more, and two more, until we've all got finished pieces that we can roll with. Now, if you record something you don't really like, don't discard it, we may be able to use it for the group projects.

And speaking of which, group projects will start once everyone has signed in to a thread, and I'll give some additional instructions for those things.

So, I think that's all for now, any questions, concerns? If not, you have two weeks for your rough draft pieces.

We want to give the community something that they've never seen before, something that will make them think, "Wow, this is more awesome than anything else I've ever seen." Secondly, primarily action maps make it in - We want to make this Metanet++, and once all is said and done, all of the maps should flow in difficulty from 00-0 all the way up to 199-4 (Once we're done). If I remember right, you don't make too many jumpers so you're all good there.

Uhhh, what else - Unique tilesets are a big plus, they catch the eye and keep the player enthralled, and so on.

#372967 6 2007-10-19T06:13:51Z Kablizzy
Nineteen downloads, and two replies?

Man. I'll give this thing the ol' Legacy treatment.

00-0 Matchplay - Very nice, but suffers from the "hard opener" complex. Probably could've been a bit shorter.

00-1 Bing Bong the Wild Calling - Again, very nice. Something unique and fresh.

00-2 o_O - Wahahahahahahahahaha! Why wasn't this your opener, man? This thing's hilarious, easy, and fun as Hell..

00-3 Tileset Under Construction - Amazing thematics on these. The key, though, is to not run out of these ideas later in the pack as most levelpacks tend to.

00-4 A Watched Pot never Rings - o_O_O Holy freaking crap, that ending terrified me. I didn't like that part, but the rest was great.

01-0 Oct. - I guess I can see the theme, but I don't particularly like it. We have a bit of a rule in Legacy - if it uses bugs, glitches, or NaNs, it's a bad idea. We've broken the rule once or twice, and both instances have turned out worse than if we had done things the proper way.

01-1 HI - I love this tileset, but I think you could have done more with it. Still nice map.

01-2 F.R.A.C.T.U.R.E - Again, not really my kind of level, but very neat theme.

01-3 At the Behest of the Villagers - Nifty lil' level. Likes it.

01-4 Cocos - Definitely different. Good mine placement.

All in all, great start. Keep these up!

#375580 385 2007-10-30T21:21:08Z Kablizzy
Okay, fellas, we're coming down to the final stretch here. Here was my thought. I was looking through the maps the other day, and I thought, "Wait, if I've got close to 50 maps, and Tim's at 50, and Brad's at 50, and Dave, Tannar, Andrew, Alex, and Bracken all have 20 or so, and Sendy's got 40 in the Kablendy pack... Well, shit, we're almost to our goal already!

So, here's where I think we stand:

Tim: 50
Brad: 50
Myself: 40
Tannar: 20-25
Dave: 20-25
Andrew: 20-25
Bracken: 20-25
Sendy: 20-25 (Kablendy Pack, Sendaroo)
Kevin: 20-25
AleX: 10-15

Now, assuming the highest output for each, that puts us at 305 maps. Assuming the lowest, we've got 270. Now, I'll assume the lowest for each of us because I'm certain there are a few maps that we can do without in each dude's pack. Now, with this setup, you fellows with ranges might have to do a couple more maps to fulfill quota (Since we might want to end up cutting a few from the packs anyway, just to get the best of the best from each pack), so shoot for 5-10 above these numbers, and then cut down from there.

What I'll be doing from here on out is sifting through everyone's stuff, and providing a cut/keep tally so everyone knows which ones I think are Zenith-worthy, and which can go into Ampersand, or onto NUMA, or into a personal pack of yours. I suggest you all do the same with the other packs as well. For those of you not at your goal range yet - no worries - from what I've seen, the majority of what we have now is good enough to carry us through with just a handful of tweaks and extra maps. Also, for the final pack, I can throw in a couple of my better reject maps if all else fails, and I'm sure that Tim and Brad can do the same.

With that said, fantastic push, guys. We're hitting this thing right on time.
#375591 37 2007-10-30T22:23:39Z Kablizzy
Sweet. Here we go. Before reading these over, hit up the Legacy General Discussion topic to see the numbers I came up with. That's what I'm basing these on. I'll be doing a Cut / Keep for these, and providing some input on how I think I can move the cuts into keeps.

Abandon - Cut. How *are* you supposed to get out of the bottom, and why would you? If I can figure those two things out, I might change this to keep. And honestly, if anything, I think you could just cut that entire top part out (Unless [And this just hit me] the top is entirely aesthetic, which would be freakin' neat).

All your base - Keep. Very nice, classic Atob.

Astro Crib - Keep. Atob sings the clues. Fantastic.

Bubblegum krusch - Keep. Another pretty one. And it plays just amazingly.

Congenital Optimist - Keep. Still like this thing a lot.

Cracked Earth - Cut. There are a few small things bugging me here. First of all, the errant little tree structure - Having it in two maps seems strange to me. I get the theme, and I kinda like it, but for whatever reason, it's weirding me out. Secondly, the map plays a bit on the long side, but it's not a bad length, just combines with the other elements strangely for me. Thirdly, the map seems to want to play a lot more cleanly - Those structures with the door switches seem like they want to be more of a theme. The tiles seem to want to be aesthetic, and the jagged parts make it seem all jumbled up.

Dairy Farming, With Lazers - Keep. This bad-boy is fun, fun, fun.

Death and Gravity - Keep. Yep. Fantastic map.

Dynamo Hold - Keep. Another great one.

Fables - Keep, Keep, Keep, Keep, Keep. One small bug, though. Those doors. Those doors ruin the whole thing for me. Close those off at the expense of standard aesthetics, and this is perhaps the best map in the pack.

Faith Isn't Fitted with a Parachute - Cut. Great, but in your lower echelon.

Fun El - Cut. Again, probably in your lower echelon. It's good, but not nearly as much as the remainder of your stuff.

GSV the Ends of Intervention - Keep. That top Laser drone is frustratingly difficult to maneuvre around, whether going left or right. Beyond that, definite keep.

Guilty Spark - Undecided? What's with the NaN'd gold on the left side and the deadly jump-pad of death down below? Beyond that, this one will probably fall in your bottom half as well.

Hang 'em High - Keep. Still like this, still would like to see those E-tiles on the lower right end in something.

Hell and a Spintap - Cut. Falls in your lower half.

Just read the Instructions - Keep. Very Quirky, very fun.

My Grain - Keep, Keep, Keep. Fantastic on so many levels.

New Rave - Keep. Another magnificent level. Although strangely, the exit being on the bottom kinda throws me. I guess that's part of it, but... Eh.

Noob Patrol - Cut. A bit on the dull side.

R Belong to us - Keep. Not sure about the naming with "All your Base" in the earlier stages, but I guess that can work out too.

Rockets and Runways - Cut. I don't really like the beginning, feels like it's just there to be there, but I wouldn't neccesarily want anything else to go in there either.

Rockets Dream iNtangible - Keep. Amazingly done, and very vintage Legacy.

Sanitary is Never this Much Fun - Cut. I again love the pipe structure, and the rest not quite as much.

Sleeper Service - Keep. I still love this thing.

Spun - Keep. I always hate how rotational symmetry comes out, but this one does it well.

Tactical Grace - Keep! Oh, man, what a great map this is.

The Precise Nature of Catastrophe - Keep. Man, did you put on your mappin' hat this week? Here's the AtoB that I remember. One bug with this one, though. I hate the gold clumps. I would strongly suggest patterning the gold up the towers like you did on the right.

Time is not on my Side - Keep. Lurv it.

Topple - Keep. Pretty middle-of-the-road. If you get something better, by all means. If not, this'll do.

Under Construction - Cut. Did I like this before? Because I kinda don't now.

Well, I was in the neighbourhood - Keep

What are the Civilian Applications? - Keep. YES. YES YES YES YE SYESYSYEYSYEYSYESYEYSEYE.

ZOMG! Aliens! - Keep. Good, but your bottom half. I'd like to see something better go in this spot, but I think it'll fly as-is.

Well, I think that's your 25, or really really close to it (Assuming you go with these). Bit of advice, I would hold off until everyone else throws in their final analyses to actually cut anything. Some others might see things differently than I.

You mean all the world to me.

You're my love guppy.

I'll stick to you like Elmer's paste.
You're my love guppy.

I'd break through a citadel.
I'd fight with a raging bull,
Though winning would seem improbable.
You're my love guppy.

My love's as strong as the mid-ocean ridge.
You shine like the rainbow bridge
or like that light inside my fridge.
You're my love guppy.

For you I'd consume haggis,
or lose the joys of Bacchus,
or live in sin with Mike Dukakis.
You're my love guppy.

For you, I'd fight against Fate,
though maybe you could lose some weight,
You're my love guppy.

I would have to sell my soul,
or gulp a quart of Tide-E-Bowl.

I'm like a geyser founting.

You're my love guppy.

#378828 206 2007-11-12T18:58:29Z Kablizzy
Edit: Animator, that's insane. o_O

Very good start on b_t's part. As for the questions -

Oh great Kablizzy, is there any similar characteristic between the chosen members of your list?

Yes. Definitely. But the list is counter-intuitive.

Oh Great Kablizzy, we beseech you: Who can we trust to give us accurate clues?

Right now, blue_tetris and I. maximo will soon be posting clues as well, and LittleViking might have a part later on, depending upon how this goes.

Why add more tiers to the puzzle when we haven't figured out what we have yet?

If we aren't supposed to have figured that stuff out yet, then why give it before this?

If we need it all together, why do you wait so long to give it?

I'ma answer all three of these, because they're all great questions, and since the other two questions were wastes of questions.

First, the tiers to the puzzle are given in a puzzling way. The biggest challenge of these is figuring out what we're trying to say, what we're trying to get at. These are very difficult puzzles, and there are many ways to interpret each clue - Thus, these become some of the most difficult and rewarding puzzles to pull off. So, when we give things like the 32:12 clue, or the list clue, you guys want to do everything all at once, but we sometimes throw red herrings in there for you guys as well. Also, the puzzle is very fluid - We have many different ways that we can go with the puzzle - It's something that you guys have a lot of input in, and giving you guys a number of different things to work on at once, you can solve one portion of the puzzle (For instance, the Rohypnol / 32:12 thing), and the rest can go unsolved, you'll just hit that part of the puzzle later on when that branch of the puzzle comes around.

Secondly, you don't need everything together - some of the mini-puzzles coincide with other parts of the puzzle, but most of it is fairly standalone to answer the current riddle and get to the next part. At the end, everything becomes clear, and if you aren't in-line with where we're going, we let everyone know at that point.

One of the reasons that I wait so long to give clues is because the most rewarding part of these for the players, I've found, is working things out with the rest of the players (Or, Hell, by oneself). And plus, when I give you guys a clue, I always start by checking your reactions to them. If you're going down the wrong path, I'll post something else in that vein until you guys come across it. The other reason that I wait so long is because I'm busy as Hell, and I can't run these as efficiently as I could two years ago when I had three days off a week.

#378877 14 2007-11-12T22:06:02Z Kablizzy
Okay, as promised, my critique for these -

Lock and Lode - My only gripe with this one is that the drones start underneath the gold. Otherwise, this one's Good to Go.

Commercial District - Aesthetics are funky, but it's so damn fun. Good to Go.

Zork du Soleil - I think this one would be better suited for & - Seems too tricksy for the main pack. Ampersand.

Beep Boop Washing Machine Woop Weebop - Still plays a bit awkward. Ampersand?

Clouds - I still love this thing, but I think this one should get a difficulty reduction. I did an edit, removing the mines from the star formations, and also fiddled with more drones, and it seemed to work out well. Difficulty Edit.

The M Line - Another one that might need a difficulty reduction. The thwumps in between the 5th and 7th pillar are awkward to maneuver around - And the dual drone setup is pretty damn tough. I did an edit with this one too, and it didn't come out too well, but I think a Difficulty Edit is in order to make the map a bit more flowy and a bit easier.

Cavern of Heart - Another one I fiddled with, I expanded a couple of the ceiling parts to ease the difficulty a bit. Just deleting the two e-tiles directly above the right-most floorguard seemed to do the trick. Difficulty Edit.

Halftone Wavetheory - The map is hard enough without the chaingun - I'd drop the chaingun in favor of maybe a laser drone or two more zap drones to maneuver around up above. Beyond that, Good to Go.

Doy Lee Thompson - The trap doors make me want to overcompensate somehow. Then again, I just don't like trap doors in general. Good to Go, I suppose.

Jerz - The bounce-block gold combination on the right is out of alignment with the other two formations with gold. Other than that, Good to Go.

Powerhouse - Good to Go, Good to Go, Good to Go, Good to Go, Good to Go, Good to Go, Good to Go.

Halcyon and on and on - The third platform on the bottom makes it hard to jump off to the rightmost platform. I think moving it one tile to the right fixes this problem nicely. Good to Go.

Beauty Malybu LP - This here's an Ampersand map. Ampersand.

White - I'll just head maximo off at the pass and call this an Ampersand map too. Ampersand.

Brazil - GODDAMNIT I HATE BRAZIL. Oh, the map's cool too. Moving around is awkward as Hell, and getting back up after getting the exit switch is just not possible for me. Difficulty Edit?

Maximalize - I forgot how damn long this thing was. I dunno. I'd call it an Ampersand map. Ampersand.

I Was Meant for the Stage - Good to Go? I dunno, something's still bugging me about this. If other people would get on commenting, maybe we could get this project done.

OrChasm - The floorguard makes it Ampersand material. I tried the right side with a gauss in the middle of the last chasm, and it seemed to work out really well. Undecided?

My Dear Doddering Teeter-Totter Tutor - I think we decided this was an Ampersand map. I'm still dumbfounded at how you actually do it. Ampersand.

Scope - Still think this'd be a prime Ampersand Map. Ampersand.

Freeway isn't Free - Egh. I'm getting that same feeling again. I dunno what's bugging me about some of these. Ampersand? I dunno.

Quicken 98 - I didn't like this before? Fuck that shit. I love this thing. See, that's the thing. One time when I play through these, I love some and hate others, and the next time I play through, it's flipped all around. Good to Go, damnit.

Pop-o-Matic Trouble - Ugh, I dunno, man. Maybe I'll take the rest up later.

#379309 4 2007-11-14T04:22:57Z Kablizzy
Fucking fucktits, I just went through all of these, and then closed my fucking browser. Gr.

Deterministic Deathtrap - Fantastic. Keep.

Do that Daddy - Probably bottom half. Dump.

Pump House Abstraction - More gold. Keep.

You can't Buy that Kind of Existnence - I like the tile structure, but the map is nigh-impossible with those thwumps at the bottom. It's a good theme, but you might want to replace the rockets with gausses, nix the drones, and throw in something else on the outside tiles.

It's Mental! - Eh. This one isn't striking me as well as it did before. Dunno why.

Club Chic - This map tries to do way too much. Waaaay too much.

Hedge maze - About average.

Cascade - Above average.

Charm Offensive - Has some difficulty problems. That gauss in the bottom left is stupid hard.

El'yortgha - Needs to be a lot shorter, I hate trap doors, the floorguards are just about impossible to get around, and so on. Probably one of your bottom half maps.

Focus Group - Too many thwumps? I think so. Love this thing otherwise.

Inferno in the Firmament - This one might do with more diversity of enemies - Less mines, more gausses?

Jump for Joy - Yes. Yes yes. Yes.

Misfit's Republic - I dunno. Average, I guess.

Radius Suck - Middlin'.

Sendy's Revenge - Way too long. Way too long.

Too Tired to Tango - Oh God, Hot hot.

Whirlwind Tour - Your maps are trying to do too much.

X-Fade - Excellent.



I'm not sure if I'm qualified to pass judgment on the rest of these, but I'll try to be objective -

(There is) Joy in Repetition - I like this a lot better than the original, but we might need a couple more gold around the map.

Arrow Flynn - Ugh. How'd we ever make this dumb thing. I hate it.

Below the D-Low - I still adore this, and think that this will be our premiere map for the pack. Maximo doesn't like that topmost mine, though.

Block and Tackle - I dislike this a lot now. Not sure why.

Breakin' up is hard (To Do) - YES. FUCKING YES.

Checkerboard Trippin' - I am now of the camp that Thwumps ruin everything. Because this would be an amazing map without the thwumps.

Civvy - Eh. Moderate.

Conundrum - I don't care if Metanet has a map like this, damnit. I want this in.

Dual Dichotomy - Still good, solid map.

Echoes - Love this thing. Love it to pieces.

Floorguy Superstar - I like everything except the top blocks with the gold in-between, but everything I've done with it turns out like ass. Beyond that, it.

I Thought it was Hilarious - I know the thwump/trap door thing is kind of the theme here, but it won't make the final cut, bug-wise.

Illegal Chutney - Ugh. How'd we make this thing? =/

Jewelry Never Shines - FUCKYEAH.

Laboratorio - Eh. Middlin'.

Like a Well-Oiled Machine - Man, I thought I'd like our collab maps better. Eh.

Magnificent Redemption - Don't like this one now, either.

I'll do the rest shortly.

#380421 33 2007-11-18T03:48:57Z Kablizzy
Everything you ever wanted to know about Blizzy, but were afraid to ask.

The Inspector Guardian

As an ISTJ, your primary mode of living is focused internally, where you take things in via your five senses in a literal, concrete fashion. Your secondary mode is external, where you deal with things rationally and logically. 

ISTJs are quiet and reserved individuals who are interested in security and peaceful living. They have a strongly-felt internal sense of duty, which lends them a serious air and the motivation to follow through on tasks. Organized and methodical in their approach, they can generally succeed at any task which they undertake. 

ISTJs are very loyal, faithful, and dependable. They place great importance on honesty and integrity. They are "good citizens" who can be depended on to do the right thing for their families and communities. While they generally take things very seriously, they also usually have an offbeat sense of humor and can be a lot of fun - especially at family or work-related gatherings. 

ISTJs tend to believe in laws and traditions, and expect the same from others. They're not comfortable with breaking laws or going against the rules. If they are able to see a good reason for stepping outside of the established mode of doing things, the ISTJ will support that effort. However, ISTJs more often tend to believe that things should be done according to procedures and plans. If an ISTJ has not developed their Intuitive side sufficiently, they may become overly obsessed with structure, and insist on doing everything "by the book". 

The ISTJ is extremely dependable on following through with things which he or she has promised. For this reason, they sometimes get more and more work piled on them. Because the ISTJ has such a strong sense of duty, they may have a difficult time saying "no" when they are given more work than they can reasonably handle. For this reason, the ISTJ often works long hours, and may be unwittingly taken advantage of. 

The ISTJ will work for long periods of time and put tremendous amounts of energy into doing any task which they see as important to fulfilling a goal. However, they will resist putting energy into things which don't make sense to them, or for which they can't see a practical application. They prefer to work alone, but work well in teams when the situation demands it. They like to be accountable for their actions, and enjoy being in positions of authority. The ISTJ has little use for theory or abstract thinking, unless the practical application is clear. 

ISTJs have tremendous respect for facts. They hold a tremendous store of facts within themselves, which they have gathered through their Sensing preference. They may have difficulty understanding a theory or idea which is different from their own perspective. However, if they are shown the importance or relevance of the idea to someone who they respect or care about, the idea becomes a fact, which the ISTJ will internalize and support. Once the ISTJ supports a cause or idea, he or she will stop at no lengths to ensure that they are doing their duty of giving support where support is needed. 

The ISTJ is not naturally in tune with their own feelings and the feelings of others. They may have difficulty picking up on emotional needs immediately, as they are presented. Being perfectionists themselves, they have a tendency to take other people's efforts for granted, like they take their own efforts for granted. They need to remember to pat people on the back once in a while. 

ISTJs are likely to be uncomfortable expressing affection and emotion to others. However, their strong sense of duty and the ability to see what needs to be done in any situation usually allows them to overcome their natural reservations, and they are usually quite supporting and caring individuals with the people that they love. Once the ISTJ realizes the emotional needs of those who are close to them, they put forth effort to meet those needs. 

The ISTJ is extremely faithful and loyal. Traditional and family-minded, they will put forth great amounts of effort at making their homes and families running smoothly. They are responsible parents, taking their parenting roles seriously. They are usually good and generous providers to their families. They care deeply about those close to them, although they usually are not comfortable with expressing their love. The ISTJ is likely to express their affection through actions, rather than through words. 

ISTJs have an excellent ability to take any task and define it, organize it, plan it, and implement it through to completion. They are very hard workers, who do not allow obstacles to get in the way of performing their duties. They do not usually give themselves enough credit for their achievements, seeing their accomplishments simply as the natural fulfillment of their obligations. 

ISTJs usually have a great sense of space and function, and artistic appreciation. Their homes are likely to be tastefully furnished and immaculately maintained. They are acutely aware of their senses, and want to be in surroundings which fit their need for structure, order, and beauty. 

Under stress, ISTJs may fall into "catastrophe mode", where they see nothing but all of the possibilities of what could go wrong. They will berate themselves for things which they should have done differently, or duties which they failed to perform. They will lose their ability to see things calmly and reasonably, and will depress themselves with their visions of doom. 

In general, the ISTJ has a tremendous amount of potential. Capable, logical, reasonable, and effective individuals with a deeply driven desire to promote security and peaceful living, the ISTJ has what it takes to be highly effective at achieving their chosen goals - whatever they may be.

Quote: Ditocoaf, November 24, 2007 09:14 pm
It's hard to actually get advice on your maps here; the only place you're allowed to post a link to your map is in the Map ratings thread or map commenting thread, and usually you only get cursory answers there. It's not really set up to get feedback for people learning map design. If someone posts a map in the User Levels forum, they get a link to the Map Ratings thread, and a lock.
Wait, really? I've never really seen any of that since Brickman. Just browsing through the last few hundred threads, I see maybe two or three locked threads, and the rest just don't have a lot of posts. Granted, I spend much less time in the Custom Levels subforum than others, but that doesn't seem to be the problem.

We just talked this over a bit, and we reached a bit of a consensus. The reason people don't get much advice here is because people are more interested in getting feedback than giving it. The fact is that people don't look at the map-rating thread because they want to play some maps. They look at it because they want their maps rated and critiqued. They're not going to put much time or effort into giving feedback on a map they didn't want to play anyway. Plus, the community has evolved so far away from "Custom Levels," we're onto levelpacks and theme packs - And people who are just now finding the community and starting to make their first map with twenty-eight chainguns and mines lining the sides just won't get a whole lot of attention, because everyone has seen it, and everyone has done it. Single maps by some dude who has never made a map before isn't going to be much of an enjoyable or rewarding experience, and you're right, it's not set up for commenting or making mappers better at what they do. But by the same token, people can't be forced into commenting on maps that they don't want to play to begin with.

#18221 1 2007-12-01T12:25:24Z Kablizzy
Dronies Voting 2007 is Closed!

Welcome to Dronies Voting 2007. Voting will occur starting today, December 1st, 2007 and will end on December 31st, 2007. Results will be announced shortly thereafter. The Mare and Raigan Award for Contribution to the Community will be included in the results.

Here are the voting rules. You may only vote once for each category. Once you have submitted your vote form, you will not be allowed to submit again, so I suggest scanning the list, and choosiing wisely before making your selections. Save your choices in a .txt file if need be.

Importante! Just like last year, you may not vote for yourself. Vote for someone else. It makes for good sportsmanship.

Enclosed directly below are all of the nominees for this year. Nominees were chosen based upon raw nomination count to reach at least five nominees, and less than ten nominees. In categories where more than ten nominees were selected, tiebreaker votes were given to community members who had not already nominated for that category. In instances where less than five valid nominations were received, the remaining nominees were chosen. All nominees are listed in alphabetical order (I think - it's 5 AM).

In order to vote, we require your Username either on the forums or on NUMA as well as an E-mail address. The Legacy Team does not distribute your E-mail address in any way, and after the season is over, all votes will be deleted. If you don't feel comfortable giving out your E-mail address, you may input a random E-mail address, but in that instance, if there are problems with your votes, we will have no way to contact you about them.

#385698 442 2007-12-03T08:37:43Z Kablizzy
The point of the puzzle, as with all past puzzles, is to figure out the point of the puzzle. I know that sounds kinda vague, but I think we're gonna call this one a day. The ambience and suspense is long gone from this one, but I have a bit of a story behind these. Sit a while, and grampy Blizzy'll tell ya'll a tale. If you need to piss or grab a drink, do so now. Reading through these threads can get a bit tedious.

Now, first and foremost, let me explain a bit for you new folk what the point of the puzzles are. At the very basest level, all these are meant to do is to give you guys something to do. It's an activity that we craft so you guys can enjoy your time here a bit better - Something to take fondly with you on your journey in life.

The second thing that these puzzles are meant to do is to reveal something - usually a secret. I think the first one we did was the Kablizzy Fiasco - When the forum first started, we had the default IPB forum markers for the forums - Nothing was customized for the first 6 months or so of the forum's existence - so come January 1st, 2005, we were planning on unveiling the new, customised forums - complete with new forum markers, icons, banner, and organization. It was nothing like the skin that we have now, but it was amazing considering our combined knowledge of forums at the time.

So, the Kablizzy Fiasco went off without a hitch, and a few months later, LV sent me a message over AIM, asking me if I wanted to be a part of the Youth and Beauty Brigade. He told me that nothing would stand in his way. It only took us a few more minutes to turn it into a full-fledged forum scavenger hunt, of which TTK and nevermore came out on top. The Y&BB did really fantastically as a forum puzzle as well, everyone was really into it and very clever with all of the puzzles. The point of the Y&BB was just as an activity to go through. At the end of this one, though, nevermore and TTK got T-shirts of their choice as prizes.

And then came the Grand-daddy - It's Coming! Back in late 2005, after the forums got hacked, maximo was planning on doing a levelpack full of 100 maps for his return (At the time, 100 maps in a single pack was unheard of, especially by the same author), and shortly thereafter, he invited LV, tktktk, nevermore and I to help him out. At first, we thought we would each do 100 maps for a total of 500, but we only hit 400 for our first launch, so we decided to do two expansions - 300 each to make for 1000 total maps. Our plan was to match Mare and Raigan's number of levels and release alongside v1.5 (Which is still the current plan), and so we decided that we would play a bit of a guessing game with the forumers that was reminiscent of the Y&BB. And at the end, the answer was to reveal what The Legacy Team was working on; The first levelpack, taking over NedCon and the NTTS, the Dronies, the Hall of Fame, and so on. But towards the end, my communication with maximo broke down, and things fell through.

And then there was COFFEE, which I never participated in. Maybe Trogs or nevermore can fill you guys in there. They did a Y&BB 2, and then there was the Pony Parade, the Disco Dance Studio, and a bunch of other stuff, but you guys get the gist. Read through those threads (Or what you need to be able to grasp the idea of these).

As for this, I'm tired tonight, I'll get into answering it later. What you guys should do is isolate the clues, and figure out what I'm trying to tell you with them. For instance, you guys are correct in thinking that I'm leavin' the 'g' off of certain words. What could that mean? Well, you could take it as a number of things - You could take all of the gs out of the names provided on that list we gave you. You could simply make a note saying "Not G, Minus G or Missing G." Try to think of common phrases that might be related. "Negative Gs", or I could simply be referring to 1 Less G N Da Hood. So in kind, what could I be trying to tell you guys with the body parts? Were the misspellings of "elbow" and "handlebar" intentional? I think so, we haven't corrected them or told you guys that you're off-track, you just have to isolate and start guessing. I've really given you guys all the clues you need to solve, so keep it up.

#390635 62 2007-12-18T10:44:17Z Kablizzy
Quote: capt_weasle, December 18, 2007 01:05 am
Yet through that definition we should all be rocks? Because human does not equal hammer, does not equal umbrella, does not equal whatever. You can say that the brain fires some stuff here, reacts through stuff here, and eventually comes up with the best mathematical pathway to best lead you from the couch to the toilet. Your brain gets the impulse from your eyes that say "idiot, there is a foot stool there. Walk around," and the brain calculates, and you eventually move. You can make every logical statement to determine that our brains work scientifically, and that situation A results in situation B; no more, no less. But that is all cut down with the one thing that really defines some line between us and a hammer: a difference between right and wrong. Two people are drowning, your wife and your child. Your brain calculates that the most logical thing to do is save your wife, as you can only save one. However, you and your wife both know that saving your child is better, reasons you can decide. You go against every logical instinct in your body to save your child. Why? Because that is what you think is right. I think this is essentially our "free will," to determine what makes things moral, and what does not. If we only worked on logic, we'd be in a terrible world. In terms of making things work it would be a perfect world, as if logic prevails then everything will eventually be scientifically designed to be perfect. But in such a place, there would probably be - just as an example - the worst form of slavery. We recently discussed Time on the Cross, a book which showed how economically profitable slavery actually was. Take away what John C. Calhoun said about slavery (his reasons were through racism, not economics), and slavery was a system that turned out a major profit. I wish I had the introduction to Time still, but it seemed to show slavery worked. Yet take one step back and slavery is obviously horrific, proven through American history, the Holocaust (Jewish in forced labor camps), etc. If you think otherwise, you are a rock. When the debate of God vs. Science boils down, I think the major factor is what is right vs. what is correct.
But why do you "decide" which is right? Because things that you have experienced up to that point lead you to that "decision." Maybe you and your wife had a conversation about what you would do if she and your daughter were drowning. Let's assume that you had this big discussion over it and decided that you would save your daughter. You get into the situation, you save your daughter. A -> B.

But wait! You could totally choose to save your wife instead, right? That's not because of right or wrong, it's because something happened in between your discussion with your wife and the event to influence your choice. We may not *want* to work purely on logic, but logic is quite a different beast than Determinism. Determinism is a powerful tool - It helps us determine thousands of things every day. Whether you think it *would* be slavery is irrelevant - We live in that world, right now. Genetics, Psychology, Psychiatry, Engineering, Mathematics, the Entirety of sciences - It all runs on Determinism. All of us do. Free will is irrelevant. Give me a brief synopsis of your childhood, and I guarantee that I can predict some relatively specific things about your personality, emotional state, and current position in life. Why? Because of causation, man. Determinism is what I thrive on. If I didn't have determinism, I wouldn't be able to do much of anything.

For instance, I often walk to work. Sometimes, I take the scenic route, and other times, I take the direct route. What determines this? Free Will? I don't think so. On nice summer days, I take the scenic route. On wintry days when I'm five minutes late for work, I take the direct route. I don't see any problem with saying the weather almost *exclusively* determines my path to work. If I got mugged on the scenic route one day, I'd be less inclined to take that route. But I would also be less inclined to walk in general. I would be less inclined to be out at night. I would be less inclined to be out alone. I would be less inclined to visit ATM machines. I might develop complexes that prevent me from smelling roses if I was assaulted in a rosebush. But wait, you say. What if the person isn't affected like that? What if I become more inclined to take the scenic route instead? Maybe I'm looking for revenge. Maybe I'll start carrying a knife. Maybe my experiences up until that point led something in my head to trigger. Maybe I meet the guy again on that same path. Maybe I freeze in terror. Maybe I just snap and lose it and kill the dude. But an outside observer doesn't see all that. Does that mean it doesn't function like that? Nope. All determinism. Determinism at its best.

In the Nature vs. Nurture debate, the only correct answer is *both*.

Like Dave said, how do you label an atom right or wrong? How do you call a synapse "correct" while calling another "incorrect?" Would you call a genetic predisposition to being homosexual bad? Would you call it good?

And hey, Slavery is a great business. It does turn out a huge profit. But why is it wrong? What's wrong with rape or murder? What the Hell are freedoms and personal liberties, anyway? Why have a Geneva Convention at all?

#18655 1 2008-01-02T02:41:58Z Kablizzy
Happy New Year and Congratulations to all of the Dronies Winners!

Today, it has finished. When we began on The Legacy Project over two years ago, we had wanted for the pack to be a hundred maps to signify maximo's return to the community - Something that, even then, was all-but-unheard of. But as myself and LittleViking and nevermore and tktktk joined, we wanted to do something a bit more grandiose. So, we shot for 500 maps, 100 from each of us. But after some deliberation, we wanted something more long-lasting than just a single pack of a few hundred maps. And so, it was decided that The Legacy Project would consist of 1000 maps total, spread over three packs - 400 for the initial release, and 300 for each subsequent release. And today, the final portion of the puzzle is finished. And to start 2008 off, we have a number of treats for you all.

For those of you who have been unaware of Legacy's goings-on, let us fill you in!

First and foremost, we would like to announce three more new additions to the Legacy Team; Sendy, Barabajagal, and astheoceansblue! As busy as our schedules are, as a team, we decided that we need some more new faces in Legacy - With Sweep gone, and with nevermore and Lucidium entirely MIA this year - and with the rest of us plugging away through school and work and life in general - We needed some additional mapping power to the final of the three packs. So, we decided that, for Zenith, we needed some fresh ideas and some amazing mappers, and that, we have gotten. As of today, astheocreansblue, Barabajagal, and Sendy will all be helping work on projects for the team on a permanent basis. These three have single-handedly been setting mapping standards for years now, and I am proud to say that they have now officially joined The Legacy Team for all projects, current and future. These will probably be the last of the Legacy additions for some time, so enjoy them as you would enjoy a savory steak.

Secondly, today marks the end of the Dronies 2007! Voting has ended, and the results are up in the Legacy Subforum for your perusal.

Thirdly, I would like to re-announce InsomNicon III! Our very, very tentative date is January 4th, but we might have some last-minute changes to that date, but don't expect that to be cemented at all until we're certain of our schedules.

Fourthly, I would like to announce our next big project: The Legacy Compilation! Over the coming months, The Legacy Team will be re-organizing all of the maps from the three Legacy packs, and creating a gigantic, 1000-map bonanza for everyone's enjoyment! We are still in discussions over the specifics, but the end result will be all three Legacy Packs combined into one!

Next, I am proud to announce the long-awaited dedication maps for Caero, Lord_Day, and Cerberus! We have been saving all of our big guns for today, and we felt that hanging on to the dedication maps until today would likely be the best move for publicity purposes. We thought that these three should get as much exposure as possible, as they were the best of the best during Legacy's Expanse contest. So, without further ado, you can find the dedication maps here;

Caero
Lord_Day
Cerberus

And finally, the coup de grace. The moment that many of you have been waiting an entire year for. Today, we are launching Zenith, the final 300-map installment to our massive 1000-map anthology! Zenith adds 300 levels to the existing 700, all made by eleven of The Legacy Team's thirteen members - tktktk, maximo, sweep, Barabajagal, atob, Sendy, blue_tetris, KinGAleX, LittleViking, krusch, and myself - As well as the map made by Caero for his magnificent showing during the Legacy: Expanse contest. Zenith is meant as the final expansion pack to the Legacy project, continuing in the same vein as the Origins pack and the Expanse pack, with new ideas, new map styles, and hopefully, some brand-new perspectives upon the game. Over the past year, we nine have tirelessly played and re-played through the pack, tweaking and balancing, and arranging the pack to be in tip-top shape for you all to enjoy.

Download Zenith

Alongside Zenith, we are proud to present the Legacy: Zenith Contest! Like the Legacy: Origins Contest and the Legacy: Expanse Contest, the Legacy: Zenith is designed to provide incentive for you all to further enjoy the levels that we provide. The contest is a race, and a challenge, to find the fastest, most skilled and most dedicated players here. The first 20 people to complete Legacy will be awarded and recognized for their accomplishment. Please, please, please read all of the rules before entering, and follow the submission rules included here;

Contest Rules

Contest Sumbission: TheLegacyProject@gmail.com

Contest Deadline: March 1, 2008

Contest Rules:

- Once you complete the Legacy: Zenith pack in its entirety, you will submit your N userdata.sol file by e-mail to The Legacy Team for review. For help finding your .sol file, please consult the first post of this thread.

- E-mails must be marked "Legacy: Zenith Submission" in the subject line, along with your N username. (Ex. Legacy: Zenith Submission - Kablizzy)

- All Submissions Must include completed Demo data from each of the 300 Zenith levels. MAKE SURE YOUR DEMO DATA IS COMPLETE. Incomplete submissions may result in disqualification.

- Please be aware that your .sol file contains your username and password. The Legacy Team will not use, store, or even look at this information. If you are still not comfortable submitting a file with your password in it, you can change your info before submitting. Inside the Configure menu, set your username as LegacySubmission and your password as dummy (with the e-mail address left blank) and press "change user." You can then submit without any private information being sent.

- In the case that your .sol file is very large, you can upload your file to iHud.com and e-mail the link given to you to The Legacy Team. iHud is a free file-hosting service that allows for files up to 50 MB in size without requiring users to register.

Prizes

Grand Prize

- A Legacy T-shirt, custom-made by the Legacy Team!

- A Dedication map on Numa - the N User Map Archive!

- A Custom Signature, for use on the forums!

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- Access to the Custom Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A place in the N Hall of Fame, alongside the greatest N players!


For the Runner-Up:

- A Legacy T-shirt, custom-made by the Legacy Team!

- A Dedication map on Numa - the N User Map Archive!

- A Custom Signature, for use on the forums!

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- Access to the Custom Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A place in the N Hall of Fame, alongside the greatest N players!


For the Second Runner-Up:

- A Legacy T-shirt, custom-made by the Legacy Team!

- A Dedication map on Numa - the N User Map Archive!

- A Custom Signature, for use on the forums!

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- Access to the Custom Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A place in the N Hall of Fame, alongside the greatest N players!


For the remainder of the top 20:

- Access to the Custom Forum Usergroup, "Legacy Alumni!"

- A Custom Title, of your choosing, for use on the forums!

- A "Zenith Finalist" sig tag, for use on the forums!

For those who placed in the top 20 for Legacy: Origins, Legacy: Expanse, AND Legacy: Zenith:

- Your choice of: A free copy of N+ for the platform of your choice, sponsored by The Legacy Team OR A Legacy T-shirt, custom-made by the Legacy Team

- A Custom Signature signifying your placement amongst the top 20 in ALL THREE contests!

#396852 56 2008-01-04T22:35:19Z Kablizzy
Quote: sweep, January 04, 2008 09:08 am
Quote: Kablizzy, 2008-01-03T23:32:38Z
My comment stands. Deplorable.
You say this without any justification or reason. I am curious to know on which grounds you see it as deplorable - moral, I presume? In what way?
I've said it too many times to re-state it, the war's been fought and lost. You justify the ends on a technicality and call it "not wrong" so that you can feel better about the wrong that's being done. Deplorable. I don't care how much the record companies make, "Stickin' it to the man" is nowhere near a good reason, and anecdotal evidence of "let's say..." gets you nowhere. I could provide diametrically opposite reasons to yours and justify them with the exact same anecdotal evidence that you've given for the exact opposite outcome. You state that there are totally some economic benefits to people downloading music illegally, but the demographic of those that *might* perpetuate from such a miniscule situation are so negligible as to be nonexistent. Only those who are honest enough to stick entirely by very strict morals will actively go out and buy an album when they already have the music downloaded, and that demographic is *tiny*. You're speaking in pure hypotheticals and using technicalities, and neither provide any justification for illegal downloading not being bad - let alone enough to convince someone that it could be in any way beneficial - and certainly not enough whatsoever to be overwhelmingly so. A solid portion of the justification is simply rebellion-in-practice, and enough is enough. Making the point that some random artist "just might" not be against illegal downloading... as justification? Shaun, come on, you know how to debate better than this. I don't think illegal downloading brings the industry to its knees, the music industry has plenty of money left over - but to misrepresent the facts based upon hypotheticals when you have none to present is irresponsible. The RIAA isn't some grand conspiracy to oppress you and only you, and to think otherwise (As the pro-piracy dude that was quoted on the first page does) is balderdash.

And isn't this vigilante-ism? Sure, giving music away free might be a horrible idea. It might be great. It might kill a kitten. It might start a new world order. Downloading illegally might be awesome, it might be awful. It might be yellow. It might grow posies in a garden. All hypotheticals. You're advocating illegal downloading to these kids because it's "not that bad," right? They're impressionable, and they see you as a figurehead. You're a role model to these kids. They look up to you as much as they look up to anyone around here, and you know that if anyone could speak out against this with validity, it'd be me. I don't pay attention to the press, I make my own decisions, and this is the decision that I've reached. You have free will within confines, because society is a confine. It's a big one. If we were animals with free will, it'd be an entirely different story, but we're not. We're humans, in a community. In a global community now. And while things might very well be changing, they need to change for the better, and not for the worse. To rage against the RIAA seems like it's just pure, unadulterated rebellious nature. Telling the man that he can't tell you what to do. It's the 4chan syndrome, man. Mindless "me-too-ism." Everyone do what's wrong and only what's wrong, and nothing else? Hack and lie and cheat and steal and laugh at death and burning cats? The Internet is taking us into a bad bad place, man. And this is certainly a part of it.

It'd be one thing if you could correlate illegal downloading to anything, but you simply can't. Thus, a crusade based upon it is fruitless, irresponsible, and frankly, deplorable.

#18885 1 2008-01-19T11:39:17Z Kablizzy
On Christmas Eve, I lost my job. And for the past 20-some days, I've been looking for something comparable - As my last job paid me just enough to make rent and eat most days. Which was fine on my end. And, thusfar, I've found nothing. For the past month, I've been living off of the generous Christmas bonus of my previous employer, and my last paycheck for 2007 - And to-date, it's been going along famously. But once February 1st hits, my rent is due, and assuming I don't find a job, I might face eviction. I say might because I'm not sure how my landlords will react, but I can't make any assumptions until I can reach them (They're on vacation. How nice for them).

Well, little did I know that the job market here in Colorado was ass. The jobs that I'm finding are either McDonald's-related, or require some sort of degree. With me in the process of earning my Bachelor's, that leaves me with the bottom-of-the-barrel jobs that I can't take. I'll elaborate as to why here shortly.

Atop this, it's time for School again. Starts on Tuesday. And my school was gracious enough to award me a Student Loan for the term. Unfortunately, they accepted a few hundred too many people for the Student Loans this year, and I got an E-mail last night saying that my Loan was revoked, and I'm not going to receive any of the $1500 that was going to pay for the rest of my classes. So, since I get no money from that this semester, I have to drop down to minimum status. But that's okay! I have other financial aid which will come relatively close to covering the cost of school. Only about $150 short there.

Now, at this point, you might be asking why I'm going to school if I'm out of a job and can't afford it. Well, I have outstanding loans from previous semesters that I have to begin paying off if I'm not enrolled in at least half-time status at school. So, regardless of my situation, I've gotta stay in school until I finish, or begin paying a massive chunk of a Student Loan that I'm not ready to begin paying on, nor have the ability to begin paying on, back to the whole Lack-of-Job thing. So, I've gotta stay in school for at least 6 credit hours.

So, what I need from you guys today is threefold. I'm $141 USD short on tuition for the semester. I'm at bare-minimum status to keep my loan from biting me in the ass, which I can handle, so long as I can pay the tuition. Books can... Well, I don't know what I'll do for books. When I started the post, I didn't think that far ahead. As for Rent, I've got just short of $500 in my savings account, which leaves about $160 of my rent for February unpaid. Which again, Not sure if I can resolve that or not, but we'll see when I call the landlords back on Monday. Hopefully, they'll be back from vacation then.

And then, of course, I need employment. I've been browsing the paper and Careerbuilder, Monster, hotjobs, and I've been driving around, but there's just nothing out here in the way of a high-school graduate who can't stand working in the restaurant industry. Nothing that pays more than $7 or $8 an hour, anyway. Which won't go anywhere near supporting me. I'd ideally like to not work retail ever again, but honestly, anything to support me at this point would be wonderful. So, any advice for other options for where to look there would be more-than-welcome.

So what I'm doing here is a fundraiser, of sorts. I'm not asking for donations so much as I'm asking for credit. My idea was to have some of you invest in merchandise (T-shirts, copies of N+ that I could ship to you, whatever else you can think of that I can buy you sometime over the next six months) now, in exchange for said items later, when I get back on my feet. You'd basically be buying the items, but they'd be delayed for a few months to help Blizzy out a bit in the here and now. I hope you guys know me well enough to trust me in this, I've got nothing to back this but my solemn word. My goal for the fundraiser would be ideally about $300 USD to cover rent and tuition, but that's rather really lofty, so just being able to pay my rent would buy me enough time to get a job, get my tuition paid late with whatever penalties come along with it, and go on from there. And, of course, this would need to be by the end of the month.

I really hate to ask for something like this, but I'm kinda in freak-out mode over the situation. I'm supposed to keep my personal life rather separate from the forums, and I hate that I'm using the News Forum for this, but since I've got no family who isn't in the same position as I am or worse, I'm at my last-resort. So whatever you guys can do would be amazing.

Thanks,
~Matt
#402298 22 2008-01-20T11:40:49Z Kablizzy
Well, guys. I've got a happy-as-balls update. Thanks to you amazing folks, we've raised just around $250 of the $300 needed already, and not only that, I have a ton of job-hunting resources that I can pursue first thing tomorrow. Those links are amazing, I'ma spend most of the day tomorrow running through those to see if I can't find anything there. You guys have all sparked ideas in my head that I had never even pondered - I'm still a rube in the job-hunting field. I've only ever held one actual job, and I've never been on an interview. Not once. I just got the job on merit. I've never had to make a resum, and this was just the worst situation for me to have to 'take the plunge', so to speak.

One thing I forgot to mention about the job-hunt is that School is a factor. A big reason why I can't take a 9-5 job Monday through Friday is because I do school on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I could do night classes for some of my classes eventually, but for this semester, my Tuesday and Thursday go from 8:30 in the morning until 6:00 or so at night, and this close to the semester, I wouldn't be able to change. So, at least until Fall, that limits almost any professional jobs I'd be able to apply for seriously, which also limits my pay.

Oh, and I've been getting asked why I can't take those bottom-of-the-barrel jobs, since I didn't get around to elaborating like I said I would. The problem with the job that pays $7 an hour is threefold - First, if I take a job for two weeks and then find something better, I'll quit and have a two-week job on my resum. Not a terribly big deal. The second problem is that $7 an hour doesn't come anywhere near supporting me - Even moving slightly towards the goal of paying my bills is better than nothing, yes, but as I said, it would be a very temporary thing for me since I couldn't sustain myself on it for long, and by that, I mean at all. I wouldn't make any of my bills on a $7 per hour job, which doesn't necessarily rule it out, but it makes it incredibly unappealing. I mean, with my last job, my entire paychecks went to Rent, Food, Transportation, and stuff like Utilities, Credit Card Payments, and so on. And thirdly, I want to move up in the world for once. My entire life, I've lived in a place where I've always been well-off enough to avoid abject poverty and food stamps, but I've never really been well-off enough to support myself. And the only reason that I'm not married right now is because I have a job that barely can support myself - Let alone a second person. The main reason my mother-in-law forbids the marriage from happening is probably because of my financial situation. She's worried that I won't be able to support her daughter. And damnit, I am too. I'm terrified of that. So, my goal with this freedom from the job that I spent the last decade at is to get into a place where I can not only make my bills and pay my tuition, but also be able to save some money for a car, a house, and a wedding, and hell - Maybe even have some extra cash left over for a luxury or two. I deserve a movie once every six months or so.

And, to clarify, I didn't get fired, I walked out. My mom and I worked at the same place, and he was being abusive towards her, so we called it quits in the most literal sense possible. Which might seem hasty, but it's been going on there for seven years now, and the situation was such that we couldn't continue working when he was doing what he was doing. But to top that off, the 'generous Christmas bonus' that I mentioned was mysteriously included and taxed on my last paycheck - despite it being a cash-in-hand bonus - so instead of getting the full $600 that I was expecting on my last paycheck, I only took home just short of $400 of it. Which was just a cruel thing to do on my boss' part, and part of the reason why I'm in the hole to begin with.

Also! The Tax thing is ingenious. I'm hoping my W-2 gets here in a timely fashion, but since we left the job on rather bad terms, I'm kinda up in the air with how those are even going to get to us. I'm hoping he just slaps a stamp on them and sends them to us, but that remains to be seen as well. He's proven himself to be a spiteful bitch, so I'm not sure how that'll end up.

pepi: Bachelor's is going to be in Journalism, so after this semester, I'll also have the option of Internships open to me. This all really just had some awful timing, right when we're going into a recession and the job market is falling apart, and right when I can't do an internship, and so on and so forth.

Insofar as Tutoring, that's a fantastic idea, but I'm not too confident of my knowledge in any given area. I could totally tutor English, and that's something I'll look into on Tuesday when I hit school.

I'm no coder, but if I knew any place that needed a coder, I'd give it a shot, if nothing else. Now Ghost Writing, I would totally be down for. Thanks for the kind words on my writing, that's something I'd never even pondered until you said something.

Like Animator and wedgie said, I know there's 'something' out there, it's just a matter of getting me into that 'something.' As it stands, though, I've got more than enough time now to apply for a plethora of things, and see if I can get something better than the bottom, and thanks entirely to you guys.

So! There are a few ways to help if you're still inclined. I have my ever-present paypal account, which - If you don't know - is Kablizzy {at} MSN [dot] com. In the comment box, specify what you want from me, or PM me your request, and like I said, when I get back in the positive, it'll be my first priority. On the T-shirt thing, LV and I are going to be making our own T-shirts, for The Real N, Space Pimp, Legacy, Another Day, as well as some extra random shirts that used to be featured on my Zazzle page. If you want to Pre-order any shirt, you can order from the aforementioned The Real N, Space Pimp, Legacy, or Another Day designs, or you can request custom designs within reason (The printing process is a bit limiting, so I'm not sure what we can and can't do yet, but the more you guys request, the better we'll know our limitations). And of course, we'll be coming up with new designs every rare while that won't even have anything to do with the community, but will just be funny or irreverent. So, with all that said, they're going to run for either $11.95 or $12.95, and you guys can pre-order the shirts now, or at least, when LV and I get the designs up and running. I'll need LV to weigh in on this part, since he's the expert. We'll likely be setting up a business paypal account for it so that it's nice and easy to pay via credit card or whatever.

As for the N+ thing, I promised you guys who live outside of the U.S. that I will be more than happy to send out copies of N+ for you, since it likely won't be available outside of America/Canada. This is still in full-effect, and after a PM or two about it, I've decided that you guys can "Pre-Order" the copies through me, and when I get my hands on 'em, I'll send the copies out. So, if you do want to Pre-Order a copy of N+ for that reason, here's what I need;

A PM with your Name and Address (Obviously), and how much you're paying for the game (I've been quoted prices ranging from $9.95 to $19.95 USD, so one of those two, I assume), and then what system you need the copy for. Remember, N+ is coming to Xbox LIVE Arcade, and I don't believe it'll be featured in stores, so this pre-order thing would only apply for the handheld versions. And don't worry, if you over-pay, I'll be glad to issue refunds for those of you that do - When we find out the actual retail price of the games in question.

So with that in mind, you guys, thank you. Thank you all for being my friends and comrades and family for these past (almost) four years. You guys make me proud to be able to call myself a member of this community - I've had the privilege to call this place my home away from home, and I wouldn't want it to be any other place.
