Let's keep this on topic, mm? I would also go in for a professional pregnancy test, which I believe Planned Parenthood does. Like Dave said, false positives on store-bought tests can be common. hCG is a hormone treatment for infertility, and it's an outside chance for a 17 year-old, but it's one of a few things that can give a false positive on a pregnancy test.

Like Mosh said, don't rush things. You guys have long enough to decide how to handle this. If it comes down to an abortion, then that's what it comes down to. If you guys feel like adoption is the best option, then by all means. I'm sorry you guys didn't find out the night of, Dave and I would've been a lot more help the day after, but as it is, I would check with Planned Parenthood and get some guidance from a professional.

As everyone else has said, I don't think you guys could handle a child at this stage in your lives, so the best advice I can give you is to get in touch with Planned Parenthood (You can visit their website here or contact them through any of these means. Keep us updated.

Edit: Exactly as Scythe said. Also, here's a couple more resources I forgot to toss in:

http://www.drdrew.com/Office/faq.asp?id=1076&section=5002

http://www.drdrew.com/Office/faq.asp?id=1078&section=5002

http://www.americanpregnancy.org/links/

http://pegasus.cc.ucf.edu/~feecwg/teen.html

Also, for future reference, the phone number 1-888-not-2-late is a resource for emergency contraception, which won't help in this case, but they may know where to refer you if all else fails.

Also, read up on your rights as teens - I *believe* that you guys can consent to an abortion without parental consent, but your religious background and what state you live in will affect that as well. Something else that I would suggest is to tell your parents eventually. They may be angry, sure, but they're the best people to have on your side. Like I said, read up on your rights before going further, and be sure to take any big steps slowly. Don't tell anyone right away if you don't have to, but just make sure to talk to a professional first and foremost.

I separate the Internet into two distinct entities - The near Internet and the deep Internet - The near Internet are the places that normal folk use - Myspace, Yahoo, Wikipedia, Google, Sports Sites, Stock Trading Sites, Youtube, to an extent. The deep Internet is the place where we dwell - Forums, Messageboards, and other sites that require a larger input - Communities, and such.

The near Internet is a good resource - It's a highly-regulated, corporate place. It's a very unobtrusive place. I see it as the Downtown of the Internet - Where most of the people are very bland and 'normal.'

The deep Internet is a horrendous place - It's the anarchy-in-action rural principality of the Internet. It's the part of the Internet where the insane Klansmen and the crazy sexual deviants lie - It's the shack in Minnesota, it's where the freakish killers and terrorists and furries and pedophiles roam. And I hate it. I want it to be destroyed. I want it destroyed in the worst way. It's unlimited connectivity for the worst of the worst.

I love the near Internet (Of which I consider this a place), but the deep Internet needs some regulation.

#19139 1 2008-02-10T22:44:10Z Kablizzy
Lawful Good is known as the "Saintly" or "Crusader" alignment. A lawful good character typically acts with compassion, and always with honor and a sense of duty. A lawful good nation would consist of a well-organized government that works for the benefit of its citizens. Lawful good characters include righteous knights, all paladins and most dwarves. Lawful good creatures include the noble golden dragons.

Lawful Good characters, especially paladins, may sometimes find themselves faced with the dilemma of whether to obey Law or Good when the two conflict - for example, upholding a sworn oath when it would lead innocents to come to harm - or conflicts between two orders, such as between their religious law and the law of the local ruler.

In the Complete Scoundrel sourcebook, Batman, Dick Tracy and Indiana Jones are cited as examples of Lawful Good characters. In the real world, the Scout Oath of the Boy Scouts of America also expresses a Lawful Good ideal.

Lawful Neutral is called the "Judge" or "Disciplined" alignment. A lawful neutral character typically believes strongly in Lawful concepts such as honor, order, rules and tradition, and often follows a personal code. A Lawful Neutral society would typically enforce strict laws to maintain social order, and place a high value on traditions and historical precedent. Examples of Lawful Neutral characters include a soldier who always follows orders, a judge or enforcer that adheres mercilessly to the word of the law, a disciplined monk, and the Dungeon Master of a D&D game.

Characters of this alignment are neutral with regard to Good and Evil. This does not mean that Lawful Neutral characters are amoral or immoral, or do not have a moral compass; but simply that their moral considerations come a distant second to what their code, tradition or law dictates. They typically have a strong ethical code, but it is primarily guided by their system of belief, not by a commitment to Good or Evil.

James Bond, Odysseus, and Sanjuro from Yojimbo are Lawful Neutral.

Lawful Evil is referred to as the "Dominator" or "Diabolic" alignment. Characters of this alignment show a combination of desirable and undesirable traits: while they typically obey their superiors and keep their word, they care nothing for the rights and freedoms of other individuals. Examples of this alignment include tyrants, devils, organized criminals, those with samurai-like aspects, and soldiers who follow the chain of command but enjoy killing for its own sake.

The game rules devote the most detail to this alignment, since it frequently creates interesting mastermind villains. Lawful Evil characters are loath to break laws or promises. This reluctance comes partly from their nature and partly because they depend on order to protect themselves from those who oppose them on moral grounds. Some lawful evil villains have particular taboos, such as not killing in cold blood (but having underlings do it) or not letting children come to harm (if it can be helped). They imagine that these compunctions put them above unprincipled villains.

Artemis Entreri is a prime example of Lawful Evil, as are Boba Fett of Star Wars and X-Men's Magneto.

Neutral Good is known as the "Benefactor" alignment. A neutral good character is guided by his conscience and typically acts altruistically, without regard for or against Lawful precepts such as rules or tradition. A neutral good character may cooperate with lawful officials but does not feel beholden to them. A doctor that treats soldiers from both sides in a war would be considered Neutral Good.

Examples of Neutral Good characters include Zorro and Spider-Man.

Neutral alignment, also referred to as True Neutral, is called the "Undecided" or "Nature's" alignment. This alignment represents neutral on both axes, and tends not to feel strongly towards any alignment. A farmer whose only concern is to feed his family is of this alignment. Most animals, such as monkeys, lacking the capacity for moral judgement, are of this alignment.

Some neutral characters, rather than feeling undecided, are committed to a balance between the alignments. They may see Good, Evil, Law and Chaos as simply prejudices and dangerous extremes.

Druids frequently follow this True Neutral dedication to balance, and under Advanced Dungeons & Dragons rules were required to be this alignment. In an example given in a D&D rulebook, a typical druid might fight against a band of marauding gnolls, only to switch sides to save the gnoll's clan from being exterminated.

Lara Croft, Lucy Westenra from Dracula, and Han Solo in his early Star Wars appearance are Neutral.

Neutral Evil is called the "Malefactor" alignment. Characters of this alignment are typically selfish and have no qualms about turning on their allies-of-the-moment. They have no compunctions about harming others to get what they want, but neither will they go out of their way to cause carnage or mayhem when they see no direct benefit to it. A villain of this alignment can be more dangerous than either Lawful or Chaotic Evil characters, since he is neither bound by any sort of honor or tradition nor disorganized and pointlessly violent.

Complete Scoundrel cites X-Men's Mystique and Sawyer of Lost as Neutral Evil characters.

Chaotic Good is known as the "Beatific" or "Rebel" alignment. A chaotic good character favors change for the greater good, disdains bureaucratic organizations that get in the way of social improvement, and places a high value on personal freedom. Most elves are chaotic good, as are some fey.

Starbuck from Battlestar Galactica, Malcolm Reynolds from Firefly, and Robin Hood are examples of Chaotic Good individuals.

Chaotic Neutral is called the "Anarchist" or "Free Spirit" alignment. A character of this alignment is an individualist who follows his or her own heart, shirks rules and traditions. They typically act out of self-interest, but do not enjoy seeing others suffer. Many adventurers are of this alignment.

An unusual subset of Chaotic Neutral is "strongly Chaotic Neutral", describing a character who behaves chaotically to the point of appearing insane. Characters of this type may regularly change their appearance and attitudes for the sake of change, and intentionally disrupt organizations for the sole reason of disrupting a Lawful construct.

Captain Jack Sparrow, Al Swearengen from the TV series Deadwood, and Snake Plissken from Escape from New York are verifiably Chaotic Neutral characters.

Chaotic Evil is referred to as the "Destroyer" or "Demonic" alignment. Characters of this alignment tend to have little respect for rules, other peoples' lives, or anything but their own selfish desires. They typically only behave themselves out of fear of punishment.

Carl Denham from King Kong and Riddick from Pitch Black are Chaotic Evil.

Edit: If you're unsure, Wizards has a Neat Test to figure it out. But I'd rather you guys try and reach an answer by introspection.

Ron Hubbard for what he is. Thetans in a volcano? Soulcatchers? When I first saw that South Park, I thought, "Oh, you have absolutely got to be shitting me." If you create a forum, it is your responsibility to make sure that no content on your forum is breaking any of the rules outlined within this document. We expect you to moderate the content of these forums regularly, otherwise your forum will be deleted.

Well, because Forumer says so, but beyond that, because Keron is legally responsible for this place. And so are LV and I. And a lot of the things that go on at 4chan are prosecutable offences. Quote: "Moot"
There has been a lot of rumbling on /b/ [and the rest of the site] for the past few months, heckyears, about the quality of posts on the board(s). As we all know, there is no barrier to posting on 4chan. We don't have mandatory user registration, and God willing, never will. I'd like to keep the site as open to all users as possible (yes, that includes new ones too), while still enforcing a minimum quality standard. This can't be resolved via posting limitations and moderation alone; there is a very large component of it that needs to come from the userbase itself. For as many changes as I've made to /b/, hit and miss as they might have been, I still firmly believe that the real power to change lays within the users themselves. The 4chan staff doesn't generate the content on this siteyou do. We provide the framework, and the community provides the rest.

What does that mean to anyone else? Because to me, that means that Anonymity just doesn't work. It produces that unfathomable stream of crap that will never go away. I want to petition congress to crack the fuck down on Internet, and get some regulations in place, but I think it's a bit too late for that. It's already gone as far as it can go. I have to understand the psychology of things like this, I need to know why people act the way they act, and why they do the things they do. And I can't for the life of me get the attraction to 4chan. So, another question. What would you say is the worst part of the community, and why? I'd say it's B&T. It's the closest thing to 4chan we've got here, I think. I've been trying to kill it for ages now, but then "people wouldn't have a place to be vulgar," right? Or whatever the fuck the argument against it was. What-the-fuck-ever. You guys know why we have a vulgarity rule, right? The only reason we have a vulgarity rule is because of the retards. I don't care when KA cusses. Not a bit. Why? Because he knows how to regulate it. Yeah, he's vulgar, but he knows he's doing it. He knows the affect it has. In kind, I don't (much) care when Suki browses 4chan. Why? Because he knows how to regulate it. Does an 8 year-old know how to regulate these things? Probably not. Maybe an exceptionally bright 8 year-old might have this gift where he can look at a severed horsecock and not be changed for it. But most of the rest of us can't. And that's what I want to protect. It's the same thing I say about doing drugs. If you've got a 170 IQ, and you smoke yourself down to 150? Whatever, not a big deal. But if you start out at 80, a high-school dropout, and smoke yourself down further... Well, boy, you just done smoked yourself retarded. Right? Do you guys understand that logic? Back to the vulgarity rule, people say, "Well, hey, why can mods cuss and we can't?" Well, that's mostly because we don't care if you cuss every now and again. I have a feeling this post is going to be quite vulgar, and I apologize for that, but I'm not posting "LUL FAGZ," I'm posting some coherent, pragmatic rhetoric that has a point and an impact. The reason you get warned for vulgarity is because you post in someone's map thread and say, "this iz shit lol." Is that what we want around here? If we were all halfway mature, I'd rescind the vulgarity rule in a God-Damn heartbeat. But we have the rule up because some of you children don't know how to handle it. So we have to make you handle it. To borrow another 4chan meme, the rules may be stupid and arbitrary, but God help you if you break them. So, what other part of the community would you call the worst? If not B&T, I'd say the IRC. And everyone who no longer visits #n seems to agree. It's amazing connectivity, but folk like BumBumMilkToffee don't get it. They don't understand what it's there for. They can't come in and say, "Hey, guys. What's goin' down?" They have to come in and "LUL CHIKINZZZZZZZZZAAAAAAAAA" the channel apart. That's why we don't spend time there. You guys turn us off. Dave and I enjoy having political discussions - He and I fucking *revel* in them - , but when that's being interrupted with "HAY DO U THINK BARRAK IS A GAY?????" What the fuck do you want us to do? Why can't you guys grasp this? I've sat here for the past eigth fucking hours editing this post just to try and get this message out to you guys. I can't fathom that you can't provide anything pertinent to a serious discussion - It's all gotta be about decapitations and furry porn and what a 1337 haxer you are, and such. Why is it any surprise that I can't relate to half of you? I honestly don't give a shit if you just did a barrel roll in Starfox. Can we talk about the good ol' days, or something? Please? Anything? Tell me about the show you're watching. Talk to me about a game we both play, or something. Challenge me to a game of Quad. If I'm not up for it at the moment, I apologize, but we've all got to make a little more effort here, right? Right? There are some of you who I have never heard a single serious thing from. Ever. It's all trivial and menial and very insignificant - And guys - that kills me. The retarded tripe absolutely kills me inside. And I can't do that all the time. I can't even do that most of the time. So, when I jump into #n, and I'm greeted by "hay blizz lol," how is it that none of you can grasp my fury? Why do I go hide out in #angrydome half the time? I'm in the channel for three seconds, and the first thing anyone says makes me want to leave. And the funny thing is - I don't get why none of you see it, either. For those of you who might still not get this, why is this rated higher than this? What causes one to be found hilarious, and the other not? What's wrong with BBMT? He's of this caliber of user that we have here that doesn't respect the community. He doesn't get how things here work, and he'd be better suited at 4chan, with the other jerkasses. Or, he can straighten up and be a fucking contributing member of the community. I was talking to Vash tonight, and he said, "Man, I've been here three years, and I haven't contributed a thing." Yeah, well. That's what happens, right? Hey, let's tie this into Anon! Guess what Anon posts on /b/? Nothing but insignificant, trivial, menial bullshit! WOW! WHAT A COMPARISON! Is it becoming a bit more clear to you guys? Because I'm trying my hardest to clarify what my problem with Anon is so that next time someone asks me what the big deal is, I can just point to this post, let 'em read for an hour, and hopefully sway their opinion. I'm pouring my heart out here, and it's tearing me up that I have to go to these lengths to get you guys to see this.

Topo: Y'know who else no one took seriously? Germany, circa 1930 or so. Everyone said "Aw, they're not all that bad. Just annexing some territory, not that big of a deal." Yeah, these kids might be kinda unorganized at the moment, but I've seen Anon grow expo-fucking-nentially over the past three days. THREE DAYS. Not even mentioning the past two years. Two years ago, 4chan wasn't on anyone's tongue around here, and y'know what? We were fine with that, right? But now, here we are, Anon is a force. It's a force, guys. Top 300 Alexa. Top three-fucking-hundred. 4chan outranks the AIM website. It outranks World of Warcraft's site. It outranks monsters like Mozilla and Wal-Mart, Mapquest, Symantec, Newgrounds, Skype, Ebaum's, and even Forumer itself. And it's now huge because no one thought that 4chan was anything but inocuous. But now they're mobilized, and they have direction. That's dangerous. Good lord, that's dangerous. It certainly could fizzle out like many other things, but think of the other road that this could go down. If things go badly, Anon could do some nasty things. Hearkening back to one of the first questions I asked, Do you guys understand how many folk call themselves Anon? Three-fucking-million. Organize three million people. See what they can do all at once. I don't think you'd like the results. Hell, I can name a good 20 people here who could call themselves Anon. In a way, you could call me the same. And I hoped to God that they couldn't manifest in the real world, but guess what? Here we are.

And I love you all, but when I don't get that love and respect back, I'm not really the type to just fling my arms up and walk away, I'm the type to fix it, damnit. And that's why even the "Down in Flames" thing isn't even me giving up - it's largely a scream for help. Someone speak out with me. Someone join me on this. I want to, I really do, but the reason I'm posting these for you guys to read isn't because I want to debate, but because I want you guys - ALL of you guys - to know why the 4chan rule was in place (IT WASN'T OBVIOUS?????), and why 4chan is representative of a much, much larger problem that no one is even so much as acknowledging. If you guys can take that at face value, that's great. If not, there's not much more I can say.

Quote: "blue_tetris", 2008-02-15T01:50:47Z
Wanna know the real problem with /b/? The problem with /b/ and its members is that they aren't funny, and they don't have a community. No one on the boards is actively trying to innovate new humor which is good. No one on the boards does anything but regurgitate the same nonsense they've heard a thousand times before. There's no innovation and there's no spirit.

Moreover, it's easy to be on /b/. You don't need a personality. You just need to help traffic memes. You become part of a large and ineffectual wave--the ocean of piss they so often use as allegory. Metanet was a constant challenge to come up with novel ideas, funny stuff, and personal affects. There was something for posterity, and you forged a personality.

/b/ isn't funny. It isn't effective. It isn't anything that its members believe it to be. They get stuck there because they view it as instantaneous reward for little effort. Because they think irreverence and arbitrariness is tantamount to humor. Because they have lost the ability to innovate. It's another dead-end hold of the Internet, and it's easy to find and easy to become a "community member" of, so people join.

So, really, 4chan as a whole is not as bad a site as Nemesis may have you believe. They even have nice wallpapers. It's good to exchange images sometimes. But the culture surrounding it is a trap for those without personalities, or those willing to forfeit them. Blizz and I have systematically watched each person who joined 4chan become someone else. And this someone had no personality. They had a head filled with YTMND- and ebaumsworld-style memes which they believed had significance.

They participated as worthless members of a large, unfunny plot to do something wholly boring. And they did so wittingly.

The fact that people on 4chan can feel "bad ass" for submitting spam to the Internet anonymously is nothing short of mircaulous to me. It is herd logic incarnate. It is the living proof that people would prefer to feel mildly connected than to have unique and novel ideas about stuff. That sucks, but that's the world we live in. Thankfully, as 4chan grows (since newfags like the members of the Metanet forums have started joining), it dies. The larger it gets, the more worthless its individuals become. Eventually, I can only imagine that people will leave because they are entirely ineffectual.

Or... they'll stay forever because they feel like they have friends who have the same piqued sense of "absurd humor" that they have.

But 4chan isn't bad. It's just not good either. It's the new ebaumsworld. And I imagine people who used to use 4chan as an imageboard hate what you new arrivals have done. They used to create new memes, now they steep in the old ones. They used to at least pretend to innovate, now they act like bad asses standing on the less-than-witty foundations of what used to be an okay website.

I dunno how people can feel so bad ass when they're anonymous. I'm the precise opposite of anonymous, and I imagine that I am worth at least 7,000,000 /b/ users--and that figure is roundabout. I get shit done and I affect the world by being Dave and being loud. Do you think Scientology is going to care when you march motivation signs and Cockmongler images up to their doorsteps? The memetics and (un)culture of the /b/tards will always be more important to them than any of their proposed goals. They will never affect change, and they'll evolve into something even stupider as the years go on. I imagine the site will crumble, and millions of idiots will be left without lives.

As for the typing "lulz faggg" and other such idiotic Internet stuff, for the sake of irony:

There's an old Chinese proverb that states: "You can only suck one dick in satire. Surely, several dicks later, you must be a cocksucker." I don't believe people can immitate and pretend habitually. They become the people they satire. They become cocksuckers.

You're all a bunch of cocksuckers.

The only issue that I take with all of that is the claim that 4chan isn't bad, or that it used to be "okay" (To borrow a quote, "Remember when /b/ was good? /b/ was never good"). It helps harbor some really negative things. I think Ebaums is a horrible place, too. But I can even chalk that up to personal opinion. But it's also my responsibility to keep stuff like 4chan away from the community, as is set by who we are. And that much can't be chalked up to personal opinion. It's something that we, as mods, need to do, because we have a higher moral standard than that. We've built this great community, and damnit, I want to am going to keep it that way. And beyond these little viewpoint differences, we think the same on the issue. And I think you guys would do good to read that quote just once more.

Edit: And TTK, you'd be entirely right. You would be 100% right, if we enforced it. We don't warn for that stuff. We should, and I do, and only I do, and the staff tells me that I'm out of line for a lot of it. But if that's what it takes to reach a consensus, I'm all behind keeping the rules that much tighter. And some of the memes are genuinely funny... once or twice. I won't say that they aren't. I've chuckled at some /b/ stuff once or twice, and I wouldn't even mind having it around if they actually were funny. But people can't differentiate between good funny and bad funny, and because of that, we can't let any of it in. That's why there was just this blanket-ban. How many of you dislike the GLAAAAYYYYSHUR! thing? Ask yourselves why that's no longer funny, and I think you'll find your answer as to why memes shouldn't be allowed around here.

Edit: mysterypower came back to the IRC today. Didn't take him 10 minutes to get himself banned. Take a wild guess as to why.

Another preface; Alrighty, guys. I've decided to put this bad-boy up as well. I don't want responses, all I want is for you guys to read it in your leisure time. This post is wholly unfinished, and as such, a bit shorter than my last (it turned out to be way the fuck longer). So, this time around, just enjoy the ride, and don't bother about replying. Just soak it in and try to understand the regurgitated themes.

Ultima and Broghs warned me that another post of this size would dilute the message. And it probably will. But I guess I'm also writing this for posterity, too. So if you don't feel like crashing your way through another 10,000 words of text, I'll understand. Also, as kind of a top-wise addendum, we've had more IRC bannings within the past couple days than we've had in weeks. And I forsee four or five more coming over the next few days if folk don't shape up.

Ian: I think you might be misunderstanding a bit, which is fine, because that post was stupidly long. In either case, I think you might be using a double standard for how to deal with Anonymous. Sure, there are billions of people who you'll deal with in the world, but when you meet them, they're not all going to say "Epic Lulz!" to you. They all have a personality. They have an identity. Anon doesn't have this. That's the difference in your analogies. Your friends aren't anonymous. Your friends aren't a part of a Hivemind organization called "Ireland." They're individuals. They live in a place called "Ireland," but they're not all for the exact same thing. And I know, "Anon isn't either," right? But how do we differentiate? They're all the same. You can't tell one Anon from the next. Put a mask on your friends, and all of Ireland, and give them the same mannerisms. Give them all the same voice, and the same potential hazards. Let's say only half of them have firearms, and only half of those with firearms have the intent to shoot you. Will you treat them the same then? You'd damn well better, or you'll get shot. Paper airplane, remember? Let's trade the paper airplane in for a firearm. Only one student has it, and he's the only student with the intention to use it, but the second the teacher turns around, that student will use the firearm. Now, let's say that during class conversations, the other students joked about shooting the teacher. What does she do then? What if the students weren't in the classroom? What if they were all... Oh, I don't know... ANONYMOUS. See the flaw in the logic? You can't compare your friends with Anonymous, or with the country of Ireland, because they exist, they live in places, they're tangible, they have personalities and dreams, goals, identities. But more than that, they don't come up to you and try to show you pictures of their dead daughter that they just raped. They don't threaten to kill you, they don't do anything that Anon does. Thus, it's irrational to compare Anon with Ireland. When you look at Anon, all you see is the trash. No one's serious on /b/, and they're hardly serious when they venture out into... Oh, I don't know... here! Or there! Or anywhere! It's all Lulz, right? How do you take any Anon seriously when all they show you is this affront of "Legion" and "Anon"? When you meet someone from Ireland, you expect a personality and uniqueness. You expect them to act with a sense of decency and with some tact. You expect them to be a human with unique ideas and unique strengths, weaknesses, beliefs, and so on.

But look at /b/. What can you expect from /b/? You expect the memes, you expect the chaos - Defined by lack of moral compass, remember? When it's *ALL* you are, you can't expect any differently. But here's the kicker - On a whole different level, we do stereotype real-world people. We stereotype them based upon race, religion, credo. We stereotype them on the basis of hair color, skin color, political affiliation. And these people aren't even all the same! They don't even act remotely the same! A black conservative man from Russia could be *entirely* different from another black conservative man from Russia. Now before you rush in and say one Anon can be totally different from another, hear me out. When you talk to the two black conservative men, what would they say to you? One might say that they support communism. The other might say that he hates socialist doctrine altogether. One might have a wife, the other might be gay. Now, whilst this may also be true of Anon, when you sit two Anon down and talk to them, what do you get? "WE ARE LEGION, WE DO NOT FORGIVE. WE ARE BORG." You get the whole mob mentality thing - Sure, they might have varying degrees of idiocy, but how do you know? How do you even determine what part of what Anon is serious when nothing that any of them says can be taken in any way but with lulz? They're all Anonymous. They're all the same. They all tout the same merits - None. They all tout the same beliefs - None. They all tout the same rules - None. See where this is going? Remember my lowest common denominator statement? Why doesn't that apply? When they ACTIVELY CLAIM to be one gigantic, conglomerate, faceless butcher, then what's the problem in treating them like one gigantic, conglomerate, faceless butcher? They are *ALL* trolls and they all claim to lack morals, so if they want things that way, that's what they get. I'm not going to have sympathy for one of them or two of them or any of them - Why should I? They're all faceless butchers to me, because that's all they show me. If they weren't "all that bad," then don't you think I would treat them as not all that bad?

They claim that they are legion, and that they are everywhere. Fuck dealing with them individually. If one strays here and starts posting "lulz fagz," what part of that tells me that they have anything to contribute to the community, or an identity worth salvaging? If one of them comes here and posts a moving poem about the human condition, then they obviously know how to break away, and they have something to contribute to the community. Very clear-cut, right? If all they post is memes, pardon the reference, but "GTFO MY INTERNETS," yeah? I know we don't want that type of trash here, and you guys all know it too. And it seems as though they can't control the memes, it's just another day at the office. But that's the problem! Few of them *DO* have the ability to break away! It bleeds over into everything! That's my problem! It's everywhere! I can't escape it. This was my sanctuary from it - I could come here and be content in knowing "Ahhh, Metanet. My sweet Metanet. YOU aren't corrupted." And then, it became, "Ahhh, Metanet. My sweet Metanet. You're my only fri... Wait, what!? Epic Lulz!? Where the shit did that come from!? Oh, for fuck's sake..." That's how quick it happened. First, it was Suki. And God help me, I closed my eyes, and stuck my fingers in my ears, and kept repeating, "It's gonna go away, it's gonna go away, just wait out the storm." But it only got worse. Never better. Every time I opened one eye, there was another instance of it, and another, and another. And then I started moderating other places, and I realized that this shit wasn't isolated anymore. It was out of control. I had stuck my fingers in my ears for too long, it had gotten out of control. Wildfire status. But seriously, when I know that they're not going to post anything relevant or useful to US AND OUR COMMUNITY, then what's the problem? I've got no sympathy for guys like this, and I know you guys are about "giving everyone a chance," but Goddamnit, It's like the boy who cried wolf - The first few posts I saw on /b/, I thought, "Wait, is he serious? I... hm. Really? I don't know if he's being serious or not." But after keeping tabs on them for a couple years non-stop, I've learned that nothing there can be taken seriously. It's all trash and trolling. Falsehoods and rumor, right? But I don't even mean that, I'm not being clear. I mean, it's serious business, right? But even that's a joke. I think the first thing they've done without pretense is this project chanology thing, but even this isn't /b/. I look at it and go, "Wait, that's not the Anon I know. Protestst? Good cause? No, no, no, no, no. Something's up here." Right? Isn't that the dichotomy we've reached? I'll get into "Two Anon" theory here in a bit. You guys have opened my eyes, to an extent.

So, off on a different tangent, you're right - The only IRL focus that we've seen is the protests, thusfar. But when I say real-world manifestations, I mean, in part, the Chocolate Rain thing. Did you follow along how empowered Anon was when Tay Zonday got on TV, around the middle of last year? It was tangible, dude. Anon was all, "Wow, we've got this power, now how are we gonna use it?" And no one - No one who wasn't familiar with him understood why the Hell he was famous. I saw the people in Letterman's audience staring in horror at this kid at the keyboard, with the "What the shit is this?" look on their faces. They didn't get why he was famous. I did. Because Anon got his video spam-viewed on Youtube. They made a change in the world, however small it might have been. But that gave them this idea that, man, they have power in numbers. Do you know how many online polls they've completely assfucked the results of, just through force of numbers? It's a *whole* lot. And that was only concerning to me and me alone. Everyone called me fucking insane. But now, here we are, half a year later, and Anon is slightly larger. Why is no one else concerned yet? Why can't we take the precautions neccesary just in case something horrible goes down? Again, let me ask you guys - Why does our community thrive, and why do we love it here? Please, for the love of God, ask yourselves that. If you said 'Because we run the community exactly the way we do,' you're right. We ban the idiots, and keep the good members. And hey, there are even some dudes who have gotten banned, and turned out to be amazing members. Take rocket_thumped. He was banned from the IRC for God-knows-how-long, but we gave him another chance, and it turned out fine. Luminaflare got in deep, deep shit when he was first hanging out here. He got permabanned, dodged the ban (Unwittingly, I think), and got banned another few times. But y'know what he did? He apologized to me. He said that he was sorry, and didn't mean to cause a fuss, and now he's back, and he's a fine member. He's a /b/tard too on occasion, and he tosses out some memes every now and then, but he knows that I don't like them, and God fucking help him, he tries his hardest to keep them to a minimum, /for me/. And shit, I overlook a whole Hell of a lot in #n. I really do. S'why I don't spend much time there. I don't want to have to ban anyone. I've said that numerous times now. I don't want you to leave, but if you're disrupting the rest of the community, that's how it has to go. That sucks, I know. "This hurts me more than it hurts you," right?

But you guys trust me when I say that I want what's best for this place, right? Again, do we want this to be a shithole, or don't we? I find it really hard to look at HoI and know that it went to shit directly after I left. Because it did. I left, and 4chan slid right in. Every Admin, every user there has tinges of it. It's tainted the whole fucking place. That was my project, man. It was my baby. And it's being ruined. HoI was exponentially more strict than we are here, and it's slowly rotting away. None of the staff does anything anymore, and I mean in many ways. It takes two months to change a single turn, and I hop on IRC there, and everyone's dropping 4chan links and memes at each other - but where's the problem, you ask? The problem is that the memes have replaced the once-amazing community. And there's just no coming back from it, so I've abandoned it. It's a lost cause. I'll pick it back up again once it dies off. It's like I stepped away from the computer, and stepped back into a motherfucking Hitchcock film, y'know? Warhol paintings of tomato soup and shit on the walls. All because I'm not there anymore. So as such, I find it hard to call my own methods into question when they all work so damn well, y'know? Please don't take that as arrogant, because I want to just be as straight-up as I can here, but here's my thing; I can go get hired immediately at any Forum on the Internet. And why? Becuse of how well I run this place. And if I lose how well this place runs, I lose all credibility. I lose all confidence in myself if this shit goes down in flames. This place is the reason for who I am today - It proved to me that I can be the best at something, damnit. I joined up at Gunbound only on the merit of what I've done here. They hired me on as an Admin without so much as glancing at my resum, and then after my absence, they re-hired me on as Admin with no qualms. I'm a permanent staffer there on the merit that I'm me. Once Gunbound hired me, I impacted the site the first day I was there. I revolutionized HoI, and Hell, I like to think that I've kinda revolutionized this place too. Now, don't get me wrong, I don't want to say that I'm the reason for Metanet's success. Metanet is certainly the reason, but I want to keep it successful. And I hope you guys do too. I don't want Mare and Raigan to come home to a letter from the FBI saying that their forums are being investigated on charges of conspiracy and child porn distribution and so on. In all honesty, I have little, if nothing, to do with Metanet's success. But for the forums and particularly the IRC, they've adopted this sense of community, haven't they? And it's because those of us who were here during the Forum's early days shaped the forum. And it's because of all of you who have come along and contributed the coolest shit to the community. That's what makes us what we are. LV and I came up with the idea of having an IRC channel. Dave pioneered Vent for us. But more than that, we've set the rules for how to behave here. Why, all of a sudden, when Anon's entered into the equation, something changes? Do we do things a certain way here or don't we? I like to think we do. And I don't want thanks or recognition for the amount of time and effort that I've put in here. Because we all (The mods in particular) have put in tireless hours to keep this place as it is. I'm a very small part of this place, and yeah - Sometimes I joke, "Man, this place would be lost without me," - there's a part of that, deep down somewhere in me, that I wonder if it's true. If I wasn't here as a valve for what 4chan content came to us, what would the forums be like? Because we sure don't enforce the rules as strictly as we need to if this stuff gets through anyway. What kind of a raging shithole would IRC be if I weren't the "Bad Cop?" If everyone's a Good Cop, then where's the counterbalance? Too much of one thing is awful, especially in a situation like this.

But it's not even about that, right? I feel like I've stood in front of this doorway, holding my arms out, telling everyone, "No, damnit! You can't come in!" And now, I let my arms down, shrug, and the flood gates are just gonna open the balls up. And you guys know how I feel about the community - this is where it all started for me. My first moderator job was here. I take responsibility for this place, because this place reflects upon me, whether good or bad. And if some random outsider walks through and sees all the posts in alternating caps, and images of cat-asses with the caption "UH O! U GOT FARTED LOLOLOL," how do you think that reflects upon me? They'd say, "Jeez, what kind of jackass runs that forum? But here's what's even scarier about it. What I'm really afraid of is that same person coming here, seeing that same image of a cat ass with that same fucking caption, AND NOT THINKING TWICE ABOUT IT. Isn't that a dreadful prospect? So, yeah, I'd even go so far as to say the memes are that bad - They reflect badly upon us all. Are we that type of community? The fact that I even need to ask that is concerning, isn't it?

Anyway, you go on to say that enturbulation is trying to distance itself from /b/. And that's great. I honestly love hearing that. And something was made clear to me earlier today as I was first writing this up. That there are indeed now two portions of Anonymous. It baffled me, it really did. So, I had to sit and analyze it. And it came to me that these new Anon aren't actually Anon. They might be at face value, but do they really know what Anon is *actually* about? I posit that no, they don't. They see the same things that you see. They see Enturbulation as a good place, a place where nothing bad happens. The mods crack down on hate speech, they crack down upon everything that /b/ mods never would. Why the Hell would they do that if they were true, cruel anon? They need a face. They know that no one would support Anon: The Monster, so they have to make Anon: The Crusader. They have to change, or they don't have a case. So, there's all these old Anon who are putting their best foot forward, and all these new Anon who know no better.

You're also right, just because /b/ is lawless doesn't mean the rest of the world has to change. But it's doing so anyway. It's changing, whether we like it or not. It's changing for the worse, and you're also right, it only spreads to places that are gullible, and weak. But tell me, everyone reading this - What happens when EVERY place is gullible and weak? If this is the case, then wouldn't we see the old, tired memes everywhere? Wouldn't we see the idiots in every corner of every internet chatroom and on every forum? WELCOME TO FEBRUARY, 2008. You can't go anywhere without a meme. Memetics has become a culture unto itself. It's the new Aim-speak. It's the new leet.

I saw a comment on youtube that said, and I quote, "Learn some grammar, guys. My God." And it was rated down! None of the actual flames on the video were, just that one and only that one. My first response was, of course, "Are you kidding me?" But my second reaction was that of, "Oh, this again. Just par for the course." But I'm sick of it being par for the course. I'm done with the idiots being on top just becaue there's more of 'em. Take xkcd, for instance. Man, I love(d) xkcd, until about three minutes ago. I thought the xkcd dudes were on my side, what with the originality bot and all (Speaking of which, #n is super-fucked). Anyway, someone told me that today's xkcd was hilarious, so I visited, and it was damn funny. And I thought to myself, "Hey, I haven't been to xkcd in a while, I'll browse the archives!" So, I started at today's, and went back a few. I'd seen a couple that LV had linked to, so I went back a few more. I went back ten comics. Two 4chan references. I go back two more. Another one. It's all. over. the. fucking. place. I can't. Fucking. Stand it. Guys. xkcd is supposed to be intelligent, man. They're just like me - They know when communities grow past a certain point, they begin to suck. They even have a theory on signal-noise relations. I love theory. They know everthing I know, and they still promote the tide. Unwittingly? Yeah, maybe. But to be honest, I don't even know what to say after seeing this. I mean, I don't know the xkcd community, but I bet if I went into their IRC prior to the originality bot, I'd see the same stupid shit that I see here on occasion, but exponentially worse due to community size. And they wanted to quash that. And I respect that. But they support the tide. And I don't respect that. They say they want originality, but their comics re-use tired old memes. Time was, I never saw this calibre of humor on their site. It was all high-quality. And now, it's headed in exactly the direction that they themselves claim they don't want to go. Even xkcd, guys. If that's not kinda sickening, I'm not sure what is. And yeah, maybe I'm making a bit too big of a deal out of each of these instances. But when you see all the things that I see on the Internet, and start hypothesizing about where this is all going, it gets to be a bit worrisome.

Animator messaged me on IRC the other day. He wanted me to teach him every 4chan meme I know so he can avoid them in the future. Secondly, I told him that this isn't even about 4chan, or Anonymous. It's about the Internet as a whole, and how accepting it is of shit like this. I asked him where he first learned to use the memes and catch-phrases, and he has never been to 4chan. He learned them from friends. That's how memes work, and spread. But I then asked him what the Hell Epic Lulz meant to him. He didn't have an answer. I asked him what the Hell Over 9000 meant, why the Hell anyone would even say that, let alone repeat it ad-nauseam, and again, he had no answer. I still see tons of people calling stuff "Fail," and that might be one of these memes that I concede for the good of the fight. It might be too far along for me to stop the bleeding there. And so I got him to go introspective a little bit, and from the other side of this Internet Tube that he and I shared, I heard something click. Yeah, he still uses some minor "WTF?" every now and again, but he's trying. For fuck's sake, he's trying his ass off. And I respect the balls out of that. I'm calling it right here, Animator is the next Yanni.

Let's talk about Gunbound for a moment. Remember Kimmie? Why did we ban Kimmie, does anyone remember? Because she was just generally an annoyance, right? She broke rules, she multi-accounted on NUMA, she cussed excessively, et cetera. Well, the whole of the Gunbound community is like that. Few bother to punctuate their posts, and those who do are like Suki - Intelligent, but posting 4chan memes for the lulz. And then all the little half-bastards take that as "just fucking hilarious" and mimic it. And that's how it spreads. That's why I'm afraid of it, because any given /b/tard can go to any other forum and whether wittingly or unwittingly, shit it up. It's already happened here in scads. You wouldn't see any of this back in our day, right? How has the forum changed over these past four years? I know that both of you remember the early days where even a random troll was a rarity - Now it's... maybe a weekly occurrence? Maybe more? But not only that, our respected members are now the trolls. We used to be appalled at them, now they're the ones appalled at me. Some twist of fate.

In either case, that's what frightens me. Our normal members becoming this type of idiot. I'm trying my hardest to look out for you guys, and with most of you sitting at a decade younger than me, I feel like I have a responsibility to at least give you guys the option of chivalry and valor. Like I said a while ago, I take pride in how well this place runs, and if no one else does, I can't be the only one to keep up the fight. And the problem with that thinking only comes in when no one else seems to think that this is a problem. That is what really frightens me. "Oh, they're not all that bad, Blizz." They say. How can you even begin to defend them, especially with our community at stake?

I think there's a bit of a flaw in your analogy - I don't want you (Or the other mods) to treat everyone you meet like a child molester. That would indeed be unfair. But I do want you to treat the /b/tards as what they are - /b/tards. That's all we can classify them as, right? No one of them is going to be neccesarily worse than another, sure, but how do we know which are the "good ones" just out to post a couple memes, and how do we know which are the "bad ones" out to spread this gospel? A good number of /b/tards are seriously out for blood - Anyone who speaks out against /b/ has gotten a face-full of liquid wrath, and I am risking my reputation, my good name, and to an extent, the community, to post these two ginormous things up.

But through all this, you say to me, "Blizz, that's what the warn system is for! Let it take due process!" Right? But I can't. And here's why - There are a lot of weaker-willed members here. There are children here. /b/ is 18+, the vast majority of our users are under 18. Therefore, /b/ is not allowed here. That seems like really solid logic. If we get caught spreading links to 4chan for kids that are under 18, we lose the forum. Again, do we want that? That's why we need to run an extra-tight ship, and I grant that during Mr. Monsterpost up there, that could be easily overlooked. And more than that, the warn system didn't work. We don't enforce these rules nearly strictly enough, and we need to get back on track, particularly with N+ hitting... Right now. It's best-foot-forward time, and we need the reigns tightened up as much as we can for this new generation of gamer.

But this isn't a joke, this isn't something to be taken lightly. This is our community, and again, if you want to take it lightly, then we can just head Limez off at the pass and request that we get shut down, and Mare and Raigan can moderate their own forums when the new ones get uploaded to the site. Because, like I said, we're already in danger of losing the forum, even with as strict as we are currently, and any further motion towards the mountain of shit looming in the distance is only going to get worse for us. Ideally, we shouldn't let half of the things go on here that we do, and I'm not sure why we do let half of them go on, but we can't let this go any further into this direction, right? I hope we all agree there. From reading over your posts, I know you do.

Lemme give an analogy. Let's say that I'm standing in a field. In front of me, there's a house. A rather normal-looking house, most people that pass by don't think twice about it. Within this house lives the Manson Family. In the back yard of this house, I see the Mansons doing horrible, horrible things. I see them raping babies and performing blood rituals, sex with their farm animals, the whole nine yards. But in the front yard, the Manson family holds Watermelon-Eating Contests!

Let's say Mark Bunker drives by, and he just loves watermelon. As we all know, that's his thing. Let's say a bus full of tourists drives by, and stops off to partake in the watermelon-eating contest. Let's say a few carloads of other folk drive by and stop, and it's just one great, big watermelon-eating extravaganza! Now, the tourists don't know about the baby raping going on in the back yard. Mark Bunker sure doesn't have an idea, but they all conglomerate around this idea of the Watermelon-Eating Contest. They can't see the back yard, and all the shit that goes down there, but they totally support the Manson family, because they hold Watermelon-Eating Contests! WHAT A COOL FAMILY, right? So, do I think Mark Bunker would put his reputation on the line for Anon? If he doesn't know how deep the rabbit-hole goes, absolutely. He doesn't know about the blood rituals, because all he sees is the Watermelon-Eating contest. If that's all he knows, shit yes, he's gonna put his reputation on the line for it. Just the same as you would. You guys can't see the atrocities happening on the other side of the house.

Have you guys seen the Anti-Smoking episode of South Park? The one with Rob Reiner? Here's a transcript of one of the parts that I found interesting;

Quote
Rob Reiner: Oh, God-damnit, do I have to explain this again?! Smoking is bad, people! So if we have to be a little extreme to stop it, it's okay!
Kyle: No it isn't, you fat turd! Because, I've learned something today. You just hate smoking, so you use all your money and power to force others to think like you. And that's called fascism, you tubby asshole!
Rob Reiner: GOD-DAMNIT THERE'LL BE NO MORE SMOKING!!
Stan: It wasn't the tobacco companies' fault that we smoked. It was our fault, us! We should all take personal responsibility instead of letting fat fascists like him tell us what to do!

Fascism at its best, yeah? I feel a lot like Rob Reiner here, and while the two situations are eerily similar, what Stan says at the end there is the key to this whole thing. He's entirely right, we *should* take personal responsibility for stuff like this, but what happens when no one does so? As I've said in the past, if you guys would just step up a little bit and take some responsibility, these silly rules would never have to surface, at all. The rules are correlatory to what unfathomable jackasses you've been, and are continuing to be. So, please, please stop being jackasses? What happens when no one bothers to take responsibility? What happens when there is no Tobacco company to blame? What happens when not only no one bothers to take responsibility, but refuses outright? What if the reason they can operate is because no one has to take responsibility? Who has to step in? As silly as it sounds, Rob Reiner. Now, do you see why that's crucial? In Stan's outrage, he calls Rob Reiner a fascist because he thinks he knows what's best for people. But what if Rob Reiner is right? What if Rob Reiner hates smoking for the good of humanity? What if that's what eventually does us in, and Rob Reiner is the only roadblock to everything coming to a crashing halt? Wouldn't you want someone to speak up and stop the madness? I'd much much rather live comfortably under a fascist than to live in fear under no rule at all. But beyond that, what if Rob Reiner is right? We all know what smoking does - but it's still legal. It's still encouraged. It's still popular and fun. What happens when no one takes any Goddamn responsibility? Do we just sit back and watch the world go to shit? That'd be all well and good if, after all the shit was gone, we could clean up and start anew, but we can't.

And you know my nature, you know what I want for the community, and you know that my intentions are good. And to be frank, I think we've done a damn fantastic job at keeping the community as fun and welcoming as we have, right?

I mean, despite TS being a perpetual cocknob to newcomers, and rocket_thump's occasional insanities, and some of the other regulars who can't seem to keep their behavior under control regardless, Everyone else has conglomerated pretty well. And I don't think that's really hurt anyone's identity at all, right? Or am I incorrect there? I mean, really. If everyone on the IRC were as responsible as you or LV or KA, or Atilla, we would never need rules. The tripe would never show up. If everyone had this same ability to know right from wrong and when too far is too far, there wouldn't be a single rule on the forums or on #n, we'd just exist and have a grand old time. We'd be just fine in a ruleless community, because we would all know each other, and be responsible enough to know each other's boundaries. But add BumBum into that mix, or kkstrong, or Hell - Anyone who we've had problems with. What would he do in a ruleless environment? If you said "Fuck it up for $400, Alex," you got the Daily Double.

To give an example, I asked Borealis tonight when we were going to hear some more Noctambulant stuff. His reply was "IN DUE TIME SAR." Do you think I care that he purposefully misspelled "Sir"? Not a bit. Why? Because OtherDave is a really even-keel dude. He's an amazing conversationalist, he has some really unique, bright views. He has his own religion. He's not an atheist to stick it to the man, he doesn't "h8 linkin prk," he listens to his own blend of music, he believes in his own blend of religion, and he doesn't impose that on others. kkstrong? BumBum? Not so much. There's a gap there, right? You can feel it, I know you can. You look at Borealis, and your mind goes, "Groovin' dude. Musician. Knows his shit." You look at McP, and your mind says, "Spam. Idiot. Troll. 2-page warn log." Right? That's how we define people. That's what we do. As humans, we conceptualize people in that way. If that's elitist, then so be it. I won't lecture you on Psychology, because I know you know it as well - if not better - than I do. You know what "exposure and immersion" means. You know communication theory, and all that. You know how important the "Nurture" is in Nature vs. Nurture. Where do these kids get the idea that this stuff is funny? Fuck if I know, but you and I both know where this road leads.

So, I mean, really? Do you guys believe me when I say that this is for the good of the community?

Like Ultima said last night, "Aren't you just confusing bad grammar with 4chan?" Well, yes and no. To me, the old internet troll and the new internet troll are one in the same. They're both idiots, I don't like either. Someone who's just illiterate and lacking tact, I just don't like on principle. Is that fair? Shit no. But again, this place isn't always fair. We're not always going to convene the high council to see if we're leaving the illiterate jackass out in the cold. For instance, I banned kkstrong tonight from the IRC, as I said above. And I told him to appeal his case to KA. So, when KA got in for the night, I told him that kkstrong was banned and if KA wanted to reverse the ruling, to knock himself out. KA didn't care. As far as he was concerned, kkstrong got what was coming to him. Sucks to be him. Should've straightened up. That's how I look at it too. kkstrong thought it was hilarious, and even had the balls to ask me how long the ban was for.

Edit: And here we are, days later, and he says he has no idea why he's banned. So, for whatever reason, he's back in #n, dicking it up. And he hasn't even so much as *seen* this thread yet, and even if he did, I severely doubt that he'd rummage through this much text to see what the reason is. In fact, very few of you have seen the thread, and for you guys reading through all of my tripe, I really appreciate it.

Edit Number Two: Oh, Jesus, guys. I'm so sorry. I don't mean to write this much, I really don't. No hurry on this, really. I don't expect you guys to devote this much time to the subject like I do. I'm so anal about this crap.

Edit For the Hat Trick (2-15): And then there are nights like this, when I jump into #n, and everything clicks. Everyone's so Goddamn cool, I actually cried tonight at how well we all got together in #n. I want to write this down and make this clear now, because I fear I'll forget it later, but I shed some tears over how awesome our community *is*. Even with its foibles, it's still our community against the Internet, and I like that. I like how we stick together through everything, and that we're this awesome place where we all know each other and hang out. If we were like this all the time, I'd never have a problem. We'd ban the random jackasses, and we'd go on unadulterated.

Edit Once More (2-16): And then again, there are days like today, when I jump into #n, and everyone's a fucking retard. I don't get why it changes so readily. That's what I mean - Last night, we had sixteen groovy dudes online, and this afternoon, all the jackasses were out in force. It doesn't make any sense to me.

Edit one Last Time: It's a 4chan meme. They're all 4chan memes. They're all from the same collective Internet asshole. And again, this isn't even about 4chan or Anon. I don't think it ever was. They're just commonalities in Internet retardation that I can point to 4chan as the source of. I can point to Anon, and say, "There they are. That's what's wrong with you guys," but in reality, it goes a lot deeper. Like I said before, 4chan is the least of our worries. I haven't even touched on the deep stuff through these rants. This is the watered-down, non-philosophical, layman's version.

#416765 10 2008-03-14T11:32:06Z Kablizzy
Intriguing topic.

My Strengths:

Strict Action Maps / Metanet-Style Maps
Technical Gameplay
Minimalism
Object-Placement
Aesthetics
Map Packs

My Weaknesses:
Races, N-Art, DDAs, Survivals, Puzzles, etc.
Creativity
Playtesting / Refining

My mapmaking is an odd-style. I do many different types of mapping, depending upon what I want to do. For Legacy, I usually make 500 maps, and cut it down to 40 or 50, or however many we decide on keeping. For NUMA (And for projects), I adopt a more open-ended style, but I pride myself on my tilesets and my unique action ideas. None of my tilesets are mind-blowing (With the exception, maybe of Eclectic), but I never step out on a limb that I'm unsure of.

My mapping is slow and methodical and a result of nearly four years straight of mapping nightly. I'm akin to maximo in this way - We both map in the traditional, old-school Metanet way.

Most of my maps are built off a cluster of E-tiles, and I add things from there.

I could go on, but that should be good.
