#425117 2 2008-04-05T00:54:31Z Kablizzy
Greetings, all! I've been talking a lot about writing this article, and I've finally got around to finishing it. Now, a few things before I begin - First and foremost, <b>this is not a mapmaking guide</b>. For those of you expecting it to be, look elsewhere. This is meant to be for folk who already know how to map, have already found their own style, and already understand how to utilize NED to their advantage. With that said, this can be used as a tool to further refine and expand your mapmaking techniques, and to better understand some very subtle things about game theory that most new (and some advanced) mapmakers tend to either overlook or ignore. Secondly, this article is meant to help mapmakers with making an episodic map pack. This isn't meant for NUMA maps, and this isn't meant (as much) for non-episodic map packs. Now, I think I should define what I mean by NUMA maps, episodic map-packs, and non-episodic map-packs.

<ul><li>NUMA Maps-</li> NUMA maps are - at their basest, most fundamental level - Casual maps. There is no set guide to making good casual maps - They can be funky, they can be innovative, they can be strange, they can be nigh-impossible. They can be completely unplayable, they can be art, they can be DDAs, they can be anything. There are few rules for making a good NUMA map, and none whatsoever for making a NUMA map at all, because it's more an art form than a science. NUMA maps, are - definitionally - freeform. They lack constraint, but they flow freely with innovation and thought. And not all of them, mind. Some are just a smattering of objects and tiles that one could hardly call a map, but that is the beauty of the NUMA map - it can be anything. Even the worst map that someone submits can be salvaged and tweaked and turned into something brilliant. NUMA Maps can be of any length, any difficulty, any style, and any form. They can even lack a style entirely. The doors are wide open with a NUMA map, as they are meant to be played on their own.

<li>Non-Episodic Map Packs-</li> I choose to list these prior to Episodic Map-Packs for an important reason. Non-Episodic Map-Packs have less constraints upon them than Episodic Map-Packs do. Non-Episodic Map-Packs (Hereafter referred to as NEMPs) are a gateway, of sorts, between NUMA maps and Episodic Map-Packs. NEMPs have the ability to be a collection of maps, perhaps with a theme, perhaps not. NEMP maps can include any number of styles easily - they can integrate well or poorly, they can be played in any order, they can function as a whole, or as a fun collection of maps from the same author. These maps can differ greatly in style, or they can all be tied together with a common tileset, enemy, or gold placement. It can have any number of maps, and the maps within can be of any length and difficulty. How this differs from Episodic Map Packs? That information follows. Now, some NEMP maps have been submitted to NUMA. Take <a href="http://numa.notdot.net/user/tktktk">tktktk</a>'s Simple Challenge Series. Functionally, the Simple Challenge Series fits the Non-Episodic theme perfectly, but it was submitted to NUMA. But the idea is the same - they are meant to be a pack, a series, and despite the submission method, the goal stays. Despite this, NEMPs can be as simple as a collection of NUMA maps, or as complex as a pack with a theme. But the distinguishing factor about an NEMP is the distinct lack of a guideline.

<li>Episodic Map-Packs-</li> Episodic Map-Packs, on the other hand, have more stringent guidelines to abide by. When you sit down to create an Episodic Map-Pack (Hereafter referred to as EMPs), you have to take a number of things into account that you don't necessarily have to take into account with NEMPs and NUMA maps. When you strive to make an EMP, your goal is to mimic the Metanet levels from the game, arrange them in an episode format, and further into a column format, and present the pack as a whole. The first thing that you have to take into account, obviously, is arrangement and length. Each map should compliment the others in an episode, and even in a column, and the maps should be neither too short nor too long. Each map should be played in order of relative difficulty, and as you play through the episode, the column, and the pack, the player should feel the theme of the pack well - That is to say that while a player is playing through your pack, the feeling that you want to convey through your maps should be felt fully. This is perhaps the most difficult part of crafting the episodic pack; It is vital to understand that the atmosphere and mood that you may want to get across to the player may not always be the perception of the pack that the player Now, purists like myself will also take into account "episode time" - Something that refers to the time it takes to complete an entire episode of five maps. Currently, the userlevels menu doesn't account for this time, but for a good balance of level difficulty and length, one must also take into consideration episode time. Episode time is a difficult thing to gauge, but each of the five levels within an episode should contain enough gold to finish the episode with an excess of time on the clock. This may come to be more important during the v1.5 release of N, but as it stands, the only reasons to take episode time into account are for principle, and to assist in measuring difficulty and length.

Whilst each map functions on its own, the purpose of the pack is to invoke both a theme and a mood, whilst also providing quality gameplay and aesthetic presentation. EMPs take far more thought and planning to execute well, as there are so many more things you have to take into account when putting together an EMP. NEMPs can take on this same level of stringency, but it is less a rule than it would be a luxury. With EMP maps, you should give thought to each object's placement within a map, each tile's effect upon the map, and fiddle with differing placements. Playtesting is also key when putting an EMP together - each map should be tested for length, difficulty, placement, and timing. Each Episodic Map's length should be shorter than the average level, so as to make the episode's length between the length of 2.5 to 5 NUMA maps. Length during the early levels should be nearer to 2.5; Whereas episode length during the later levels in a column should be nearer to 5. It's not that long maps don't have a place in map packs - They do. They really do. Long maps need to be mixed well with shorter, simpler maps, but the type of NUMA longmap that we've come to grow used to is strictly outside of a pack setting. And more complex maps absolutely ruin flavour and kill theme - The maps need to be unique and memorable, and when you come across the sixteenth map with eight switches, all hidden under bounce blocks, all guarded by 8 chaingun drones and seeker drones, smattered with mines, and on and on and on and on and on, it gets so repetitious. You have to strike a good balance between short and long maps, simplistic and complex ones, and so on. The challenges within each map and within each episode should also become progressively more difficult, but also progressively more innovative.

</ul>

This article is meant to explore, in-depth, what makes an EMP tick. As I said above, when you construct an EMP, you are mimicking what Metanet has set into motion. While there is room for innovation, there are some

Patterns - Metanet Utilizes a lot of patterns. Pattern recognition is absolutely huge in aesthetics, and is a big part of what is and is not appealing to the eye. Now, having one or two things that shoot off from this isn't a bad thing, but the only maps from this pack that I remember are the ones that included patterns.

Simplicity - Minimalism makes packs. Long maps don't belong in map packs. Packs, more often than not, are meant to be played as a whole, rather than just a conglomeration of maps. If it were just a smattering of different maps, you'd be better suited to submit them to NUMA as a series. Simple maps don't need to be short, and don't need to blow by. And good simple maps don't. Simplicity in a map doesn't dictate anything about the map's gameplay - It just takes skill as an author to utilize the simplicity in the right ways. Minimalism and unique execution are keys in what makes a good episodic map. If you make long maps, you're not necessarily a bad author, you're just a NUMA author. You don't do packs as well, because you can't grasp the idea of minimalism and simplicity. Look at every Mare and Raigan level - They do minimalism better than anyone. So, confusing difficulty and distance with aesthetic principles is where I think we're going wrong here. Simple maps have a perfect place in packs, particularly episodic packs, because the pack is meant to be played as a whole, rather than as 124 really long, grueling maps.

Physics - One of the lesser-thought themes in a Metanet map is the idea of Physics that they use. They use a ton of jumps, but not in the same way as NUMA authors do. Metanet uses downward jumps, making landings difficult to stick. They do this in a few other ways, too, but one of the most predominant things that their maps accomplish is, basically, to showcase their physics engine!

Space - I still haven't mastered space management, but Metanet does it beautifully. Their tilesets draw the eye to the action, and away from the empty space - In fact, in most of their maps, you don't notice empty space. This is perhaps the trickiest thing to get the hang of once you become an established mapper, but it's perhaps the most rewarding to get a good hold of, and most NUMA mappers (I'd say a vast majority, even) don't even have the concept at all.

Deviation - Perhaps the most overlooked rule of the MetaMap is Deviation. All of these rules

In fact, let me link you guys to a little something we began on a while ago. It's not finished, but it should give a couple ideas for ya'll;

<a href="http://c.1asphost.com/Aspirincomic/Map_Theory.html">Map Theory</a> (It all seems like really basic stuff, but you'd be surprised at how few people actually understand how this stuff affects gameplay).

For instance, take Raigan's post about SUBLiME, made <a href="http://metanet.2.forumer.com/index.php?showtopic=18162&view=findpost&p=377185">here</a>.








In either case, take <a href="http://www.instructables.com/id/E3F2Q19F23Z388R/">Instructables</a> (Which everyone needs to read) that Mare and Raigan put up this morning.

Consistency, patterns, flow, themes, utilizing space, physics, and simplicity. That's how you make a MetaMap. And I don't mean to detract from what you're saying l_d, but I think it's a pretty standard bottom-line that Minimalism and simplicity are cornerstones of design for packs. The reason you don't notice it in good maps is because those maps don't blow by - Take Zag and Brambles and Shambles from the first Legacy pack. Both are very simplistic levels at heart, but neither "blow by," and both are lengthy and memorable. A strictly short map can be good, too, but short maps are more often simple than long maps, and simplistic maps can either be short or long, difficult or easy. It's the execution that dictates all that. But long maps can make a pack just as easily - so long as those maps are executed well. And from what I've seen from past packs, long maps are more often suited for NUMA, since most people map for packs like they would map normally - they don't change anything when making a map pack. And those are the types of long maps that kill a pack. So, long maps do have their place in a pack, but the type of long maps that most starting authors put in to packs are those that are suited for NUMA - I make a distinction between a NUMA map and a pack map - Because there is certainly a large difference between the two.

Oh, and you're absolutely right - That's not how you make good maps. I never said they were the best maps, but I did say that they were pack maps. And that's the point, map packs aren't a collection of the 50 best maps you can make, they're a collection of 50 maps that work well together and compliment each other. I don't care about individual maps. Individual maps are NUMA maps - Map packs rely on so much more. Making good maps is an entirely different thing than making a good map *pack*. But map-packs *are* MetaMaps. That's how you make packs. That's what mapmaking for map packs is, at its heart. You're mimicking the Metanet ideal. You certainly are able to make long, arduous maps, but those don't belong in a pack as well as more balanced maps do. You have to plan the entire experience, instead of the map-to-map traversing. They don't belong in an episodic format as well because they don't *fit* in that episodic format. Again, you can certainly make them, and you can be an unbelievable NUMA mapper, as most people here are. But those people are awful at packs for these very reasons - They make single maps, as opposed to MetaMaps. And that's the key.

So, you can be a great single mapmaker, and an awful levelpack maker all at the same time. And when you put together a pack, you're attempting to do put together a set of maps that work well together, and that's why Metanet maps are heralded by me in this fashion - I'm an episodic mapper, and an awful NUMA mapper. That's how it's always been. And I didn't figure that our until I started with Legacy. Once I started doing work with the Legacy boys, everything suddenly clicked - My maps had purpose, they had rhythm and flow and everything that they needed to have - Because they fit within a greater whole. Love in an Elevator was an Episodic map. But no one liked it - No one paid it any mind. Same with all of the other 100+ maps I've submitted to NUMA over the years - No one likes them. Why? They're certainly not terrible maps. They're just not NUMA maps. The people who map for NUMA map with one goal in mind - And that's the map itself. People who map for a pack have an entirely different goal in mind. And that's how I began my Map Theory and the "Analysis of a Metamap" project came about. My maps thrive on minimalism and simplicity, and that lends itself more readily to a column format than any single map ever could. So, in that vein, I think Mare and Raigan did a Killer job of outlining what makes a good column-map, because column maps and episodic maps are that formulaic type, it's more structured, more balanced, and it takes a whole lot of seeing the bigger picture than "Map, map, map, long map, map with mines, map with Thurgood Marshall, map, map..."

And that's why packs like these fail (I really don't mean that for this particular pack, I'm just making a point). They don't come together in the fashion that they need to in order to succeed. And that's entirely where a map-pack needs to fall - It has to feel cohesive and it has to feel different than just a smattering of NUMA maps. So, really, I don't think we have a disagreement at all - Good mapping is good mapping, but good mapping for a levelpack is a much, much different beast. And beyond that, the thing that I outlined in my original post was referring specifically to Metanet Maps, and the article that I was going to write on them, so I think that everything I said therein is quite accurate. And beyond *that*, even, Mare and Raigan's instructional that I linked to is for people to get strictly better at making Metanet Maps, those maps for SUBLiME that will be representing Metanet in these episodes - In the main games for N+.

kkstrong - I don't remember *any* of the maps that I made for Vehemence, let alone playing through them. Those were a wacky 4 days, that's for sure. Plus which, Vehemence was more of a speed project - We didn't ever take the time to refine and make the maps flow together, it's more of a collection than a pack.

They certainly don't have to be in the Metanet style, you're right. And if I said that above, then I misused the term 'style.' MetaMap packs are episodic packs, and the reason you put out a pack of levels is to mimic the episodic format, and not so much to mimic the Metanet Style. If that isn't your goal, then you've missed the idea of map packs altogether. Sendy's maps may have been amazing (In fact, all of her maps are amazing), but here's the thing - She didn't sacrifice an ounce of style to make her maps fit into an episodic setting. Her episodes worked unbelievably well in the episodic setting because she understood the principles behind why you put out an episodic pack (And Hell, if she didn't, she sure did a Hell of a job of bluffing it). She made her levels more minimalistic, simplistic, and worked with the themes of the game, the timer, the physics, and spacial differences. And this isn't a stylistic thing, it's something that has to change for your maps to fit into episodes. I'm not even entirely sure why, but episodes just need this cohesive feel to them in order to feel like an episodic pack.

Now, don't get me wrong, people release levelpacks every day that go against this very idea. Non-episodic packs are all over, and they're great packs, but they're not MetaMap packs. They're not meant to be Episodic packs, they're meant to be a collection of NUMA maps. And style has nothing to do with the thought that they're not episodic, it's the thought that each map was a separate entity from each other map - No thought is given to organization, no thought is given to where levels go in the pack, no thought is given to the timer, or to the aesthetics of the episode, or any of that. Again, it's just a bunch of NUMA maps. Sendy did a fantastic job of incorporating Minimalism into her pack, particularly in maps like Honeycomb Chambers and Gnarley Grotto - All of the flavour is still full there, but the maps are simplistic, and to what end? To make the pack Episodic. And because of that, they fall into the category of MetaMaps, and not due to her style, but due to the theme of the pack - The theme of episodes. If you look at Sendy's NUMA maps, and then at her columns, you'll see a drastic difference in execution, but almost zero difference in style. But even here, her style contrasts quite a bit with Metanet's style. Sendy puts bounce blocks in out-of-the-way locations, makes longer-type maps, and decorates tiles like none other. All of which go against Metanet's style, but don't necessarily go against the episodic ideal. Which is why her pack works. She didn't make single maps, she made episodic maps, and in her style. And that's the key point to what I was saying above - It's not at all about Metanet's mapping style, it's about the theme of what episodes are made for.

So, if your pack isn't a MetaMap collection, it's a NUMA-level collection. If the pack is the former, then the idea is to mimic the Episodic format, right? If the pack is the latter, then it's just a collection of NUMA-levels in a text file. Sendy went that extra step to make sure the levels were flavourful enough to play through as a whole, instead of just a few maps of increasing difficulty. Which is where the "rift" comes in. And, if you're just submitting a bunch of NUMA maps in a text file, why not just go the extra mile and submit them as a series on NUMA? Because that's all it really is. If you're releasing a pack, you have to have at least some thought to cohesion and conglomeration, or the pack ends up falling short.

In either case, as you said, I think it rather comes down to a difference in style and a difference of what we each like, rather than a problem with the mapping themes. Because they're two separate areas of thought. Episodic Maps vs. NUMA Maps is where I'm coming from, where I think you're thinking more along the lines of a difference of styles.

#425126 11 2008-04-05T01:08:34Z Kablizzy
Treatise on Research and Game Development

I began writing this up a number of years ago, during Magic: the Gathering's early years, and I had forgotten all about it until recently, when I began playing PoxNora.

<b>Research and Development</b>

Research and Development is the heart and soul of any company's future. You can have any amount of marketing and advertising and spend any amount of money on packaging design, but in the end, it's the concept product that decides a company's future.

Monsoon? Give me a break. Why was Monsoon nerfed? Monsoon was a really good, solid spell with a plethora of applications.


<b>Psychology, Communication, and Impacts Upon a Work Environment</b>

Stages of Conflict -
Decision
Steamroll - Win/Lose
Compromise - Lose/Lose - Nerfs always compromise
Consensus - Win/Win

Self-Fulfilling Propechy - Perception shapes reality.

Reflected Appraisal, also called a "Through the Looking Glass" Analysis... We see things through the eyes of others. Relates to ego, arrogance, stubbornness.

Self-Concept - So resistant to change that we seek out information that tends to conform to our current perception of the situation.

A great deal of what we see depends upon what we are looking for.

Unrealistic expectations of the game-state, of others, and even of themselves.

Supportive Climate for Change. Relatively stable, yet flexible, set of perceptions.

Understanding - List of things that you know about the situation.
Esteem - How you feel about things on that list.

Always fix the mistakes, and never the blame.

Perceived situation - Situation you believe it to be in moment of honest examination

Interpersonal Conflict:

Taking the perspective of another person is always more difficult, but it is often the most important lesson in debate situations.

Message Overload - The intensity and frequency of messages is high.

Message Complexity - Density of the message itself.

Pre-judgment coming into debates.

Listening/Interpretive reading - Do you intend not to listen?

Communication Climate - Energy between people. Can either be postive or negative.

Having fun and relaxing - Boosts communication, Oxytosin

Recognition - Recognize that the person is there.

Acknowledgement - Let them know you are listening.

Endorsement - Let them know that their world view of the situation is valid.

Don't think the way you communicate is the only way to do so.

A debate is an exchange of information. An argument is an exchange of beliefs. A fight is an exchange of insults.

Conflict is natural and beneficial.
Incompatible goals
Unrealistic Expectations
Differing Rates of Growth

Selfishness - Humans (Players) are selfish. As such, we have a tendency to respond to the environment based upon our percieved needs.

Gap between reality and perceived reality. We are only ever aware of a small part of the environment.

We Begin communications based upon our needs.

Better Communication - Based on others' needs.

Selection - Select what you are paying attention to (Intensity, Repetition, Motives)

Scripts - Guide to Behaviour, Guide to Actions.

Schema - Mental structures by chunking and grouping information together.

The processes with which we analyze the world can often be misleading.

Prototype - Closest example you have in your mind.

Personal constructs - Yardstick, Measurement, Least -> Most, Measurement of the range of satisfaction.

Stereotypes -> Take away individuality.

Braceleting -> Side issues



Defense Mechanisms -> Overt impacts upon communication choices.

Fixation - Choice to stop at a certain level of psychological growth.

Regression - Reached a certain level of psychological growth, choose to revert to an earlier state.

Avoidance - Eliminate the anxiety of conflict, avoid situation.

Humor - Divert anxiety or conflict by making fun of it.

Interpersonal communication traits -
Co-operative - Issue-oriented
Obstinate - People-Oriented
Escapist - Avoidance-oriented

Grace - Excusing someone who has no right to deserve forgiveness.

Archetypes - Turtle - Passive, wants needs met, apt to be martyr.
Shark - Win/Lose
Teddy Bear - Nothing's ever wrong, conflict unsettling
Fox - Compromise, BalanceRelational Goals
Owl - Consensus, Personal and relational goals equal, can be very exhaustive.

Subliminal communication, reading between the lines.

Unlike a potato, a boiled-down speech becomes less dry.

Credibility, Confidence, and "faking it."



So, really, the field of Research and Development is more about communication techniques and ways to successfully present a case than it is about being able to crunch numbers and balance systems.

Specifically relating to game development, however, there needs to exist an air of understanding of a number of fundamental concepts. First and foremost is the idea of human err. This idea also integrates back into the whole "Fix the problem, not the blame," doctrine, in that game analysis is rarely a numbers game, it is a conceptual game. It deals with problems of a conceptual nature, and all problems that arise are almost exclusively conceptual problems, and not numbers problems. As related to stat-based games, it is never the fault of the numbers, but the fault of the basic game concepts that don't fit into the mould of the game.

For instance, in a game using only integers, percentages become either less or more effective due to rounding. Thus, a 50% increase in a given area (Let's say 7) will always either result in either ten or eleven, and no other number. But what happens when that difference between ten and eleven means the difference between underpowered and unusable? It is certainly not the fault of the numbers that makes a thing imbalanced - The concept parameters were shattered, stepped outside of, and what was once thought to be in acceptable realms is no longer that way.


<b>Nerfing</b>

<b>All</b> nerfs should ideally occur during development. When an R&D team goes in to balance a new set, their main job is to make sure the result is a fun, flavourful environment, where everything flows together and works well within the confines of the game. Beyond that, an R&D team is meant to initially catch any potential areas of abusability in the game-state. Now, this doesn't always happen. Many things can get in the way.

The following is a list of runes in PoxNora that have, to-date, been suggested as "too powerful." Runes with an asterisk beside the name are runes that have been subject to restructuring during the course of the game.

#425129 14 2008-04-05T01:15:18Z Kablizzy
Psychological Disorders and Ramifications of Detrimental Behaviour

I'd like to speak a bit today about the Virginia Tech shootings that occurred this week here in the U.S. I've heard a lot of opine on the matter, and I think I should set a few things straight.

First and foremost, about this Cho guy. Yeah, he had some problems, he did. And what he did is inexcusable, it really was, but does anyone ever stop to think what would cause something like this? What would cause someone to snap like that? Does anyone stop and think that there may have been a progression of what this guy went through throughout his life?

Most people agree that this guy was crazy. He had a lot of problems. But were those problems inherent in him, or was it instilled in him? This goes way back to the whole idea of nature vs. nurture.

Now, each time I try to write one of these articles, the magnitude seems to come out all wrong, and the initial purpose lost. I can't seem to breach this barrier of thought to really, truly express what is running through my head. Ever heard the saying "If you see a rat, there's five more that you don't see?" That's what my thought process is akin to. Whenever I write one of these articles, what I say just barely scratches the surface of what's going through my head. A lot of the stuff that I think on these subjects is very intangible, and the thought processes so complex, that I rarely get to succinctly put forth all of the nuances of these things that I write on. So, for every article that I put up here, there are five larger parts to that article that you don't see. There's a larger idea on my head that I'm not touching upon.

#425136 19 2008-04-05T01:29:36Z Kablizzy
So, I'm good at logic. In A Practical Study of Argument, by Trudy Govier, she states:

QUOTE
A person who tries to persuade you by rational argument will claim that because the premises are true or acceptable, the conclusion should be accepted. The arguer is saying, in effect,
Premise 1
Premise 2
Premise 3
Premise N
Therefore...
Conclusion


She then goes on to explain how a cogent argument can be supported:

QUOTE
The basic elements of a cogent argument, referred to here as the ARG conditions, are as follows:

1. Its premises are all acceptable. That is, it is reasonable for those whom the argument is addressed to believe these premises. There is good reason to accept the premises...
2. Its premises are properly connected to the conclusion...The condition may be usefully subdivided into two parts:
a. The premises are genuinely relevant to the conclusion... that is, they give at least some evidence in favor of the conclusion's being true.
b. The premises provide sufficient or good grounds for the conclusion...


So, taking those into consideration, and I abbreviated a lot, since her book is leagues deeper than that, anyway, using those conditions, you can evaluate any argument.

So, let's take your argument in kind.

QUOTE
1.) Whatever exists, has a cause
2.) The universe had a begining
3.) Therefore, the Universe had a cause


Now, let's go first to the A condition, Acceptability of premises. In order to properly judge an argument, we have to determine whether statements one and two are acceptable, within a reasonable doubt. In order for a premise to be acceptable, it needs to meet one of the following:
1. It is supported by a subargument that is cogent.
2. It is cogently supported elsewhere, without dispute,by the arguer or another person, and the fact is noted.
3. It is known a priori to be true.
4. It is a matter of common knowledge.
5. It is supported by appropriate testimony.
6. It is supported by appropriate appeal to authority.
7. It is not known to be unacceptable, as such, and can serve provisionally as the basis for argument.

Now, taking into account the above factors, I don't think that either premise 1 or premise 2 meet any of the requirements for being acceptable. Neither statement is supported by subargument, neither statement is supported without dispute elsewhere, neither statement is a priori true, neither statement is common knowledge to be true, neither statement can be proven by either testimony or appeal to authority, since no testimony nor authority is appropriate enough to back such a claim. The only thing that is even remotely close to proving the premises is number 7, but I will tell you why they are indeed unacceptable.

#425165 37 2008-04-05T02:04:18Z Kablizzy
[b]Big, Big Announcement, guys.[/b]

Well, Ive got a lot of news tonight, and a lot of time to say it in, so Ill be elaborating as well as I can on everything that needs to be said. 

First off, Id like to announce a rather big staff change. This is my official resignation from staff at Heroes of Ivalice. Most of you already know this in some form or another, or have been aware of it coming for some time, now. However, I feel that many of you still do not quite know why exactly this decision has been made, and I feel, personally, that I owe it to you all to come clean with everything thats happened over the past weeks and months, and bring it to everyones attention, as opposed to keeping secrets, and being shadowy about the whole affair, like I have done. I feel that it is my responsibility to inform you all about whats been going on, and to reveal the reasons why I felt the need, and have seen fit to resign from staff. Before I get into all that, though, Id like for you all to keep in mind that I have been working with the good of the sim in mind, and from whats gone on over the past few months, I cannot, and will not let this go on one second longer. Before I begin explaining, I want to say that these views are my own, and do not reflect the views of the remainder of the staff. Im simply providing the reasons why I am leaving.

With that in mind, the Ishy / Arkain / Greywolfe situation has been going on behind the scenes for quite some time now, and has worn everyone thin, on all sides. When we first started the game, Arkain was assigned as Kandor Reina, and Ishy was assigned as Saint Victor (Actually, I believe they picked the roles.  I only clarify this because everything within this document is going to be contested in some form or another, so Im covering my bases). When they were assigned to these roles, they were given some loose guidelines for how these kingdoms were to act. Amongst these goals, for Gallione, were to play Kandor to be Militaristic, and for Glabados, to play Victor to be a sort of Anti-hero, ruling with a Vote or Die attitude towards heretics. In doing so, the tones for those kingdoms were relatively set for the game. Unfortunately, the boundaries for rulers were overlooked while starting, and all kingdoms began to expand far more rapidly than they were supposed to. Among other kingdoms, Gallione expanded far beyond its boundaries to be the largest kingdom in the game. This was slated for no sooner than the first year or two, but happened within the first handful of months. This, I really had no problem with. The kingdoms expanded a bit fast, they did what they felt they needed to do to survive. 

However, Arkains fervor for playing Kandor as overtly militaristic quickly became an issue for the games longevity. No kingdom was supposed to advance so readily upon another, nor so soon. When Arkain took Thieves Fort under the Gallione banner, a large chunk of propositions became obsolete, as they depended upon the kingdoms not expanding for a long, long while. The entirety of Exeum Ditaria was considered to be dissolved, and that proposition arc was given up upon. This wasnt much of a big deal, as it was a mistake on my part to think that such things would go perfectly.

When Arkain invaded Fovoham, it was a big deal for us, as no kingdom was supposed to be eliminated from the game quite that soon, which is the position that we were put in, having to face what was on our plate. After discussing what to do, we made the decision that Arkain should expand his borders no further, and brought it up. Our request was ignored outright, and Gallione invaded Fovoham. Thus, after much more discussion, we came up with the idea that the remnants of Exeum Ditaria would amass their forces in order to get revenge upon Gallione for taking their home, and to buy us at least a turn to discuss what else to do. This went over quite successfully, causing Gallione to retreat. In the process, Arkain was cited as complaining about Exeum Ditarias forces moving through his lands unseen. Which is oddly funny, since he insisted upon ignoring our request, and then took it upon himself to complain when we did something about it. I dont like being forced into a corner, and then told that Im not allowed to fight, if you get my drift. The first battle of Fovoham was called off, with Gallione retreating.

We discussed things further during the following turn, and came to the conclusion that Gallione should not move further into Fovoham. Again, we brought this up, and thought that it was made fairly clear that we didnt want any further aggression brought upon Fovoham. Instead, our request was again ignored outright, as Arkain amassed the entirety of his forces to attack Fovoham a second time. In doing so, he moved troops from all of his cities, into Zeakden and Mandalia, and declared an attack with them on the same turn, both of which being illegal actions for troop movement, in the sense that troops can only move one city per turn, and if a unit of troops enters a city on a given turn, they are unable to attack in the same turn. 

Now, before I go any further, I want to stress that movement of troops and attacking with said troops was not something that was covered in-depth, as we assumed that all staff members were aware of the existing rules at the other sims that we are all a part of. After all, I believe that there is only one, perhaps two staffers who were uninvolved in other sims prior to HoI, and we assumed that it was common knowledge, and if it wasnt, that those who were confused about it would ask. This was not the case. In Arkains defense, though, it could easily be said that he neither knew of what we wanted for Kandors goals, nor for troop movements until it was brought to his attention. And thats fine. We informed him that it wasnt a legal troop movement, he concurred, and we moved on. The very same happened when we asked him not to invade further. But even after our concerns [I]were[/I] brought to his attention, we were ignored, and he pressed his agenda on, regardless. Either way, his first instance of attacking before he was supposed to and moving troops in a way that he wasnt supposed to can be overlooked, and I do not hold him responsible for that whatsoever. It was a shortcoming of not making things clear, and after which, there should have been no problem, nor any discussion on the matter. It was a dimension of development that we didnt foresee, and thus, I take full responsibility for not making clear the rules on troop movements and the rules and aims on how kingdoms were expected to act in relation to other kingdoms, as well as expansionism.

But regardless, the first time Arkain invaded Fovoham, we made it clear that we did not want further aggression upon any kingdoms for a while, and that Kandor should back off the aggression a bit, and stew for a while. So, we believed for this to be settled. Back to Arkains second attack on Fovoham. After we made it clear that none of us were happy with his invasion, he amassed his troops in Mandalia and Zeakden, and attacked Fovoham once again, even with the troops who had just arrived that turn. Again, we went into discussions, and I was confident enough in my tactics to believe that I could beat his force of 900 strong with Fovohams forces at that time. In doing so, I believed that Arkains troops would be depleted, and the aggression would end. Unfortunately for Fovoham, and for the storyline, the Gallione forces pulled out a victory, and Kandor took Fovoham, at which point, we again made it clear that no further aggression upon the kingdom of Fovoham would be tolerated, due to storyline purposes. Again, we were ignored outright, and Arkain continued playing the overtly militaristic role that we had requested him not to continue playing for a while. After which, Fovoham disbanded, and Gallione took Riovanes. This, to me, was fine, as I wouldnt expect him to just leave an empty city open for the taking. That was completely in-character for Kandor. The remainder of his aggression, however, was completely unwelcome.

So, to clear these things up a bit, I took it upon myself to speak to Arkain, Ishy, Redbird, and Greywolfe about it, airing my displeasure about the whole situation. What I was told by them all was that our storyline must be able to flow and adapt to things like this, and be able to take on challenges within smoothly, which I completely agree with, and which our storyline did, quite famously. But what wasnt mentioned, by any of them, is that the entire time all this was going on, we were voicing our concerns over Arkains movements, and despite our displeasure, requests, and demands for him to cease his actions, Arkain made no move whatsoever to rectify those actions, and, to be frank, gave no indication that he cared about what we wanted at all, nor what was good for the game. I agree that a storyline needs to mesh and flow, and be able to change, but this entire debacle should never have occurred to begin with. There should have been no need for the storyline to change, it was going fine just the way we had it. And, regardless of the storyline, we made it clear that Arkains actions were not to be tolerated, and were ignored outright. The reason we have a storyline is because we have ideas planned for you guys to take a part in, and, to be completely blunt, the storyline was the only thing that we even had ready for version one launch. And that was thoroughly destroyed by the problems that have been plaguing the sim since April. 

So, some of you may be wondering at this point why nothing was done about all of this. Well, the answer is quite a bit more complex than you think, and Ill be getting into it a bit later on, as well. But at this point in time, around the time Riovanes Disbanded, I was content with the fact that Arkain wasnt aware of what he was doing at the time, and wasnt aware of what was expected of him. The first incident or two, I could forgive, but to press on as he did was unforgivable. Thus, no action was taken against him for two main reasons: First, because he wasnt aware of our expectations of him, and second, because he told us that he was planning on retiring Kandor, and handing over his kingdom to his PCs to rule. This was acceptable, and in the GMNPC shuffle, we assigned Anatollos to him, fully expecting him to retire Kandor and begin to play Anatollos. We made it clear here, as well, that this was something that needed to happen sooner rather than later, and we were yet fully expectant of him to be playing Anatollos within a month or two, game time. 

But instead, Arkain continued his hostilities, this time with other nations, proclaiming his Kingship over all of Ivalice, and inciting war with Lesalia. This, to me, was far beyond unacceptable. The agreement between us was that Kandor was to retire, and hand the kingdom off to his PCs to rule. This did not happen whatsoever. In addition, after airing further concerns to Ishy, Arkain, Greywolfe, and Redbird, it came to my attention that Arkain fully planned on warring with Lesalia, and upon crushing Lesalia, planned to attack Glabados beyond that. Again, I found this completely unacceptable, for two reasons: First, it was blatantly clear by this point that Arkains advances upon other kingdoms was not only unwelcome this early in the game, but also disobeying direct orders from the remainder of the staff. Secondly, and more importantly, because it then became painfully clear that he had no intention of retiring Kandor any time soon, as per our agreement. Beyond that, it also became clear to me that he had no intention whatsoever of paying any heed to our concerns or requests. Which is something that is unacceptable from a member of our staff.

So, again, I found myself airing my concerns at Ishys crew, being met with the same The storyline should adapt argument that they had used before, again, defending Arkains actions to the end. To blind oneself to someones wrongs simply due to relation is ridiculous, and the fervor with which they defend each other only makes me realize that no matter what we say in this matter, in their eyes, they will be right, and we will be wrong, and I think that its time for us to go our separate ways. And that brings us back to the question, Why wasnt anything done about him? And as I said, that answer is complex. 

As most of you know, Ishy, Greywolfe, Redbird, and Arkain are friends IRL. And, to me, it was a terrible move to have them working on staff together, particularly at different levels of staff involvement. And Ive been aware for some time now that Ishys relationship with Arkain, as well as with Greywolfe, has been nothing short of unprofessional. In all of the conversations that Ive had with Ishy, Greywolfe, and Arkain, Ive discovered that not only were all three of them acting unprofessionally, but that all three of them were also acting directly against the best interests of the sim as a whole, and rather, acting in the best interests of [I]themselves[/I]. Despite the fact that its clearly stated in both the rules and the staff activity drafts that no staff member is to view information outside of the staff forums, such information flowed freely and carelessly amongst them. It is a bannable offense for 

This, I will go into shortly. Many have questioned me as to why we would keep such people on staff. Even Redbird and Greywolfe, after hearing what I had to say, questioned why we would keep Ishy on staff. 

Thus, for the sake of the sim, and for the sake of keeping the peace amongst everyone, I opted to keep my opinions hidden, and to not voice my concerns about Ishy and Arkain, time and again, despite the severe detriment that they were providing for the sim. Now, what would make us want to have Ishy no longer on staff, to begin with? First and foremost, Ishys inexcusable attitudes, towards staff and players alike, was the first of many things that alerted me that Ishy may not be right for an Admin position, let alone a staff position. Secondly, it was brought to my attention a while back by Greywolfe that Ishy had begun to alter his GMNPCs stats without authorization of any other staff member. Not necessarily a big deal if he would have come to the other staff about it, but when you get into just straight-up cheating, and thinking that you can get away with it, well, thats inexcusable. Thirdly, upon hearing that Lionel, Lesalia, and Gallione may be attacking him, Ishy threatened to metagame if any aggression were to come to the church, in the form of calling down miracles to annihilate all opposition, which was not an agreed part of what Victor was able to do. If Ishy had it in his head that Victor should be able to do that, then he should have brought it up with the remainder of the staff. I understand that hes an Admin, but to throw his weight around as though he is the only Admin is not something Ill tolerate.

But back to the point at hand. We, as a staff, after Greywolfes Kurohana incident, made it [I]perfectly[/I] clear to all staff members that staffers were not, under any circumstances, and regardless of reason, to plot against PCs, particularly not to kill them. While I didnt agree with this totally, I followed it, for the good of the sim. When Greywolfe got wind of the ruling, he threw a fit, and quit staff, setting himself up as a martyr, and assuming that he was being scapegoated into quitting. This was not the case. When the ruling went up, it was the culmination of many staff plots that had gone up, but the only plot from a staff member that had resulted in the death of a PC was the one sent in by Greywolfe. In addition, when Bruggers character, Rugger Cole was excommunicated from Gallione, a price was set upon his head, and plots were sent in to bring him back to Gallione to stand trial for treason and a handful of other charges. On top of that, when Crazy attempted to plot to kill a member of Limberry, the plot was completely cancelled, for this very same reason. When Arkain captured Riovanes, he killed one of the PC-officers. In addition to that, once Arkain made his proclamation declaring Kingship over all of Ivalice, The PCs in Lesalia responded in kind. They compiled their own proclamation, denouncing Kandors right to the throne. Once this happened, Arkain sent a plot to a band of assassins to kill Malice and Mordreds characters, both PCs. To this, I was outraged, as was the assassin whom he contacted, who just happened to be a member of the kingdom of Lesalia. The assassin refused Arkains offer outright, both on principle of in-character relations, as well as the simple fact that it was clear to everyone that staff were not, under any circumstances, to plot against PCs. Yet, he did it anyway, blatantly disregarding our staff rules. When he got wind that the assassin refused to run his plot, he threw a tantrum, over what, I still have no idea. After this, a number of kingdoms agreed to rise up against this Gallione threat, to quell Arkains aggression. Goug, Lesalia, Lionel, Bethla, and New Murond formed a coalition against Gallione. Upon hearing this, Arkain threw yet another tantrum. The coalition was a completely valid IC move against someone who was attempting to oppress the land against everyones will, but it seems that since things did not go his way, yelling and complaining about it to everyone whose ear he could bend would somehow rectify the problem. 

On top of all of this, staff tensions were at a nigh-constant peak due to the arguments that Ishy, Greywolfe, and Arkain would constantly bring to the table. Arguments would erupt over the smallest things, but only when it involved one of those three directly. If one of us were to bring up a point, it would be swiftly and viciously countered by Arkain, Ishy, and Greywolfe, arguing silly technicalities that had little bearing on the situations at hand, and ignoring what the remainder of us thought best for the sim. Particularly over the Kurohana incident, when we decided that staff members should not plot against PCs, Greywolfe was swiftly and harshly defended by Ishy and Arkain, complaining wildly about how unfair it was to single out Greywolfe for something such as that. It happened time and again when Arkain refused to listen to our requests and demands, Ishy jumped right in, bellowing and cursing at everyone like a maniac, adopting an Im right, youre wrong, and thats the way it is attitude, mostly because he knew that if we opposed him, he could just shut HoI down, and that would be the end of it. It happened time and again, and particularly around the time of Arkains quitting a short time ago, Ishy jumped readily to Arkains aid, with vile words spoken about everyone except Arkain, steaming and complaining about what a terrible injustice had been done him. It is my full belief that no matter a staff members relation to anyone on the forums, staff are here to be unbiased and fair to all, not just to friends and comrades, and not so blinded by unwarranted loyalties to IRL buddies that the sim suffers because of it. Ishy did just this, solely because of his relation to Greywolfe and Arkain, and despite the situation, he berated our members and staffers in kind.

Upon MotBs voicing of his opinion on the kingdom of Sweegy, Greywolfe quickly informed Ishy, who stormed into the IRC channel, berating and demeaning MotB in ways that no member should ever be forced to put up with. The very same went on with Prince RXI, and other members of our sim, and it wasnt acceptable then, and it most certainly isnt acceptable now. In addition to this, Ishy has made a pact with MotB to bring him back into the sim if he helps Ishy gather evidence against Prince RXI. Why would he do such a thing? Because the Prince RXI incident had to do with one of his comrades. It is my full belief that no matter your IRL relation to someone, your duty is to the sim, and only to the sim, and the behaviours that Ishy and crew have displayed in relation to each other is nothing short of Goddamn disgusting. To abandon all senses of logic and reason in order to defend a friend of yours, whether that friend is in the wrong or not, is sickening, particularly when said friend(s) berate you behind your back and wonder why you have a staff position in the first place is ridiculous, and I, for one, will no longer stand for it.

Right before Arkain resigned from staff, a pair of our sim members made accusations that Arkain was cheating. While I do not believe that Arkain was actually cheating overtly, beyond the troop movements that I detailed above, I do believe that certain things were overlooked to the point where they could have easily have been seen as such. But instead of handing out a simple warning, and discussing it with staff, Arkain and Ish went on a rampage, promptly throwing massive tantrums and whining about how unfair things are, threatening to do this and that, voicing their blatant dislike over these wild allegations, most of which have since been proven to be true, all of which I have included in this announcement, and all of which, I am prepared to back up 100%.

When these allegations were brought to the staffs attention, I received an angry message from Greywolfe calling the allegations nothing short of bullshit, and expressing his outrage over not being able to defend himself, despite the fact that all of this information was contained in the staff forums, and, Greywolfe not being staff anymore, is absolutely and completely none of his concern, nor was it for his eyes whatsoever. Had Ishy not mentioned anything, Greywolfe would have (Rightfully so) had no say in the matter. In addition, showing information contained within the staff halls of such a sensitive nature is an offense worthy of demotion anyway, and I have quite a large chunk of proof that information flowed exceedingly freely between the trio of Ishy, Arkain, and Greywolfe. Formulae contained within the GM halls are not to be shown to anyone lower than a GM, and doing so, as it clearly states within the thread, in and of itself, is reason enough for removal from staff, and permanent removal from the game. 

In addition to all of this, there is more that this trio has done in direct opposition to the forward progression of the sim, and I can no longer tolerate it.

The ways that Arkain, Ishy, and Greywolfe have acted are befitting of nothing more than common internet trolls, and none of them should ever be in a position of power, whether together or alone, and so long as any of them are on staff, or related to the game, I will not be. There is no excuse for the behaviours that have been displayed by this trio, and I am no longer going to stand by idly and allow this to go along.

Thus, it is with a heavy heart that I am announcing my official resignation from Heroes of Ivalice staff. Normally, in situations such as this, I would give them a chance to defend themselves, but for the behaviours that have been displayed here by them over the past months, no explanation would [I]ever[/I] suffice. It is my full belief that none of these members were ever involved in the sim for the good of HoI, but rather, were here solely for their own enjoyment, and only their own enjoyment, and nothing else. Their stubborn, arrogant, and elitist attitudes, as well as their unwillingness to change said attitudes despite the sims best interests, paired with the fact that they thought they could get away with said behaviour, as well as all of the things that Ive listed here, has earned them my ire. 

Now, all of this isnt to say that Ish and Grey and Arkain are bad guys. Im not trying to stack the deck against them, and I feel as though they do deserve some sort of defense in this matter. All three of them, while on staff, did their part as they could, when they could, and, as a matter of fact, I once held them all in the highest regard, until all of this happened. I was close friends with them all until all this came about, but when the entire staff, as well as the entire sim, has been compromised for the twisted enjoyment of a select few individuals in the sim, and for such a lengthy period of time, it was time for me to go. As Ive stated before, my duty to this sim is as an Admin first, and as a friend second, and that is what I expect for absolutely all staff members, regardless of relations to other staff members and/or players. I am, as well as the rest of the HoI staff, are 100% dedicated to giving you guys, the playerbase, the best experience with the sim as possible. And I believe that removing myself from staff is the best thing for the sim. If I continue to play this charade any longer, I will be no better than a simple hypocrite, and that is not something that I can bear any longer. 

With all this in mind, I feel that I do hold quite a bit of responsibility in this matter. Instead of the actions that Ive taken, keeping quiet about my views and motives, I should have instead voiced them to all parties, and taken care of this beforehand. But to be completely honest, The attitudes that have been displayed by this trio, as well as the sickening behaviours displayed by them, has caused me to lose faith in myself to continue on. 

So, on to the Raiser incident. The bolded part was meant to be mass-PMed to all staff prior to his ban. And the later bolded part is the reason for his ban. He was threatening to hack HoI and have access to the forums deleted, or something. I dont know the whole story, but needless to say, it needed to be done. I dont take kindly to threats, in any capacity, real or not, particularly when it comes to the sim.

So, first off, Id like to respond to this publically, as many of you have gotten wind of this, in some form or another. Our entire purpose here at HoI is for you guys. When you tell me that Im scapegoating someone for something that they did, it doesnt sit well with me. If you screw up, its your own damn fault, as Ive outlined here. Ive been more than professional over all of this, as has Kairo, and I had no intention to pick Arkain apart until he took it upon himself to ignore our every attempt to reason with him. Ill make no mistake that Ive been the most vocal over Arkains departure from our storyline, but the point of the sim isnt for the good of the staff, its for the good of the player. While on staff, it is expected of all staff members to adhere to what is reasonable and logical, and despite trying to talk and reason with Ish/ Arkain/ Greywolfe, they asserted that killing PCs off and attacking kingdoms was the right thing to do. 

Yes, Kurohana was Greywolfes PC, when you join staff, you have a responsibility to the playerbase to make the game fun for them, not to make the game fun for yourself. Ive sacrificed countless hours, days, months, whatever, for the good of the player, and seeing all of that go completely to ruin because Grey, Arkain, and Ish get offended at everything thats said in conflict with any of their views is ludicrous.

As for Arkain, theres a big difference between deterring from our storyline for a PC and deterring from our storyline for a staff member. Arkain had it within his power at all times not to do what he did. And it was the consensus of the entire staff and a good portion of the players that what Arkain was doing was wrong. But despite this, he continued pushing his luck, over and over and over again, and it came to the point where I couldnt handle it anymore. We let this crap go on for far, far too long to begin with, and then they pushed it even farther. Arkains second offense should have been worthy of removal from staff. Not to mention the free-flowing sharing of information between them all. The things that go on amongst staff, in the staff forums are of no concern to those who are not on staff, and this bond was broken at every turn by Ish, Arkain, Greywolfe and Redbird. This is a ban-worthy offense in and of itself, and there should have never been any discussion on this matter, particularly when there are those who would be so deceitful as to try and make us look like the bad guys in this situation. 

I took the high road; I kept my mouth shut this whole time. As did everyone. No one turned on Arkain like vultures until he gave us the proverbial finger over and over and over and over and over and over again, and made it clear that he had no intention of keeping the game fun for the players, but kept steamrolling on in his own interests. We allowed Arkain to ruin storyline arc after storyline arc, continuously asking him, requesting of him, and finally demanding of him that he stop. But he didnt. He became indignant and self-righteous, and continued to do as he wished to do, regardless of consequence, arguing ridiculous technicalities that werent even relevant to what he was doing. He assumed no responsibility for his actions, and, strangely, tried to scapegoat the remainder of us to be the bad guys. He did what he wished against the entire staffs will, and then plotted to kill PCs, knowing full well that it was strictly forbidden for staff. And when confronted with it? He and Ish throw their tantrums, and Red and Grey spread lies like this to make people like Raiser believe that things went on that didnt go on. 

[u]In addition, Im sure there will be a rather severe backlash to this, and many complaints flying around, mostly about how Im making up stories and exaggerating and treating them unfairly, and scapegoating them all, so Im willing to back up every last one of my statements here. I have absolute and uncontestable proof to all of this, and said proof is 100% available to absolutely everyone that wishes to see it, upon request. I will not allow further lies and slander to be spread so wantonly, particularly when the delicate balance of HoI lies in these worn hands. Ishy, Arkain, and Greywolfe can complain about these accusations all they wish, but I guarantee that my proof will prove to anyone who has a doubt that what I have said here is unwaveringly true.[/u]

All I wanted for you guys was a good sim that you could have fun with. And due to the actions and behaviours of a few bad apples, thats been thoroughly and completely ruined for me. Im sorry its had to come to this, as Ive had tons and tons of stuff planned, but I simply will not be on the same staff as a person who condones and promotes the behaviour of those who wish to ruin the sim. Thus, I am doing the following. I am calling for the immediate resignation of Ishy. The only way I will return to staff at this point is if Ishy resigns, and doesnt come back. Ever. If he doesnt resign, youll never see my ugly mug again.

Phew. Long post. I doubt this will even fit into a single post.

[b]Big, Big Announcement, guys.[/b]

Well, Ive got a lot of news tonight, and a lot of time to say it in, so Ill be elaborating as well as I can on everything that needs to be said. 

First off, Id like to announce a rather big staff change. This is my official resignation from staff at Heroes of Ivalice. Most of you already know this in some form or another, or have been aware of it coming for some time, now. However, I feel that many of you still do not quite know why exactly this decision has been made, and I feel, personally, that I owe it to you all to come clean with everything thats happened over the past weeks and months, and bring it to everyones attention, as opposed to keeping secrets, and being shadowy about the whole affair, like I have done. I feel that it is my responsibility to inform you all about whats been going on, and to reveal the reasons why I felt the need, and have seen fit to resign from staff. Before I get into all that, though, Id like for you all to keep in mind that I have been working with the good of the sim in mind, and from whats gone on over the past few months, I cannot, and will not let this go on one second longer. Before I begin explaining, I want to say that these views are my own, and do not reflect the views of the remainder of the staff. Im simply providing the reasons why I am leaving.

First and foremost, Id like to make it clear that Ive been the reason behind most of the tensions here at HoI. Most of you know about whats been going on with Ishy / Arkain / Greywolfe, but what most of you dont know is that Ive been planning on removing all three of them from staff for some time now. Ever since the debacle with Kurohana, Ive been planning on a coup of sorts, to remove all three from staff, without their knowledge whatsoever. Ill go into this a bit later. 

The situation has come to light, and for my part in all of this, I have chosen to abandon my position here, for the good of the sim. This evening, I was approached by Ish about my plot to ban him once our new domain went up. Ive been planning this for some time, in order to clear up many staff problems that weve been having. In hindsight, these problems werent caused by Ish, but caused by myself.

#425936 45 2008-04-07T09:02:47Z Kablizzy
Even if I were to determine afterwards that it were an enormous mistake, I'd still do it. It's strange, and even a bit arrogant (Well, a lot arrogant) to think that I've somehow got the keys to life, but the way that life presents itself, I view it in a specific way. And it's not easy being green, as they say.

Like Dave said, when you know what life is about, at its basest level, you don't have anything to look forward to. And at some point, you come around, and you end up having to live life anyway. Because at some point, pessimism drops off the edge, and falls into optimism's waiting lap. But I'm not there yet. I'm constantly defeated by nothing at all. Knowledge is power, to an extent, but more than that, and you just spin your wheels in the air. I think too much about too many things, and it becomes a game between me and my brain to figure out all of life's complexities. And while I'm doing it, I sit here, doing nothing at all.

Anyway, I know Dave, and he has a lot of the same type of wisdom that I have - In fact, I see a lot of myself inside him. And vice versa.

...

But for those of us who ponder as a career choice, that's all we end up doing. I'm not sure if I (And he) can actually be successful or fulfilled. And that fucking sucks to think about. Which I do. Often. And thus, we come back to square one.

#426018 48 2008-04-07T19:15:51Z Kablizzy
Quote: Keron Cyst, April 07, 2008 12:37 pm
Then change such a horrid view.
Ahahahahahahahah. Ahahahaah. Ahahah. You're classic.

I'm not quite sure how much of my life I've told you, but I've been at this proverbial bottom-of-barrel situation a number of times in my life. I've been poverty-stricken, my entire family has died, and I didn't think there could be another level of bullshit to sink to. But sure enough, there is, and I'm there.

How do you continue the struggle when you have nothing to struggle for? Everyone around me is successful with no effort. It's handed to them. I have to work my balls off to stay poverty-stricken. Not to stay afloat - but just to slow the financial bleeding - I have to work many times harder than anyone else around me, just because of the situation I was born into. I was born in-debt, difficult as that may be to grasp.

Something that Dave said a while ago struck me - There are people in the world who can't change their circumstances. There are people who are born into situations that they can't claw their way out of. That's life. We're born, we die. Men in my family don't live past fifty. Call this a mid-life crisis, but you're right in part - I'm beyond considering suicide. How I've been able to go this long without being a raging alcoholic is nothing short of miraculous to me. I guess I'll share this with you guys -

http://thenothingspace.blogspot.com/

I was going to post that publicly, but I decided it'd be better kept to friends than random internet denizens. I don't even remember what I wrote there, but it's mostly stream-of-consciousness.

I dunno. Maybe I'm overreacting. But in tallying up all the things I own, I come up with the grand total of -$7000 or so. That's right, taking into account everything that I own, I owe someone $7000. If I were to die right now, taxpayers would have to eat $7000 of debt from me. I've got eleven cents in my checking account, and a High-School graduate in this economy isn't even worthy of a McDonald's job. When I say that I have no money, I don't mean "except the equity in my house and my car and the $10,000 in savings bonds that my Grand-pappy gave me," I mean none. I mean that my assets equal less than nothing. I am, in fact, worse off than a homeless person, on paper. And given another month of this, I'll be right there with 'em. I guess you could call me worth less. Ahahah. I'm a riot.

I've no family, I've no prospect of family. And even as bad as things seem, I still have the will to get up in the morning, put on my smiley face, and go wave to the adoring fans. I don't know how. Y'know what my best two traits are? Thinking and Manipulation. People call me The Mindfuck for a reason - Why does everyone here adore me? Fuck if I know. I show them what they want to see, I guess. That's why everyone loved me at my old job too - I can change modes depending upon who I'm with. The only people I can really relax and hang out around are those that I cling onto - There's a small handful of people here, and an even smaller handful in the real world that I would do the justice of calling 'friend'. And these are the people who I let my guard down with - They're the people who I don't have to put on a smiling face for, I can just be myself, and they won't judge me. They're the people who I want to come to my wedding (Which is, for the most part, another bluff - It's closer to say that Gayathri and I want to get married, but in reality, will never get the chance to) and who I want to keep in contact with when I'm gone from here.

Insofar as game development, no one wants to hire a jackass like me. For all the touting and posturing I do in declaring myself a Game Developer, I've really never done it. I've really never done anything - I can twist my words in such a way as to make it seem that I've got a bunch of life experience, but most of it is bullshit. It's bluffing. So I've made a couple map-packs, and helped shape a game or two that was already in-progress. So I'm a good writer. No one will hire a good writer unless I can show them something that I've gotten published. So I can fake a smile. I'm 'great' with people, but I don't want to be. I hate people. I can't Goddamn stand people. Back to the thinking thing, I can point out flaws in every person around me, and to toss in a quote, "I hate mankind, for I think myself one of the best of them, and I know how bad I am." People make me miserable, and interacting with people is perhaps the thing I'm best at. Who says God is without a sense of irony?

Knowledge of life comes inherently to me. It's not a matter of preponderance or changing a view. It's just there. I can't change any 'view,' because I wouldn't believe the change. I can't tell myself that I'm not going to die - Life is life. It is what it is. The truth is - We're born, we live for anywhere between 0 and 78.4 years, and we die. Some of us work, some of us toil. Most of us get sick. All of us experience heartache. How do I change that? How does a change of viewpoint give me a new skill to toss out to a potential hiring manager? I can't put "Self-proclaimed Jack-of-all-Trades" on a rsum. No one wants to hire an amateur. No one wants to deal with me, they want someone with at least 2 years of experience in any field that I would go into. How do you get that experience? Balls if I know. In reality, I'm a fragile, frightened man. What I put forth here is all posturing and imagery; I have a good, solid head on my shoulders and I have I've got some brilliant thoughts in my head. Those things don't do a thing for me, in reality. They allow me to point out flaws and criticize everyone, but those people I criticize can all do things that I can't. Everyone's good at something - What I'm good at isn't marketable. There's no room for an Aristotle or a Darwin in this society. Prophets and Scholars are a deceased profession. I can't get paid to sit here and say, "Why?" in this day and age. I need skills. I need marketability. Stuff I just don't have.

Jumping in and striving is all well and good, but I don't have anything to strive for. And I don't mean that in the whiny, nihilistic sense, I mean that there is literally nothing for me to strive for. I am good at some things, but the things that I'm good at aren't going to do much for me. I'm not a good sportsman, I don't know business. I know lots about people, but without a little piece of paper on my wall that tells someone that I know lots about people, they could give a shit. After this semester, I can no longer attend school unless I get a miraculous grant from some mysterious government agency, and I can't get a good job unless the economy miraculously turns around. Where does that leave me, man?

I know that sounds very narrow, but I've spent my entire life at-odds with life itself. You know what kind of drive that I have; What kind of perseverance I hold, so what does it mean when life gets me down? I've spent my entire life struggling to get myself into a position where I can actually make something of myself - I figure if I can save X amount of money, or get Y amount of education, that things will be fine, but the rug keeps shifting underneath me. It has been for the last quarter-century. When I was born, homes were $50,000 around here; Gasoline was $.79 a gallon. And now, homes here are little less than a Quarter of a Million dollars. Gas is over 3.00 now. The savings that my Grandfather had was wasted entirely on his medical bills - And he was the only man in our family who had a savings. Everyone else has been a complete low-life. I was born into a society where I don't belong - Morally, idealistically, financially, and otherwise. I'm turning into my father, despite my best intentions. I've been a failure thusfar, in every way except one. I'm an eloquent bitch. I've got a brain that just won't quit. If I could make money off it somehow, I would, but everything I've tried has been a dead-end. It's more defeating than one would think when every aspect of your life is a failure. And having to crawl myself up out of a pit just to be average or normal is not something that I'm capable of. I guess that's what separates folk like me from the greats - I mean, Shania Twain was poverty-stricken, and she took her guee-tar to Tennessee, and totally made it. Ah, if only I weren't such an awful vocalist. I can't go camp out in my van. I don't own a fucking van. I can't liquidate assets, pack up and move. I'm not capable of taking chances, because even the slimmest chance of failing means I'm homeless for life. My chances have to be certainty. I can't rely on luck, because luck has never been on my side. It's always worked against my family, and I've learned that I have very few options open to me that are actually decent.

I sometimes wonder if my time here is preordained to be short-lived. I wonder why I can't have a fulfilling career, or a long-term relationship. And I wonder why I don't have any skills to facilitate a long, healthy, rich, fulfilling life. Perhaps I wasn't meant to be down here for all that long. Maybe I've just got one lesson to learn, and then off I go. Perhaps I wasn't meant to live to more than 30; Maybe I'm destined to just reach one person that I won't meet until I'm 28, affect their life, and be done with it. Perhaps that's why I'm not supposed to be married, or why I can't finish school - Maybe I'm just not meant to. It sure makes sense that way. When the chips are stacked against you, you can either play the ante until your stack is gone, or you can go all-in. I'm not really willing to go all-in because I think I'm supposed to have all of these things. I feel that I'm supposed to be happy, but maybe that's just not in the cards for me. Perhaps I have to eat the Queen of Spades every game for a reason.

What the Hell am I even posting for? I don't expect anyone to 'get' my situation - It's mine to deal with as I can. I'm just still searching for my answers, and I'm still not convinced that those answers exist for me.

Good morning! Welcome to Week 6 of the Monday Night NUMA Map League.

Since George is unable to run this week, I will be taking over for him. This week, hearkening back to Sketch's Ten Minute Map Ladder Tournament, this week's theme will be Ten-Minute Maps. This is a concept we haven't tried before, so I'm expecting it to go over extremely well. All maps must be made within a ten-minute time-frame of when you began. I want to see how brilliant you guys are with a time limit. Whenever you guys are ready, let's see what you guys have!

Announcements:
- Due to starting a bit late, the Submission Deadline will be extended slightly.
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, April 16th.
- These will be done on the honor system, so either time yourself, or have someone else time you.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Limited Resources

Administrators:
  • George
  • Kablizzy
Rules:
  • All submissions must be entered into NUMA.
